knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Secant Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Hessian-approximation form of a smooth unconstrained variable-metric secant framework and distinguishes its general symmetric form from its positive-definite variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, and choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a symmetric nonsingular matrix \(B_0\in\mathbb R^{n	imes n}\). At each index \(k\in\mathbb N_0\) for which \(B_k\) is nonsingular, a variable-metric secant method chooses \(\alpha_k>0\), sets \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}
abla f(x_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and defines \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\). It then selects a symmetric matrix \(B_{k+1}\) satisfying the secant equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\); continuation in this form also requires \(B_{k+1}\) to be nonsingular. In the positive-definite variant, one instead takes \(B_0\succ0\) and selects steps and updates that maintain \(B_{k+1}\succ0\); the compatibility condition \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\) is then necessary for a positive-definite matrix to satisfy the secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In Hessian-approximation form, a variable-metric secant method computes each search direction from a symmetric nonsingular matrix and updates that matrix to reproduce the latest gradient change along the step. A positive-definite variant additionally requires the updates to preserve positive definiteness and therefore requires positive curvature along each accepted secant pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}\) and \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\); in the positive-definite variant, \(B_{k+1}\succ0\) and necessarily \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric Hessian-approximation matrix at iteration k.
Search direction computed from the current matrix and gradient.
Positive step length at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, deterministic quasi-Newton modeling; the definition covers direct and inverse matrix representations without imposing a particular update formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathfrak V_k=(s_k,y_k,M_k,\mathcal C_k,\mathcal U_k)\] is a variable-metric secant model when \(M_k\in\mathcal C_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), the next metric is \(M_{k+1}=\mathcal U_k(M_k;s_k,y_k)\in\mathcal C_{k+1}\), and it satisfies either the direct secant equation \[M_{k+1}s_k=y_k\] or the inverse secant equation \[M_{k+1}y_k=s_k.\] In the direct convention the local step solves \(M_kd_k=-\nabla f(x_k)\); in the inverse convention it is \(d_k=-M_k\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-metric secant model consists of a changing matrix approximation, its admissible matrix class, the displacement-gradient pair, and an update map. The updated matrix must interpolate the observed gradient change: in the direct convention it satisfies \(M_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), while in the inverse convention it satisfies \(M_{k+1}y_k=s_k\). The matrix is then used respectively through a linear solve or a matrix-vector product to form a quasi-Newton direction.

immediate_consequences_latex:
If a direct metric \(B_k\) is positive definite, then \(d_k=-B_k^{-1}
abla f(x_k)\) is a descent direction whenever \(
abla f(x_k)
eq0\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not require symmetry, positive definiteness, low rank, or least change; those are additional structural choices.
Nonsmooth generalized secant relations and stochastic gradient differences are outside this scope.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-pair secant information model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(x,x_+\in D\), \(s=x_+-x\neq0\), and \(y=F(x_+)-F(x)\). For minimization, \(F=\nabla f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact single-pair interpolation data; measurement error and relaxed secant equations are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal I(s,y)=\{(s,y,Q(y,s)):s\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\},\ y\in\mathbb R^n\},\qquad Q(y,s)=\{B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:Bs=y\}.\] The pair \((s,y)\) is the secant information, and \(Q(y,s)\) is its direct feasible model. If \(y\neq0\), the inverse feasible model is \[Q^{-1}(s,y)=\{H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:Hy=s\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-pair secant information model records a nonzero displacement \(s\), the associated change \(y\) in the mapped quantity, and the affine set of matrices that reproduce this observation. A direct model is any matrix \(B\) satisfying \(Bs=y\). When \(y\neq0\), an inverse model is any matrix \(H\) satisfying \(Hy=s\). In optimization, \(y\) is the gradient difference, so the secant equation makes the new quadratic model recover the previous gradient at the previous iterate.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
For \(m_+(z)=f(x_+)+
abla f(x_+)^T(z-x_+)+	frac12(z-x_+)^TB(z-x_+)\), \[Bs=y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
abla m_+(x)=
abla f(x).\]
special_cases_latex: For an affine map \(F(z)=Az+b\), one has \(y=As\) exactly.
immediate_consequences_latex: The constraint \(Bs=y\) supplies \(n\) scalar linear equations for the \(n^2\) entries of an unrestricted matrix.
boundary_notes: The equation alone generally does not determine a unique matrix.
A symmetric feasible matrix requires the compatibility implicit in symmetry; positive-definite feasibility additionally requires positive curvature.

notation.meaning: Affine set of direct matrices satisfying the secant observation.
Affine set of inverse matrices satisfying the inverse secant observation.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pair Secant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine model class determined by one displacement–gradient pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\neq 0\). A single-pair symmetric secant model for \((s,y)\) is any matrix \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\) satisfying \[Bs=y.\] Given a reference matrix \(B_0\in\mathbb{S}^n\), its correction \(E=B-B_0\) therefore belongs to the affine constraint set \[\mathcal E(s,r)=\{E\in\mathbb{S}^n:Es=r\},\qquad r=y-B_0s.\] Thus one pair constrains only the action of the model along \(s\); an update rule selects one element of this affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single secant pair requires the symmetric model to map the step to the observed gradient change; an update rule chooses among all matrices satisfying that constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is admissible exactly when \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\) and \(Bs=y\), equivalently \(E=B-B_0\in\mathcal E(s,y-B_0s)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility condition for a positive-definite single secant equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when one secant pair admits a symmetric positive-definite realization of the form $J_+J_+^T$ with $J_+$ nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $s_c,y_c\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $s_c\neq 0$. There exists a nonsingular matrix $J_+\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ such that $J_+J_+^Ts_c=y_c$ if and only if $s_c^Ty_c>0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For vectors s_c and y_c with s_c nonzero, a nonsingular matrix J_+ such that J_+J_+ transpose maps s_c to y_c exists exactly when the inner product of s_c and y_c is positive.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multi-pair secant model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_m]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) and \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), where every \(s_i\neq0\) is a retained displacement and \(y_i\) is its corresponding gradient or residual difference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite collections of exact secant pairs in a finite-dimensional direct or inverse matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direct multi-pair secant family is \[\mathcal Q(Y,S)=\{B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:BS=Y\}=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{B:Bs_i=y_i\}.\] Its inverse counterpart is \[\mathcal Q^{-1}(S,Y)=\{H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:HY=S\}.\] A direct family is consistent exactly when \(Yz=0\) for every \(z\in\ker S\); equivalently, the linear assignment \(s_i\mapsto y_i\) is well defined on \(\operatorname{range}S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-pair secant model requires one matrix to interpolate several retained displacement-difference pairs simultaneously. Stacking the displacements as columns of \(S\) and the corresponding differences as columns of \(Y\), the direct constraint is \(BS=Y\), and the inverse constraint is \(HY=S\). The direct system is feasible precisely when every linear dependence among the columns of \(S\) is also a linear dependence among the corresponding columns of \(Y\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[BS=Y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Bs_i=y_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
\[\mathcal Q(Y,S)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\ker S\subseteq\ker Y.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(m=1\), the family reduces to the ordinary single-pair secant model.
If \(m=n\) and \(S\) is nonsingular, the direct model is unique and equals \(B=YS^{-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(\operatorname{rank}S=r<n\), the constraints determine \(B\) only on the \(r\)-dimensional space \(\operatorname{range}S\).
boundary_notes: Symmetry or positive definiteness may make an otherwise consistent unrestricted family infeasible.
This definition does not prescribe which historical pairs should be retained or discarded.

notation.meaning: Matrices whose columns are retained secant displacements and differences.

knowledge_statements.title: Multisecant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous secant interpolation for finitely many vector pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For pairs \((s_i,y_i)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), form \(S=[s_1\ \cdots\ s_m]\) and \(Y=[y_1\ \cdots\ y_m]\). A multisecant Hessian model is a matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfying \[BS=Y,\] equivalently \(Bs_i=y_i\) for every \(i\). If symmetry or positive definiteness is required, the admissible class is intersected with \(\mathbb S^n\) or \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\), respectively; these intersections can be empty when the stored pairs are incompatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multisecant model simultaneously maps every stored step to its corresponding gradient difference, optionally subject to symmetry or positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is a multisecant model precisely when \(BS=Y\).

children.top_down_role: Models using block-valued displacement or curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Secant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block form of simultaneous secant constraints and their correction equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S,Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\), and let \(B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be a reference model. Writing \(B=B_0+E\), the block-secant equation has the equivalent representations \[BS=Y\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad ES=R,\quad R=Y-B_0S.\] Columnwise, \(ES=R\) comprises the equations \(Es_i=y_i-B_0s_i\). Consequently, a block update is any correction chosen from \(\{E:ES=R\}\), with additional structural restrictions such as \(E\in\mathbb S^n\) imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stacking secant pairs into blocks converts simultaneous interpolation into one matrix equation; the correction maps the step block to the residual block.

notation.meaning: block correction to the reference model
block secant residual Y minus B_0 S

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Pair Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility condition for a symmetric multisecant interpolant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S,Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\). There exists a symmetric matrix \(B\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfying \(BS=Y\) if and only if both \[\ker S\subseteq\ker Y\qquad\text{and}\qquad S^{\mathsf T}Y=Y^{\mathsf T}S.\] The kernel condition ensures that every linear dependence among stored steps is obeyed by the corresponding gradient differences. The symmetry condition is equivalently the collection of cross-pair identities \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_j=s_j^{\mathsf T}y_i\) for all \(i,j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric multisecant interpolation is possible exactly when gradient differences respect step dependencies and every pair of stored secants satisfies the cross-symmetry identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{B\in\mathbb S^n:BS=Y\}\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(\ker S\subseteq\ker Y\) and \(S^{\mathsf T}Y=Y^{\mathsf T}S\).

notation.meaning: null space of the linear map represented by S
the ith columns of S and Y

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated kernel and cross-symmetry conditions are the correct finite-dimensional feasibility conditions for a symmetric solution of BS=Y, but this nontrivial if-and-only-if extension theorem has no citation. An authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Hereditary Secant Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for retaining previously imposed secant equations after an update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(B_kS_k=Y_k\), where \(S_k,Y_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\), and set \(B_{k+1}=B_k+E_k\). The old secant information is hereditary under this update exactly when \[E_kS_k=0.\] Indeed, this condition is equivalent to \(B_{k+1}S_k=Y_k\). If a new pair \((s_{k+1},y_{k+1})\) is also imposed, the correction must simultaneously satisfy \[E_kS_k=0,\qquad E_ks_{k+1}=y_{k+1}-B_ks_{k+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An update retains all old secant equations exactly when its correction annihilates every previously stored step, while mapping the new step to its residual.

notation.meaning: blocks of previously retained secant pairs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hereditary secant property
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal J_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,k\}\) index retained pairs \((s_j,y_j)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\), with \(s_j\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-memory inheritance of direct or inverse secant equations; numerical tolerances are not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct matrix \(B_{k+1}\) has the hereditary secant property on \(\mathcal J_k\) when \[B_{k+1}s_j=y_j\qquad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J_k.\] An inverse matrix \(H_{k+1}\) has the inverse hereditary property when \[H_{k+1}y_j=s_j\qquad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J_k.\] Equivalently, with \(S_{\mathcal J_k}=[s_j]_{j\in\mathcal J_k}\) and \(Y_{\mathcal J_k}=[y_j]_{j\in\mathcal J_k}\), one requires \(B_{k+1}S_{\mathcal J_k}=Y_{\mathcal J_k}\) or \(H_{k+1}Y_{\mathcal J_k}=S_{\mathcal J_k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hereditary secant information means that the current matrix satisfies not only the newest secant equation but every equation selected for retention from earlier iterations. Thus the property is indexed by an explicit history set. In direct form the current matrix maps every retained displacement to its recorded difference; in inverse form it performs the reverse mapping.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[B_{k+1}\in\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J_k}Q(y_j,s_j).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal J_k=\{k\}\), heredity reduces to the current single-pair secant condition.
Full heredity uses \(\mathcal J_k=\{0,\ldots,k\}\); limited heredity uses a proper subset.
immediate_consequences_latex: Adding a retained pair can only shrink the feasible family of hereditary matrices.
Linear dependence among retained displacements imposes the corresponding consistency conditions on their differences.
boundary_notes: A usual one-pair quasi-Newton update need not preserve older secant equations.
The property concerns exact interpolation and does not assert that an update formula can maintain it under arbitrary data.

notation.meaning: Indices of secant pairs retained at iteration k.
Stacked retained displacement and difference matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent variable-metric representations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be a symmetric positive-definite direct metric, \(H=B^{-1}\), and let \(L\) be nonsingular lower triangular with positive diagonal such that \(B=LL^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingular positive-definite matrices in finite dimensions; indefinite factorizations require a different factor convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable metric may be represented by any member of the equivalent triple \[B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n,\qquad H=B^{-1}\in\mathbb S_{++}^n,\qquad L\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\ \text{lower triangular},\ \operatorname{diag}(L)>0,\ B=LL^T.\] For a secant pair \((s,y)\), the direct and inverse constraints are \(Bs=y\) and \(Hy=s\). The model step is equivalently \[Bd=-g,\qquad d=-Hg,\qquad LL^Td=-g.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same positive-definite variable metric can be stored as a Hessian approximation \(B\), its inverse \(H\), or a Cholesky factor \(L\) satisfying \(B=LL^T\). These are representation choices for the same linear operator and yield the same step in exact arithmetic. Their secant equations and computational operations differ: the direct and factored forms use solves, whereas the inverse form uses a matrix-vector product.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[Bs=y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Hy=s\] when \(H=B^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: With \(B=I\), one has \(H=I\), \(L=I\), and \(d=-g\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness is explicit in all three representations and guarantees a unique descent step for nonzero \(g\).
boundary_notes: If \(B\) is singular, an ordinary inverse representation is unavailable.
A Cholesky factor does not represent a symmetric indefinite metric; an \(LDL^T\) factorization is needed instead.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Approximation Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct variable-metric representation of local gradient variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an iterate displacement \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and gradient difference \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\), a Hessian-approximation representation stores \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) as an approximation to local gradient curvature. Its secant interpolation equation is \[B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.\] When \(B_k\) is nonsingular, the associated quasi-Newton search direction is obtained by solving \[B_kp_k=-
abla f(x_k),\] without explicitly forming an inverse matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct representation stores a symmetric Hessian approximation, enforces that it maps the latest step to the gradient change, and computes directions by solving a linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(B_k\) is nonsingular when defining \(p_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct Hessian-approximation representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\neq0\), and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional direct quasi-Newton models; symmetry and definiteness are optional refinements unless explicitly imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct Hessian-approximation representation at iteration \(k\) is a matrix \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) used as the quadratic coefficient in \[m_k(x_k+p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp.\] Its secant update \(B_{k+1}\) is required to satisfy \[B_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\] and its quasi-Newton direction is defined by \[B_kd_k=-g_k\] whenever this system has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian-approximation representation stores a matrix \(B_k\) as the curvature coefficient of the local quadratic model. The updated matrix interpolates the observed gradient difference through \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). A search direction is obtained by solving \(B_kd_k=-g_k\). If symmetry is imposed, the quadratic coefficient depends only on the symmetric matrix; if positive definiteness is imposed, the model is strictly convex and the resulting nonzero direction is descending.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The secant equation is equivalent to gradient interpolation by the next model: \[\nabla m_{k+1}(x_k)=g_k.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), the direction is the Newton direction.
For \(B_k=I\), the direction is steepest descent.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(g_k\neq0\), then \(g_k^Td_k=-g_k^TB_k^{-1}g_k<0\).
boundary_notes: The secant condition does not by itself guarantee invertibility or positive definiteness.
For nonsymmetric \(B_k\), only its symmetric part contributes to the scalar quadratic term.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Hessian Approximation Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse variable-metric representation and its dual secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inverse-Hessian representation stores \(H_k\in\mathbb S^n\) as an approximation to the inverse of local curvature. For the pair \((s_k,y_k)\), its inverse secant equation is \[H_{k+1}y_k=s_k.\] The quasi-Newton direction is then formed directly as \[p_k=-H_k\nabla f(x_k).\] If \(B_{k+1}\) is nonsingular and \(H_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^{-1}\), then \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\) are equivalent representations of the same secant information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse representation maps gradient changes back to steps and computes a search direction by matrix–vector multiplication; for nonsingular models it is equivalent to the direct representation.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable at the paired iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inverse secant condition is \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\), and it is equivalent to \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) under inversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Factored Metric Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite metric represented through a nonsingular square-root factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factored positive-definite metric is represented as \[B=LL^{\mathsf T},\] where \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular; equivalently, an upper-triangular convention may use \(B=R^{\mathsf T}R\). This representation guarantees \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Its direct secant equation becomes \[L(L^{\mathsf T}s)=y.\] Conversely, every \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) admits such a factorization, with a unique lower-triangular Cholesky factor having positive diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representing the metric by a nonsingular Cholesky-type factor enforces symmetry and positive definiteness automatically, while the secant equation becomes a factored linear relation.
assumptions_latex: For uniqueness, \(L\) is lower triangular with positive diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=LL^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite, and every \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) has a unique normalized Cholesky representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factored positive-definite metric representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), and let \(L_k\) be its unique lower-triangular Cholesky factor with positive diagonal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite direct metrics represented by Cholesky factors in finite precision; indefinite factorizations are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factored metric representation stores \[B_k=L_kL_k^T,\qquad L_k\ \text{lower triangular},\qquad (L_k)_{ii}>0.\] A factored secant update produces \(L_{k+1}\) such that \[L_{k+1}L_{k+1}^Ts_k=y_k.\] The associated direction is defined by the two triangular systems \[L_kz_k=-g_k,\qquad L_k^Td_k=z_k,\] which together are equivalent to \(B_kd_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factored metric representation stores the Cholesky factor of a positive-definite Hessian approximation instead of the dense matrix itself. The factor determines \(B_k=L_kL_k^T\). A factored secant update changes the factor so that its product satisfies the direct secant equation. The quasi-Newton step is computed by forward and backward triangular solves, preserving an explicit positive-definite representation whenever the updated factor remains nonsingular with positive diagonal.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[L_kz_k=-g_k,\ L_k^Td_k=z_k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B_kd_k=-g_k.\]
special_cases_latex: For a diagonal \(L_k\), the metric is diagonal with entries \((L_k)_{ii}^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Nonsingularity of \(L_k\) implies \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and uniqueness of the step.
The representation avoids reconstructing and refactorizing a dense updated metric when a direct factor update is available.
boundary_notes: A Cholesky factor cannot represent an indefinite metric.
Not every algebraic matrix update admits a stable direct update of its factor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural geometry of secant metrics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb M_n=\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(\mathcal A=A_0+\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb M_n\) be an affine class with translation space \(\mathcal S\), and let \(s\neq0\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional matrix-space geometry with exact affine structural and secant constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variable-metric structural geometry associated with \((\mathcal A,s,y)\) is the feasible intersection \[\mathcal F(\mathcal A;y,s)=\mathcal A\cap Q(y,s),\qquad Q(y,s)=\{B\in\mathbb M_n:Bs=y\}.\] A metric update is structure preserving when \(B_+\in\mathcal F(\mathcal A;y,s)\). Given an inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_W\) on \(\mathbb M_n\), a least-change structural update is the metric projection of the old matrix onto this intersection whenever it is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric structural geometry views matrix updates as motion in a finite-dimensional matrix space. An affine set \(\mathcal A\) encodes persistent structure such as prescribed zeros, fixed entries, or symmetry. The secant equation defines another affine set \(Q(y,s)\). Their intersection is the feasible geometry of matrices satisfying both kinds of information. A matrix norm supplies the notion of distance used to select one feasible update from that geometry.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(B\in\mathcal A\), every structure-preserving change has the form \(B_+=B+E\) with \(E\in\mathcal S\), and the secant condition becomes \[Es=y-Bs.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\mathcal A=\mathbb S^n\), the geometry is the symmetric secant family.
For a prescribed sparsity pattern, \(\mathcal A\) is the corresponding matrix subspace or affine translate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Feasibility is equivalent to the residual \(y-Bs\) lying in \(\{Es:E\in\mathcal S\}\).
boundary_notes: The positive-definite cone is not affine, so positivity is an additional convex constraint rather than part of the affine model used here.
If the intersection is empty, exact structure preservation and the exact secant equation cannot both be imposed.

notation.meaning: Affine structural class and its translation subspace.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric low-rank secant correction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B=B^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(s\neq0\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r=y-Bs\) be the secant residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symmetric rank-constrained corrections of a direct matrix; preservation of positive definiteness is not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric rank-at-most-\(q\) secant correction is a matrix \[E=UCU^T,\qquad U\in\mathbb R^{n\times q},\quad C=C^T\in\mathbb R^{q\times q},\] such that \[Es=r.\] The updated matrix \(B_+=B+E\) is symmetric, satisfies \(B_+s=y\), and obeys \(\operatorname{rank}(B_+-B)\le q\). The corresponding feasible correction geometry is \[\mathcal E_q(r,s)=\{E\in\mathbb S^n:Es=r,\ \operatorname{rank}E\le q\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric low-rank update changes a symmetric matrix by a symmetric correction whose rank is bounded. Writing the correction as \(UCU^T\) makes symmetry explicit. The correction must map the displacement \(s\) to the current secant residual \(r=y-Bs\); then the updated matrix satisfies the secant equation. Rank-one and rank-two formulas are the principal special cases.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[B_+s=y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Es=y-Bs.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(q=1\), a feasible nonzero correction has the form \(E=\alpha uu^T\).
Classical symmetric rank-two formulas lie in \(\mathcal E_2(r,s)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every correction in \(\mathcal E_q(r,s)\) has a range containing \(r\) when \(r\neq0\).
If \(r=0\), the zero correction is feasible and leaves the matrix unchanged.
boundary_notes: Low rank and symmetry alone do not guarantee positive definiteness.
The factorization \(UCU^T\) is nonunique.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Update Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frobenius least-change theorem for a symmetric correction satisfying one secant residual equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s,r\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\neq0\). Among all symmetric corrections \(E\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfying \(Es=r\), the unique minimizer of \(\lVert E\rVert_F\) is \[E_*=\frac{rs^{\mathsf T}+sr^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}s}-\frac{r^{\mathsf T}s}{(s^{\mathsf T}s)^2}ss^{\mathsf T}.\] Hence the orthogonal projection of a symmetric reference model \(B_0\) onto the affine secant set \(\{B\in\mathbb S^n:Bs=y\}\) is \(B_0+E_*\), with \(r=y-B_0s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unique Frobenius-nearest symmetric secant model is obtained by adding the displayed rank-at-most-two correction determined by the step and its secant residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Two Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct BFGS rank-two secant correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^{\mathsf T}Bs\neq0\) and \(y^{\mathsf T}s\neq0\). The direct BFGS correction is \[B_+=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{y^{\mathsf T}s}.\] The correction \(B_+-B\) is a sum of two symmetric rank-one matrices and therefore has rank at most two. It satisfies the secant equation \(B_+s=y\) and preserves symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct BFGS update combines two symmetric rank-one terms, producing a rank-at-most-two correction that satisfies the secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(B_+\) is symmetric, satisfies \(B_+s=y\), and has \(\operatorname{rank}(B_+-B)\leq2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-definite secant metric class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(s\neq0\), and let \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\) denote the symmetric positive-definite matrices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact single-pair compatibility with positive-definite direct and inverse metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direct curvature-compatible metric class is \[\mathcal P(y,s)=\{B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n:Bs=y\}.\] It is nonempty exactly under the curvature condition \[s^Ty>0.\] When this condition holds, the inverse curvature-compatible class is \[\mathcal P^{-1}(s,y)=\{H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n:Hy=s\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature-compatible direct metric is a symmetric positive-definite matrix that also satisfies the secant equation. Such a matrix can exist only when the observed curvature \(s^Ty\) is positive, because \(s^TBs=s^Ty\). Conversely, positive curvature permits a positive-definite symmetric extension of the prescribed action on the span of \(s\). The inverse class is defined analogously by reversing the secant mapping.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(B\in\mathcal P(y,s)\), \[s^Ty=s^TBs=\|B^{1/2}s\|_2^2>0.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(y=\gamma s\) with \(\gamma>0\), then \(B=\gamma I\) belongs to the class.
If \(s^Ty\le0\), the class is empty.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal P(y,s)\) yields a strictly convex quadratic model and a descent quasi-Newton direction for a nonzero gradient.
boundary_notes: Positive semidefinite metrics permit the boundary value \(s^Ty=0\) only with additional degeneracy.
The condition concerns one secant pair; simultaneous multi-pair positive-definite feasibility requires further compatibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Metric Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definiteness preservation by the direct BFGS update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and assume the curvature condition \(y^{\mathsf T}s>0\). Define \[B_+=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{y^{\mathsf T}s}.\] Then \(B_+\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(B_+s=y\). Thus the BFGS rank-two map preserves the positive-definite metric class whenever the incoming secant pair has positive curvature; if \(y^{\mathsf T}s\leq0\), no positive-definite matrix can satisfy that secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS preserves positive definiteness under positive secant curvature; nonpositive curvature is incompatible with any positive-definite model satisfying the same secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_+\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(B_+s=y\); moreover, existence of any \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) with \(Ms=y\) requires \(y^{\mathsf T}s>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Pair Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of one secant pair with a symmetric positive-definite direct metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\neq 0\). There exists a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfying the secant equation \(Bs=y\) if and only if \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\). Thus positive curvature is precisely the compatibility condition for the pair \((s,y)\) to belong to a positive-definite direct-metric class. If a particular positive-definite matrix \(B_k\) is prescribed, an update must additionally satisfy the chosen structural or least-change restrictions, but no such restriction can overcome failure of \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant pair admits some symmetric positive-definite direct metric exactly when its curvature product is positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Metric Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating inner-product metrics from symmetric indefinite secant models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric nonsingular matrix \(B\) with both positive and negative eigenvalues defines an indefinite secant regime: \(u^{\mathsf T}Bu\) is not a squared norm, and the direction \(p=-B^{-1}g\) need not satisfy \(g^{\mathsf T}p<0\). Compatibility with a secant equation alone does not prevent this regime. For example, with \(B=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), \(s=e_2\), and \(y=-e_2\), one has \(Bs=y\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y=-1\), while \(B\) remains symmetric and invertible but indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric secant matrix may be invertible yet indefinite; its quadratic form is not a norm, and its search direction need not descend.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists g\neq0:\ g^{\mathsf T}(-B^{-1}g)\geq0,\qquad u^{\mathsf T}Bu\ \text{takes both signs}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine secant hyperplane and metric projection
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb M_n=\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(s\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_W\) be an inner product on \(\mathbb M_n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine geometry of unrestricted exact direct secant constraints under a fixed matrix-space inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine secant set is \[Q(y,s)=\{B\in\mathbb M_n:Bs=y\}=B_0+\mathcal N_s,\qquad \mathcal N_s=\{E\in\mathbb M_n:Es=0\},\] for any \(B_0\) satisfying \(B_0s=y\). Its metric projection is \[P_{Q}^{W}(A)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in Q(y,s)}\|B-A\|_W.\] For the Frobenius metric, \[P_Q^F(A)=A+\frac{(y-As)s^T}{s^Ts}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct secant equation defines an affine subspace of matrix space. Any feasible matrix serves as an origin, and the associated translation space consists of corrections that annihilate \(s\). Once an inner product is chosen on matrix space, the closest feasible matrix is the metric projection of the old matrix onto this affine set. Under the ordinary Frobenius norm, this projection is the rank-one Broyden correction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[B\in Q(y,s)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B=B_0+E\ \text{for some }E\text{ with }Es=0.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(As=y\), then \(P_Q^F(A)=A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The unrestricted Frobenius projection changes only in the rank-one direction generated by the residual \(y-As\) and the displacement \(s\).
boundary_notes: Intersecting \(Q(y,s)\) with symmetry or sparsity changes the projection formula.
Iteration-dependent inner products produce a changing rather than fixed affine metric geometry.

notation.meaning: Translation subspace of matrices annihilating s.
Metric projection onto the affine secant set.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial Scaling Choices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar initialization of direct or inverse metrics from an available curvature pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), initialize an inverse metric by \(H_0=\gamma_H I\), where \(\gamma_H=(s^{\mathsf T}y)/(y^{\mathsf T}y)\), or initialize a direct metric by \(B_0=\gamma_B I\), where \(\gamma_B=(y^{\mathsf T}y)/(s^{\mathsf T}y)=\gamma_H^{-1}\). Both choices are positive definite and match the secant curvature in the scalar least-squares sense. If no reliable curvature pair is available, choose any prescribed \(\gamma>0\) and use \(H_0=\gamma I\), terminating initialization after checking finiteness and positivity of the scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use reciprocal positive scalar multiples of the identity, commonly scaled by the latest curvature pair, to initialize direct and inverse metrics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Time Initial Scaling of a Variable Metric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded Shanno–Phua initial-scaling procedure, separated from the extract's iterative SSVM scaling rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(H_0=I\). Determine \(\alpha_0\) by a line search giving sufficient objective decrease, or, whenever the quotient is well defined, set \[\alpha_0:=\gamma_0=\frac{s_0^Ty_0}{y_0^TH_0y_0}.\] Before computing \(H_1\), replace \(H_0\) by \[\widehat H_0=\alpha_0H_0\] and compute \(H_1\) from \(\widehat H_0\). This procedure scales the metric only at initialization, whereas SSVM performs scaling at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with the identity metric, scale it once by an initial stepsize or the stated curvature quotient before forming the first update, and thereafter do not repeat the scaling operation. This contrasts with SSVM scaling at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \alpha_0\text{ is obtained by a sufficient-decrease line search, or }y_0^TH_0y_0\neq0\text{ and }\alpha_0=\frac{s_0^Ty_0}{y_0^TH_0y_0}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat H_0=\alpha_0H_0\text{ is used to compute }H_1\text{, with scaling applied only at initialization}

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Metric Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector and symmetric-matrix geometries induced by a positive-definite weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric positive-definite weight \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), define the vector inner product and norm by \(\langle u,v\rangle_W=u^{\mathsf T}Wv\) and \(\|u\|_W=(u^{\mathsf T}Wu)^{1/2}\). On the space \(\mathbb{S}^n\) of symmetric matrices, define \(\langle A,C\rangle_{W}=\operatorname{tr}(WAWC)\) and \(\|A\|_{W}=\|W^{1/2}AW^{1/2}\|_F\). Positive definiteness of \(W\) makes both bilinear forms inner products and both displayed functions norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite weight induces compatible inner products and norms on vectors and symmetric matrices through multiplication and congruence.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Invariant Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivariance of direct and inverse metric models under nonsingular linear reparameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=Tz+b\) with nonsingular \(T\). If gradients, displacements, and metric matrices transform as \(g_z=T^{\mathsf T}g_x\), \(s_x=Ts_z\), \(y_z=T^{\mathsf T}y_x\), \(B_z=T^{\mathsf T}B_xT\), and \(H_z=T^{-1}H_xT^{-\mathsf T}\), then the secant equations and metric search directions are equivariant: \(B_xs_x=y_x\) if and only if \(B_zs_z=y_z\), and \(p_x=-H_xg_x\) implies \(p_x=Tp_z\) for \(p_z=-H_zg_z\). An update rule is affine invariant when applying it before or after these transformations gives the same transformed matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a nonsingular affine change of variables, properly transformed secant equations, metrics, and search directions represent the same computation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variational least-change secant update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(s\neq0\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) encode admissible structure, and let \(\|\cdot\|_W\) be a strictly convex matrix norm induced by an inner product.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional least-change updates over a nonempty structural secant feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variational least-change update of \(A\) is \[A_+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}}\frac12\|B-A\|_W^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad B\in\mathcal A,\ Bs=y.\] Equivalently, \[A_+=P^{W}_{\mathcal A\cap Q(y,s)}(A).\] If the feasible set is nonempty and closed and the squared norm is strictly convex, this definition selects at most one update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational least-change update is the admissible secant matrix closest to the current approximation in a specified matrix metric. The feasible set combines the exact secant equation with a structural class such as symmetry or sparsity. Thus an update family is determined by three choices: the secant data, the admissible matrix geometry, and the distance used to measure change.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update is the metric projection \(P^{W}_{\mathcal A\cap Q(y,s)}(A)\).
Writing \(E=B-A\), the same problem is \[\min_E\tfrac12\|E\|_W^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad A+E\in\mathcal A,\ Es=y-As.\]
special_cases_latex: With \(\mathcal A=\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and the Frobenius norm, the solution is the rank-one Broyden update.
With \(\mathcal A=\mathbb S^n\) and the Frobenius norm, the solution is the Powell symmetric Broyden least-change update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing either the structural class or the metric can produce a different update while preserving the same secant equation.
boundary_notes: If the feasible intersection is empty, this exact constrained definition has no solution and a relaxed formulation is required.
The definition does not assert positive definiteness unless it is included in the feasible class.

notation.meaning: Projection onto C in the W-induced metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Matrix-Norm Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form weighted least-change projection onto one symmetric secant constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\), \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(s\neq0\), and set \(r=y-Bs\) and \(c=W^{-1}s\). The unique solution of \(\min_{E=E^{\mathsf T}}\|W^{1/2}EW^{1/2}\|_F\) subject to \(Es=r\) is \[E_* =\frac{rc^{\mathsf T}+cr^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}c}-\frac{s^{\mathsf T}r}{(s^{\mathsf T}c)^2}cc^{\mathsf T}.\] Consequently \(B_+=B+E_*\) is the unique symmetric matrix satisfying \(B_+s=y\) that has minimum weighted change from \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted least-change secant update is the unique orthogonal projection of the current symmetric matrix onto the affine secant constraint.

notation.meaning: weighted displacement W inverse times s

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Frobenius least-change update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(s\neq0\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mathcal A\) be a closed admissible matrix class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided weighted Frobenius metrics and exact secant constraints in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the two-sided weighted Frobenius norm by \[\|E\|_{M,F}=\|MEM\|_F=\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(ME^T M^2EM)}.\] A weighted matrix-norm secant update is \[A_+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A,\ Bs=y}\frac12\|B-A\|_{M,F}^2.\] For symmetric updates one takes \(\mathcal A=\mathbb S^n\); other affine structural classes may be substituted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted matrix-norm update chooses the secant matrix whose change is smallest after a nonsingular two-sided scaling by \(M\). The weight changes which matrix directions are considered expensive. Together with the secant equation and an admissible class, it defines a metric projection problem. Ordinary Frobenius least change is recovered when \(M=I\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\widetilde E=M(B-A)M\), the objective is the ordinary Frobenius norm \(\|\widetilde E\|_F\) in scaled matrix coordinates.
special_cases_latex: Appropriate pair-dependent weights yield variational characterizations of DFP or dual BFGS updates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(M\) is nonsingular, \(\|\cdot\|_{M,F}\) is a norm and its squared objective is strictly convex.
boundary_notes: A singular weight defines only a seminorm and can destroy uniqueness.
The weight may be fixed or iteration dependent; these choices define different update systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Variational Characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-equivariant formulation of least-change secant updates as metric projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_x\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(s_x,y_x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\mathcal{G}_x\) be a positive-definite self-adjoint operator on \(\mathbb{S}^n\). Assume \(\{C_x\in\mathbb{S}^n:C_xs_x=y_x\}\neq\varnothing\), and define \[B_{+,x}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{C_x\in\mathbb{S}^n,\ C_xs_x=y_x}\|C_x-B_x\|_{\mathcal{G}_x},\qquad \|E_x\|_{\mathcal{G}_x}^2=\langle E_x,\mathcal{G}_xE_x\rangle_F.\] For a nonsingular change of variables \(x=Tz+b\), set \(s_x=Ts_z\), \(y_z=T^{\mathsf T}y_x\), \(B_z=T^{\mathsf T}B_xT\), and \(C_z=T^{\mathsf T}C_xT\). If \(\mathcal{G}_z\) is transported so that \(\|T^{\mathsf T}E_xT\|_{\mathcal{G}_z}=\|E_x\|_{\mathcal{G}_x}\) for every \(E_x\in\mathbb{S}^n\), then congruence maps the two feasible sets bijectively and their unique minimizers satisfy \[B_{+,z}=T^{\mathsf T}B_{+,x}T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-change secant projection is affine equivariant when the secant data and matrices transform by the corresponding coordinate rules and the matrix metric is transported isometrically.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{G}_x\) is positive definite and self-adjoint on \(\mathbb{S}^n\)

nonsingular linear part of the affine coordinate transformation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Congruence-invariant variational update rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal U(A;s,y)\) be a direct secant update rule, and let \(T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular. Under \(x=Tz\), set \(\widetilde A=T^TAT\), \(\widetilde s=T^{-1}s\), and \(\widetilde y=T^Ty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact covariance under nonsingular linear changes of coordinates for direct Hessian representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variational secant rule \(\mathcal U\) is congruence invariant when, for every nonsingular \(T\) and every admissible \((A,s,y)\), \[\mathcal U(T^TAT;T^{-1}s,T^Ty)=T^T\mathcal U(A;s,y)T.\] A variational characterization is invariant when its feasible class and matrix metric transform so that the transformed minimization problem has precisely this equivariant minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant variational characterization is one whose update commutes with a nonsingular linear change of variables. Direct Hessian approximations transform by congruence, displacements contravariantly, and gradient differences covariantly. Applying the update before or after this transformation must therefore produce congruent matrices. This definition concerns the update rule together with its feasible class and distance, not merely the secant equation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The diagram consisting of coordinate transformation and update application commutes for every nonsingular \(T\).
The transformed secant equation is preserved because \[(T^TBT)(T^{-1}s)=T^T(Bs)=T^Ty.\]
special_cases_latex: For orthogonal \(T\), the ordinary Frobenius norm is invariant under the congruence action.
Full affine invariance generally requires a data-dependent or metric-dependent weighting rather than an unweighted Frobenius norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: Congruence-invariant update rules do not depend on the particular linear coordinate representation of the same quadratic model.
boundary_notes: Translation of the base point is immaterial to secant differences and is not part of the displayed linear transformation.
No inspected source supplied a precise general definition with the full quantification over nonsingular coordinate changes.
review_flags: Precise source support is needed for the full congruence-invariance definition and transformation law.
Available least-change sources discuss scaling but do not explicitly support every quantified clause stated here.

Structured Least-Change Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-change secant projection restricted to an admissible linear matrix structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathcal{S}\), where \(\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{S}^n\) is a closed linear subspace encoding a prescribed matrix structure, and let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). For \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\neq0\), define \(\mathcal{F}=\{C\in\mathcal{S}:Cs=y\}\). If \(\mathcal{F}\neq\varnothing\), compute the structured least-change update as \[B_+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\in\mathcal{F}}\|W^{1/2}(C-B)W^{1/2}\|_F.\] The minimizer exists and is unique, belongs to \(\mathcal{S}\), and satisfies \(B_+s=y\). If \(\mathcal{F}=\varnothing\), no exact structured secant update exists under this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a structured secant update by projecting the current matrix onto the structured secant-feasible set in the weighted matrix norm; the update is unique when that set is nonempty, and no exact update exists when it is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{S}^n\) is a closed linear subspace and \(B\in\mathcal{S}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structured affine least-change secant update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J(x)=C(x)+A(x)\), where \(C(x)\) is available and \(A(x)\) must be approximated in an affine structural class \(\mathcal A=A_0+\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Let \(s=x_+-x\neq0\) and \(y=F(x_+)-F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact least-change updating of the unavailable structured component of a Jacobian or Hessian decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a component secant target \(y^{\#}\) and define \[Q(y^{\#},s)=\{B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:Bs=y^{\#}\}.\] A structured least-change update is \[A_+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A\cap Q(y^{\#},s)}\|B-A\|_W.\] The default target \[y^{\#}=y-C(x_+)s\] makes the complete approximation \(J_+=C(x_+)+A_+\) satisfy \[J_+s=y.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured least-change update applies the secant principle only to the unavailable component of a decomposed derivative. The approximated component is constrained to an affine class encoding known structure, such as symmetry, sparsity, fixed rows, or fixed columns. Among matrices satisfying both the component secant equation and this structure, the update chooses the one closest to the old approximation. Subtracting the action of the known component from the full difference gives a default component target that enforces the ordinary secant equation for the completed Jacobian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(E=A_+-A\), the correction satisfies \[E\in\mathcal S,\qquad Es=y^{\#}-As,\] and has minimum \(W\)-norm among such corrections.
special_cases_latex: If \(C\equiv0\), the definition reduces to an ordinary structured secant update.
Taking \(\mathcal A=\mathbb S^n\) produces a symmetric structured update; taking a sparsity subspace produces a sparse update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Known derivative information in \(C(x_+)\) is preserved exactly rather than re-estimated by the secant correction.
Feasibility requires \(y^{\#}-As\in\{Es:E\in\mathcal S\}\).
boundary_notes: A problem-specific target may replace the default when it better approximates the action of the unavailable component.
If the structural and secant constraints are inconsistent, an exact structured least-change update does not exist without relaxation.

notation.meaning: Known and approximated components of the derivative.
Secant target for the approximated component.
Affine class encoding retained matrix structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense symmetric quasi-Newton update family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k
eq0\), and let \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\). A direct matrix \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) approximates a Hessian, while an invertible inverse matrix \(H_k\in\mathbb S^n\) approximates its inverse.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, dense full-matrix secant updates; limited-memory and prescribed-sparsity representations are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense symmetric quasi-Newton update family is a collection of maps \(U_k:(M_k,s_k,y_k,\theta_k)\mapsto M_{k+1}\in\mathbb S^n\), where \(M_k\) is stored as a full \(n\times n\) matrix and \(\theta_k\) is an optional family parameter, such that every admitted update satisfies either the direct secant equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) or the inverse secant equation \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\). Classical members are distinguished by the rank and algebraic form of \(M_{k+1}-M_k\), by whether positive definiteness is preserved when \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and by direct-inverse representation duality. BFGS and DFP are symmetric rank-two positive-definiteness-preserving updates under positive curvature; SR1 is a symmetric rank-one update that may be indefinite; the Broyden class parametrizes rank-two updates containing BFGS, DFP, and, for a data-dependent parameter, SR1; PSB is the Frobenius-minimal symmetric secant correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense symmetric quasi-Newton update family consists of full-matrix maps taking a current Hessian or inverse-Hessian approximation and a secant pair to a new symmetric matrix satisfying the corresponding secant equation. Its classical members are classified by correction rank, definiteness behavior, direct versus inverse representation, and family parameter. BFGS and DFP preserve positive definiteness under positive curvature, SR1 can be indefinite, the Broyden class parametrizes several updates, and PSB is the Frobenius-minimal symmetric secant correction.
assumptions_latex: \(s_k\neq0\), and every denominator appearing in the selected update is nonzero.
For a positive-definiteness-preserving member, \(s_k^Ty_k>0\) and the current matrix is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{k+1}\in\mathbb S^n\) is stored densely and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) or \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\), with family membership determined by its correction formula and admissible parameter set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(B_k\) and \(H_k\) are nonsingular and mutually inverse, direct and inverse update representations describe the same updated metric precisely when \(H_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: BFGS, DFP, SR1, members of the Broyden class, and PSB are classical dense symmetric secant updates.
immediate_consequences_latex: A full dense realization requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) matrix storage, apart from auxiliary vectors.
The secant equation fixes the action of the updated matrix on one measured direction but does not uniquely determine a symmetric matrix without an additional update rule.
boundary_notes: A nonsymmetric rank-one Broyden update for nonlinear equations is not part of this symmetric Hessian-update definition.
Limited-memory and sparse quasi-Newton schemes represent different operation domains even when derived from the same algebraic formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense symmetric quasi-Newton update family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Davidon Symmetric Rank-One and BFGS Hessian Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense symmetric Hessian-approximation updates satisfying a quasi-Newton secant equation, including the rank-one denominator failure rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $d_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$, $g_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)$, and let $H_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be symmetric. Writing $r_i=H_i d_i-g_i$, if $r_i^{T}d_i\ne0$, the unique symmetric rank-one correction of $H_i$ satisfying $H_{i+1}d_i=g_i$ is
\[
H_{i+1}=H_i-\frac{r_i r_i^{T}}{r_i^{T}d_i}.
\]
If $r_i^{T}d_i=0$, or if $|r_i^{T}d_i|\ll\|r_i\|\,\|d_i\|$, this adjustment is skipped and $H_{i+1}=H_i$. If $g_i^{T}d_i\ne0$ and $d_i^{T}H_i d_i\ne0$, the rank-two BFGS update
\[
H_{i+1}=H_i+\frac{g_i g_i^{T}}{g_i^{T}d_i}-\frac{H_i d_i d_i^{T}H_i}{d_i^{T}H_i d_i}
\]
satisfies $H_{i+1}d_i=g_i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric quasi-Newton Hessian approximation is updated to satisfy the secant equation. Davidon's unique symmetric rank-one correction is used only when its denominator is safely nonzero; otherwise it is skipped. The displayed rank-two BFGS formula also satisfies the secant equation when both of its denominators are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_{i+1}^{\mathrm{rank\text{-}one}}=H_i-\frac{r_i r_i^T}{r_i^T d_i},\qquad H_{i+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=H_i+\frac{g_i g_i^T}{g_i^T d_i}-\frac{H_i d_i d_i^T H_i}{d_i^T H_i d_i},\qquad H_{i+1}d_i=g_i

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic, DFP with a symmetric positive-definite initial inverse approximation and exact line searches reaches a minimizer by iteration n.
assumptions_latex: \(H_k\text{ is generated by the DFP update}\)

conclusion.target: a minimizer of the positive-definite quadratic objective
conclusion.nonasymptotic_bound_latex: x^n\text{ is a minimizer, so termination occurs in at most }n\text{ iterations}.

step_and_control_rule: exact line search at every iteration
oracle_and_noise: no stochastic noise or inexactness stated

boundary_notes: Finite termination is asserted only for a quadratic objective with positive-definite Hessian and exact line searches.
The result does not provide a convergence guarantee for general nonlinear objectives or inexact line searches.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS line-search method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), let \(H_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and choose a step length \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, full-memory BFGS with a Wolfe line search and an inverse-Hessian realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The BFGS method is the iteration \(p_k=-H_kg_k\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), where \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the Wolfe conditions and \(\rho_k=(y_k^Ts_k)^{-1}\). Its inverse-Hessian approximation is updated by \(H_{k+1}=(I-\rho_ks_ky_k^T)H_k(I-\rho_ky_ks_k^T)+\rho_ks_ks_k^T\). The iteration is continued until a prescribed termination condition, such as \(\|g_k\|\leq\varepsilon\), holds. The Wolfe curvature condition and descent of \(p_k\) imply \(y_k^Ts_k>0\), so the displayed update is defined and preserves symmetry and positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The BFGS method computes the search direction as the negative current inverse-Hessian approximation times the gradient, obtains a step length satisfying the Wolfe conditions, forms the step and gradient-difference vectors, and applies the BFGS inverse update. Positive curvature makes the update well defined and preserves a symmetric positive definite inverse-Hessian approximation.
assumptions_latex: At every nonterminal iteration, \(p_k=-H_k\nabla f(x_k)\) is used and \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the Wolfe conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(B_k=H_k^{-1}\), the equivalent direct update is \(B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(H_0=I\) makes the first search direction the negative gradient.
A positive scalar multiple of \(I\) may be used to reflect the scale of the problem.
immediate_consequences_latex: The inverse update satisfies \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\).
Each dense iteration, excluding function and gradient evaluations, requires \(O(n^2)\) arithmetic and storage.
boundary_notes: Without positive curvature the undamped BFGS formula does not provide the stated definiteness guarantee.
This definition excludes damped BFGS and limited-memory BFGS.

notation.meaning: Real symmetric positive definite n-by-n matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS Iteration with Direct Matrix Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core BFGS iterate and direct-matrix recurrences; the extract makes no convergence claim and does not define the curvature vector y_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At every iteration for which the displayed expressions are defined, the BFGS method sets
\[
d_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k,\qquad s_k=\alpha_kd_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k=x_k-\alpha_kB_k^{-1}g_k,
\]
and updates the direct matrix approximation according to
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever the formulas are defined, BFGS uses d_k = -B_k^{-1}g_k, takes s_k = alpha_k d_k and x_{k+1} = x_k+s_k, and applies the displayed rank-two direct-matrix update to B_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of BFGS on Strictly Convex Quadratics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic BFGS with exact line searches and a positive-definite initial Hessian approximation on a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
f(x)=\tfrac12x^T A x-b^T x+c,\qquad A=A^T\succ0,
\]
on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $H_0\succ0$. At iteration $i$, set $v_i=-H_i^{-1}\nabla f(x_i)$, choose $x_{i+1}=x_i+t_i v_i$ by exact line search, and obtain $H_{i+1}$ from the BFGS Hessian update. Unless $\nabla f(x_i)=0$ at an earlier iteration, the method generates $A$-conjugate search directions. Moreover, for the applicable preceding indices, it preserves the extended secant equations $H_{i+1}d_j=g_j$ and satisfies $\nabla f(x_{i+1})^T v_j=0$. Consequently, it reaches the unique minimizer in at most $n$ iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a strictly convex quadratic in n variables, BFGS with a positive-definite initial Hessian approximation and exact line searches generates conjugate directions, preserves the earlier secant equations, and reaches the unique minimizer after at most n searches, unless it terminates earlier at a zero gradient.
assumptions_latex: x_{i+1}=x_i+t_i v_i\text{ with }t_i\text{ chosen by exact line search}
H_{i+1}\text{ is obtained by the BFGS Hessian update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k=x_\star\text{ for some }k\le n;\qquad v_{i+1}^TAv_j=0,\quad H_{i+1}d_j=g_j,\quad \nabla f(x_{i+1})^Tv_j=0\text{ for the applicable preceding indices}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS invariance, numerical sensitivity, conditional self-correction, and DFP duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative structural properties of dense BFGS. The self-correction statement is not a quantitative convergence or finite-step guarantee and is explicitly conditional on an adequate line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Variable-transformation invariance of a quasi-Newton update requires the defining least-change objective to be invariant under the same transformation; the stated weighted norms give this invariance for the DFP and BFGS constructions. When 0<y_k^Ts_k\ll1, \rho_k=(y_k^Ts_k)^{-1} is large and the inverse-BFGS formula may generate very large entries in H_{k+1}. BFGS nevertheless has a qualitative tendency to correct curvature estimates that impede progress, but this self-correcting behavior is asserted only with an adequate line search; Wolfe conditions provide the stated curvature-sampling safeguard. Finally, DFP and BFGS are dual under s\leftrightarrow y and B\leftrightarrow H.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invariant weighted least-change formulations make the updates invariant to corresponding variable transformations such as scaling. A very small positive curvature product can produce large inverse-metric entries. BFGS tends to repair harmful curvature estimates only when coupled with an adequate line search, with Wolfe conditions supplying the stated safeguard. DFP and BFGS are dual under interchange of the secant vectors and of the direct and inverse metrics.
assumptions_latex: The least-change objective and its weighting are invariant under the variable transformation under consideration.
s_k\text{ and }y_k\text{ are the displacement and gradient-change vectors, and }H_k=B_k^{-1}.
For the qualitative self-correction property, BFGS is coupled to an adequate line search; Wolfe conditions are the stated sufficient sampling safeguard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{transformation invariance};\qquad 0<y_k^Ts_k\ll1\Longrightarrow\text{possible large entries in }H_{k+1};\qquad \text{line-search-dependent self-correction};\qquad \mathrm{DFP}\xleftrightarrow[\,B\leftrightarrow H\,]{\,s\leftrightarrow y\,}\mathrm{BFGS}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct and inverse BFGS representation pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(H=B^{-1}\), \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(s^Ty>0\). Define \(\rho=(s^Ty)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic algebraic representations of one dense BFGS update under positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direct-inverse BFGS representation pair is \(B^+=B-\frac{Bss^TB}{s^TBs}+\frac{yy^T}{y^Ts}\) and \(H^+=(I-\rho sy^T)H(I-\rho ys^T)+\rho ss^T\). The pair is defined by the requirement that \(H^+=(B^+)^{-1}\), with the direct secant relation \(B^+s=y\) and inverse secant relation \(H^+y=s\). Both corrections are symmetric and have rank at most two. When \(B\) and \(H\) are positive definite and \(s^Ty>0\), both updated matrices are positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct BFGS formula updates a Hessian approximation, while the inverse formula updates its inverse. Starting from mutually inverse positive definite matrices and a secant pair of positive curvature, the two displayed formulas produce mutually inverse positive definite matrices satisfying the direct and inverse secant equations. Each changes its current matrix by a symmetric correction of rank at most two.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(V=I-\rho ys^T\), the inverse update is \(H^+=V^THV+\rho ss^T\).
special_cases_latex: If \(y=Bs\), then \(B^+=B\) and \(H^+=H\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The direct form supports linear solves with \(B^+\); the inverse form applies the search-direction metric by matrix-vector multiplication.
The two representations encode the same secant metric in exact arithmetic.
boundary_notes: If independently rounded or modified, stored direct and inverse matrices need not remain exact inverses.
The formulas require positive curvature for the stated positive-definiteness result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS inverse update and direct–inverse dual representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The first recursion is the extracted inverse BFGS formula. The alternative formula is retained exactly as extracted, although its use of \(\gamma_k\) in the second numerator and \(\delta_k\) in the corresponding denominator is nonstandard and may reflect a source or extraction-level notational inconsistency. The extract's finite-recovery and conjugacy claims are excluded because it supplies only convex quadraticity and omits such necessary algorithmic hypotheses as exact line searches and nondegeneracy. Positive-definiteness preservation additionally requires a positive curvature pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For update pairs satisfying the indicated nonzero-denominator conditions, the extracted inverse BFGS recursion is
\[
S_{k+1}=S_k+\left(1+\frac{\gamma_k^T S_k\gamma_k}{\gamma_k^T\delta_k}\right)\frac{\delta_k\delta_k^T}{\gamma_k^T\delta_k}-\frac{\delta_k\gamma_k^T S_k+S_k\gamma_k\delta_k^T}{\gamma_k^T\delta_k}.
\]
The extract also gives the alternative representation
\[
P_{k+1}=P_k+\frac{\gamma_k\gamma_k^T}{\gamma_k^T\delta_k}-\frac{P_k\gamma_k\gamma_k^T P_k}{\delta_k^T P_k\delta_k},
\]
and describes the direct and inverse BFGS representations as dual to the corresponding DFP representations. For the inverse update, \(S_k\succ0\) together with \(\gamma_k^T\delta_k>0\) implies \(S_{k+1}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extract presents the inverse BFGS rank-two update, an alternative direct–inverse representation, and their stated duality with DFP. Positive definiteness of the inverse approximation is preserved when the current approximation is positive definite and the curvature pairing is positive. The stronger quadratic finite-recovery and conjugacy claims require hypotheses not supplied in the extract.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct BFGS Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian-form BFGS rank-two update for one nondegenerate secant pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric direct metric \(B\) and vectors \(s,y\) satisfying \(s^{\mathsf T}Bs\neq0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y\neq0\), the direct BFGS update is \[B_+=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.\] The correction is symmetric and has rank at most two. It satisfies the direct secant equation \(B_+s=y\). When \(B\succ0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), both denominators are positive and \(B_+\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct BFGS replaces two rank-one curvature components of a symmetric Hessian approximation and exactly enforces the new secant equation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The direct Hessian-approximation form of BFGS, together with the implementation boundary for refactorizing and solving a general dense system at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let B_k\succ0,\ s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k
eq0, and y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k), with y_k^Ts_k>0. The direct BFGS update corresponding to the inverse-BFGS formula is B_{k+1}=B_k- rac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+ rac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}. A naive implementation that freshly factors and solves B_kp_k=-

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Direct BFGS Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact direct-matrix representation after a finite sequence of BFGS updates; it underlies, but is not itself restricted to, limited-memory BFGS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $k\geq1$, let $B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite, and let $(s_i,y_i)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfy $s_i^Ty_i>0$ for $i=0,\ldots,k-1$. Suppose $B_k$ is obtained by applying the corresponding $k$ direct BFGS updates to $B_0$. Define $S_k=[s_0,\ldots,s_{k-1}]$, $Y_k=[y_0,\ldots,y_{k-1}]$, $D_k=\operatorname{diag}(s_0^Ty_0,\ldots,s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})$, and $(L_k)_{ij}=s_{i-1}^Ty_{j-1}$ when $i>j$ and $0$ otherwise. Then
\[
B_k=B_0-[B_0S_k\;Y_k]\begin{bmatrix}S_k^TB_0S_k&L_k\\L_k^T&-D_k\end{bmatrix}^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}S_k^TB_0\\Y_k^T\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The curvature conditions ensure that the middle matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a symmetric positive-definite matrix and applying k direct BFGS updates with positive-curvature pairs gives the displayed compact formula for B_k. It uses the stacked correction matrices S_k and Y_k, their diagonal curvature matrix D_k, and a strict lower-triangular cross-product matrix L_k. Positive curvature ensures that the small middle matrix is nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: B_k\text{ is obtained from }B_0\text{ by the corresponding }k\text{ direct BFGS updates.}

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse BFGS Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-Hessian BFGS update in factored rank-two form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^{\mathsf T}y\neq0\). With \(\rho=(s^{\mathsf T}y)^{-1}\) and \(I\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) the identity matrix, the inverse BFGS update is \[H_+=(I-\rho sy^{\mathsf T})H(I-\rho ys^{\mathsf T})+\rho ss^{\mathsf T}.\] It is symmetric and satisfies the inverse secant equation \(H_+y=s\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), then \(H_+\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse BFGS uses a symmetric factored correction that enforces the inverse secant equation and preserves positive definiteness under positive curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse BFGS update and secant condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-two inverse-metric BFGS representation under the stated positive-curvature condition. The unsupported qualitative claim that BFGS is the most stable scheme is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let H_{k+1}=H_k+\Delta H_k. If \langle\gamma_k,\delta_k\rangle>0, define
\[
\beta_k=1+\frac{\langle H_k\gamma_k,\gamma_k\rangle}{\langle\gamma_k,\delta_k\rangle},\qquad
\Delta H_k=\beta_k\frac{\delta_k\delta_k^T}{\langle\gamma_k,\delta_k\rangle}-\frac{H_k\gamma_k\delta_k^T+\delta_k\gamma_k^T H_k}{\langle\gamma_k,\delta_k\rangle}.
\]
Then H_{k+1}\gamma_k=\delta_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the positive curvature pairing, the stated inverse BFGS rank-two update satisfies the quasi-Newton secant equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS secant-pair and inverse-update stage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the closing fragment of Algorithm 6.1. It defines the secant pair, invokes the inverse-BFGS update by its explicit source cross-reference, increments the counter, and returns to the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After x_{k+1} is computed, set s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k and y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k); compute H_{k+1} using the inverse-BFGS update referenced as (6.17); then set k\leftarrow k+1 and repeat the loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After accepting a new point, BFGS forms the displacement and gradient-change vectors, applies the referenced inverse-BFGS update, increments the iteration counter, and repeats.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse-Hessian BFGS update and weighted local norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-form BFGS representation together with the matrix norm introduced for its local analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Provided \(s_k^Ty_k\ne0\), the inverse-Hessian BFGS form is
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kg_k,
\]
\[
H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{(s_k-H_ky_k)s_k^T+s_k(s_k-H_ky_k)^T}{s_k^Ty_k}-\frac{(s_k-H_ky_k)^Ty_k}{(s_k^Ty_k)^2}s_ks_k^T.
\]
For \(A=\nabla^2f(x^*)\), the associated weighted Frobenius norm is
\[
\|E\|_{\mathrm{BFGS}}=\|A^{1/2}EA^{1/2}\|_F.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse-Hessian BFGS method steps by minus H_k times the gradient and updates H_k by the displayed rank-two formula. Its local analysis uses the Frobenius norm of A^{1/2}EA^{1/2}, with A equal to the Hessian at the solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse BFGS rank-two formula is well defined for a nonzero curvature inner product and preserves positive definiteness when the current matrix is positive definite and that inner product is positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic equivalence of direct and inverse BFGS updates under matrix inversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(H=B^{-1}\), and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\). Let \(B_+\) be the direct BFGS matrix and let \(H_+\) be the inverse BFGS matrix formed from the same pair \((s,y)\). Then both matrices are positive definite and \[H_+=B_+^{-1}.\] Consequently the direct secant equation \(B_+s=y\) and inverse secant equation \(H_+y=s\) describe the same updated metric, and either representation can be recovered uniquely from the other by inversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite starting metric and positive curvature, direct and inverse BFGS formulas produce matrices that are exact inverses.
