knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS weighted minimal-change geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(s_k^Ty_k>0\). Let \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) satisfy \(Ws_k=y_k\), and define \(\|A\|_W=\|W^{1/2}AW^{1/2}\|_F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inverse-BFGS geometry expressed as a weighted Frobenius projection onto the inverse secant affine space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The BFGS curvature-metric geometry is the weighted minimal-change problem \(H_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{H\in\mathbb S^n}\{\|H-H_k\|_W:H y_k=s_k\}\). Its unique update is \(H_{k+1}=(I-\rho_ks_ky_k^T)H_k(I-\rho_ky_ks_k^T)+\rho_ks_ks_k^T\), where \(\rho_k=(y_k^Ts_k)^{-1}\). Thus BFGS replaces the current inverse metric by the closest symmetric metric, in the specified weighted Frobenius geometry, that interpolates the measured curvature pair. Positive curvature makes the secant constraint compatible with a positive definite updated metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS curvature-metric geometry views the inverse update as a projection. Among symmetric matrices satisfying the new inverse secant equation, it selects the matrix closest to the current inverse metric in a weighted Frobenius norm whose weight maps the step to the gradient displacement. The unique minimizer is the standard inverse BFGS formula and remains positive definite under positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{H=H^T,\,Hy_k=s_k}\|H-H_k\|_W\) equals the inverse BFGS update and belongs to \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A scale-compatible choice is the average Hessian \(W=\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x_k+\tau s_k)\,d\tau\) when it is positive definite, since then \(Ws_k=y_k\).
special_cases_latex: When the secant equation already holds, \(H_ky_k=s_k\), the minimal correction is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: The defining geometry is invariant under compatible nonsingular linear changes of variables.
Only the newly observed secant direction is imposed exactly; remaining metric information is changed minimally in the selected norm.
boundary_notes: The weight matrix is part of the variational characterization and need not be computed by a practical implementation.
This definition concerns inverse BFGS, not Euclidean Frobenius projection, which yields a different symmetric update.

notation.meaning: Weighted Frobenius norm used by the BFGS projection.

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS Curvature Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact curvature boundary for positive-definite BFGS direct and inverse metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), let \(H=B^{-1}\), and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\neq0\). Positive curvature, \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), is necessary and sufficient for the standard direct and inverse BFGS formulas formed from \(B\), \(H\), and \((s,y)\) to yield a positive-definite inverse pair satisfying the exact secant equations. Specifically, under positive curvature the formulas are well defined and produce \(B_+\succ0\), \(H_+=B_+^{-1}\succ0\), \(B_+s=y\), and \(H_+y=s\). If \(s^{\mathsf T}y<0\), the formulas are defined but cannot produce a positive-definite exact-secant matrix; if \(s^{\mathsf T}y=0\), the formulas are undefined and no positive-definite matrix can satisfy \(B_+s=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive curvature is exactly the condition under which standard BFGS produces positive-definite direct and inverse exact-secant metrics from a positive-definite inverse pair; zero curvature makes the formulas undefined, and negative curvature prevents positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s^{\mathsf T}y>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{the BFGS formulas yield }B_+\succ0,\ H_+=B_+^{-1}\succ0,\ B_+s=y,\ H_+y=s.\]

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS Metric Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-form geometry of the direct BFGS Hessian update under positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and assume \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\). The direct BFGS update is
\[
B_+=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
It satisfies \(B_+s=y\). Moreover, for every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
z^{\mathsf T}B_+z=z^{\mathsf T}Bz-\frac{(z^{\mathsf T}Bs)^2}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{(z^{\mathsf T}y)^2}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
Thus the old metric is retained on directions \(B\)-orthogonal to \(s\) and Euclidean-orthogonal to \(y\), while the secant direction is adjusted to match the observed curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS changes the positive-definite metric only through two rank-one terms, enforces the secant equation, and preserves the old quadratic form on directions orthogonal to both update components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_+s=y\), and \(B_+\) has the displayed rank-two quadratic-form geometry.

notation.meaning: current direct Hessian or metric approximation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted least-change characterization of the inverse BFGS update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational characterization of the symmetric correction in the inverse BFGS formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the inverse BFGS update as \(H^{(k+1)}=H+E\), where \(H=H^{\mathrm T}\), and define \(\eta=\delta-H\gamma\). For the weighted norm \(\|\cdot\|_W\), with \(W\delta=\gamma\), the BFGS correction \(E\) solves \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\widetilde E}\ \|\widetilde E\|_W\quad\text{subject to}\quad \widetilde E^{\mathrm T}=\widetilde E,\qquad \widetilde E\gamma=\eta.\] The constraints impose symmetry and the quasi-Newton condition, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse BFGS correction minimizes the weighted matrix norm among symmetric corrections satisfying the quasi-Newton equation, when the weight maps delta to gamma.
assumptions_latex: H^{(k+1)}=H+E\text{ is the inverse BFGS update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\widetilde E}\left\{\|\widetilde E\|_W:\widetilde E^{\mathrm T}=\widetilde E,\ \widetilde E\gamma=\eta\right\}.

children.top_down_role: Boundary cases where the expected metric definiteness is not retained.

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS Definiteness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp curvature boundary for positive definiteness of the direct BFGS update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\ne0\). For \(s^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\), define
\[
B_+=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
Then \(B_+\succ0\) if and only if \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\). If \(s^{\mathsf T}y<0\), then \(s^{\mathsf T}B_+s=s^{\mathsf T}y<0\), so \(B_+\) is not positive definite. If \(s^{\mathsf T}y=0\), the displayed BFGS formula is undefined, and no symmetric positive-definite matrix satisfying \(B_+s=y\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive curvature is exactly the boundary for preserving positive definiteness. Negative curvature gives a negative quadratic form along the step, while zero curvature makes the formula undefined and an SPD secant metric impossible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_+\succ0\iff s^{\mathsf T}y>0\); nonpositive curvature prevents an SPD BFGS secant update.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-curvature boundary for positive-definite secant updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The reviewed statement isolates the positive-definiteness boundary supported by the extract; the paragraph's broader DFP and BFGS representations are not forced into this narrower node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k=\alpha_kp_k and y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k). A symmetric positive-definite matrix B satisfying Bs_k=y_k exists if and only if s_k^Ty_k>0. Consequently, s_k^Ty_k\leq0 precludes a positive-definite secant matrix. If \alpha_k>0, 
abla f(x_k)^Tp_k<0, and the Wolfe curvature condition holds with c_2<1, then y_k^Ts_k\geq(c_2-1)\alpha_k
abla f(x_k)^Tp_k>0. Strong convexity likewise gives s_k^Ty_k>0 for distinct x_k and x_{k+1}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive displacement–gradient curvature is exactly the feasibility boundary for a positive-definite secant matrix. Nonconvex objectives need not satisfy it automatically, but a Wolfe line search along a descent direction guarantees it; strong convexity guarantees it between distinct points.
assumptions_latex: f is differentiable at x_k and x_{k+1}.
For the Wolfe guarantee, \alpha_k>0,\ \nabla f(x_k)^Tp_k<0, and the Wolfe curvature condition holds with c_2<1.
For the strong-convexity guarantee, f is strongly convex and x_{k+1}\neq x_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense BFGS realization policy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \((s_k,y_k)\) be a candidate secant pair, and let \(u\) denote unit roundoff. A dense implementation may store either \(B_k\), its inverse, or a Cholesky-type factor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic dense BFGS implementation policy, including representation, admission, and initial scaling choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense BFGS realization policy is a rule selecting: (i) an unfactored update of \(B_k\), followed when needed by factorization; or a factored update maintaining \(B_k=L_kL_k^T\) or \(L_kD_kL_k^T\); (ii) admission of the curvature pair only when \(s_k^Ty_k>\sqrt{u}\,\|s_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2\), with \(B_{k+1}=B_k\) when the test fails; and (iii) a positive definite initial scale, such as \(B_0=I\), a scaled identity, or a positive definite problem-informed approximation. In the admitted case, the selected representation must realize the same BFGS secant matrix in exact arithmetic. A factored realization updates factors in \(O(n^2)\) work, while an unfactored Hessian realization may incur an additional factorization when a step requires it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense BFGS realization policy specifies whether the full Hessian matrix, its inverse, or a factorization is maintained; which curvature pairs are accepted; and how the initial positive definite scale is chosen. A numerically small or nonpositive curvature pair is skipped. Accepted factored and unfactored implementations represent the same BFGS matrix in exact arithmetic, but they differ in computational cost and suitability for downstream step computations.
assumptions_latex: The maintained initial representation corresponds to a matrix in \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
The implementation has a unit-roundoff parameter \(u>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy returns either the unchanged representation or a dense representation of the positive definite BFGS matrix satisfying \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Maintaining \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) gives an unfactored inverse realization whose search direction is \(-H_k\nabla f(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Setting the initial matrix to a scaled identity makes the first direction a correspondingly scaled steepest-descent direction.
A factor-maintaining realization is natural for line-search or dogleg steps requiring positive definite solves.
immediate_consequences_latex: A Cholesky-factor realization certifies positive definiteness through the factor representation.
Skipping a pair leaves the stored metric unchanged.
boundary_notes: The numerical threshold is an implementation safeguard, not a replacement for a globalization strategy.
Hook-step or shifted-system computations may require an explicit matrix and can alter the preferred realization.

notation.meaning: Unit roundoff or machine precision parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS Scaling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar initialization or restart scaling derived from a positive-curvature secant pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), define the inverse-metric scale
\[
\gamma_H=\frac{s^{\mathsf T}y}{y^{\mathsf T}y}
\]
and its reciprocal direct-metric scale
\[
\gamma_B=\gamma_H^{-1}=\frac{y^{\mathsf T}y}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
Initialize or restart with \(H_0=\gamma_H I\) or \(B_0=\gamma_B I\), respectively. The scalar \(\gamma_H\) minimizes \(\|\gamma y-s\|_2^2\) over \(\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\), while \(\gamma_B\) is chosen reciprocally so that \(B_0=H_0^{-1}\). If safeguarding is prescribed, replace the selected raw scale \(\gamma\) by
\[
\widehat\gamma=\min\{\gamma_{\max},\max\{\gamma_{\min},\gamma\}\},
\]
where \(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq\gamma_{\max}<\infty\), and output the corresponding scaled identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At initialization or restart, use the least-squares inverse-Hessian scale based on the secant pair or its reciprocal Hessian scale, optionally clipping the selected positive scale to a prescribed interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy outputs \(H_0=\gamma_HI\) or the reciprocal initialization \(B_0=\gamma_BI\), with a positive, optionally safeguarded scale.

notation.meaning: initial or restarted direct and inverse metrics
safeguarded version of the selected raw scale

knowledge_statements.title: Dense BFGS Matrix Realization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dense realization of one direct BFGS update using symmetric rank-one operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a stored symmetric matrix \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and vectors \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k>0\) and \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\). Compute
\[
u_k=B_ks_k,\qquad \alpha_k=(s_k^{\mathsf T}u_k)^{-1},\qquad \beta_k=(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)^{-1},
\]
then perform the symmetric rank-one updates
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\alpha_ku_ku_k^{\mathsf T}+\beta_ky_ky_k^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Store one triangle and mirror it when a full matrix is required. Output \(B_{k+1}\), which in exact arithmetic is symmetric, satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), and is positive definite when \(B_k\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the dense BFGS matrix using one matrix-vector product and two symmetric rank-one updates; the exact result is symmetric, secant-compatible, and positive definite under positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the direct BFGS matrix \(B_{k+1}\), with \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dense BFGS Numerical Monitoring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant acceptance diagnostics for a computed dense BFGS matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a computed matrix \(\widehat B_{k+1}\), define
\[
e_{\mathrm{sym}}=\frac{\|\widehat B_{k+1}-\widehat B_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}\|_F}{\max\{1,\|\widehat B_{k+1}\|_F\}},\qquad
e_{\mathrm{sec}}=\frac{\|\widehat B_{k+1}s_k-y_k\|_2}{\max\{1,\|\widehat B_{k+1}\|_2\|s_k\|_2,\|y_k\|_2\}}.
\]
Given tolerances \(\tau_{\mathrm{sym}},\tau_{\mathrm{sec}}>0\), the realization passes structural monitoring when \(e_{\mathrm{sym}}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{sym}}\), \(e_{\mathrm{sec}}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{sec}}\), \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), and a Cholesky factorization of the symmetrized matrix \((\widehat B_{k+1}+\widehat B_{k+1}^{\mathsf T})/2\) succeeds. Failure of any test triggers rejection, recomputation, damping, or restart rather than unconditional acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monitor symmetry, secant residual, positive curvature, and Cholesky success using scaled diagnostics; any failed test flags the dense update for corrective handling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed update is accepted only if all displayed structural and definiteness tests pass.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Davidon–Fletcher–Powell method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. Let \(H_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be an inverse-Hessian approximation, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(s_k,y_k\) be the usual secant pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, full-memory DFP with positive-curvature line-search pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The DFP method computes \(p_k=-H_kg_k\), selects \(\alpha_k>0\), sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), and updates \(H_{k+1}=H_k-\frac{H_ky_ky_k^TH_k}{y_k^TH_ky_k}+\frac{s_ks_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}\). The step-selection rule must ensure \(y_k^Ts_k>0\), for example through the Wolfe conditions. Starting from \(H_0\succ0\), the update is symmetric, satisfies \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\), and preserves positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The DFP method uses the current inverse-Hessian approximation to generate a descent direction, obtains a positive-curvature secant pair, and applies the DFP inverse update. The update subtracts a rank-one term in the old metric image of the gradient displacement and adds a rank-one term in the step direction. It satisfies the inverse secant equation and preserves positive definiteness under positive curvature.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The corresponding direct DFP update is \(B_{k+1}=(I-\rho_ky_ks_k^T)B_k(I-\rho_ks_ky_k^T)+\rho_ky_ky_k^T\), where \(B_k=H_k^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H_ky_k=s_k\), the DFP correction is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: The matrix change has rank at most two.
The method requires only first derivatives of \(f\), together with dense matrix-vector operations.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness is not guaranteed by the undamped formula when \(y_k^Ts_k\leq0\).
DFP and BFGS are different updates despite their direct-inverse duality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral action and no-deterioration boundary of the DFP update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the transformed DFP spectral property and its conditional no-deterioration guarantee. It does not promote the extract's informal discussion outside the interval condition to an unconditional theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G\succ0, H_k\succ0, R_k=G^{1/2}H_kG^{1/2}, and 0\neq r_k=G^{1/2}s_k. For the transformed DFP update, define P=R_k-\frac{R_kr_kr_k^TR_k}{r_k^TR_kr_k},\qquad R_{k+1}=P+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{r_k^Tr_k}. Then Pr_k=0 and R_{k+1}r_k=r_k. If \lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n>0 are the eigenvalues of R_k and \mu_1\ge\cdots\ge\mu_n are those of P, then \lambda_1\ge\mu_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\mu_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge\mu_n=0 and \operatorname{spec}(R_{k+1})=\{\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{n-1},1\}. Hence, if 1\in[\lambda_n,\lambda_1], then \operatorname{spec}(R_{k+1})\subseteq[\lambda_n,\lambda_1], so the extremal-eigenvalue ratio cannot increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In similarity-scaled coordinates, DFP replaces the zero eigenvalue of its rank-one downdate in the update direction by 1, while the other downdated eigenvalues interlace the old spectrum. If 1 already lies in the old spectral interval, the updated spectrum remains in that interval and its eigenvalue ratio cannot worsen. No such guarantee is asserted when 1 lies outside the interval.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DFP algorithm with exact line search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-metric DFP iteration for unconstrained differentiable optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(k=0\), \(x^{(0)}\), and a real symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H_0\). At iteration \(k\), stop if \(g^{(k)}=0\). Otherwise set \(d^{(k)}=-H_kg^{(k)}\), choose \(\alpha_k\in\arg\min_{\alpha\geq0}f(x^{(k)}+\alpha d^{(k)})\), and set \(x^{(k+1)}=x^{(k)}+\alpha_kd^{(k)}\). With \(s_k=\alpha_kd^{(k)}\) and \(y_k=g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)}\), update
\[
H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{s_ks_k^{\top}}{s_k^{\top}y_k}-\frac{(H_ky_k)(H_ky_k)^{\top}}{y_k^{\top}H_ky_k},
\]
provided the line-search minimizer exists and the displayed denominators are nonzero; then increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a positive-definite inverse-metric approximation, DFP uses minus that matrix times the gradient as its direction, performs an exact line search over nonnegative step lengths, and applies the inverse DFP rank-two update. The iteration requires an attained line-search minimum and nonzero update denominators.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-line-search quadratic properties of DFP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional properties of a well-defined DFP run on a quadratic objective under exact line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f be quadratic with Hessian G, where G^{-1} exists, and suppose the DFP updates and exact line searches are well-defined through n iterations. knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract independently supports the stated multiplication count and the model and descent consequences of positive-definite approximations. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A DFP iteration requires 3n^2+O(n) multiplications as counted in the extract. If H_k\succ0 and g_k\ne0, then d_k=-H_kg_k is a descent direction because g_k^Td_k=-g_k^TH_kg_k<0. A positive-definite inverse metric produces a descent direction for a nonzero gradient, and the corresponding positive-definite quadratic model has a unique minimizer. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct and inverse DFP representation pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(H=B^{-1}\), \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\), \(s^Ty>0\), and \(\rho=(s^Ty)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic direct and inverse representations of one dense DFP update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direct-inverse DFP representation pair is \(B^+=(I-\rho ys^T)B(I-\rho sy^T)+\rho yy^T\) and \(H^+=H-\frac{Hyy^TH}{y^THy}+\frac{ss^T}{y^Ts}\). It is characterized by \(H^+=(B^+)^{-1}\), \(B^+s=y\), and \(H^+y=s\). Both updates are symmetric rank-two modifications, and positive curvature together with \(B\succ0\) implies \(B^+,H^+\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct DFP formula updates a Hessian approximation in product form, while the inverse DFP formula updates its inverse by two rank-one corrections. If the starting matrices are mutual inverses and the secant pair has positive curvature, the updated matrices are mutual inverses, satisfy their corresponding secant equations, and remain positive definite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Expanding the direct product form gives \(B^+=B-\rho(ys^TB+Bsy^T)+\rho^2(s^TBs)yy^T+\rho yy^T\).
special_cases_latex: When \(y=Bs\), both direct and inverse corrections vanish.
immediate_consequences_latex: Either representation determines the other through matrix inversion in exact arithmetic.
The direct and inverse secant equations encode the same interpolation condition when the matrices are nonsingular inverses.
boundary_notes: The product form should not be confused with inverse BFGS, although the two formulas are related by representation duality.
Finite-precision independently maintained matrices can lose the inverse relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct DFP Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-form representation of the DFP update for a direct Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\) and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\). The direct DFP update is represented by
\[
B_+=\left(I-\frac{ys^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}\right)B\left(I-\frac{sy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}\right)+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
B_+=B-\frac{ys^{\mathsf T}B+Bsy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}+\left(\frac{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}{(s^{\mathsf T}y)^2}+\frac{1}{s^{\mathsf T}y}\right)yy^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Both forms are symmetric and satisfy the direct secant equation \(B_+s=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct DFP Hessian update has equivalent product and expanded rank-two forms, both symmetric and satisfying the secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two displayed formulas coincide and satisfy \(B_+s=y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted least-change characterization of the direct DFP update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational characterization of the symmetric correction in the direct DFP formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the direct DFP update as \(B^{(k+1)}=B+E\), where \(B=B^{\mathrm T}\), and define \(\xi=\gamma-B\delta\). For the weighted norm \(\|\cdot\|_W\), with \(W\gamma=\delta\), the DFP correction \(E\) solves \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\widetilde E}\ \|\widetilde E\|_W\quad\text{subject to}\quad \widetilde E^{\mathrm T}=\widetilde E,\qquad \widetilde E\delta=\xi.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct DFP correction minimizes the weighted matrix norm among symmetric corrections satisfying its secant equation, when the weight maps gamma to delta.
assumptions_latex: B^{(k+1)}=B+E\text{ is the direct DFP update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\widetilde E}\left\{\|\widetilde E\|_W:\widetilde E^{\mathrm T}=\widetilde E,\ \widetilde E\delta=\xi\right\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse DFP Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-two DFP representation for an inverse Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\) and \(y^{\mathsf T}Hy\ne0\). The inverse DFP update is
\[
H_+=H-\frac{Hyy^{\mathsf T}H}{y^{\mathsf T}Hy}+\frac{ss^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
The matrix \(H_+\) is symmetric and satisfies the inverse secant equation \(H_+y=s\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), then both denominators are positive and \(H_+\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse DFP subtracts the old metric component along the gradient difference and adds the observed secant component, preserving symmetry and positive definiteness under positive curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse DFP Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition of the DFP rank-two update for an inverse-Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Provided the displayed denominators are nonzero, the inverse DFP update is \[H_{k+1}=H_k-\frac{H_k\gamma_k\gamma_k^T H_k}{\gamma_k^T H_k\gamma_k}+\frac{\delta_k\delta_k^T}{\delta_k^T\gamma_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse DFP update subtracts a rank-one correction formed from H_k gamma_k and adds a rank-one correction formed from delta_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse DFP rank-two update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-curvature DFP representation obtained by imposing the secant equation on a symmetric rank-two correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H_k=H_k^T and let s_k,y_k\in\mathbb{R}^n satisfy s_k^Ty_k\ne0 and y_k^TH_ky_k\ne0. Setting u=s_k and v=H_ky_k in H_{k+1}=H_k+auu^T+bvv^T and imposing H_{k+1}y_k=s_k gives a=(s_k^Ty_k)^{-1}, b=-(y_k^TH_ky_k)^{-1}, and H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{s_ks_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k}-\frac{H_ky_ky_k^TH_k}{y_k^TH_ky_k}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing the two rank-one correction vectors as s_k and H_k y_k and enforcing the secant equation yields the inverse DFP update, provided both denominators are nonzero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse DFP rank-two update and secant equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-metric DFP representation. Positive-definiteness preservation and descent are excluded because they require the additional positive-curvature hypothesis treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_k=S_k^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(\delta_k,\gamma_k\in\mathbb R^n\), with \(\delta_k^T\gamma_k\ne0\) and \(\gamma_k^TS_k\gamma_k\ne0\). The inverse DFP update is
\[
S_{k+1}=S_k+\frac{\delta_k\delta_k^T}{\delta_k^T\gamma_k}-\frac{S_k\gamma_k\gamma_k^TS_k}{\gamma_k^TS_k\gamma_k}.
\]
The correction \(S_{k+1}-S_k\) is symmetric and has rank at most two, and the update satisfies \(S_{k+1}\gamma_k=\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse DFP formula applies a symmetric correction of rank at most two and satisfies the secant equation, provided both displayed denominators are nonzero.

knowledge_statements.title: DFP Representation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse relationship between the direct and inverse DFP formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, set \(H=B^{-1}\), and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Assume \(s^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\) and \(y^{\mathsf T}Hy\ne0\). Define \(B_+\) by the direct DFP product formula and define
\[
H_+=H-\frac{Hyy^{\mathsf T}H}{y^{\mathsf T}Hy}+\frac{ss^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
If the updated matrices are nonsingular, then the direct and inverse representations correspond exactly:
\[
H_+=B_+^{-1}.
\]
Consequently, \(B_+s=y\) and \(H_+y=s\) describe the same secant transformation in reciprocal coordinates. In particular, if \(B\succ0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), then both updates are positive definite and mutually inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from symmetric reciprocal metrics, the direct and inverse DFP formulas produce reciprocal updated metrics and encode the same secant equation.

notation.meaning: reciprocal symmetric direct and inverse approximations
corresponding direct and inverse DFP updates

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS-DFP Representation Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange duality between BFGS and DFP under matrix inversion and secant-vector interchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonsingular symmetric matrix \(M\), define
\[
\mathcal{B}(M;u,v)=M-\frac{Muu^{\mathsf T}M}{u^{\mathsf T}Mu}+\frac{vv^{\mathsf T}}{v^{\mathsf T}u}
\]
and
\[
\mathcal{D}(M;u,v)=\left(I-\frac{vu^{\mathsf T}}{u^{\mathsf T}v}\right)M\left(I-\frac{uv^{\mathsf T}}{u^{\mathsf T}v}\right)+\frac{vv^{\mathsf T}}{u^{\mathsf T}v}.
\]
Whenever all denominators and inverses exist,
\[
\mathcal{D}(M;u,v)^{-1}=\mathcal{B}(M^{-1};v,u),\qquad
\mathcal{B}(M;u,v)^{-1}=\mathcal{D}(M^{-1};v,u).
\]
Thus direct DFP is inverse-form BFGS after exchanging the secant vectors, and direct BFGS is inverse-form DFP under the same exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix inversion together with exchanging step and gradient-difference vectors converts DFP into BFGS and BFGS into DFP.
assumptions_latex: All displayed scalar denominators are nonzero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS–DFP algebraic duality
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(s^Ty\neq0\), and let \(B,H\in\mathbb S^n\) denote direct and inverse metric variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation duality between the BFGS and DFP update formulas; this is not an assertion that their optimization iterates coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: BFGS–DFP representation duality is the involutive substitution \(\mathcal D:(B,H,s,y)\mapsto(H,B,y,s)\). Applying \(\mathcal D\) to the direct BFGS formula produces the inverse DFP formula, while applying it to the inverse BFGS formula produces the direct DFP formula. Equivalently, the BFGS update in one metric representation has the DFP algebraic form in the dual representation after interchanging the step and gradient-displacement roles. Under \(H=B^{-1}\), each named update also has its own direct-inverse representation pair, but inversion does not change a BFGS update into a DFP update; the BFGS-versus-DFP exchange additionally requires \(s\leftrightarrow y\) and \(B\leftrightarrow H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS–DFP duality is the algebraic operation that swaps the direct and inverse metric variables and simultaneously swaps the step and gradient-displacement vectors. Under this operation, direct BFGS becomes inverse DFP, and inverse BFGS becomes direct DFP. Merely inverting a BFGS matrix gives the other BFGS representation, not DFP; both swaps are essential.
assumptions_latex: All denominators in the transformed formulas are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal D(U_{\mathrm{BFGS}}^{B})=U_{\mathrm{DFP}}^{H}\) and \(\mathcal D(U_{\mathrm{BFGS}}^{H})=U_{\mathrm{DFP}}^{B}\), with \(\mathcal D^2\) equal to the identity.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The formulas are dual under \(s\leftrightarrow y\) and \(B\leftrightarrow H\).
special_cases_latex: At a perfect secant fit, \(y=Bs\) and \(s=Hy\), every member of both paired representations leaves the metric unchanged.
immediate_consequences_latex: Properties stated purely through symmetry and positive curvature transfer between the paired algebraic forms.
The duality explains the parallel direct and inverse variational constructions of DFP and BFGS.
boundary_notes: Duality is an identity between update formulas, not equality of BFGS and DFP matrices generated from identical initialization.
The data-dependent iterates of the two methods can differ when ordinary inexact line searches are used.

notation.meaning: The direct-inverse and secant-vector interchange defining the duality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS–DFP Direct–Inverse Update Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange and inversion correspondence among the direct and inverse BFGS and DFP representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the displayed denominators are nonzero and all required inverses exist, with $H_k=B_k^{-1}$. The BFGS direct update is $B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}$, and an equivalent inverse form is $H_{k+1}=\left(I-\frac{s_ky_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k}\right)H_k\left(I-\frac{y_ks_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k}\right)+\frac{s_ks_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k}$. Exchanging $H_k\leftrightarrow B_k$ and $s_k\leftrightarrow y_k$ yields the corresponding DFP representations. More generally, exchange followed by inversion defines a dual-update operation that preserves the appropriate quasi-Newton equation, and applying the operation twice restores the original update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS and DFP direct and inverse formulas correspond by exchanging the direct and inverse metrics together with the step and gradient-difference vectors, followed when needed by inversion. This dual operation preserves the secant equation and is involutive.
assumptions_latex: \text{All inverses required by the dual construction exist}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal D(\mathcal D(U))=U,\qquad \mathcal D\text{ maps the BFGS and DFP direct/inverse representations into one another and preserves }H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\text{ or }B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric rank-one quasi-Newton method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), \(s_k
eq0\), and \(y_k=
abla f(x_k+s_k)-
abla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic SR1, normally embedded in a trust-region method because the model matrix may be indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SR1 method forms the residual \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\) and, when \(r_k^Ts_k\neq0\) and the update is admitted, sets \(B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{r_k^Ts_k}\). In a trust-region realization, \(s_k\) is computed from \(\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}\nabla f(x_k)^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks\); the trial point may be accepted or rejected by an actual-to-predicted reduction test, while the curvature pair can still be used to update the model. If the SR1 denominator is numerically too small, the update is skipped and \(B_{k+1}=B_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SR1 method updates a symmetric Hessian approximation by the outer product of the secant residual divided by its inner product with the step. The correction has rank one and satisfies the secant equation whenever its denominator is nonzero. Since SR1 need not preserve positive definiteness, it is commonly used with a trust-region subproblem. A near-zero denominator triggers a skipped update.
assumptions_latex: A numerical implementation supplies an admission test for a sufficiently large denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admitted update satisfies \(B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{(y_k-B_ks_k)(y_k-B_ks_k)^T}{(y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k}\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonsingular mutually inverse matrices, the inverse form is \(H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{(s_k-H_ky_k)(s_k-H_ky_k)^T}{(s_k-H_ky_k)^Ty_k}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(y_k=B_ks_k\), the current matrix already satisfies the secant equation and the zero correction is used.
The correction can introduce negative curvature even when \(B_k\succ0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The matrix change has rank at most one.
The updated matrix is symmetric but is not constrained to be positive definite.
boundary_notes: A line-search method requiring positive definite model matrices cannot use unrestricted SR1 without additional modification.
If the residual is nonzero but orthogonal to the step, no symmetric rank-one correction satisfies the secant equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SR1 Representations, Definiteness Boundary, and Skipping Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct and inverse symmetric rank-one secant updates, their denominator and definiteness limitations, and the standard safeguard for the direct update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B_k=B_k^T, q_k:=y_k-B_ks_k, and q_k^Ts_k\neq0. The unique symmetric rank-one correction satisfying B_{k+1}s_k=y_k is B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{q_kq_k^T}{q_k^Ts_k}. Likewise, if H_k=H_k^T, w_k:=s_k-H_ky_k, and w_k^Ty_k\neq0, the inverse-form SR1 update satisfying H_{k+1}y_k=s_k is H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{w_kw_k^T}{w_k^Ty_k}. Neither update necessarily preserves positive definiteness. For r\in(0,1), the direct correction is admitted only when |s_k^Tq_k|\ge r\|s_k\|\|q_k\|; otherwise B_{k+1}=B_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero SR1 denominator determines the unique symmetric rank-one correction satisfying the appropriate secant equation, in either direct or inverse form. The correction can destroy positive definiteness, and a zero denominator can prevent an SR1 correction from existing. Implementations therefore skip the direct update when its denominator is too small relative to the step and secant-residual norms.
assumptions_latex: q_k^Ts_k\neq0\text{ when the direct correction is formed}
w_k^Ty_k\neq0\text{ when the inverse correction is formed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{q_kq_k^T}{q_k^Ts_k},\qquad H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{w_kw_k^T}{w_k^Ty_k},\qquad B_{k+1}=B_k\text{ when the direct safeguard is not met}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct and inverse SR1 representation pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B,H\in\mathbb S^n\) be nonsingular with \(H=B^{-1}\), and let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(r=y-Bs\) and \(q=s-Hy\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic direct and inverse forms of a single admissible SR1 update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direct-inverse SR1 representation pair is \(B^+=B+\frac{rr^T}{r^Ts}\) and \(H^+=H+\frac{qq^T}{q^Ty}\), provided the displayed denominators are nonzero. When \(H=B^{-1}\), application of the Sherman–Morrison identity gives \(H^+=(B^+)^{-1}\). The direct form satisfies \(B^+s=y\), the inverse form satisfies \(H^+y=s\), and both corrections are symmetric with rank at most one. Neither representation generally preserves positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct SR1 adds an outer product of the direct secant residual, while inverse SR1 adds an outer product of the inverse secant residual. Starting from nonsingular mutually inverse matrices and an admissible pair, the updated matrices remain mutual inverses in exact arithmetic and satisfy the direct and inverse secant equations. Both changes have rank at most one, but either matrix may become indefinite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inverse formula is the Sherman–Morrison inverse of the direct formula whenever both updates are defined and nonsingular.
special_cases_latex: If \(y=Bs\), then also \(s=Hy\), and the existing pair already satisfies both secant equations without an update.
immediate_consequences_latex: An implementation may maintain either direct or inverse SR1 according to the linear algebra required by its step computation.
The representation pair does not supply a Cholesky certificate because definiteness is not preserved.
boundary_notes: A zero direct or inverse denominator requires a skip or a higher-rank alternative.
In finite precision, separate direct and inverse updates need not remain exact inverses.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct SR1 Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one SR1 formula for a direct Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define the secant residual \(r=y-Bs\). If \(r^{\mathsf T}s\ne0\), the direct symmetric-rank-one update is
\[
B_+=B+\frac{rr^{\mathsf T}}{r^{\mathsf T}s}
=B+\frac{(y-Bs)(y-Bs)^{\mathsf T}}{(y-Bs)^{\mathsf T}s}.
\]
The correction has rank at most one, preserves symmetry, and satisfies \(B_+s=y\). Unlike BFGS or DFP under positive curvature, this representation does not generally preserve positive definiteness because the denominator \(r^{\mathsf T}s\) may have either sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct SR1 adds one symmetric outer product of the secant residual, exactly enforces the secant equation, and need not preserve positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_+=B+rr^{\mathsf T}/(r^{\mathsf T}s)\) is symmetric and satisfies \(B_+s=y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse SR1 Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one SR1 formula for an inverse Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define the inverse secant residual \(q=s-Hy\). If \(q^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\), the inverse symmetric-rank-one update is
\[
H_+=H+\frac{qq^{\mathsf T}}{q^{\mathsf T}y}
=H+\frac{(s-Hy)(s-Hy)^{\mathsf T}}{(s-Hy)^{\mathsf T}y}.
\]
The correction has rank at most one, preserves symmetry, and satisfies \(H_+y=s\). Its denominator can have either sign, so positive definiteness is not guaranteed even when \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse SR1 adds one symmetric outer product of the inverse secant residual, enforces the inverse secant equation, and may lose positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_+=H+qq^{\mathsf T}/(q^{\mathsf T}y)\) is symmetric and satisfies \(H_+y=s\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Symmetric Rank-One Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-metric SR1 formula, its secant property, and its zero-residual and zero-denominator boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} be symmetric and define q_k=s_k-H_ky_k. When q_k^Ty_k\neq0, the inverse SR1 update is
\[
H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{q_kq_k^T}{q_k^Ty_k}.
\]
It is symmetric and satisfies H_{k+1}y_k=s_k. If q_k=0, H_k already satisfies H_ky_k=s_k. If q_k\neq0 but q_k^Ty_k=0, the SR1 formula is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse SR1 adds the outer product of the secant residual divided by its inner product with the gradient difference. The result remains symmetric and satisfies the secant equation. A zero residual needs no correction, while a zero denominator with nonzero residual makes the update undefined.
assumptions_latex: q_k^Ty_k\neq0\text{ when the correction is applied}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-inverse correspondence between direct and inverse SR1 updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, set \(H=B^{-1}\), and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Define
\[
r=y-Bs,\qquad q=s-Hy=-Hr.
\]
Assume \(r^{\mathsf T}s\ne0\), and form the direct SR1 update
\[
B_+=B+\frac{rr^{\mathsf T}}{r^{\mathsf T}s}.
\]
Then \(B_+\) is nonsingular if and only if \(q^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\). Under these conditions,
\[
B_+^{-1}=H+\frac{qq^{\mathsf T}}{q^{\mathsf T}y}=H_+.
\]
Hence the direct and inverse SR1 formulas are reciprocal representations of the same rank-one secant correction, with \(B_+s=y\) equivalent to \(H_+y=s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For symmetric reciprocal starting matrices, direct and inverse SR1 updates remain reciprocal exactly when the relevant update denominators are nonzero, and they encode the same rank-one secant correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_+=B_+^{-1}\), where \(B_+\) and \(H_+\) are the direct and inverse SR1 updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite SR1 Model Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inertia characterization for the direct SR1 Hessian update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r=y-Bs\), and \(d=r^Ts\ne0\). The SR1 update is \(B_+=B+rr^T/d\). Define \(\gamma=1+r^TB^{-1}r/d\). Then \(B_+\) is positive definite when \(\gamma>0\), singular when \(\gamma=0\), and has exactly one negative eigenvalue when \(\gamma<0\). Thus SR1 does not generally preserve positive definiteness; a negative denominator can introduce negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SR1 rank-one correction can turn a positive-definite model indefinite; a scalar inertia test determines whether the result is positive definite, singular, or has one negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}(B_+)\) is determined by the sign of \(1+r^TB^{-1}r/(r^Ts)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indefinite quadratic geometry generated by SR1
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k=B_k^T\) be an SR1 Hessian approximation, and define \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic-model geometry for trust-region SR1; no convexity of the model is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An indefinite SR1 model geometry is the pair \((m_k,\Delta_k)\) with feasible set \(\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\}\), where \(B_k\) is generated by admitted SR1 updates and may have eigenvalues of either sign. A vector \(d\neq0\) with \(d^TB_kd<0\) is a negative-curvature direction of the model. The trust-region step is any prescribed approximate or exact solution of \(\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}g_k^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks\). The radius constraint makes this subproblem bounded even when the unrestricted quadratic is unbounded below. Unlike positive-definite BFGS geometry, SR1 permits the model to encode observed negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indefinite SR1 model geometry consists of a symmetric SR1 quadratic model restricted to a trust region. The SR1 matrix may have positive and negative eigenvalues; a direction with negative quadratic curvature records nonconvex local behavior. The trust-region bound keeps the step problem bounded even though the unrestricted quadratic model could be unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^T\) is produced by the SR1 update or retained after a skipped update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model subproblem \(\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}g_k^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks\) remains well posed on its compact feasible set while allowing \(d^TB_kd<0\) for some \(d\neq0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(B_k\) is indefinite exactly when it has at least one positive and at least one negative eigenvalue; negative semidefinite or singular cases are distinct boundary geometries.
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\), the model is strictly convex and the indefinite feature is absent.
If \(g_k=0\) and \(B_k\) has a negative eigenvalue, a boundary step along a negative-curvature eigendirection decreases the model.
immediate_consequences_latex: A Cholesky-only step computation is not generally applicable.
Trust-region methods can use SR1 without forcing the Hessian approximation to be positive definite.
boundary_notes: Indefiniteness of \(B_k\) is permitted, not guaranteed, by SR1.
The model matrix is an approximation and its inertia need not equal the exact Hessian inertia.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded SR1 admission and skipping rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k=B_k^T\), \(s_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). Fix a relative threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic direct-SR1 safeguard based on the angle and magnitude of the secant residual; the inverse rule is analogous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SR1 update admission policy accepts the pair \((s_k,y_k)\) precisely when \(|s_k^Tr_k|\geq\eta\|s_k\|\|r_k\|\). If accepted and \(r_k\neq0\), it sets \(B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{s_k^Tr_k}\). If the inequality fails, or if \(r_k=0\), it sets \(B_{k+1}=B_k\). The test is scale invariant in \(s_k\) and \(r_k\) and prevents division by a denominator that is small relative to the two vector norms. A customary threshold is small, for example \(\eta=10^{-8}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SR1 admission policy compares the absolute update denominator with the product of the step norm and secant-residual norm. The update is applied only when this relative denominator is sufficiently large. Otherwise the matrix is left unchanged. This scale-invariant rule avoids unstable amplification caused by a nearly orthogonal step and residual.
assumptions_latex: The same vector norm is used on both factors in the admission test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonzero \(s_k,r_k\), admission is equivalent to \(|\cos\angle(s_k,r_k)|\geq\eta\).
The inverse admission rule replaces \((B_k,s_k,y_k,r_k)\) by \((H_k,y_k,s_k,s_k-H_ky_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r_k=0\), the secant equation already holds and no update is needed.
If \(s_k^Tr_k=0\neq r_k\), the update is necessarily rejected.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every applied correction has a denominator bounded away from zero relative to its vector scales.
A skipped update preserves symmetry and the current inertia.
boundary_notes: The safeguard controls numerical division but does not guarantee positive definiteness.
The parameter value is implementation dependent; \(10^{-8}\) is representative rather than universal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded SR1 Skipping Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-scaled admission and skipping rule for avoiding small SR1 denominators, including the unresolved degenerate-vector boundary in the extracted non-strict test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix r\in(0,1) and define q_i=s_i-H_iy_i. A small or zero denominator q_i^Ty_i can cause numerical difficulty or breakdown. The extracted rule applies the SR1 correction when
\[
|q_i^Ty_i|\ge r\lVert q_i\rVert\lVert y_i\rVert
\]
and otherwise sets H_{i+1}=H_i. Thus, whenever the admitted correction is defined,
\[
H_{i+1}=H_i+\frac{q_iq_i^T}{q_i^Ty_i};
\]
if the test fails, H_{i+1}=H_i. If q_i=0 or y_i=0, the non-strict test can hold while q_i^Ty_i=0, so the extract does not specify a well-defined correction in those degenerate cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a threshold between zero and one, SR1 admits a correction only when the absolute denominator is sufficiently large relative to the residual and gradient-difference norms; otherwise it leaves the approximation unchanged. The stated non-strict test does not by itself handle a zero residual or zero gradient-difference vector, where it can admit an undefined zero-denominator formula.

knowledge_statements.title: SR1 Acceptance Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard scale-invariant safeguard for admitting a direct SR1 correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), a nonzero step \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a gradient displacement \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set \(r=y-Bs\). Admit the direct SR1 update \(B_+=B+rr^T/(r^Ts)\) only if \(r\ne0\) and \[|r^Ts|\ge \eta\,\|r\|_2\,\|s\|_2.\] These conditions imply \(r^Ts\ne0\). The relative test excludes denominators small compared with the Cauchy–Schwarz scale and is invariant under nonzero scalar rescaling of either \(r\) or \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept the SR1 correction only when the residual is nonzero and the denominator magnitude is at least a fixed fraction of the product of the residual and step norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\ne0\) and \(|r^Ts|\ge\eta\|r\|_2\|s\|_2\) form the update-admission predicate, where \(r=y-Bs\).

knowledge_statements.title: SR1 Skipped-Update Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Skip policy complementary to the relative SR1 acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), compute \(r=y-Bs\). If \(s=0\), \(r=0\), or \(|r^Ts|<\eta\|r\|_2\|s\|_2\), skip the correction and output \(B_+=B\). Otherwise output \(B_+=B+rr^T/(r^Ts)\). The skip rule includes exact secant satisfaction and denominators that are zero or insufficiently separated from zero relative to the data scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Leave the matrix unchanged for a zero step, an already satisfied secant equation, or a denominator failing the relative safeguard; otherwise apply SR1.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singular SR1 Denominators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability mechanism when the SR1 denominator approaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r=y-Bs\ne0\), \(d=r^Ts\ne0\), and \(\Delta B=rr^T/d\). In the spectral norm, \[\|\Delta B\|_2=\frac{\|r\|_2^2}{|d|}.\] Consequently, for fixed nonzero \(r\), the correction norm is unbounded as \(d\to0\). At \(d=0\), the displayed SR1 formula is undefined for every \(r\). If additionally \(r=0\), the secant equation already holds and the appropriate action is to omit the correction rather than evaluate the quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero residual, the SR1 correction norm equals the squared residual norm divided by the denominator magnitude and becomes unbounded as the denominator approaches zero. At a zero denominator the quotient is undefined, including the zero-residual case.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-parameter symmetric Broyden class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and assume \(s_k^TB_ks_k\neq0\) and \(y_k^Ts_k\neq0\). Define \(v_k=\frac{y_k}{y_k^Ts_k}-\frac{B_ks_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The full real one-parameter direct Hessian Broyden class for symmetric quasi-Newton updating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Broyden update class is the family indexed by \(\phi_k\in\mathbb R\), \(B_{k+1}(\phi_k)=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}+\phi_k(s_k^TB_ks_k)v_kv_k^T\). Equivalently, \(B_{k+1}(\phi_k)=(1-\phi_k)B_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi_kB_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}\). Every defined member is symmetric and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). The choices \(\phi_k=0\) and \(\phi_k=1\) give direct BFGS and direct DFP, respectively; a data-dependent parameter gives SR1 when its denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric Broyden class is a real one-parameter family obtained by adding a rank-one parameter term to direct BFGS. It can also be written as an affine combination of the direct BFGS and DFP matrices. Every defined member is symmetric and satisfies the secant equation. Parameter zero gives BFGS, parameter one gives DFP, and a particular data-dependent parameter gives SR1.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(B_{k+1}(\phi_k)=(1-\phi_k)B_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi_kB_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}\).
special_cases_latex: \(\phi_k=0\) gives BFGS and \(\phi_k=1\) gives DFP.
When defined, \(\phi_k=\frac{s_k^Ty_k}{s_k^Ty_k-s_k^TB_ks_k}\) gives SR1.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(0\leq\phi_k\leq1\), positive curvature and \(B_k\succ0\) imply \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).
The family parameter changes the metric away from the imposed secant direction because \(v_k^Ts_k=0\).
boundary_notes: The full class allows parameters outside \([0,1]\), for which positive definiteness requires a sharper constraint.
The denominators exclude degenerate secant pairs.

notation.meaning: Vector defining the parameter-dependent rank-one term.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Broyden Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-Hessian Broyden class between the BFGS and DFP endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^Ty>0\). Define \(B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=B-Bss^TB/(s^TBs)+yy^T/(s^Ty)\) and \(v=y/(s^Ty)-Bs/(s^TBs)\). The convex Broyden class is \[B_+(\phi)=B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi(s^TBs)vv^T,\qquad 0\le\phi\le1.\] Every member is symmetric, positive definite, and satisfies \(B_+(\phi)s=y\); \(\phi=0\) is BFGS and \(\phi=1\) is the direct DFP endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex Broyden class interpolates between direct BFGS and direct DFP with a parameter from zero to one while preserving symmetry, secancy, and positive definiteness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional spectral-enclosure theorem for the convex Broyden parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n>0 be the eigenvalues of H_kG and suppose that 1\in[\lambda_n,\lambda_1]. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral enclosure for restricted Broyden updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-eigenvalue enclosure for restricted Broyden updates on strongly convex quadratics; exact line searches are not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
f(x)=b^Tx+\tfrac12x^TAx,\qquad A=A^T\succ0,
\]
with \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(B_0=B_0^T\succ0\). Generate
\[
p_k=-B_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,
\]
and update \(B_k\) by the Broyden formula with \(\phi_k\in[0,1]\). If
\[
\lambda_1^k\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n^k
\]
are the ordered eigenvalues of \(A^{1/2}B_k^{-1}A^{1/2}\), then
\[
\min\{\lambda_i^k,1\}\leq\lambda_i^{k+1}\leq\max\{\lambda_i^k,1\},
\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
for every \(k\). If the Broyden parameter is allowed outside \([0,1]\), this enclosure can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a strongly convex quadratic, each ordered eigenvalue of the scaled inverse approximation produced by a restricted Broyden update remains between its preceding value and one. The conclusion does not depend on exact line searches. Parameters outside the restricted interval can violate the enclosure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\quad \min\{\lambda_i^k,1\}\leq\lambda_i^{k+1}\leq\max\{\lambda_i^k,1\},\quad\text{whereas this enclosure may fail for }\phi_k\notin[0,1].

knowledge_statements.title: Full Broyden Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestricted real-parameter direct-Hessian Broyden family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\) and \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^TBs\ne0\) and \(s^Ty\ne0\). Define \(B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=B-Bss^TB/(s^TBs)+yy^T/(s^Ty)\) and \(v=y/(s^Ty)-Bs/(s^TBs)\). The full direct-Hessian Broyden class is \[B_+(\phi)=B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi(s^TBs)vv^T,\qquad \phi\in\mathbb{R}.\] Each member is symmetric and satisfies \(B_+(\phi)s=y\). Without additional curvature and parameter restrictions, a member need not be positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full direct-Hessian Broyden class allows any real parameter in a rank-one modification of BFGS. Every member is symmetric and satisfies the secant equation, but positive definiteness is not guaranteed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Broyden inverse-update family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the unrestricted real-parameter Broyden family of inverse-Hessian updates and the corresponding variable-parameter and pure methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi\in\mathbb R\), define \(H^{\phi}=(1-\phi)H^{\mathrm{DFP}}+\phi H^{\mathrm{BFGS}}\). Thus \(\phi=0\) gives DFP and \(\phi=1\) gives BFGS. When the displayed expressions are defined, \[H_{k+1}^{\phi}=H_k+\frac{p_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}-\frac{H_kq_kq_k^TH_k}{q_k^TH_kq_k}+\phi v_kv_k^T=H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}+\phi v_kv_k^T,\] where \[v_k=(q_k^TH_kq_k)^{1/2}\left(\frac{p_k}{p_k^Tq_k}-\frac{H_kq_k}{q_k^TH_kq_k}\right).\] A Broyden method selects a possibly varying sequence \((\phi_k)\); it is pure when this sequence is constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Broyden family contains every real affine combination of the DFP and BFGS inverse updates. Its symmetric correction has rank at most two and includes a rank-one special case. A Broyden method may vary the parameter between iterations; a pure Broyden method keeps it constant.
assumptions_latex: q_k^TH_kq_k>0\text{ for the displayed real-valued representation}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-line-search invariance across admissible Broyden updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterate equivalence of well-defined Broyden-class methods on general differentiable nonlinear objectives under exact directional minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider Broyden-class methods applied to the same differentiable nonlinear objective from the same initial point and initial approximation. Assume that every required update and search direction is well defined, \(\phi_k\geq\phi_k^c\), and every line search is exact. The directions produced by different admissible members are collinear and may differ only in length. Exact minimization along the corresponding line therefore produces the same next point. Hence the methods generate the same sequence of iterates, although the direction scalings and step-length values may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Well-defined admissible Broyden methods starting from the same data generate collinear search directions on a general differentiable nonlinear objective. With exact line searches, direction scaling does not change the selected point, so all such methods produce the same iterates even though their numerical step lengths can differ.
assumptions_latex: \text{the compared methods use the same }x_0\text{ and initial approximation}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full and Convex Broyden Update Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse and direct representations of the Broyden class and its named parameter choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(H_k=H_k^T\succ0\), \(B_k=H_k^{-1}\), and \(s_k^Ty_k\ne0\). The inverse Broyden class is
\[
H_{k+1}^{\phi}=(1-\phi)H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}+\phi H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}+\phi v_kv_k^T,
\]
where
\[
v_k=(y_k^TH_ky_k)^{1/2}\left(\frac{s_k}{s_k^Ty_k}-\frac{H_ky_k}{y_k^TH_ky_k}\right).
\]
For \(\phi\in[0,1]\), this is the convex Broyden class. Every defined member satisfies \(H_{k+1}^{\phi}y_k=s_k\). The choices \(\phi=0\) and \(\phi=1\) give DFP and BFGS; when their denominators are nonzero,
\[
\phi=\frac{s_k^Ty_k}{(s_k-H_ky_k)^Ty_k}
\]
gives SR1, and
\[
\phi=\frac{1}{1\mp y_k^TH_ky_k/(s_k^Ty_k)}
\]
gives a Hoshino update. The corresponding direct class is
\[
B_{k+1}^{\theta}=\theta B_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}+(1-\theta)B_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=B_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\theta w_kw_k^T,
\]
where
\[
w_k=(s_k^TB_ks_k)^{1/2}\left(\frac{y_k}{s_k^Ty_k}-\frac{B_ks_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}\right),
\quad
\theta=\frac{\phi-1}{\phi-1-\phi\mu},
\quad
\mu=\frac{(y_k^TH_ky_k)(s_k^TB_ks_k)}{(s_k^Ty_k)^2},
\]
provided \(\phi-1-\phi\mu\ne0\). Every defined direct update satisfies \(B_{k+1}^{\theta}s_k=y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full inverse Broyden class is the affine family joining DFP and BFGS, with parameters from zero to one forming its convex subclass. It satisfies the inverse secant equation and includes DFP, BFGS, SR1, and Hoshino choices where the displayed formulas are defined. An associated direct-matrix class satisfies the direct secant equation, with its parameter related to the inverse parameter by the displayed transformation.
assumptions_latex: 1\mp y_k^TH_ky_k/(s_k^Ty_k)\ne0\ \text{when a Hoshino parameter is used}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of Broyden and Fletcher–Reeves Methods on Convex Quadratics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional exact-line-search equivalence and the source's Krylov-sequence characterization of the termination integer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be a convex quadratic function with Hessian \(H\). If \(S_0=I_n\) and exact line searches are used, then a Broyden method is equivalent to the Fletcher--Reeves conjugate-gradient method. The integer \(m\) from the finite-termination theorem is the least number of independent vectors in the sequence
\[
g_0,Hg_0,H^2g_0,\ldots.
\]

The source characterizes the associated termination integer using the independent vectors in the Krylov sequence generated by the initial gradient and Hessian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination and Conjugacy of Broyden Methods on Convex Quadratics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-line-search properties of the Broyden class on a convex quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If a Broyden method is applied to a convex quadratic function with Hessian \(H\) and exact line searches are used, it terminates after \(m\le n\) iterations. For every \(k=0,1,\ldots,m\),
\[
\delta_i=S_{k+1}\gamma_i\qquad(0\le i\le k)
\]
and
\[
\delta_i^TH\delta_j=0\qquad(0\le i<j\le k).
\]
If \(m=n-1\), then \(S_m=H^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex quadratic with exact line searches, a Broyden method terminates in at most n iterations. The accumulated secant equations hold, the displacement directions are mutually Hessian-conjugate, and S_m is the exact inverse Hessian when m equals n minus one.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is a convex quadratic function on }\mathbb{R}^n
\text{the Broyden method uses exact line searches}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independence of Broyden Iterates and Associated BFGS Updates from Earlier Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-line-search invariance for Broyden parameters above their degenerate values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, suppose
\[
L(x_0)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid f(x)\le f(x_0)\}
\]
is bounded, and let \(H_0=H_0^T\succ0\). Let \(\{H_k^{\phi}\}\) be generated by Broyden-class updates satisfying \(\phi_k>\bar\phi\), where \(\bar\phi\) denotes the applicable degenerate value. For each \(k\), let \(H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}\) be obtained by applying the BFGS update to \(H_k^{\phi}\). Under exact line search,
\[
\forall k\ge0,\qquad (x_{k+1},H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}})
\text{ is independent of }(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_{k-1}).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable objective with bounded initial level set and a symmetric positive-definite initial inverse approximation, exact-line-search Broyden updates above the applicable degenerate value yield a next iterate and associated BFGS update that do not depend on earlier Broyden parameters.
assumptions_latex: H_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}\ \text{is obtained by applying BFGS to }H_k^{\phi}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Broyden Update Family

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

S_{k+1}=(1-\phi_k)S_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}+\phi_kS_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}.

The choices \(\phi_k=0\) and \(\phi_k=1\) give the DFP and BFGS updates, respectively. Where the relevant denominator is nonzero, the choices

\phi_k=\frac{\delta_k^T\gamma_k}{\delta_k^T\gamma_k\pm\gamma_k^TS_k\gamma_k}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite termination and hereditary secant properties of Broyden methods on quadratics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-line-search behavior of well-defined admissible Broyden-class methods on strongly convex quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
f(x)=b^Tx+\tfrac12x^TAx,\qquad A=A^T\succ0,
\]
and start from \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(B_0=B_0^T\succ0\). Apply a well-defined Broyden-class method with exact step lengths and \(\phi_k\geq\phi_k^c\) for every \(k\). Then: (i) the iterates are independent of the parameter choices and reach the minimizer in at most \(n\) iterations; (ii)
\[
B_ks_j=y_j,\qquad j=k-1,k-2,\ldots,1;
\]
(iii) if \(B_0=I\), the iterates coincide with those of conjugate gradients and
\[
s_i^TAs_j=0\qquad(i\neq j);
\]
and (iv), if \(n\) iterations are performed, \(B_n=A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a strongly convex quadratic, a well-defined admissible Broyden method with exact line searches has parameter-independent iterates and reaches the minimizer within n iterations. Its current matrix retains the secant equations for the listed earlier directions. With identity initialization, its iterates coincide with conjugate gradients and its directions are A-conjugate. If n iterations are performed, the final approximation equals the exact Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \alpha_k\quad\text{is an exact step length for every }k
\text{all required Broyden iterations are well defined}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\text{ is independent of the admissible parameter choices and }x_k=x_*\text{ for some }k\leq n;\quad B_ks_j=y_j\ (j=k-1,\ldots,1);\quad B_0=I\Longrightarrow s_i^TAs_j=0\ (i\neq j);\quad B_n=A\text{ if }n\text{ iterations are performed}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct Broyden-class representation and restricted parameter regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Hessian-approximation form of the full Broyden class, including its BFGS and DFP endpoints and the positive-definiteness guarantee for the restricted interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the displayed denominators are nonzero and define
\[
v_k=\frac{y_k}{y_k^Ts_k}-\frac{B_ks_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}.
\]
The direct Broyden class is
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}+\phi_k(s_k^TB_ks_k)v_kv_k^T,
\]
equivalently,
\[
B_{k+1}=(1-\phi_k)B_{k+1}^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi_kB_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DFP}}.
\]
Thus \(\phi_k=0\) yields BFGS, \(\phi_k=1\) yields DFP, and every member satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). If \(B_k\succ0\), \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and \(0\leq\phi_k\leq1\), then \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct Broyden class is an affine family joining the BFGS and DFP Hessian updates. BFGS occurs at parameter zero and DFP at parameter one, and every well-defined member satisfies the secant equation. A positive-definite current matrix remains positive definite under the curvature condition throughout the restricted interval from zero to one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-definiteness-constrained Broyden family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and let \(B_{k+1}(\phi_k)\) be the direct Broyden-class update. Define \(\mu_k=\frac{(y_k^TB_k^{-1}y_k)(s_k^TB_ks_k)}{(y_k^Ts_k)^2}\) and \(\phi_k^c=(1-\mu_k)^{-1}\), with the singular limiting case interpreted separately when \(\mu_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The portion of the full Broyden class constrained to preserve strict positive definiteness; it is broader than the convex interval \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained Broyden class family is \(\{B_{k+1}(\phi_k):\phi_k>\phi_k^c\}\), where \(B_{k+1}(\phi_k)\) is the Broyden update and \(\phi_k^c\leq0\) is its singular boundary. For \(\mu_k>1\), the matrix is singular at \(\phi_k=\phi_k^c\), positive definite for \(\phi_k>\phi_k^c\), and loses positive definiteness below that boundary. Consequently, if every update uses \(s_k^Ty_k>0\) and \(\phi_k>\phi_k^c\), an initially symmetric positive definite sequence remains symmetric positive definite. The simpler convex Broyden class \(0\leq\phi_k\leq1\) is contained in this constrained family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-definiteness-constrained Broyden family restricts the real Broyden parameter to lie above a data-dependent critical value. The critical value is nonpositive and marks a singular update. Parameters strictly above it preserve positive definiteness under positive secant curvature. This admissible range contains, but can be larger than, the convex interval from zero to one.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu_k>1\) for the finite critical-value formula; the equality case is treated by its limiting admissible range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\phi_k>\phi_k^c=(1-\mu_k)^{-1}\), then \(B_{k+1}(\phi_k)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\); at \(\phi_k=\phi_k^c\), the update is singular.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The convex Broyden restriction \(\phi_k\in[0,1]\) is a sufficient, generally nonmaximal, positive-definiteness constraint.
special_cases_latex: BFGS \((\phi_k=0)\) and DFP \((\phi_k=1)\) belong to the constrained family.
Certain negative values of \(\phi_k\) are admissible when they remain above \(\phi_k^c\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A Cholesky-based realization is available for every strictly admissible updated matrix.
The constraint is local to the current matrix and secant pair because \(\phi_k^c\) depends on \(B_k,s_k,y_k\).
boundary_notes: The strict inequality excludes the singular boundary.
This constrained family is not synonymous with the narrower convex Broyden class.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Broyden Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform parameter bound for an iteration-dependent sequence of full-Broyden updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) be an update-index set, and let \((\phi_k)_{k\in K}\in\mathbb{R}^K\) parameterize a sequence of direct full-Broyden updates. The sequence belongs to a bounded Broyden class if there exists a finite constant \(M\ge0\), independent of \(k\), such that \[|\phi_k|\le M\qquad\text{for every }k\in K.\] Equivalently, \(\sup_{k\in K}|\phi_k|<\infty\). This definition bounds only the update parameters and does not by itself guarantee positive definiteness of the updated matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of full-Broyden updates belongs to a bounded Broyden class when all its real update parameters share one finite absolute bound. Parameter boundedness alone does not guarantee positive definiteness.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Broyden Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Broyden parameters confined to a prescribed proper subset of the full class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subsetneq\mathbb{R}\) be a prescribed admissible interval. The Broyden class restricted to \(I\) consists of the updates \[B_+(\phi)=B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi(s^TBs)vv^T,	\qquad \phi\in I.\] The frequently used restricted convex class takes \(I=[0,1]\). More generally, choosing a compact interval \(I=[\underline\phi,\overline\phi]\) yields a bounded restricted class, while definiteness must be checked against the curvature pair and the admissibility boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted Broyden class limits the real Broyden parameter to a prescribed proper interval; the standard convex restriction uses the interval from zero to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_+(\phi)\) belongs to the restricted class exactly when \(\phi\in I\).

knowledge_statements.title: Broyden Parameter Admissibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-definiteness condition for the direct rank-one Broyden parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) and \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(s^Ty>0\). Define \(a=s^TBs>0\), \(B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=B-Bss^TB/a+yy^T/(s^Ty)\), and \(v=y/(s^Ty)-Bs/a\). For \(\phi\in\mathbb{R}\), set \(B_+(\phi)=B^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi avv^T\). If \(v=0\), every \(\phi\in\mathbb{R}\) produces the same positive-definite matrix. If \(v\ne0\), then \[B_+(\phi)\succ0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 1+\phi a\,v^T(B^{\mathrm{BFGS}})^{-1}v>0.\] Equivalently, \(\phi>-1/[a\,v^T(B^{\mathrm{BFGS}})^{-1}v]\). Equality is the singular boundary, while a smaller parameter gives exactly one negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a direct Broyden update based on a positive-definite BFGS matrix, a scalar rank-one test gives the exact parameter interval preserving positive definiteness. Equality marks singularity; if the correction direction is zero, every parameter gives the same matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(v\ne0\), then \(B_+(\phi)\succ0\) exactly when \(1+\phi a v^T(B^{\mathrm{BFGS}})^{-1}v>0\); if \(v=0\), every \(\phi\in\mathbb{R}\) is admissible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-definiteness threshold for a Broyden update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical Broyden parameter separating positive-definite, singular, and indefinite updates when the finite threshold is defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k=B_k^T\succ0\) and \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and define
\[
\mu_k=\frac{(y_k^TB_k^{-1}y_k)(s_k^TB_ks_k)}{(y_k^Ts_k)^2}\geq1.
\]
If \(\mu_k>1\), define the finite critical value
\[
\phi_k^c=\frac{1}{1-\mu_k}<0.
\]
Then
\[
\phi_k>\phi_k^c\Longrightarrow B_{k+1}\succ0,
\]
\[
\phi_k=\phi_k^c\Longrightarrow B_{k+1}\text{ is singular},
\]
and decreasing \(\phi_k\) below \(\phi_k^c\) makes the update indefinite. In particular, every \(\phi_k\geq0\) preserves positive definiteness. Consequently, if \(B_0\succ0\), \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and \(\phi_k>\phi_k^c\) at every iteration for which the finite threshold is defined, all generated matrices remain symmetric positive definite. The displayed finite-threshold formula does not cover the degenerate case \(\mu_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite current approximation satisfying the curvature condition, the scalar μ is at least one. When μ is strictly greater than one, the critical Broyden parameter is negative: values above it preserve positive definiteness, equality produces singularity, and lower values produce indefiniteness. Thus every nonnegative parameter is safe. The finite critical-value formula is undefined when μ equals one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_k>\phi_k^c\Longrightarrow B_{k+1}\succ0,\quad \phi_k=\phi_k^c\Longrightarrow B_{k+1}\text{ is singular},\quad \phi_k<\phi_k^c\Longrightarrow B_{k+1}\text{ is indefinite}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degenerate Broyden Parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exceptional Broyden parameter expressed through the direct and inverse approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(B_k=H_k^{-1}\) and \(s_k^Ty_k\ne0\), and define
\[
\mu=\frac{(y_k^TH_ky_k)(s_k^TB_ks_k)}{(s_k^Ty_k)^2}.
\]
If \(\mu\ne1\), the finite degenerate parameter value is
\[
\bar\phi=\frac{1}{1-\mu}
=\left(1-\frac{(y_k^TH_ky_k)(s_k^TB_ks_k)}{(s_k^Ty_k)^2}\right)^{-1}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the displayed quantities are defined and mu is not one, the degenerate Broyden parameter equals one divided by one minus mu.
