knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine family of symmetric secant updates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_c\in\mathbb S^n\), \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(s\neq0\). Let \(\mathcal S(s,y)=\{B\in\mathbb S^n:Bs=y\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General dense symmetric direct secant updates outside a commitment to BFGS, DFP, SR1, or one Broyden parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family of symmetric secant updates associated with \((B_c,s,y)\) is the affine set \(\mathcal S(s,y)\). Its Euclidean Frobenius-minimal member relative to \(B_c\) is the PSB matrix \(B_{\mathrm{PSB}}=B_c+\frac{rs^T+sr^T}{s^Ts}-\frac{r^Ts}{(s^Ts)^2}ss^T\), where \(r=y-B_cs\). Every other symmetric secant update has the form \(B^+=B_{\mathrm{PSB}}+Z\), with \(Z=Z^T\) and \(Zs=0\). Thus alternative symmetric families are obtained by imposing additional structure, weighting, scaling, rank, or definiteness conditions on the free symmetric operator \(Z\) acting on the orthogonal complement of \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All symmetric matrices mapping the step to the gradient displacement form an affine family. PSB is the member closest to the current matrix in the ordinary Frobenius norm. Every other symmetric secant update equals PSB plus a symmetric matrix that annihilates the step. Additional update families arise by constraining this free action, for example through a weighted norm, definiteness requirement, rank limit, or scaling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S(s,y)=\{B_{\mathrm{PSB}}+Z:Z=Z^T,\,Zs=0\}\), and \(B_{\mathrm{PSB}}\) is the unique minimizer of \(\|B-B_c\|_F\) over \(B\in\mathcal S(s,y)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The homogeneous freedom is the linear space \(\{Z\in\mathbb S^n:Zs=0\}\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(Z=0\) gives PSB.
Weighted minimal-change restrictions yield variable-metric updates different from ordinary Frobenius projection.
immediate_consequences_latex: The secant equation alone does not select a unique symmetric matrix when \(n>1\).
Any two symmetric secant updates differ by a symmetric matrix that annihilates \(s\).
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness is not automatic for a general member of the affine family.
The formula concerns a single secant pair; multisecant updates impose additional linear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Powell-Symmetric-Broyden Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-change symmetric update satisfying one direct secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(r=y-Bs\) and compute \[B_+=B+\frac{rs^T+sr^T}{s^Ts}-\frac{r^Ts}{(s^Ts)^2}ss^T.\] Output \(B_+\). The update is symmetric, satisfies \(B_+s=y\), has correction rank at most two, and uniquely minimizes \(\|X-B\|_F\) over all \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\) satisfying \(Xs=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PSB algorithm applies the unique minimum-Frobenius-norm symmetric correction enforcing the secant equation; its correction has rank at most two.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Powell–symmetric–Broyden update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_c\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(s\neq0\), and define the secant residual \(r=y-B_cs\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dense direct Hessian update using the ordinary Frobenius norm; positive definiteness is not imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Powell–symmetric–Broyden update is \(B^+=B_c+\frac{rs^T+sr^T}{s^Ts}-\frac{r^Ts}{(s^Ts)^2}ss^T\). Equivalently, \(B^+\) is the unique solution of \(\operatorname*{minimize}_{B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}}\|B-B_c\|_F\) subject to \(Bs=y\) and \(B-B_c\) symmetric. When \(B_c\) is symmetric, \(B^+\) is symmetric, satisfies the secant equation, and differs from \(B_c\) by a matrix of rank at most two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Powell–symmetric–Broyden update adds a symmetric rank-at-most-two correction built from the secant residual and the step. It is uniquely characterized as the matrix closest to the current approximation in the ordinary Frobenius norm among matrices satisfying the secant equation with a symmetric correction. It preserves symmetry but does not generally preserve positive definiteness.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(B^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B:B s=y,\,B-B_c=(B-B_c)^T}\|B-B_c\|_F\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r\) is a scalar multiple of \(s\), the correction has rank one.
immediate_consequences_latex: The update is defined for every nonzero \(s\), without requiring \(s^Ty>0\).
The PSB correction changes the current matrix minimally in the unweighted Frobenius geometry.
boundary_notes: PSB may produce an indefinite matrix even from a positive definite current matrix.
The ordinary Frobenius geometry is not invariant under arbitrary rescaling of variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-change characterization of the PSB update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique Frobenius-norm projection satisfying the secant and symmetry constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $H_c=H_c^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and let $s_c,y_c\in\mathbb R^n$ with $s_c\ne0$. The problem
\[
\min_{H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}}\|H-H_c\|_F
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Hs_c=y_c,\quad H-H_c=(H-H_c)^T
\]
has the unique solution
\[
H_+=H_c+\frac{(y_c-H_cs_c)s_c^T+s_c(y_c-H_cs_c)^T}{s_c^Ts_c}-\frac{\langle y_c-H_cs_c,s_c\rangle s_cs_c^T}{(s_c^Ts_c)^2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among all corrections satisfying the secant equation and the symmetry constraint, the PSB update is the unique matrix closest to the current symmetric approximation in Frobenius norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted least-change characterization of the general PSB update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique weighted-Frobenius least-change symmetric update satisfying a secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(c,s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(c^Ts>0\), and let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and nonsingular with \(Mc=M^{-1}s\). Define \(\|A\|_{M,F}=\|MAM\|_F\). Then \[\bar B=B+\frac{(y-Bs)c^T+c(y-Bs)^T}{c^Ts}-\frac{(y-Bs)^Ts}{(c^Ts)^2}cc^T\] is the unique solution of \[\min\left\{\|\widehat B-B\|_{M,F}:\widehat B s=y,\ \widehat B^T=\widehat B\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated symmetry, positivity, nonsingularity, and compatibility assumptions, the general PSB formula is the unique symmetric secant update closest to B in the weighted Frobenius norm defined by M.
assumptions_latex: M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\quad M^T=M,\quad M\text{ is nonsingular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar B=B+\frac{(y-Bs)c^T+c(y-Bs)^T}{c^Ts}-\frac{(y-Bs)^Ts}{(c^Ts)^2}cc^T=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\substack{\widehat B s=y\\\widehat B^T=\widehat B}}\|\widehat B-B\|_{M,F},\quad\text{with a unique minimizer.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local q-superlinear convergence of the PSB method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence of the unconstrained symmetric secant iteration using PSB Hessian updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^n$ be open and convex, let $f:D\to\mathbb R$ be twice continuously differentiable, and suppose $\nabla^2f\in\operatorname{Lip}_\gamma(D)$. Assume that $x_*\in D$, $\nabla f(x_*)=0$, $\nabla^2f(x_*)$ is nonsingular, and $H_0$ is symmetric. Then there exist $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ such that, if
\[
\|x_0-x_*\|_2<\varepsilon,\qquad \|H_0-\nabla^2f(x_*)\|_2\le\delta,
\]
the iteration
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-H_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k),\quad s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,\quad y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k),
\]
\[
H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{(y_k-H_ks_k)s_k^T+s_k(y_k-H_ks_k)^T}{s_k^Ts_k}-\frac{\langle y_k-H_ks_k,s_k\rangle s_ks_k^T}{(s_k^Ts_k)^2}
\]
is well defined, remains in $D$, and converges q-superlinearly to $x_*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the Hessian is Lipschitz continuous and nonsingular at a stationary point, then sufficiently close initial iterates and symmetric Hessian approximations make the PSB method well defined, keep its iterates in the domain, and yield q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: D\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is open and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The PSB iteration is well defined},\qquad \{x_k\}\subset D,\qquad x_k\to x_*\text{ q-superlinearly}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Huang generalized inverse quasi-Newton update and Greenstadt member
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(H_k\in\mathbb R^{n	imes n}\), and assume \(y_k
e0\). The matrix \(H_k\) approximates an inverse Hessian, while \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, dense inverse quasi-Newton updates. The Huang class need not be symmetric; the Greenstadt formula is a symmetric least-change member satisfying the ordinary inverse secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Huang class consists of updates \[H_{k+1}=H_k+s_ku_k^T+H_ky_kv_k^T,\] where \[u_k=a_{11}s_k+a_{12}H_k^Ty_k,\qquad v_k=a_{21}s_k+a_{22}H_k^Ty_k,\] and the coefficients satisfy \(u_k^Ty_k=\rho\) and \(v_k^Ty_k=-1\). Consequently, every member satisfies the generalized inverse secant equation \[H_{k+1}y_k=\rho s_k.\] For \(\rho=1\), the symmetric Greenstadt member is \[H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{r_ky_k^T+y_kr_k^T}{y_k^Ty_k}-\frac{y_k^Tr_k}{(y_k^Ty_k)^2}y_ky_k^T,\qquad r_k=s_k-H_ky_k,\] provided \(H_k=H_k^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Huang update changes an inverse-Hessian approximation by two outer products whose coefficient vectors lie in the span of \(s_k\) and \(H_k^Ty_k\). The two scalar constraints force \(H_{k+1}y_k=\rho s_k\). With \(\rho=1\), Greenstadt's symmetric formula uses the residual \(r_k=s_k-H_ky_k\), preserves symmetry, and satisfies \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{k+1}y_k=\rho s_k\), and the displayed Greenstadt specialization has \(H_{k+1}=H_{k+1}^T\) and \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the Greenstadt member, \(H_{k+1}\) is the Frobenius-norm nearest symmetric matrix to \(H_k\) subject to \(Hy_k=s_k\).
special_cases_latex: Imposing symmetry and \(\rho=1\) on the Huang class yields the ordinary symmetric Broyden class.
The displayed Greenstadt update is the dual, inverse-Hessian form of the Powell-symmetric-Broyden least-change update.
immediate_consequences_latex: The Huang representation has five displayed scalar parameters subject to two scalar constraints, hence three free degrees of freedom when the spanning vectors are nondegenerate.
boundary_notes: The Huang class does not generally preserve symmetry or positive definiteness.
The Greenstadt denominator requires \(y_k\ne0\); positive definiteness is not guaranteed even when \(H_k\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Huang Update Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-form symmetric secant family parameterized by a normalized vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(y,s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r=s-Hy\). For any vector \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(v^Ty=1\), define the Huang-family update by \[H_+(v)=H+rv^T+vr^T-(r^Ty)vv^T.\] Every such update is symmetric, satisfies the inverse secant equation \(H_+(v)y=s\), and differs from \(H\) by a matrix of rank at most two. Different normalized choices of \(v\) recover distinct symmetric secant updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Huang family uses any vector normalized against the gradient displacement to produce a symmetric rank-two inverse update satisfying the secant equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Huang Quasi-Newton Update Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric Huang update and the separately displayed McCormick and Pearson formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For dimensionally compatible \(S_k,\delta_k,\gamma_k\) and freely chosen parameters \(\theta,\phi,\psi,\omega\), the Huang family is
\[
S_{k+1}=S_k+\frac{\delta_k(\theta\delta_k+\phi S_k^T\gamma_k)^T}{(\theta\delta_k+\phi S_k^T\gamma_k)^T\gamma_k}-\frac{S_k\gamma_k(\psi\delta_k+\omega S_k^T\gamma_k)^T}{(\psi\delta_k+\omega S_k^T\gamma_k)^T\gamma_k},
\]
when its two denominators are nonzero. This family encompasses the rank-one, DFP, and BFGS formulas, among others. The section also gives the McCormick and Pearson updates, respectively, as
\[
S_{k+1}=S_k+\frac{(\delta_k-S_k\gamma_k)\delta_k^T}{\delta_k^T\gamma_k},\qquad
S_{k+1}=S_k+\frac{(\delta_k-S_k\gamma_k)\gamma_k^T S_k}{\gamma_k^T S_k\gamma_k},
\]
whenever the denominator of the applicable formula is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Huang formula is a four-parameter quasi-Newton update family encompassing rank-one, DFP, and BFGS updates. The section separately displays the McCormick and Pearson update formulas. Each update is defined only when its applicable denominator is nonzero.
assumptions_latex: (\theta\delta_k+\phi S_k^T\gamma_k)^T\gamma_k\ne0\text{ and }(\psi\delta_k+\omega S_k^T\gamma_k)^T\gamma_k\ne0\text{ for the Huang update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{k+1}\text{ is given by the applicable displayed update; the Huang family encompasses rank-one, DFP, and BFGS formulas.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic iterate invariance across Huang-family updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of the first n iterates for fixed initialization on a positive-definite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x^0\) and \(H_0\). Let \(x^1,\ldots,x^n\) be generated by a variable-metric algorithm whose matrix-update formula belongs to Huang's family. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic and fixed initial point and matrix, all Huang-family update formulas generate the same first n iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Greenstadt Update Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted least-change specialization of the symmetric inverse secant family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{S}^n\), let \(W\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), and let \(y\ne0\). Set \(r=s-Hy\) and \(v=Wy/(y^TWy)\). Equivalently, it is the least-change correction associated with the weight-induced geometry, with the precise weighted matrix norm determined by the chosen Greenstadt convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greenstadt updates choose the Huang parameter from a positive-definite weight, giving a symmetric inverse secant update adapted to a weighted least-change geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted least-change characterization of the Greenstadt update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The weighted-Frobenius variational characterization, followed by the source-stated zero-residual failure boundary and scaling safeguard in its NL2SOL specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let s_k,v_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n, B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}, s_k^Tv_k>0, and let T=T^T\succ0 satisfy TT^Ts_k=v_k. The unique solution of \min_B\|T^{-T}(B-B_k)T^{-1}\|_F subject to B-B_k\text{ symmetric} and Bs_k=y_k is B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{(y_k-B_ks_k)v_k^T+v_k(y_k-B_ks_k)^T}{s_k^Tv_k}-\frac{s_k^T(y_k-B_ks_k)}{(s_k^Tv_k)^2}v_kv_k^T. In the nonlinear least-squares specialization, v_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k). The unscaled correction B_k is not guaranteed to vanish as iterates approach a zero-residual solution; the stated safeguard first replaces B_k by \gamma_kB_k, where \gamma_k=\min\{s_k^Ty_k/(s_k^TB_ks_k),1\}, when the quotient is defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displayed Greenstadt-family correction is the unique weighted-Frobenius least-change correction satisfying symmetry and the secant equation. In the cited nonlinear least-squares use, the unscaled correction may fail to vanish near a zero-residual solution, motivating the stated scaling safeguard.
assumptions_latex: s_k^TB_ks_k\neq0\text{ when the scaling quotient is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_{k+1}\text{ is the unique minimizer, and }B_{k+1}-B_k\text{ is symmetric with }B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.

knowledge_statements.title: Huang–Greenstadt Structural Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General symmetric rank-two secant representation underlying Huang-type updates; historical naming and Greenstadt specialization require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\), \(s\ne0\), and \(r=y-Bs\). For any \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(v^\top s=1\), define
\[
B_+=B+rv^\top+vr^\top-(r^\top s)vv^\top.
\]
Then \(B_+=B_+^\top\) and \(B_+s=y\). Conversely, if a symmetric correction \(E=B_+-B\) has range contained in \(\operatorname{span}\{r,v\}\), satisfies \(Es=r\), and \(v^\top s=1\), the displayed rank-two correction is the corresponding symmetric secant form. A Greenstadt-type member is obtained by selecting \(v\) through a prescribed weighted least-change metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized vector generates a symmetric rank-two correction satisfying the secant equation; Greenstadt-type updates arise from metric-dependent choices of that vector.

notation.meaning: normalizing vector defining the rank-two member

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward rank-two formula is symmetric and satisfies the secant equation. However, the stated converse is not valid under only the given range and secant conditions: those conditions need not uniquely determine the displayed correction. The attribution to the Huang–Greenstadt family and the weighted least-change characterization of the Greenstadt member also require an exact authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Scaling Variable-Metric Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian-form self-scaled BFGS update with a positive scalar multiplying the inherited metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(B_k=B_k^\top\succ0\), a secant pair \((s_k,y_k)\) with \(y_k^\top s_k>0\), and a scaling parameter \(\tau_k>0\), the self-scaled BFGS update is
\[
B_{k+1}=\tau_k B_k-\tau_k\frac{B_ks_ks_k^\top B_k}{s_k^\top B_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^\top}{y_k^\top s_k}.
\]
It satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and \(B_{k+1}\succ0\). A self-scaling variable-metric method chooses \(\tau_k\) from current iteration data and computes the search direction from \(B_kp_k=-\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-scaled BFGS rescales the inherited metric before applying complementary rank-two terms, while preserving positive definiteness and the secant equation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed scaled BFGS formula has the claimed secant and positive-definiteness properties under the stated assumptions, and its role fits the topic. An authoritative locator is still required to establish that this precise parameterization and choice rule constitute the intended self-scaling variable-metric family.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-scaling variable-metric update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_k=H_k^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be an inverse-Hessian approximation and let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(s_k^Ty_k\ne0\) and \(y_k^TH_ky_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dense inverse updates obtained by scaling the retained part of a Broyden-class correction at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Broyden parameter \(\phi\) and a self-scaling parameter \(\gamma_k>0\), define \[v_k=(y_k^TH_ky_k)^{1/2}\left( rac{s_k}{s_k^Ty_k}- rac{H_ky_k}{y_k^TH_ky_k}ight).\] The self-scaling variable-metric update is \[H_{k+1}^{(\phi,\gamma_k)}=\gamma_k\left(H_k- rac{H_ky_ky_k^TH_k}{y_k^TH_ky_k}+\phi v_kv_k^Tight)+ rac{s_ks_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k}.\] A self-scaling variable-metric method uses the direction \(d_k=-H_k
abla f(x_k)\), sets \(s_k=\alpha_kd_k\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_k+s_k)-
abla f(x_k)\), and applies this update with chosen \(\phi\) and \(\gamma_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaling variable-metric method multiplies the part of a Broyden-class inverse update that retains old metric information by a positive scalar \(\gamma_k\), while leaving the secant-restoring term \(s_ks_k^T/(s_k^Ty_k)\) unscaled. Its search direction is \(-H_k\nabla f(x_k)\), and its curvature pair is formed from the accepted step and gradient difference.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The formula is obtained by applying the Broyden-class inverse update to the scaled matrix \(\gamma_kH_k\).
special_cases_latex: When \(\gamma_k=1\), the formula reduces to the ordinary Broyden class.
When \(\phi=0\), the correction is the self-scaled DFP form.
immediate_consequences_latex: The scale parameter changes the inherited metric without violating the inverse secant equation.
Positive scaling preserves positive definiteness under positive curvature and \(\phi\ge0\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a unique rule for choosing \(\gamma_k\).
If \(s_k^Ty_k\le0\), the stated positive-definiteness property does not apply.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eigenvalue Interlacing for the Self-Scaled Variable-Metric Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral interlacing regimes determined by the location of one relative to the scaled spectrum of the current SSVM matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\phi\in[0,1]$, $\gamma_k>0$, and let $\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n$ and $\mu_1^\phi\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n^\phi$ be the eigenvalues of $R_k$ and $R_{k+1}^\phi$, respectively, as defined in (5.5.11) and (5.5.24). If $\gamma_k\lambda_n\geq1$, then $\mu_n^\phi=1$ and $1\leq\gamma_k\lambda_{i+1}\leq\mu_i^\phi\leq\gamma_k\lambda_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n-1$. If $\gamma_k\lambda_1\leq1$, then $\mu_1^\phi=1$ and $\gamma_k\lambda_i\leq\mu_i^\phi\leq\gamma_k\lambda_{i-1}\leq1$ for $i=2,\ldots,n$. If $\gamma_k\lambda_n\leq1\leq\gamma_k\lambda_1$ and some $i_0\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ satisfies $\gamma_k\lambda_{i_0+1}\leq1\leq\gamma_k\lambda_{i_0}$, then the interlacing chain (5.5.23) holds and at least one of $\mu_{i_0}^\phi$ and $\mu_{i_0+1}^\phi$ equals $1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The new spectrum interlaces the scaled old spectrum. When the scaled old spectrum lies entirely above one, the smallest new eigenvalue is one; when it lies entirely below one, the largest new eigenvalue is one; and when it straddles one, the interlacing also straddles one and one of the two adjacent new eigenvalues equals one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalized quasi-Newton update safeguard system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), let \(B_k=B_k^T\), choose a trial step \(p_k\), and form an accepted displacement \(s_k\) and gradient difference \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proposed umbrella definition for deterministic smooth quasi-Newton globalization; the supplied sources support its components but not this exact named system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globalized update safeguard system is a tuple \(\mathcal S=(\mathcal G,\mathcal M,\mathcal A,\mathcal U,\mathcal R)\) with: a globalization rule \(\mathcal G\) producing or accepting \(s_k\); a secant-pair modifier \(\mathcal M(s_k,y_k,B_k)=(\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k)\); an admission predicate \(\mathcal A_k\in\{0,1\}\); an update map \(\mathcal U\); and a recovery map \(\mathcal R\). The next metric is defined by \[B_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\mathcal U(B_k,\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k),&\mathcal A_k=1,\\ \mathcal R(B_k,s_k,y_k),&\mathcal A_k=0.\end{cases}\] The maps are selected so that every metric used by the globalization mechanism is finite and has its required structural property, such as symmetry, positive definiteness for a line search, or boundedness for a trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The system couples five mathematical objects: a step-globalization rule, a transformation of raw secant data, an update-admission test, a quasi-Newton update, and a recovery action. The metric is updated from safeguarded data when the admission predicate is true and otherwise is retained, reset, regularized, or rebuilt by the recovery map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}\) is given by the displayed admitted-update/recovery rule and belongs to the structural domain required by \(\mathcal G\).
special_cases_latex: Line-search BFGS uses positive-curvature admission or damping to retain \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).
Trust-region SR1 admits indefinite models but skips an update when its rank-one denominator is too small.
immediate_consequences_latex: The raw secant pair need not be passed unchanged to the update.
Rejected curvature information triggers an explicit state transition rather than an undefined matrix formula.
boundary_notes: This is a system-level formalization rather than a standard uniquely named textbook object.
No supplied source states this exact five-component tuple, so authoritative support for the canonical naming is still required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-search coupling of a quasi-Newton metric and secant data
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(B_k=B_k^T\) be nonsingular, and let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained quasi-Newton iterations using a scalar line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search coupling regime is an iteration satisfying \[p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\qquad \alpha_k>0,\] followed by \[s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k=\alpha_kp_k,\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k,\qquad B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k).\] The admissible set \(\mathcal L_k\subset(0,\infty)\) for \(\alpha_k\) is chosen jointly with the domain of \(\mathcal U\): the regime requires \(\alpha_k\in\mathcal L_k\), descent \(g_k^Tp_k<0\), and every denominator and curvature condition needed by \(\mathcal U\). Thus the line search controls both objective progress and whether the resulting pair \((s_k,y_k)\) is admissible for the metric update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a line-search coupling regime, the current metric determines the direction, the line search determines the step length, and the accepted step determines the secant pair used by the next metric update. A valid regime specifies an acceptable set of step lengths that ensures descent and makes the selected update formula well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) and \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,\alpha_kp_k,g_{k+1}-g_k)\) for an \(\alpha_k\) admissible to both the line search and update map.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an inverse approximation \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\), one may write \(p_k=-H_kg_k\) and update \(H_{k+1}\) directly.
special_cases_latex: Exact line search takes \(\alpha_k\) from an argmin set.
A Wolfe regime defines \(\mathcal L_k\) by sufficient-decrease and curvature inequalities.
An eventual-unit-step regime has \(\alpha_k=1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\) and \(g_k\ne0\), then \(g_k^Tp_k=-g_k^TB_k^{-1}g_k<0\).
boundary_notes: A trust-region method is not a line-search coupling because it selects direction and length simultaneously.
The definition does not require the line search to find a minimizer of the one-dimensional restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Line-Search Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-dimensional minimization along each quasi-Newton search direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(p_k\) be a descent direction, so \(g_k^\top p_k<0\). The exact-line-search regime selects
\[
\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\ge0} f(x_k+\alpha p_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k.
\]
If \(\alpha_k>0\) is an interior minimizer of the line-search problem, then the first-order condition is \(\nabla f(x_{k+1})^\top p_k=0\). Thus the new gradient is orthogonal to the direction just searched.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each step exactly minimizes the objective along its descent ray; an interior solution makes the new gradient orthogonal to the search direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) is an interior line minimizer for the orthogonality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\ge0}f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), and \(\nabla f(x_{k+1})^\top p_k=0\) for an interior minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact line search along a descent direction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(p_k\ne0\) be a feasible search direction. Define \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) on a nonempty admissible interval \(I_k\subseteq[0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic scalar minimization along a fixed direction; global exact line search on the stated interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iteration is in the exact-line-search regime if, for every executed iteration \(k\), it chooses \[\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in I_k}\phi_k(\alpha)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in I_k}f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\] and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). If \(I_k=(0,\infty)\), this is exact global minimization along the positive ray. If \(f\) is differentiable and \(\alpha_k\) is an interior minimizer, then the defining first-order stationarity condition is \[\phi_k'(\alpha_k)=\nabla f(x_{k+1})^Tp_k=0.\] For \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\), the same condition is \(g_{k+1}^Ts_k=0\) whenever \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact line search chooses a step length that globally minimizes the one-dimensional restriction of the objective over the declared admissible interval. At an interior differentiable minimizer, the new gradient is orthogonal to the fixed search direction, and hence to the nonzero accepted displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in I_k}f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), with \(\nabla f(x_{k+1})^Tp_k=0\) for an interior differentiable minimizer.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(\alpha_k>0\), interior stationarity is equivalently \(g_{k+1}^Ts_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex one-dimensional restriction \(\phi_k\), the exact step length is unique.
For a convex quadratic objective and a descent direction, the minimizer has the usual closed scalar quadratic-minimization form.
immediate_consequences_latex: The exact step satisfies every comparison \(f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) for \(\alpha\in I_k\).
boundary_notes: A stationary point of \(\phi_k\) is not by itself an exact global line-search solution unless it attains the minimum on \(I_k\).
Practical inexact line searches generally do not satisfy gradient orthogonality exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Wolfe-Line-Search Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak and strong Wolfe acceptance conditions for a differentiable objective and descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(g_k^\top p_k<0\). Given \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), a step \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies the Wolfe conditions when
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_k g_k^\top p_k,
\qquad
\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^\top p_k\ge c_2g_k^\top p_k.
\]
The strong Wolfe regime replaces the second inequality by
\[
\left|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^\top p_k\right|\le c_2|g_k^\top p_k|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wolfe step provides sufficient objective decrease and controls the new directional derivative; strong Wolfe controls its absolute magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed sufficient-decrease and curvature inequalities hold, with the absolute-value inequality in the strong Wolfe variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak and strong Wolfe line-search regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(p_k\) satisfy \(g_k^Tp_k<0\). Fix \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic inexact line search for a smooth objective along a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive step length \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the Wolfe conditions if \[f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k\] and \[\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^Tp_k\ge c_2g_k^Tp_k.\] A Wolfe-line-search regime chooses such an \(\alpha_k\) at every executed iteration and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). The strong Wolfe variant replaces the second inequality by \[\left|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^Tp_k\right|\le c_2|g_k^Tp_k|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wolfe line search accepts a positive step only when it gives Armijo sufficient decrease and its new directional derivative is no longer too negative. The strong Wolfe variant also prevents that derivative from becoming too positive by bounding its magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the displayed sufficient-decrease and weak or strong curvature inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), the weak curvature condition is \(\phi_k'(\alpha_k)\ge c_2\phi_k'(0)\), while the strong condition is \(|\phi_k'(\alpha_k)|\le c_2|\phi_k'(0)|\).
special_cases_latex: For a quasi-Newton direction, \(c_2\) is commonly chosen near \(0.9\).
The strong Wolfe conditions imply the weak Wolfe curvature condition because \(g_k^Tp_k<0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: With \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), weak Wolfe curvature gives \(s_k^Ty_k\ge\alpha_k(c_2-1)g_k^Tp_k>0\).
boundary_notes: Armijo decrease alone is not the Wolfe regime.
A Wolfe step need not be close to a minimizer of the one-dimensional restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Unit-Step Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail regime in which globalization accepts every unshortened quasi-Newton trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterates generated by \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), the method is in the eventual unit-step regime if there exists an index \(K<\infty\) such that
\[
\alpha_k=1\qquad\text{for every }k\ge K.
\]
Equivalently, from iteration \(K\) onward, the globalization test accepts the full trial point \(x_k+p_k\) without backtracking or contraction. This condition is distinct from merely having \(\alpha_k\to1\): convergence of step lengths permits infinitely many shortened steps, whereas eventual unit steps do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After some finite iteration, every full quasi-Newton trial step is accepted; merely having step lengths converge to one is weaker.

notation.meaning: first index after which all steps are full

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is a precise condition defining eventual unit steps and correctly distinguishes eventual equality from convergence of step lengths. No source or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied, so the record lacks admissible evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual acceptance of full quasi-Newton steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) with \(p_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha_k>0\). A line-search implementation tests \(\alpha=1\) before shortened or enlarged alternatives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An asymptotic property of line-search Newton or quasi-Newton iterations, not a requirement that every step from the initial iterate be full.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iteration is in the eventual unit-step regime if \[\exists k_0\in\mathbb N\ \forall k\ge k_0:\quad \alpha_k=1,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k.\] For a Wolfe-coupled implementation, this additionally means that the first trial \(\alpha=1\) satisfies the Wolfe acceptance inequalities for every \(k\ge k_0\) and is therefore accepted without backtracking or interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eventual unit-step regime is one in which there is a finite index after which every accepted step length equals one. In a Wolfe implementation that tests one first, the full step must satisfy the acceptance conditions at every sufficiently late iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The step sequence satisfies \(s_k=p_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
The set \(\{k:\alpha_k\ne1\}\) is finite.
special_cases_latex: Near a nondegenerate minimizer, Newton steps under a suitable Wolfe line search are eventually unit steps.
Quasi-Newton directions satisfying the Dennis–Moré accuracy condition admit unit Wolfe steps asymptotically.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once this regime begins, line-search scaling no longer perturbs the local direction.
If the underlying full-step iteration is superlinear, eventual unit-step acceptance permits that local rate to be realized.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\alpha_k\to1\) is weaker and does not imply eventual equality.
Occasional unit steps do not constitute the regime.
The definition itself does not assert convergence or a convergence rate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature-safeguarded secant update rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B=B^T\succ0\) and let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(s\ne0\). Let \(\mathcal U(B,s,y)\) be a symmetric quasi-Newton update whose domain includes a curvature requirement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional safeguard calculus for updates, especially positive-definite BFGS-type formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curvature-safeguarded update rule consists of a modifier \(M_B(s,y)=(\widehat s,\widehat y)\), an admission predicate \(A_B(\widehat s,\widehat y)\), and a fallback map \(R_B\), with \[B_+=\begin{cases}\mathcal U(B,\widehat s,\widehat y),&A_B(\widehat s,\widehat y)=1,\\R_B(B,s,y),&A_B(\widehat s,\widehat y)=0.\end{cases}\] For a positive-definite secant update, the safeguarded pair must satisfy a quantitative curvature condition such as \[\widehat s^T\widehat y\ge\delta\,\widehat s^TB\widehat s>0\qquad(\delta>0).\] Typical choices are damping \(\widehat y=\theta y+(1-\theta)Bs\), cautious admission with \(R_B(B,s,y)=B\), or metric recovery by a positive-definite reset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature-safeguarded calculus first modifies or tests a secant pair, applies the selected update only when a positive curvature threshold is met, and otherwise executes an explicit fallback. The threshold is quantitative, so it excludes pairs that are positive only at numerically negligible scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admitted pair obeys \(\widehat s^T\widehat y>0\), and \(B_+\) is defined either by the update or by the declared fallback.
special_cases_latex: Powell damping chooses \(\theta\) so that \(s^T\widehat y=\delta s^TBs\) whenever raw curvature is insufficient.
A cautious policy uses \(\widehat s=s\), \(\widehat y=y\), and skips the update below its threshold.
immediate_consequences_latex: BFGS applied to an admitted safeguarded pair preserves positive definiteness.
Update denominators involving \(\widehat s^T\widehat y\) are bounded away from zero relative to the chosen metric scale.
boundary_notes: Positive curvature alone does not safeguard SR1's distinct denominator \(s^T(y-Bs)\).
Different update families require different admission predicates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Damped BFGS Hessian update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k=B_k^T\succ0\), \(s_k\ne0\), and \(y_k\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(q_k=s_k^TB_ks_k>0\) and \(c_k=s_k^Ty_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian-form damped BFGS with the classical Powell threshold \(0.2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\theta_k=\begin{cases}1,&c_k\ge0.2q_k,\\ \dfrac{0.8q_k}{q_k-c_k},&c_k<0.2q_k,\end{cases}\qquad r_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k.\] The damped BFGS update is \[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{s_k^Tr_k}.\] Thus the ordinary BFGS formula is applied to the modified secant pair \((s_k,r_k)\), and the new matrix satisfies the modified secant equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=r_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Damped BFGS replaces a gradient difference with a convex combination of that difference and the model vector \(B_ks_k\). It uses the raw pair when curvature is at least twenty percent of the model curvature; otherwise it chooses the mixing coefficient so that the modified curvature equals exactly that threshold, then performs the standard BFGS update.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When damping is active, \(s_k^Tr_k=0.2s_k^TB_ks_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(s_k^Ty_k\ge0.2s_k^TB_ks_k\), then \(\theta_k=1\), \(r_k=y_k\), and the update is ordinary BFGS.
Formally, \(\theta_k=0\) would retain \(B_k\); the prescribed rule uses a positive interpolating value in the insufficient-curvature case.
immediate_consequences_latex: All denominators in the displayed update are positive.
Positive definiteness is retained even when the raw pair fails \(s_k^Ty_k>0\).
boundary_notes: The update satisfies a modified, not raw, secant equation whenever \(\theta_k<1\).
The formula does not make an intrinsically indefinite target Hessian positive definite in an approximation-theoretically exact sense.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Damped BFGS update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise damping of a BFGS curvature pair before applying the direct Hessian update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given $B_k=B_k^T\succ0$ and nonzero $s_k$, define
\[
\theta_k=\begin{cases}
1,&s_k^Ty_k\geq0.2s_k^TB_ks_k,\\
\dfrac{0.8s_k^TB_ks_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k-s_k^Ty_k},&s_k^Ty_k<0.2s_k^TB_ks_k,
\end{cases}
\qquad r_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k.
\]
Then update
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{s_k^Tr_k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a symmetric positive-definite matrix, retain the original curvature vector when it has sufficient curvature; otherwise blend it with the current model action. Use the resulting damped vector in the direct BFGS formula.
assumptions_latex: s_k,y_k\text{ are defined as the displacement and gradient-difference vectors in the surrounding SQP construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{s_k^Tr_k},\quad\text{with }r_k\text{ and }\theta_k\text{ given by the stated damping rule.}

knowledge_statements.title: Powell Damping Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell-damped Hessian-form BFGS with a configurable retained-curvature fraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(B_k=B_k^\top\succ0\), \(s_k\), \(y_k\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set \(q_k=s_k^\top B_ks_k\) and
\[
\theta_k=\begin{cases}1,&s_k^\top y_k\ge\eta q_k,\\
\dfrac{(1-\eta)q_k}{q_k-s_k^\top y_k},&s_k^\top y_k<\eta q_k,
\end{cases}
\qquad \bar y_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k.
\]
Then \(s_k^\top\bar y_k\ge\eta q_k>0\). Update
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^\top B_k}{q_k}+\frac{\bar y_k\bar y_k^\top}{s_k^\top\bar y_k}.
\]
The conventional Powell choice is \(\eta=0.2\); the family permits any fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Powell damping blends the measured gradient displacement with the predicted one until sufficient positive curvature holds, then performs BFGS.

notation.meaning: predicted quadratic curvature along the step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameterized Powell curvature damping family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B=B^T\succ0\), \(s\ne0\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and choose a curvature fraction \(\delta\in(0,1)\). Put \(q=s^TBs\) and \(c=s^Ty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized Hessian-form extension of classical Powell damping; \(\delta=0.2\) is the standard cited choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Powell damping family defines \[\theta_\delta=\begin{cases}1,&c\ge\delta q,\\ \dfrac{(1-\delta)q}{q-c},&c<\delta q,\end{cases}\qquad \widetilde y_\delta=\theta_\delta y+(1-\theta_\delta)Bs,\] and applies BFGS to \((s,\widetilde y_\delta)\): \[B_+=B-\frac{Bss^TB}{s^TBs}+\frac{\widetilde y_\delta\widetilde y_\delta^T}{s^T\widetilde y_\delta}.\] The defining curvature identity is \[s^T\widetilde y_\delta=\begin{cases}c,&c\ge\delta q,\\\delta q,&c<\delta q.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chosen fraction \(\delta\), Powell damping leaves a secant pair unchanged when raw curvature reaches \(\delta\) times the current model curvature. Otherwise it blends the gradient difference with \(Bs\) by the unique displayed coefficient that raises modified curvature to exactly \(\delta s^TBs\), and then applies BFGS.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^T\widetilde y_\delta\ge\delta s^TBs>0\), so the displayed BFGS update is well defined and positive definite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The coefficient is the solution in \([0,1]\) of \(s^T[\theta y+(1-\theta)Bs]=\delta s^TBs\) when \(s^Ty<\delta s^TBs\).
special_cases_latex: \(\delta=0.2\) gives the classical rule with numerator \(0.8s^TBs\).
If raw curvature passes the threshold, the member equals ordinary BFGS.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing \(\delta\) imposes a stronger lower curvature floor but modifies more secant pairs.
boundary_notes: The inspected source explicitly fixes \(\delta=0.2\); the continuously parameterized family is an algebraic generalization of that rule.
The method does not satisfy \(B_+s=y\) when damping is active.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative BFGS Damping Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General convex-blending damped BFGS family, separated from Powell's particular coefficient rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k=B_k^\top\succ0\), \(s_k\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and \(y_k\in\mathbb R^n\). A convex-blending BFGS damping rule selects \(\theta_k\in[0,1]\) and forms
\[
\widetilde y_k=\theta_k y_k+(1-\theta_k)B_k s_k,
\]
subject to a prescribed curvature safeguard \(s_k^\top\widetilde y_k\ge\mu_k>0\). It then applies
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_k s_k s_k^\top B_k}{s_k^\top B_k s_k}+\frac{\widetilde y_k\widetilde y_k^\top}{s_k^\top\widetilde y_k}.
\]
Different specified rules for \(\theta_k\) and positive thresholds \(\mu_k\) define members of this generic damping class. Every admitted member satisfies \(B_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^\top\succ0\) and \(B_{k+1}s_k=\widetilde y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-blending damping rule combines the measured and predicted gradient displacements, requires positive safeguarded curvature, and then applies BFGS to obtain a positive-definite matrix satisfying the modified secant equation.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B=B^T\succ0\), \(s\ne0\), and \(y\in\mathbb R^n\). Let \(z(B,s,y)\) be a reference curvature vector and let \(\theta(B,s,y)\in[0,1]\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An alternative BFGS damping family is specified by maps \(z\) and \(\theta\) and forms \[\widetilde y=\theta(B,s,y)y+[1-\theta(B,s,y)]z(B,s,y),\] subject to a uniform admissibility condition \[s^T\widetilde y\ge\mu(B,s)>0.\] Its Hessian update is \[B_+=B-\frac{Bss^TB}{s^TBs}+\frac{\widetilde y\widetilde y^T}{s^T\widetilde y}.\] To be distinct from the Powell family, the reference map, threshold, or mixing law is not identically \(z=Bs\) with the classical piecewise Powell coefficient.

The sole structural requirement is a strictly positive quantitative curvature bound, after which standard BFGS is applied to the modified pair.

Modified Secant-Pair Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasi-Newton methods that replace the measured secant pair before applying an update formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. For \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), a modified secant-pair method constructs \((\widetilde s_k,\widetilde y_k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\), usually with \(\widetilde s_k=s_k\), from the iteration data and applies a quasi-Newton update satisfying
\[
B_{k+1}\widetilde s_k=\widetilde y_k.
\]
In a positive-definite BFGS implementation, assume \(B_k=B_k^\top\succ0\), \(\widetilde s_k\ne0\), and \(\widetilde s_k^\top\widetilde y_k>0\). Then
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_k\widetilde s_k\widetilde s_k^\top B_k}{\widetilde s_k^\top B_k\widetilde s_k}+\frac{\widetilde y_k\widetilde y_k^\top}{\widetilde s_k^\top\widetilde y_k},
\]
which is positive definite and satisfies the modified secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified secant-pair method alters the observed step or gradient difference before applying an update. With positive modified curvature, the BFGS formula produces a positive-definite matrix satisfying the modified secant equation.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde s_k\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(\widetilde y_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\widetilde s_k^\top\widetilde y_k>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Newton methods based on transformed secant pairs
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(B_k\) be a Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional class encompassing damping, regularization, and corrected gradient differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A modified secant-pair method specifies a transformation \[M_k:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n,\qquad (\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k)=M_k(s_k,y_k,B_k),\] and an update map \(\mathcal U\) such that \[B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k),\qquad B_{k+1}\widehat s_k=\widehat y_k.\] The transformation is nontrivial when \((\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k)\ne(s_k,y_k)\), and it must place the pair in the domain of \(\mathcal U\), for example by enforcing \(\widehat s_k^T\widehat y_k>0\) for positive-definite BFGS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified secant-pair method transforms the actual displacement and gradient difference before applying a quasi-Newton formula. The resulting matrix satisfies the secant equation for the transformed pair, not necessarily for the raw observations, and the transformation must enforce all domain conditions of the selected update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}\widehat s_k=\widehat y_k\), with \((\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k)\) admissible for \(\mathcal U\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(\widehat s_k=s_k\), the method is a modified gradient-difference method.
When \(\widehat y_k=y_k\), it is a modified-displacement secant method.
special_cases_latex: Damped BFGS uses \(\widehat s_k=s_k\) and \(\widehat y_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k\).
Regularized secant pairs may use \(\widehat y_k=y_k+\tau_ks_k\) with \(\tau_k\ge0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Secant consistency is transferred from raw data to the chosen corrected data.
A curvature-enforcing transformation makes positive-definite BFGS algebraically admissible.
boundary_notes: A skipped update with \(B_{k+1}=B_k\) is not generally a modified secant update unless the retained matrix satisfies the modified secant equation.
No inspected source states this exact abstract class as a canonical named definition.

Source support is needed for the class breadth and canonical terminology.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cautious curvature-based admission and skip policy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k=B_k^T\), let \((s_k,y_k)\) be a candidate secant pair with \(s_k\ne0\), and let \(\mathcal U\) be a quasi-Newton update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic update-skipping rule; the threshold may be absolute, Euclidean-relative, or metric-relative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cautious update admission policy chooses a nonnegative threshold functional \(\tau_k=\tau(B_k,s_k,y_k)\) and defines \[A_k=\mathbf 1\{s_k^Ty_k>\tau_k\}.\] The metric transition is \[B_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k),&A_k=1,\\B_k,&A_k=0.\end{cases}\] For positive-definite BFGS, a typical scale-aware policy takes \(\tau_k=\varepsilon\|s_k\|\|y_k\|\) or requires \(s_k^Ty_k\ge\delta s_k^TB_ks_k\), with \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\). For SR1, cautious admission instead tests the update denominator \[|s_k^T(y_k-B_ks_k)|\ge r\|s_k\|\,\|y_k-B_ks_k\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cautious policy evaluates a quantitative reliability test before updating. If the test passes, it applies the chosen quasi-Newton formula; otherwise it keeps the current metric. BFGS policies test positive curvature, whereas SR1 policies test whether the rank-one denominator is sufficiently large relative to its vector factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}\) equals the admitted quasi-Newton update or exactly \(B_k\) according to the stated predicate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The policy is a two-state transition with states \(\mathrm{accept}\) and \(\mathrm{retain}\).
special_cases_latex: Dennis–Schnabel skip BFGS when \(s_k^Ty_k\le\sqrt{\mathrm{macheps}}\|s_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2\).
The standard safeguarded SR1 rule uses a small \(r\in(0,1)\), commonly about \(10^{-8}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Rejected pairs cannot create small denominators in the guarded update formula.
Retention preserves every structural property already possessed by \(B_k\).
boundary_notes: Frequent BFGS skipping can prevent the metric from capturing curvature and is not equivalent to damping.
The appropriate predicate depends on the update family.

children.title: Cautious Update Admission
children.top_down_role: Conservative quality regimes for admitting curvature updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Cautious Update Admission
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-threshold gate for admitting a positive-definite quasi-Newton update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a secant pair \((s_k,y_k)\) with \(s_k\ne0\), a cautious admission policy with threshold \(\varepsilon_k>0\) admits the quasi-Newton update only if
\[
\frac{s_k^\top y_k}{\lVert s_k\rVert^2}\ge\varepsilon_k.
\]
For an admitted BFGS update this implies \(s_k^\top y_k>0\), so a positive-definite \(B_k\) produces a positive-definite \(B_{k+1}\). The threshold may be fixed or iteration-dependent, but its specification is part of the policy; failure of the test invokes the policy's skip or modification branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An update is admitted only when measured curvature per squared step length exceeds a positive threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admission occurs exactly when \(s_k^\top y_k\ge\varepsilon_k\lVert s_k\rVert^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated normalized-curvature gate is internally consistent and implies positive BFGS curvature when admitted. Because cautious-update policies use multiple threshold variants, an authoritative source with an exact locator is required to support this particular policy and its scope.

children.title: Skipped-Update Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where unreliable curvature information is excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Skipped-Update Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguard branch that retains the current metric when an admission or denominator test fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A_k\) denote the update-admission predicate evaluated from \(B_k,s_k,y_k\). A skipped-update regime uses
\[
B_{k+1}=\begin{cases}
\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k),&\mathcal A_k\text{ is true},\\
B_k,&\mathcal A_k\text{ is false},
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\mathcal U\) is the selected quasi-Newton update. The search direction at the next iteration is computed from the retained or updated matrix. If \(B_k\succ0\) and every admitted update preserves positive definiteness, then skipping also preserves positive definiteness, although no new secant equation is imposed on a skipped iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a safeguard fails, the method keeps its current metric; definiteness is retained, but the newest secant information is not incorporated.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_k\) is a specified Boolean admission test.
\(\mathcal U\) preserves positive definiteness whenever admitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg\mathcal A_k\Rightarrow B_{k+1}=B_k\); hence \(B_k\succ0\Rightarrow B_{k+1}\succ0\) on a skipped iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branch rule correctly describes update skipping, including preservation of positive definiteness and loss of the new secant relation. Its algorithm role fits the leaf, but no admissible source or standard-field rationale is provided.

children.title: Repeated-Skipping Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of useful metric evolution after persistent update omission.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Skipping Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent safeguard rejection preserves stability but can prevent quasi-Newton curvature learning and superlinear behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider cautious admission with a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) and skipping whenever \(s_k^\top y_k<\varepsilon\lVert s_k\rVert^2\). If this failure occurs for every \(k\ge K\), then
\[
B_k=B_K\qquad(k\ge K),
\]
so no later secant pair is incorporated. Consequently, positive definiteness of \(B_K\) may persist, but neither satisfaction of the later secant equations nor a Dennis–Moré approximation condition follows from the update mechanism. Concretely, for \(f(x)=-\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert^2\), every nonzero step has \(y_k=-s_k\), so the cautious test fails for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the safeguard rejects every later pair, the metric freezes; stability may remain, but secant learning and superlinear-convergence conditions can fail.
assumptions_latex: \(s_k^\top y_k<\varepsilon\lVert s_k\rVert^2\) for all \(k\ge K\), with \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=B_K\) for all \(k\ge K\), and later secant equations need not hold.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Persistent rejection directly implies that the metric freezes, and the concave quadratic example indeed forces rejection under the stated test. An external locator is required for the claimed failure-boundary interpretation involving Dennis–Moré behavior; the example should also remain explicitly identified as nonconvex and unbounded below.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic trust-region model with a quasi-Newton Hessian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained trust-region model; \(B_k\) may be positive definite or indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region quasi-Newton model at \(x_k\) is \[m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\frac12p^TB_kp,\] where \(B_k\) is generated or maintained by a quasi-Newton update. A trial step is an exact or approximate solution of \[\min_{\|p\|\le\Delta_k}m_k(p).\] With predicted reduction \(\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\) and actual reduction \(\operatorname{ared}_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)\), define \[\rho_k=\frac{\operatorname{ared}_k}{\operatorname{pred}_k}\] whenever \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\). Acceptance of \(x_k+p_k\) and adjustment of \(\Delta_k\) are functions of \(\rho_k\); after gradient information is available, \(B_k\) is updated from an appropriate secant pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model matches the objective value and gradient at the current point and uses a quasi-Newton matrix for its quadratic term. Its step minimizes the model only inside a radius. The ratio of actual to predicted reduction governs whether the trial point is accepted and whether the radius expands, stays fixed, or contracts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\) solves or approximates the displayed constrained quadratic problem, and model quality is measured by \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constant \(f(x_k)\) may be omitted from the subproblem without changing its minimizers.
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\) and the unconstrained minimizer lies inside the ball, the trust-region step is \(-B_k^{-1}g_k\).
If \(B_k\) is indefinite, the bounded trust region still gives a meaningful quadratic subproblem.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method can use indefinite curvature without requiring a descent direction for an unrestricted line search.
Shrinking \(\Delta_k\) restricts the model to a more local neighborhood.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require exact solution of the trust-region subproblem.
Acceptance and radius thresholds vary across algorithms and are not fixed by the model definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region SR1 Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region quadratic model coupled to a safeguarded symmetric-rank-one Hessian update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), symmetric \(B_k\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\), compute an approximate solution \(p_k\) of
\[
\min_{\lVert p\rVert\le\Delta_k} m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp.
\]
Accept or reject \(x_k+p_k\) using the ratio of actual to predicted reduction and update \(\Delta_k\) accordingly. For an accepted displacement \(s_k\), set \(y_k=\nabla f(x_k+s_k)-g_k\) and \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). If
\[
|r_k^\top s_k|\ge\rho\lVert r_k\rVert\lVert s_k\rVert
\]
with \(\rho\in(0,1)\), use \(B_{k+1}=B_k+r_kr_k^\top/(r_k^\top s_k)\); otherwise skip the SR1 update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region subproblem controls possibly indefinite SR1 models, while a denominator test skips numerically unstable rank-one updates.
assumptions_latex: The SR1 formula is used only when its denominator safeguard holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted SR1 update is symmetric and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\); otherwise \(B_{k+1}=B_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded SR1 trust-region model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(B_k=B_k^T\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense Hessian-form SR1 embedded in a trust-region globalization; indefinite matrices are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region SR1 model uses \[m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\frac12p^TB_kp,\qquad \|p\|\le\Delta_k.\] After computing a trial displacement \(s_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_k+s_k)-g_k\), put \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). For a fixed \(r\in(0,1)\), update by \[B_{k+1}=\begin{cases}B_k+\dfrac{r_kr_k^T}{r_k^Ts_k},&|r_k^Ts_k|\ge r\|r_k\|\|s_k\|,\\B_k,&|r_k^Ts_k|<r\|r_k\|\|s_k\|.\end{cases}\] Trial-point acceptance and radius adjustment use the ratio of actual to predicted reduction of \(m_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SR1 model minimizes a possibly indefinite quadratic inside a radius. It updates the model matrix by the symmetric rank-one formula only when the denominator is sufficiently large relative to the norms of its factors; otherwise it retains the current matrix. The trust-region reduction ratio globalizes the trial step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model matrix remains symmetric, and every admitted update satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\); rejected updates give \(B_{k+1}=B_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The admission test bounds the cosine magnitude between \(r_k\) and \(s_k\) below by \(r\) when both vectors are nonzero.
special_cases_latex: A typical numerical choice is \(r=10^{-8}\).
If \(r_k=0\), the secant equation already holds and retaining \(B_k\) is appropriate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The denominator cannot be small relative to the rank-one numerator factors on an admitted update.
Indefiniteness of \(B_k\) is allowed and can represent negative curvature.
boundary_notes: SR1 does not generally preserve positive definiteness.
If the update is skipped, the new matrix need not satisfy the latest raw secant equation.
The symbol \(r\) for the threshold is distinct from the residual vector \(r_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and predicted reduction for a positive-definite quadratic trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an iterate \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(x_k\), define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and let \(\Delta_k>0\). Define
\[
m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp,
\qquad
p_k=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\lVert p\rVert_2\leq\Delta_k}m_k(p).
\]
Then \(p_k\) exists and is unique, and \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\geq0\). If \(g_k\neq0\), then \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quasi-Newton quadratic model over a positive-radius Euclidean trust region, the minimizing step exists uniquely and gives nonnegative predicted reduction; the reduction is strictly positive when the current gradient is nonzero.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\) exists uniquely and \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\geq0\), with strict inequality if \(g_k\neq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifecycle of a safeguarded variable metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) be the admissible metric set, such as \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\) for a line-search method or a bounded subset of \(\mathbb S^n\) for a trust-region method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed state-machine formalization of metric initialization, updating, degradation detection, recovery, and retirement; no exact authoritative definition was located.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A metric recovery lifecycle is a state sequence \((B_k,z_k)\in\mathcal D\times\{\mathrm{active},\mathrm{degraded},\mathrm{reset}\}\) with an initialization map \(B_0=I_0(x_0)\in\mathcal D\), a candidate update \(\widetilde B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\), a health predicate \(h_k=H(\widetilde B_{k+1},s_k,y_k)\), and transition \[(B_{k+1},z_{k+1})=\begin{cases}(\widetilde B_{k+1},\mathrm{active}),&h_k=1,\\(\mathcal R(B_k,s_k,y_k),\mathrm{reset}),&h_k=0,\end{cases}\] where \(\mathcal R(B_k,s_k,y_k)\in\mathcal D\). The health predicate may test curvature, definiteness, conditioning, boundedness, or update-denominator reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifecycle treats the quasi-Newton matrix as guarded state. It initializes an admissible metric, proposes updates while the metric is active, declares degradation when a health test fails, and invokes a recovery map that returns the matrix to the admissible set before later updates resume.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k\in\mathcal D\) for every lifecycle state, and every failed health test triggers the declared recovery transition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The lifecycle is a finite-state machine whose continuous state is the metric matrix and whose discrete state records metric health.
special_cases_latex: Retention recovery takes \(\mathcal R(B_k,s_k,y_k)=B_k\).
Identity or scaled-identity recovery takes \(\mathcal R=\gamma_kI\) with \(\gamma_k>0\).
Regularization recovery takes \(\mathcal R=B_k+\lambda_kI\) with \(\lambda_k\) chosen to restore admissibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: An invalid candidate metric is never passed directly to a mechanism requiring membership in \(\mathcal D\).
Repeated failures can be represented without leaving the admissible state space.
boundary_notes: The exact discrete states and health tests are implementation- and method-dependent.
A skipped update is one recovery transition, not the entire lifecycle.
No inspected source states this exact named state-machine object.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: initialization, update skipping, regularization, and resetting are standard metric-management actions, but the exact lifecycle/state-machine definition is not supported by an inspected source.
A precise source is required for the canonical name, state set, and transition contract.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled-Identity Metric Reset
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k,H_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be mutually inverse Hessian and inverse-Hessian approximations, and let \(\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma\) satisfy \(0<\underline\gamma\leq\overline\gamma<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic quasi-Newton methods; the definition concerns replacement of a metric before subsequent secant updates, not merely multiplication of an existing metric by a scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scaled-identity inverse-metric reset is the map \(\mathcal R_\gamma^H(H_k)=\gamma I\), where \(\gamma\in[\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma]\). Its direct-metric counterpart is \(\mathcal R_\gamma^B(B_k)=\gamma^{-1}I\). A scaled-identity reset family is \(\mathfrak R=\{\mathcal R_\gamma^H:\gamma\in[\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma]\}\), together with a rule selecting \(\gamma\), commonly \(\gamma_k=(s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})/(y_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})\) when \(s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}>0\), optionally projected onto \([\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma]\). After resetting, any retained secant pairs are applied afresh to \(H_k^0=\gamma_k I\); a complete reset applies no retained pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family replaces the current positive-definite inverse-Hessian approximation by a positive scalar multiple \(\gamma I\), equivalently replacing the Hessian approximation by \(\gamma^{-1}I\). The scalar may be chosen from the most recent curvature pair and bounded within a prescribed positive interval. Subsequent quasi-Newton corrections are then applied to this new base matrix; discarding all pairs gives a complete reset.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Resetting \(H_k\) to \(\gamma I\) is equivalent to resetting \(B_k\) to \(\delta I\) with \(\delta=1/\gamma\).
A memoryless BFGS reset is the special case \(H_k^0=I\) followed by one BFGS correction from the latest pair.
special_cases_latex: The unscaled identity reset uses \(\gamma=1\).
The curvature-scaled L-BFGS base uses \(\gamma_k=(s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})/(y_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every reset matrix has condition number \(\kappa_2(\gamma I)=1\).
Positive lower and upper bounds on \(\gamma_k\) give uniform spectral bounds \(\underline\gamma I\preceq H_k^0\preceq\overline\gamma I\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe when a reset is triggered.
If \(s^Ty\leq0\), the displayed curvature scaling is not a positive reset parameter and requires a separate fallback rule.

notation.meaning: Real symmetric positive-definite matrices of order n.

children.title: Identity Metric Resets
children.top_down_role: Metric recovery through an unscaled identity initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Identity Metric Resets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard restart of an inverse-Hessian quasi-Newton metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an iteration index \(k\) at which a restart has been requested, discard every stored curvature pair and replace the inverse-Hessian approximation by
\[
H_k\leftarrow I_n.
\]
Compute the next metric step from \(p_k=-H_kg_k=-g_k\), subject to any separate line-search or trust-region globalization rule. Thus the first post-reset direction is the steepest-descent direction in the Euclidean metric; subsequent accepted curvature pairs may again update \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identity reset deletes curvature history, sets the inverse metric to the identity, and makes the next unglobalized direction steepest descent.
assumptions_latex: The implementation uses an inverse-Hessian metric \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_k=I_n\) and the unglobalized post-reset direction is \(p_k=-g_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: identity restart is a standard quasi-Newton recovery operation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Identity Metric Resets leaf and is mathematically coherent under the inverse-Hessian convention, but no inspectable source supports the combined policy of clearing all history, setting the metric to identity, and describing subsequent updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled-Identity Metric Resets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scalar restart of an inverse-Hessian metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a restart request and a chosen scalar \(\gamma_k>0\), discard the stored quasi-Newton history and set
\[
H_k\leftarrow\gamma_k I_n.
\]
The resulting unglobalized direction is \(p_k=-\gamma_k g_k\). Because every eigenvalue of \(H_k\) equals \(\gamma_k\), the reset metric is symmetric positive definite and has spectral condition number one. Later accepted curvature pairs may update this initial metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled-identity reset clears history and replaces the inverse metric by a positive multiple of the identity, producing a well-conditioned descent metric.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive scaled-identity initialization is standard in quasi-Newton methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Scaled-Identity Metric Resets leaf, and the spectral claims follow from a positive scalar identity metric. An exact source is still required for the reset operation and history-clearing policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Reset Scale Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded secant-based scale for inverse-Hessian resets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a curvature pair \((s,y)\) with \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), bounds \(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq\gamma_{\max}\), and the inverse-Hessian convention, form
\[
\widehat\gamma=\frac{s^{\mathsf T}y}{y^{\mathsf T}y},
\qquad
\gamma=\min\{\gamma_{\max},\max\{\gamma_{\min},\widehat\gamma\}\}.
\]
Reset \(H\leftarrow\gamma I_n\). If no admissible pair exists, use a prescribed fallback \(\gamma_{\rm def}\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\). The clipping guarantees a positive, uniformly bounded reset metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the inverse-metric reset scale from the latest positive-curvature pair, clip it to prescribed bounds, and use a bounded fallback when no valid pair exists.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed secant scale is the standard inverse-Hessian scalar initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-Hessian scaling formula and clipping are plausible, and algorithm is the correct role for this leaf. However, the choice of newest admissible pair, clipping bounds, and fallback are implementation policies requiring an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning-Triggered Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral trigger for restarting an unreliable positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k=H_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) be the current inverse-Hessian metric and choose safeguards \(0<\underline h<\overline h<\infty\) and \(\kappa_{\max}\geq1\). A conditioning-triggered restart is requested exactly when
\[
\lambda_{\min}(H_k)<\underline h,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\lambda_{\max}(H_k)>\overline h,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\kappa_2(H_k)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(H_k)}{\lambda_{\min}(H_k)}>\kappa_{\max}.
\]
An implementation may replace the exact eigenvalues by certified lower and upper spectral estimates while preserving the same predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart when the inverse metric has an eigenvalue outside prescribed bounds or its spectral condition number exceeds the allowed threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restart predicate is the displayed disjunction of lower-spectrum, upper-spectrum, and condition-number violations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral thresholds give a checkable restart safeguard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate content kind, but the assertion that restart occurs exactly under this three-part spectral predicate is an implementation-specific policy. A source must establish the predicate, thresholds, and permitted use of spectral estimates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning-Triggered Quasi-Newton Restart
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be a direct or inverse variable metric, let \(\widehat\kappa_k\geq1\) estimate \(\kappa_2(M_k)\), and fix a threshold \(\kappa_{\max}>1\) and a reset map \(\mathcal R_k\) with values in \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic safeguard policy. The condition estimate may be computed exactly or from factors, compact matrices, or spectral bounds, but that estimator is external to the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conditioning-triggered restart is the state transition \(M_k^+=\mathcal R_k(M_k)\) if \(\widehat\kappa_k>\kappa_{\max}\), and \(M_k^+=M_k\) otherwise. The restart state also replaces the active secant history \(\mathcal P_k\) by a prescribed retained subset \(\mathcal K_k\subseteq\mathcal P_k\), with a complete restart defined by \(\mathcal K_k=\varnothing\). A spectrally triggered variant restarts whenever \(\widehat\lambda_{\min}(M_k)<\mu_{\min}\) or \(\widehat\lambda_{\max}(M_k)>\mu_{\max}\), where \(0<\mu_{\min}<\mu_{\max}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy monitors an estimate of the variable metric's condition number or extreme eigenvalues. If the estimate violates a prescribed admissible range, it replaces the metric by a positive-definite reset metric and deletes all or a specified portion of the stored secant history. Otherwise the metric and history are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M_k,\mathcal P_k)\mapsto(M_k^+,\mathcal K_k)\), with restart exactly on the declared conditioning event and \(M_k^+\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a positive-definite metric, the exact trigger \(\kappa_2(M_k)>\kappa_{\max}\) is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\max}(M_k)/\lambda_{\min}(M_k)>\kappa_{\max}\).
special_cases_latex: A scaled-identity complete restart takes \(\mathcal R_k(M)=\gamma_kI\) and \(\mathcal K_k=\varnothing\).
A partial restart retains only pairs passing a separately specified curvature or age test.
