knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure-Aware Limited-Memory Secant Representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(m\ll n\), and let \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\). Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) encode an exploitable matrix structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale finite-dimensional quasi-Newton models represented implicitly from a bounded history while preserving either low-storage form or a declared structural class such as sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structure-aware limited-memory update at iteration \(k\) is a metric \(M_k\in\mathcal S\) represented by a structured base \(M_k^0\in\mathcal S\) and at most \(m\) recent correction pairs \(\mathcal P_k=\{(s_i,y_i):i\in I_k\}\), \(|I_k|\leq m\), through an update composition \(M_k=\mathcal U_{i_r}\circ\cdots\circ\mathcal U_{i_1}(M_k^0)\), or an algebraically equivalent compact form \(M_k=M_k^0+U_kC_kU_k^T\) with \(U_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), \(q=O(m)\). Structure awareness requires either \(M_k\in\mathcal S\) explicitly or that products, solves, and projections involving \(M_k\) use the structure of \(M_k^0\) and the narrow correction matrix without forming a dense \(n\times n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The update stores a structured base metric and only a bounded number of curvature pairs. These data define the current quasi-Newton matrix through repeated secant corrections or an equivalent base-plus-low-rank representation. The method is structure-aware when the resulting matrix preserves a prescribed class, or when all required operations exploit the base structure and narrow correction factors without dense storage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k=M_k^0+U_kC_kU_k^T\) with \(M_k^0\in\mathcal S\), \(|I_k|\leq m\), and correction width \(q=O(m)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The representation may be stored as curvature pairs, as compact outer-product matrices, or as update factors, provided these forms define the same linear operator.
special_cases_latex: L-BFGS uses BFGS corrections and normally a scaled-identity base.
Sparse secant updating takes \(\mathcal S\) to be matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern.
immediate_consequences_latex: Pair storage is \(O(mn)\), rather than \(O(n^2)\), when the base has an economical representation.
The compact correction acts only through a subspace of dimension at most \(q=O(m)\).
boundary_notes: Not every structured update simultaneously preserves positive definiteness, exact secant equations, and a prescribed sparsity pattern.
The definition excludes schemes whose retained history grows without a fixed memory bound.

notation.meaning: Declared structural class of symmetric matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limited-Memory BFGS Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and memory \(m\geq1\), and define \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic unconstrained line-search L-BFGS using inverse-Hessian approximations and correction pairs satisfying positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(I_k=\{\max(0,k-m),\ldots,k-1\}\), choose \(H_k^0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), and obtain \(H_k\) by applying inverse-BFGS corrections in chronological order to \(H_k^0\): \(H\leftarrow V_i^THV_i+\rho_is_is_i^T\), where \(\rho_i=(y_i^Ts_i)^{-1}\) and \(V_i=I-\rho_iy_is_i^T\), for \(i\in I_k\). The L-BFGS direction is \(p_k=-H_k\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies the Wolfe conditions. The new pair \((s_k,y_k)\) is stored and the oldest pair is discarded when the memory bound would be exceeded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: L-BFGS builds an implicit inverse-Hessian approximation by applying BFGS corrections from at most the \(m\) most recent step and gradient-difference pairs to a positive-definite base matrix. It multiplies the gradient by this implicit operator to obtain the search direction, chooses a Wolfe line-search step, stores the new pair, and removes the oldest pair when necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k=-H_k\nabla f(x_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and the active history contains at most \(m\) pairs.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The product \(H_k\nabla f(x_k)\) may be evaluated by the two-loop recursion without forming \(H_k\).
special_cases_latex: For \(m=1\) and \(H_k^0=I\), the method is memoryless BFGS.
Before the history fills, choosing a fixed \(H_k^0=H_0\) reproduces the corresponding initial full-memory BFGS corrections.
immediate_consequences_latex: If every retained pair has \(s_i^Ty_i>0\), inverse-BFGS corrections preserve positive definiteness.
The pair representation requires \(O(mn)\) storage.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover bound constraints or trust-region L-BFGS variants.
Pairs failing positive curvature require skipping, damping, or another safeguard not fixed here.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unrolled Direct Representation of Limited-Memory BFGS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a limited-memory direct BFGS matrix as a base matrix plus stored rank-two corrections and records its qualitative cost disadvantage relative to compact representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the direct BFGS update, define
\[
a_i=\frac{B_i s_i}{(s_i^T B_i s_i)^{1/2}},\qquad b_i=\frac{y_i}{(y_i^T s_i)^{1/2}}.
\]
Then
\[
B_{i+1}=B_i-a_i a_i^T+b_i b_i^T,
\]
and retaining the most recent \(m\) curvature pairs gives the unrolled limited-memory representation
\[
B_k=B_k^0+\sum_{i=k-m}^{k-1}\bigl(b_i b_i^T-a_i a_i^T\bigr).
\]
Recovering the \((a_i,b_i)\) pairs from stored \((s_i,y_i)\) pairs and applying this representation is considerably more expensive than the compact-representation approach.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each direct BFGS update is the previous matrix minus one rank-one term and plus another. Unrolling the most recent m updates expresses the limited-memory matrix as a base matrix plus those rank-two corrections. Implementing limited-memory BFGS this way is considerably more expensive than using its compact representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k=B_k^0+\sum_{i=k-m}^{k-1}(b_i b_i^T-a_i a_i^T),\quad a_i=\frac{B_i s_i}{(s_i^T B_i s_i)^{1/2}},\quad b_i=\frac{y_i}{(y_i^T s_i)^{1/2}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Procedure for Unrolling the BFGS Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequentially recovers the normalized rank-one factors of the retained direct BFGS updates from stored curvature pairs and a base matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=k-m,k-m+1,\ldots,k-1\), perform sequentially
\[
b_i\leftarrow \frac{y_i}{(y_i^T s_i)^{1/2}},
\]
\[
\widetilde a_i\leftarrow B_k^0s_i+\sum_{j=k-m}^{i-1}\left[(b_j^Ts_i)b_j-(a_j^Ts_i)a_j\right],
\]
\[
a_i\leftarrow \frac{\widetilde a_i}{(s_i^T\widetilde a_i)^{1/2}}.
\]
Here \(\widetilde a_i\) denotes the intermediate value assigned to \(a_i\) before normalization in the source procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process the retained curvature pairs from oldest to newest. Normalize each y-vector to obtain b_i. Apply the base matrix and all previously recovered corrections to s_i to obtain an intermediate vector, then normalize that vector to obtain a_i.

knowledge_statements.title: L-BFGS Curvature-Pair Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered limited-memory storage used by inverse L-BFGS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterates \(x_i\) and gradients \(g_i=\nabla f(x_i)\), define
\[
s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i,
\qquad y_i=g_{i+1}-g_i,
\qquad \rho_i=(y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i)^{-1}.
\]
With memory limit \(m\geq1\), the L-BFGS history at iteration \(k\) is the chronologically ordered set of at most the \(m\) most recent accepted pairs \((s_i,y_i)\) satisfying \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i>0\). Rejected pairs are not stored, and each stored pair carries its scalar \(\rho_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: L-BFGS stores at most the most recent m accepted displacement and gradient-difference pairs, each having positive curvature and an associated reciprocal curvature scalar.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at the sampled iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The history contains at most \(m\) chronological pairs with \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i>0\) and \(\rho_i>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: chronological positive-curvature pair storage is standard L-BFGS structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the curvature-pair storage leaf, but requiring every stored pair to satisfy strict positive curvature and excluding all rejected pairs describes a particular acceptance policy. An L-BFGS-specific source and locator are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded L-BFGS Curvature History
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For iterates \(x_i\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\), and fix a memory capacity \(m\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage object for deterministic L-BFGS; only accepted curvature pairs are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The L-BFGS curvature-pair store at iteration \(k\) is the ordered sequence \(\mathcal P_k=((s_i,y_i))_{i\in I_k}\), where \(I_k=\{\max(0,k-m),\ldots,k-1\}\) after excluding rejected pairs, the order is chronological, and every stored pair satisfies \(y_i^Ts_i>0\). Equivalently, it is represented by matrices \(S_k=[s_i]_{i\in I_k}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\), \(Y_k=[y_i]_{i\in I_k}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\), with \(r_k\leq m\), together with \(\rho_i=(y_i^Ts_i)^{-1}\). On acceptance of \((s_k,y_k)\), it is appended and the oldest pair is deleted if the capacity would exceed \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The storage object is a chronological queue of at most \(m\) accepted step and gradient-difference pairs. Each pair has positive curvature. It can equivalently be stored as two narrow matrices whose corresponding columns are the step and gradient difference, plus reciprocal curvature scalars. Adding a new accepted pair evicts the oldest pair when the queue is full.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal P_k|=r_k\leq m\), \(S_k,Y_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\), and \(\rho_i>0\) for every stored pair.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The ordered queue \(\mathcal P_k\) and the column matrices \((S_k,Y_k)\) encode the same history when column order is preserved.
special_cases_latex: If \(k<m\) and no pair is rejected, \(r_k=k\).
For \(m=1\), only the most recent accepted curvature pair is stored.
immediate_consequences_latex: The two vector arrays use at most \(2mn\) scalar entries, apart from metadata and curvature scalars.
Chronological ordering supplies the reverse and forward traversals required by the two-loop recursion.
boundary_notes: Storage alone does not specify the base matrix or the search direction.
A pair with nonpositive curvature cannot be used in the positive-definite inverse-BFGS formula without modification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recent-curvature storage principle of L-BFGS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit curvature-pair storage and history truncation in Euclidean L-BFGS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a dense \(n\times n\) inverse-Hessian approximation is impractical to store or manipulate, L-BFGS represents the approximation implicitly using a small collection of length-\(n\) curvature-pair vectors. Only information from the most recent iterations is retained, and older pairs are discarded as the history advances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: L-BFGS avoids storing a dense inverse-Hessian approximation by retaining a short history of curvature pairs. New pairs replace older ones as the iteration proceeds.
assumptions_latex: The problem has \(n\) variables and successive iterates and gradients are available.

knowledge_statements.title: L-BFGS Two-Loop Recursion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free application of the inverse L-BFGS approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(g_k\), stored pairs indexed from oldest \(j=1\) to newest \(j=\ell\), and \(H_k^{(0)}\succ0\), initialize \(q\leftarrow g_k\). For \(j=\ell,\ldots,1\), set
\[
\alpha_j\leftarrow\rho_j s_j^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad q\leftarrow q-\alpha_jy_j.
\]
Set \(r\leftarrow H_k^{(0)}q\). For \(j=1,ldots,\ell\), set
\[
\beta_j\leftarrow\rho_jy_j^{\mathsf T}r,
\qquad r\leftarrow r+s_j(\alpha_j-\beta_j).
\]
Output \(p_k=-r\). In exact arithmetic, \(r=H_kg_k\), where \(H_k\) is generated by the corresponding inverse-BFGS updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two backward-and-forward passes through stored curvature pairs compute the inverse L-BFGS product with the gradient without forming a dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(p_k=-H_kg_k\) in exact arithmetic.

notation.meaning: initial inverse metric for the stored update sequence

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: displayed recursion is the canonical inverse L-BFGS two-loop calculation

An authoritative locator is also needed to verify indexing, ordering, and equivalence to the chronological inverse-BFGS updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: L-BFGS Two-Loop Operator Evaluation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(((s_i,y_i))_{i=a}^{k-1}\) be \(r\leq m\) ordered pairs with \(y_i^Ts_i>0\), set \(\rho_i=(y_i^Ts_i)^{-1}\), and let \(H_k^0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact evaluation of the inverse L-BFGS operator defined by the retained pairs; the input may be the current gradient or any vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The L-BFGS two-loop recursion maps \(v\) to \(H_kv\) as follows. Set \(q=v\). For \(i=k-1,k-2,\ldots,a\), set \(\alpha_i=\rho_is_i^Tq\) and \(q\leftarrow q-\alpha_iy_i\). Set \(r=H_k^0q\). For \(i=a,a+1,\ldots,k-1\), set \(\beta_i=\rho_iy_i^Tr\) and \(r\leftarrow r+s_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i)\). The returned vector is defined to be \(H_kv=r\), where \(H_k\) is the inverse-BFGS matrix obtained by applying those pairs chronologically to \(H_k^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the input vector, the first loop traverses stored pairs from newest to oldest and removes gradient-difference components while saving coefficients. The base inverse metric is then applied once. The second loop traverses pairs from oldest to newest and adds step components. The returned vector is exactly the action of the implicit L-BFGS inverse metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r=H_kv\) after the reverse loop, one application of \(H_k^0\), and the forward loop.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(v=\nabla f(x_k)\), the L-BFGS search direction is \(p_k=-r\).
special_cases_latex: With no stored pair, the recursion returns \(H_k^0v\).
With \(H_k^0=\gamma_kI\), the middle operation is a scalar-vector multiplication.
immediate_consequences_latex: Excluding the base multiplication, \(r\) stored pairs require \(4rn\) scalar multiplications in the standard count.
The dense matrix \(H_k\) need not be formed or stored.
boundary_notes: The loop order is essential because successive BFGS corrections generally do not commute.
The recursion assumes nonzero positive pair curvatures so that every \(\rho_i\) is defined.

notation.meaning: Work vectors in the two loops.
Pair coefficients generated by the reverse and forward passes.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact L-BFGS Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-rank block representation of sequential inverse-BFGS updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_\ell]\), \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_\ell]\), \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i)\), and let \(R\) be upper triangular with \(R_{ij}=s_i^{\mathsf T}y_j\) for \(i\leq j\). For \(H_0=H_0^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and positive pair curvatures,
\[
H_\ell=H_0+[S,H_0Y]
\begin{bmatrix}
R^{-\mathsf T}(D+Y^{\mathsf T}H_0Y)R^{-1}&-R^{-\mathsf T}\\
-R^{-1}&0
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}S^{\mathsf T}\\Y^{\mathsf T}H_0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
This equals the matrix obtained by applying the \(\ell\) inverse-BFGS updates chronologically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse L-BFGS matrix equals its initial metric plus a rank-at-most-2ℓ correction assembled from stored step and gradient-difference blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed compact matrix equals the chronological inverse-BFGS update sequence and differs from \(H_0\) by rank at most \(2\ell\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the block formula is the standard compact inverse-BFGS representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Direct L-BFGS Matrix
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_r]\), \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_r]\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), \(r\leq m\), with \(s_i^Ty_i>0\), and let the base matrix be \(B^0=\delta I\), \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact outer-product representation of the direct BFGS Hessian approximation generated by a bounded ordered history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1^Ty_1,\ldots,s_r^Ty_r)\) and the strictly lower-triangular matrix \(L\) by \(L_{ij}=s_i^Ty_j\) for \(i>j\) and \(L_{ij}=0\) otherwise. The compact L-BFGS direct matrix is \(B=\delta I-[\delta S\;Y]\begin{bmatrix}\delta S^TS&L\\L^T&-D\end{bmatrix}^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}\delta S^T\\Y^T\end{bmatrix}\). It is the matrix obtained by applying the direct BFGS formula chronologically to \(B^0\) using the stored pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct L-BFGS Hessian approximation equals a scaled identity minus an outer-product correction formed from the narrow step and gradient-difference matrices. All coupling among stored pairs is contained in a small \(2r\)-by-\(2r\) matrix built from their inner products. This representation defines the same operator as the chronological BFGS updates without storing a dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\delta I-\Psi M^{-1}\Psi^T\), where \(\Psi=[\delta S\;Y]\in\mathbb R^{n\times2r}\) and \(M=\begin{bmatrix}\delta S^TS&L\\L^T&-D\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{2r\times2r}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The displayed formula is a base-plus-rank-at-most-\(2r\) representation.
Applying the stored direct BFGS corrections sequentially produces the same \(B\).
special_cases_latex: For \(r=0\), \(B=\delta I\).
Taking the \(m\) most recent pairs gives the usual moving-window compact L-BFGS matrix.
immediate_consequences_latex: A product \(Bv\) can be evaluated using narrow matrix products and a \(2r\)-dimensional solve.
Only \(S\), \(Y\), their inner products, and the base scalar need be stored.
boundary_notes: The formula represents the direct Hessian approximation, not the inverse matrix used by the two-loop recursion.
Loss of positive curvature can make the standard BFGS compact construction unsuitable without safeguards.

notation.meaning: Narrow correction factor and small core matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rolling-History Compact L-BFGS Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct compact BFGS representation using an iteration-dependent scaled-identity base matrix and the most recent m correction pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix $m\geq1$. The correction-pair history is refreshed at each iteration by deleting the oldest pair and adding the newest pair. During the first $m$ iterations, the finite-update compact BFGS construction is used with $B_k^0=\delta_kI$, where $\delta_k=1/\gamma_k$. For $k>m$, define
\[
S_k=[s_{k-m},\ldots,s_{k-1}],\qquad Y_k=[y_{k-m},\ldots,y_{k-1}],
\]
\[
D_k=\operatorname{diag}(s_{k-m}^Ty_{k-m},\ldots,s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}),
\]
and, for $1\leq i,j\leq m$,
\[
(L_k)_{ij}=\begin{cases}s_{k-m+i-1}^Ty_{k-m+j-1},&i>j,\\0,&i\leq j.\end{cases}
\]
Provided the middle matrix is nonsingular, applying the $m$ retained BFGS updates to $B_k^0=\delta_kI$ gives
\[
B_k=\delta_kI-[\delta_kS_k\;Y_k]\begin{bmatrix}\delta_kS_k^TS_k&L_k\\L_k^T&-D_k\end{bmatrix}^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}\delta_kS_k^T\\Y_k^T\end{bmatrix}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The compact direct L-BFGS matrix uses a rolling window of the m newest correction pairs. After the initial iterations, the oldest pair is dropped and the newest is appended. Applying those m BFGS updates to the iteration-dependent scaled identity delta_k I yields the displayed compact formula, whose middle matrix has dimension 2m.

knowledge_statements.title: Unrolled L-BFGS Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-sum expansion of chronological inverse-BFGS updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,\ell\), let \(\rho_i=(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i)^{-1}\) and \(V_i=I-\rho_i y_i s_i^{\mathsf T}\). If
\[
H_i=V_i^{\mathsf T}H_{i-1}V_i+\rho_i s_is_i^{\mathsf T},
\]
then
\[
H_\ell=P_0^{\mathsf T}H_0P_0+
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\rho_iP_i^{\mathsf T}s_is_i^{\mathsf T}P_i,
\quad
P_i=V_{i+1}\cdots V_\ell,
\quad P_0=V_1\cdots V_\ell,
\]
where an empty product is \(I\). This is the unrolled inverse L-BFGS matrix generated by the stored pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrolling inverse-BFGS updates expresses the L-BFGS metric as a transformed initial metric plus transformed positive rank-one pair contributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_\ell\) has the displayed product-sum representation and is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unrolled Direct L-BFGS Sum
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B^0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and let \(((s_i,y_i))_{i=a}^{k-1}\) be an ordered history with \(y_i^Ts_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-Hessian BFGS representation obtained by explicitly expanding each rank-two correction over the retained window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=a,\ldots,k-1\), define \(b_i=y_i/(y_i^Ts_i)^{1/2}\). Recursively set \(\widetilde a_i=B^0s_i+\sum_{j=a}^{i-1}[(b_j^Ts_i)b_j-(a_j^Ts_i)a_j]\) and \(a_i=\widetilde a_i/(s_i^T\widetilde a_i)^{1/2}\). The unrolled L-BFGS matrix is \(B=B^0+\sum_{i=a}^{k-1}(b_ib_i^T-a_ia_i^T)\). It represents the chronological direct-BFGS corrections generated from the same base and retained pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each direct BFGS correction is written as one positive and one negative rank-one term. The positive vector is a normalized gradient difference. The negative vector is obtained by applying the previously accumulated corrections to the current step and normalizing the result. Summing these rank-one terms with the base matrix gives the unrolled limited-memory Hessian approximation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update form \(B_{i+1}=B_i-a_ia_i^T+b_ib_i^T\) and the displayed finite sum define the same chronological operator.
special_cases_latex: With one retained pair, \(B=B^0+b_ab_a^T-a_aa_a^T\).
With no retained pair, the representation is \(B=B^0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(r\) retained pairs, the correction has rank at most \(2r\).
Matrix-vector multiplication uses the stored \(a_i,b_i\) vectors and the base operator.
boundary_notes: When the oldest pair changes, the dependent \(a_i\) vectors generally must be recomputed.
This representation is typically more expensive to refresh than the compact representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unrolled L-BFGS inverse-update representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the L-BFGS inverse-Hessian approximation as successive inverse-BFGS updates of an iteration-dependent initial matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\), \(\rho_i=(y_i^Ts_i)^{-1}\), \(V_i=I-\rho_i y_i s_i^T\), and \(\mathcal U_i(H)=V_i^THV_i+\rho_i s_i s_i^T\). Given \(H_k^0\) and the retained pairs indexed by \(i=k-m,\ldots,k-1\), the L-BFGS approximation is
\[
H_k=(\mathcal U_{k-1}\circ\cdots\circ\mathcal U_{k-m})(H_k^0).
\]
Expanding this composition gives the unrolled product-and-rank-one representation, from which \(H_k\nabla f(x_k)\) can be evaluated using the retained vectors without explicitly forming the generally dense matrix \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The L-BFGS inverse-Hessian approximation is obtained by applying the inverse-BFGS update successively to an initial matrix using the retained curvature pairs. Its product with the current gradient can therefore be evaluated without forming the dense approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(y_i^Ts_i\ne0\) for every retained pair, so each \(\rho_i\) is defined.
\(H_k^0\) is a chosen initial inverse-Hessian approximation and may depend on \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: L-BFGS History-State Transition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix memory capacity \(m\geq1\). Let \(\mathcal P_k\) be an ordered sequence of accepted curvature pairs before processing the candidate \(c_k=(s_k,y_k)\), and let \(A_k\in\{0,1\}\) denote its acceptance decision.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The lifecycle of a moving-window L-BFGS history, including initialization, growth, steady-state eviction, rejection, and complete restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\operatorname{tail}_m\) to retain the last at most \(m\) elements of an ordered sequence. The standard history transition is \(\mathcal P_{k+1}=\operatorname{tail}_m(\mathcal P_k\mathbin{\|}c_k)\) when \(A_k=1\), and \(\mathcal P_{k+1}=\mathcal P_k\) when \(A_k=0\), where \(\|\) denotes ordered append. Initialization is \(\mathcal P_0=\varnothing\). A complete restart is the additional transition \(\mathcal P_k\mapsto\varnothing\). Thus accepted pairs fill the history until capacity, after which each accepted pair evicts the oldest retained pair; rejected pairs do not enter the state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The history begins empty. An accepted curvature pair is appended, and only the most recent \(m\) pairs are retained, so a full history loses its oldest pair whenever a new one is accepted. A rejected pair leaves the history unchanged. A complete restart empties the history. These transitions distinguish initial growth, fixed-capacity operation, rejection, and restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal P_k|\leq m\) for every state reachable from \(\mathcal P_0=\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an always-accepted sequence without restarts, \(\mathcal P_k=((s_i,y_i))_{i=\max(0,k-m)}^{k-1}\).
special_cases_latex: During initial growth, \(|\mathcal P_k|<m\) and an accepted pair causes no eviction.
At capacity, an accepted pair performs one FIFO eviction and one append.
immediate_consequences_latex: The state size remains bounded independently of the iteration count.
A restart returns the next metric construction to its base approximation unless new pairs are subsequently accepted.
boundary_notes: The source supports continual refresh and also discusses all-at-once flushing as a distinct, generally less effective policy.
The acceptance predicate itself belongs to a curvature safeguard and is not fixed by this lifecycle definition.

notation.meaning: Operator retaining the newest m sequence elements.

review_flags: Pair rejection is a standard lifecycle extension; the cited algorithm explicitly states append and oldest-pair deletion but does not formalize an acceptance indicator.

Let \((s_{\ell},y_{\ell})\) be the newest accepted pair and choose \(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq\gamma_{\max}\). Define
\[
\widehat\gamma_k=\frac{s_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}y_{\ell}}{y_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}y_{\ell}},
\qquad
\gamma_k=\min\{\gamma_{\max},\max\{\gamma_{\min},\widehat\gamma_k\}\},
\qquad H_k^{(0)}=\gamma_k I_n.
\]
If the history is empty, use a prescribed \(\gamma_{m def}\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\). This initialization is symmetric positive definite and approximates the inverse-Hessian scale along the newest secant pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize each L-BFGS recursion with a clipped scalar identity derived from the newest accepted curvature pair, using a bounded default for empty history.

knowledge_statements.title: L-BFGS History Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and product costs induced by a fixed memory limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a memory limit \(m\geq1\), and at iteration \(k\) retain \(\ell_k=\min\{m,a_k\}\) accepted pairs, where \(a_k\) is the number currently available after the latest reset. Storing \(S_k,Y_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times\ell_k}\) requires \(2n\ell_k\) scalar vector entries, apart from \(O(\ell_k)\) coefficients. Applying the inverse L-BFGS approximation by two-loop recursion uses \(O(n\ell_k)\) arithmetic and \(O(n\ell_k)\) storage; hence both are \(O(nm)\) in the fixed-memory model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With at most m stored pairs, L-BFGS uses O(nm) storage and O(nm) work for each inverse-metric product.
assumptions_latex: Each stored curvature vector lies in \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pair storage and one two-loop inverse-metric product both have complexity \(O(nm)\).

knowledge_statements.title: L-BFGS History Replacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-in, first-out replacement of a bounded curvature history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current history \(\mathcal H_k\) be ordered from oldest to newest and contain at most \(m\) pairs. For a candidate pair \((s_k,y_k)\), first apply the prescribed acceptance test, including \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\). If the pair is rejected, set \(\mathcal H_{k+1}=\mathcal H_k\). If it is accepted and \(|\mathcal H_k|<m\), append it. If it is accepted and \(|\mathcal H_k|=m\), delete the oldest pair and append \((s_k,y_k)\). The resulting history remains chronological and has cardinality at most \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted pairs are appended; once memory is full, the oldest pair is removed first. Rejected pairs leave the L-BFGS history unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal H_{k+1}\) is chronological, contains only accepted pairs, and satisfies \(|\mathcal H_{k+1}|\leq m\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded chronological L-BFGS histories conventionally use FIFO replacement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the History Replacement leaf, but FIFO replacement and the unspecified prescribed acceptance test are implementation choices rather than universal consequences of L-BFGS. An exact source must support this lifecycle policy.

knowledge_statements.title: L-BFGS History Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance test for curvature pairs retained by a limited-memory BFGS implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\). Given constants \(\varepsilon_c>0\), \(0<\underline\gamma\leq \overline\gamma\), and \(\varepsilon_d>0\), call \((s_k,y_k)\) history-admissible when \[s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\geq \varepsilon_c\lVert s_k\rVert\lVert y_k\rVert,\qquad \underline\gamma\leq \frac{s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}s_k}\leq \overline\gamma,\qquad \lVert s_k\rVert\geq\varepsilon_d.\] A history has acceptable quality when every stored pair is history-admissible; rejected pairs are not used in the two-loop recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An L-BFGS history is acceptable when every retained displacement pair has sufficient positive curvature, controlled scaling, and a nonnegligible step length.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at the sampled iterates.
All thresholds are fixed before testing the pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained pair has positive curvature and bounded secant scaling.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifies this particular L-BFGS history-quality predicate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Moving-Window Quasi-Newton Update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be a specified quasi-Newton update formula acting on symmetric matrices and a secant pair, let \(M_k^0\in\mathbb S^n\) be a base matrix, and let \(I_k\) index at most \(m\) retained pairs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General limited-memory construction encompassing direct or inverse BFGS, SR1, and other update formulas for which an implicit or compact representation is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A general limited-memory quasi-Newton matrix is \(M_k=\mathcal U_{(s_{i_r},y_{i_r})}\circ\cdots\circ\mathcal U_{(s_{i_1},y_{i_1})}(M_k^0)\), where \(i_1<\cdots<i_r\), \(r\leq m\), and the retained pairs are refreshed by deleting old information and adding accepted new information. The matrix may approximate either a Hessian \(B_k\) or its inverse \(H_k\), and it is stored through the base, the pairs, and any small core matrices needed to apply the resulting operator. The base may vary with \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general limited-memory update starts from an iteration-dependent base matrix and applies a chosen quasi-Newton correction formula using only a bounded ordered set of retained secant pairs. The resulting Hessian or inverse-Hessian approximation is represented implicitly by the base, pair vectors, and small auxiliary matrices. The history is continually refreshed rather than allowed to grow with the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k=\mathcal U_{i_r}\circ\cdots\circ\mathcal U_{i_1}(M_k^0)\) with \(r\leq m\) and bounded representation size.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When available, the sequential composition can be replaced by an algebraically identical compact outer-product form.
special_cases_latex: Inverse-BFGS corrections give L-BFGS.
Direct SR1 corrections give a limited-memory SR1 Hessian model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The retained secant information is bounded by \(m\) pairs.
Direct and inverse limited-memory models can support trust-region, line-search, or constrained methods according to which operator is required.
boundary_notes: Different update formulas impose different denominator and definiteness conditions.
A flush-and-restart history policy is distinct from continual moving-window refresh.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Limited-Memory BFGS and SR1 Realizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact structure and cost for direct L-BFGS, its constrained and trust-region uses, the compact SR1 representation and self-dual inverse form, and the SR1 positive-definiteness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a compact direct L-BFGS matrix retaining $m$ correction pairs, the correction to the basic matrix factors through long-and-narrow matrices and a $2m\times2m$ middle matrix. Updating $B_k$ requires approximately $2mn+O(m^3)$ operations, and computing $B_kv$ requires $(4m+1)n+O(m^2)$ multiplications. Such direct matrices can be used in unconstrained trust-region methods and in bound-constrained or generally constrained methods, including as approximations to a Lagrangian Hessian. A comparable compact inverse-BFGS realization exists and gives an unconstrained L-BFGS implementation of similar cost.

Let $B_0=B_0^T$, and suppose $B_k$ results from $k$ SR1 updates with pairs $(s_i,y_i)$. Define $S_k=[s_0,\ldots,s_{k-1}]$, $Y_k=[y_0,\ldots,y_{k-1}]$, $D_k=\operatorname{diag}(s_0^Ty_0,\ldots,s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})$, and $(L_k)_{ij}=s_{i-1}^Ty_{j-1}$ for $i>j$ and $0$ otherwise. Whenever the middle matrix is nonsingular,
\[
B_k=B_0+(Y_k-B_0S_k)(D_k+L_k+L_k^T-S_k^TB_0S_k)^{-1}(Y_k-B_0S_k)^T.
\]
Because SR1 is self-dual, the inverse representation is obtained by replacing $(B,s,y)$ with $(H,y,s)$. A limited-memory SR1 realization replaces $B_0$ by the iteration-dependent basic matrix $B_k^0$ and retains the $m$ newest correction pairs. Unlike L-BFGS, limited-memory SR1 need not produce positive-definite approximations near a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The compact direct L-BFGS correction uses narrow matrices and a small 2m-by-2m matrix. Updating it costs about 2mn plus a cubic-in-m term, and applying it to a vector costs (4m+1)n plus a quadratic-in-m term. It can serve in trust-region and constrained methods, while a compact inverse-BFGS form has comparable implementation cost. A sequence of SR1 updates has the displayed compact form; self-duality gives the inverse form by swapping direct with inverse matrices and s with y. Keeping only the newest m pairs produces limited-memory SR1, which is not guaranteed to remain positive definite near a solution.
assumptions_latex: m\geq1\text{ correction pairs are retained for the limited-memory cost statements.}
B_0=B_0^T\text{ for the compact SR1 representation.}
B_k\text{ is obtained from }B_0\text{ by }k\text{ SR1 updates with pairs }(s_i,y_i)_{i=0}^{k-1}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cost}(\operatorname{update}B_k)\approx2mn+O(m^3),\qquad \operatorname{cost}(B_kv)=(4m+1)n+O(m^2),\qquad B_k^{\mathrm{SR1}}=B_0+(Y_k-B_0S_k)(D_k+L_k+L_k^T-S_k^TB_0S_k)^{-1}(Y_k-B_0S_k)^T,\text{ and limited-memory SR1 need not be positive definite near a solution.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Roles and History Policies in Limited-Memory Quasi-Newton Updating
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct and inverse curvature roles, compact realizations, and correction-pair retention policies in general limited-memory updating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: L-BFGS is an unconstrained line-search method that implicitly updates an inverse-Hessian approximation $H_k$, whereas trust-region methods require a direct Hessian approximation $B_k$. Constrained methods may analogously require approximations to the Hessian or reduced Hessian of the Lagrangian. Compact outer-product representations permit efficient direct and inverse realizations of standard quasi-Newton updates. In the limited-memory policy considered here, correction pairs are continually refreshed by deleting old information and adding new information. The alternative policy of filling storage and then discarding nearly all retained pairs is reported to be less effective computationally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: L-BFGS implicitly updates an inverse-Hessian approximation, while trust-region methods require a direct Hessian approximation; constrained methods may require Hessian or reduced-Hessian approximations for the Lagrangian. Compact outer-product forms support efficient direct and inverse implementations. The chapter uses a rolling correction-pair history and reports that nearly complete history resets after storage fills are less effective in practice.
assumptions_latex: \text{Only a limited collection of correction pairs is retained.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Compact direct or inverse realizations can be combined with rolling correction-pair replacement in limited-memory quasi-Newton methods.}

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory SR1
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-Hessian limited-memory SR1 update with a denominator safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric seed \(B_0\), retained pairs \((s_i,y_i)\), and \(0<\eta<1\), process the pairs chronologically. At pair \(i\), set \(r_i=y_i-B_i s_i\). If \(\lvert r_i^{\mathsf T}s_i\rvert\geq\eta\lVert r_i\rVert\lVert s_i\rVert\), update \[B_{i+1}=B_i+\frac{r_i r_i^{\mathsf T}}{r_i^{\mathsf T}s_i};\] otherwise set \(B_{i+1}=B_i\). Retain at most \(m\) accepted pairs, discarding an older pair when necessary. Output the linear operator \(v\mapsto Bv\), evaluated from the seed and retained rank-one corrections without storing a dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limited-memory SR1 stores only recent accepted secant pairs and applies safeguarded symmetric rank-one corrections to a seed operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted correction is symmetric and satisfies \(B_{i+1}s_i=y_i\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k^0\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(S=[s_1,…,s_r]\), \(Y=[y_1,…,y_r]\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), \(r\leq m\). Define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_i^Ty_i)\) and \(L_{ij}=s_i^Ty_j\) for \(i>j\), zero otherwise.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limited-memory direct-Hessian update from the symmetric Broyden family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric \(B_i\), a pair \((s_i,y_i)\) with \(s_i^{\mathsf T}B_i s_i\neq0\) and \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\neq0\), and \(\phi_i\in\mathbb R\), define \(w_i=y_i/(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i)-B_i s_i/(s_i^{\mathsf T}B_i s_i)\) and update \[B_{i+1}=B_i-\frac{B_i s_i s_i^{\mathsf T}B_i}{s_i^{\mathsf T}B_i s_i}+\frac{y_i y_i^{\mathsf T}}{s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i}+\phi_i(s_i^{\mathsf T}B_i s_i)w_iw_i^{\mathsf T}.\] Retain at most \(m\) pairs and parameters, and reconstruct products from a seed operator and these low-rank corrections. Output the resulting operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_0\) be a fixed seed and let an update procedure produce an operator \(\mathcal U(B_0;S,Y)\) from curvature matrices \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_p]\) and \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_p]\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact aggregation of \(\mathcal P\) is an ordered sequence \(\widetilde{\mathcal P}=((\widetilde s_1,\widetilde y_1),\ldots,(\widetilde s_q,\widetilde y_q))\), with \(q<r\), such that \(\mathcal U_{\widetilde{\mathcal P}}(M^0)=\mathcal U_{\mathcal P}(M^0)\), where \(\mathcal U_{\mathcal P}\) denotes chronological composition. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Symmetric Secant Update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\{1,…,n\}^2\) be a symmetric sparsity pattern containing the diagonal, let \(\mathbb S_\Omega^n=\{B\in\mathbb S^n:B_{ij}=0\text{ for }(i,j)\notin\Omega\}\), and let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Hessian approximations with a prescribed known sparsity pattern; existence and definiteness depend on the selected update formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse secant update is a map \(\mathcal U_\Omega:\mathbb S_\Omega^n\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb S_\Omega^n\) such that, whenever its feasibility conditions hold, \(B^+=\mathcal U_\Omega(B;s,y)\) satisfies \(B^+s=y\), \((B^+)^T=B^+\), and \(B^+_{ij}=0\) for every \((i,j)\notin\Omega\). A canonical least-change instance selects, among all matrices satisfying these constraints, one minimizing a declared matrix norm distance from \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse secant update maps a symmetric matrix having a prescribed zero pattern to another symmetric matrix with the same zero pattern while enforcing the latest secant equation. A least-change variant chooses the feasible updated matrix closest to the current approximation in a specified norm.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Membership \(B^+\in\mathbb S_\Omega^n\) is equivalent to symmetry together with \(B^+_{ij}=0\) outside \(\Omega\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Omega=\{1,…,n\}^2\), the sparsity restriction disappears.
The Frobenius least-change update is obtained by minimizing \(\|B^+-B\|_F^2\) over the sparse secant affine set.
immediate_consequences_latex: The updated approximation can be stored using only entries indexed by \(\Omega\).
boundary_notes: The sparse secant constraints may be infeasible for a given \((s,y,\Omega)\).
The update is not generally guaranteed to be positive definite or scale invariant.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Preserving Update Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant-update families constrained to a prescribed symmetric sparsity pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\) be symmetric and contain every diagonal index, and define \[\mathbb S_E^n=\{B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:B=B^{\mathsf T},\ B_{ij}=0\text{ whenever }(i,j)\notin E\}.\] A sparsity-preserving secant-update family is a collection of maps \(U_E:\mathbb S_E^n\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb S_E^n\), defined on an admissible domain, such that \(B^+=U_E(B,s,y)\) satisfies \(B^+s=y\). Consequently, every update remains symmetric, introduces no entry outside \(E\), and enforces the current secant equation whenever that equation is feasible in \(\mathbb S_E^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity-preserving update maps a sparse symmetric metric to another with the same prescribed zero pattern while satisfying a feasible secant equation.
assumptions_latex: The sparsity pattern \(E\) is symmetric and includes the diagonal.
The affine system \(B^+s=y\) has a solution in \(\mathbb S_E^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Least-Change Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted projection of a reference metric onto sparse symmetric secant constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\in\mathbb S_E^n\), a nonzero step \(s\), a vector \(y\), and a positive-definite self-adjoint weight operator \(W\) on \(\mathbb S_E^n\), compute \[B^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\in\mathbb S_E^n}\ \frac12\langle X-B,W(X-B)\rangle_F\quad\text{subject to }Xs=y.\] Stop with infeasibility if the affine constraint has no solution in \(\mathbb S_E^n\); otherwise output the unique minimizer. This update changes the previous approximation as little as possible in the weighted norm while preserving the specified zero pattern and satisfying the secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse least-change update is the weighted nearest sparse symmetric matrix satisfying the new secant equation.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is positive definite and self-adjoint on \(\mathbb S_E^n\).
The constraint set \(\{X\in\mathbb S_E^n:Xs=y\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A unique \(B^+\in\mathbb S_E^n\) exists and satisfies \(B^+s=y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Frobenius Sparse Least-Change Secant Matrix
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_\Omega^n\), where \(\Omega\) is a symmetric prescribed sparsity pattern, and let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct sparse Hessian update defined by a constrained Frobenius-norm projection; positive definiteness is not imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sparse least-change update is any solution \(B_{k+1}\) of \(\min_{B\in\mathbb S^n}\|B-B_k\|_F^2\) subject to \(Bs_k=y_k\) and \(B_{ij}=0\) for every \((i,j)\notin\Omega\). Since feasible variables vanish outside \(\Omega\), the objective is equivalently \(\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}(B_{ij}-(B_k)_{ij})^2\). The object is defined only when this constrained problem is feasible; uniqueness follows when the feasible set is nonempty because the squared Frobenius norm is strictly convex on the matrix-variable subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The update is the symmetric matrix with the prescribed zero pattern that satisfies the current secant equation and changes the previous sparse approximation as little as possible in Frobenius norm. It is therefore a projection of the old matrix onto the affine set of sparse symmetric matrices satisfying the secant equation, provided that set is nonempty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The objective may be summed only over \(\Omega\) because all entries outside the pattern are fixed at zero.
special_cases_latex: With a full pattern, this becomes the unweighted symmetric Frobenius least-change secant problem.
immediate_consequences_latex: The updated matrix preserves the prescribed sparsity pattern and satisfies the latest secant equation.
The update need not be positive definite.
boundary_notes: The construction is not invariant under arbitrary linear rescaling of variables.
The cited source reports practical and modeling limitations of this particular Frobenius least-change criterion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factor-level realization of a sparse symmetric secant correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a sparse factorization \(PBP^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) of the current symmetric approximation. Given a sparse symmetric secant correction \(\Delta B\) represented as \(UCU^{\mathsf T}\), form \[P(B+\Delta B)P^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}+(PU)C(PU)^{\mathsf T}.\] Apply symmetric sparse rank-update or downdate operations, with pivoting when required, to obtain \(L^+,D^+\). Accept only if the computed factors satisfy a prescribed residual tolerance for \(P(B+\Delta B)P^{\mathsf T}-L^+D^+(L^+)^{\mathsf T}\); otherwise refactorize or reject the correction. Output the updated factors and permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse factor implementation applies a low-rank secant correction directly to sparse symmetric factors, verifies the factorization residual, and refactorizes if necessary.
assumptions_latex: The correction has a low-rank representation \(UCU^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted factors represent \(B+\Delta B\) to the prescribed residual tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Factor-Level Secant Update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) possess a stored sparse factorization \(P_k^TB_kP_k=L_kD_kL_k^T\), where \(P_k\) is a permutation, \(L_k\) is sparse unit lower triangular, and \(D_k\) is diagonal or block diagonal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-level mathematical object in which the factorization, rather than a dense updated matrix, is the persistent representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse factor-update implementation of a secant map \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k;s_k,y_k)\) is a transition \((P_k,L_k,D_k,s_k,y_k)\mapsto(P_{k+1},L_{k+1},D_{k+1})\) satisfying \(P_{k+1}^TB_{k+1}P_{k+1}=L_{k+1}D_{k+1}L_{k+1}^T\), with the factors stored in sparse form and the matrix \(B_{k+1}\) not required to be formed densely. If a positive-definite Cholesky form is used, \(D_k\) may be absorbed so that \(P_k^TB_kP_k=R_k^TR_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse factor-update implementation stores a permuted sparse factorization of the current quasi-Newton matrix. When a secant correction is accepted, it updates or refactorizes those sparse factors so that their product equals the corrected matrix, without requiring persistent dense storage of that matrix. Positive-definite cases may use Cholesky factors; indefinite cases require a suitable symmetric-indefinite factorization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive-definite \(B_{k+1}\), the factor identity may be written \(P_{k+1}^TB_{k+1}P_{k+1}=R_{k+1}^TR_{k+1}\).
special_cases_latex: A diagonal-plus-low-rank metric may be applied using its base factor and low-rank correction rather than an explicit sparse refactorization.
An indefinite sparse update may use block-diagonal \(D_{k+1}\) with one-by-one and two-by-two pivots.
immediate_consequences_latex: Linear systems with the updated metric are solved through the stored factors rather than by forming an inverse.
boundary_notes: Factor sparsity may experience fill-in even when the matrix has a sparse prescribed pattern.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partitioned structure-exploiting quasi-Newton update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have a partially separable representation \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\phi_i(U_i x)\), where \(U_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n}\) and normally \(n_i\ll n\). Write \(x_{[i]}=U_i x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, possibly nonconvex optimization with a known, possibly overlapping element decomposition. The definition concerns Hessian-model construction, not globalization or convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partitioned structure-exploiting update maintains symmetric local matrices \(B_{[i],k}\in\mathbb{S}^{n_i}\) and assembles the full metric as \[B_k=\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}U_i^T B_{[i],k}U_i.\] For a step \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), its local displacement and gradient difference are \(s_{[i],k}=U_i s_k\) and \(y_{[i],k}=\nabla\phi_i(U_i x_{k+1})-\nabla\phi_i(U_i x_k)\). Each eligible local matrix is updated by a symmetric quasi-Newton map \[B_{[i],k+1}=\mathcal U_i(B_{[i],k},s_{[i],k},y_{[i],k}),\qquad B_{[i],k+1}s_{[i],k}=y_{[i],k},\] while an ineligible or safeguarded element may be left unchanged. The resulting global model is the sum of the lifted local models and can be applied without forming a dense global matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partitioned structure-exploiting update represents the objective as a sum of low-dimensional element functions. It stores one symmetric quasi-Newton matrix for each element, updates that matrix with the displacement and gradient change restricted to the element variables, and lifts and sums the updated matrices to obtain the full-space metric. Element variable sets may overlap, so the construction is partitioned by functions or curvature contributions rather than necessarily by disjoint coordinates. The local secant equations are imposed in the element spaces; they do not generally imply one global secant equation unless the local gradient changes sum consistently to the full gradient change.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and the maps \(U_i\) and element gradients \(\nabla\phi_i\) are available.
Each applied local update \(\mathcal U_i\) is well defined for its selected pair \((s_{[i],k},y_{[i],k})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}U_i^TB_{[i],k+1}U_i\), with every applied local update satisfying \(B_{[i],k+1}s_{[i],k}=y_{[i],k}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic curvature term satisfies \(p^TB_kp=\sum_i(U_ip)^TB_{[i],k}(U_ip)\).
The matrix action is \(B_kv=\sum_iU_i^TB_{[i],k}(U_iv)\), so explicit global assembly is optional.
special_cases_latex: If the coordinate sets are disjoint and cover \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the assembled metric is block diagonal up to permutation.
If \(n_e=1\) and \(U_1=I\), the construction reduces to an ordinary full-space quasi-Newton update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local storage is \(\sum_i O(n_i^2)\) rather than necessarily \(O(n^2)\).
Overlapping element maps automatically reproduce the sparsity induced by the element decomposition.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness of the global matrix requires suitable properties of the local matrices and collective coverage by the maps \(U_i\).
An elementwise BFGS update may be unavailable when its local curvature product is nonpositive; SR1 or safeguarding is a nearby variant.

Space of real symmetric matrices of order n_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elementwise quasi-Newton model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\phi_i(U_i x)\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with \(U_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n}\), element point \(z_{i,k}=U_i x_k\), and local gradient \(g_{i,k}=\nabla\phi_i(z_{i,k})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth partially separable objectives. Each model approximates one element function in its intrinsic variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elementwise quasi-Newton model at \(x_k\) is the family of local quadratics \[m_{i,k}(d_i)=\phi_i(z_{i,k})+g_{i,k}^Td_i+\tfrac12d_i^TB_{i,k}d_i,\qquad B_{i,k}\in\mathbb S^{n_i},\] together with the assembled full-space model \[m_k(p)=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}U_i^TB_{i,k}U_i\right)p.\] After \(x_k\) changes to \(x_{k+1}\), define \(s_{i,k}=U_i(x_{k+1}-x_k)\) and \(y_{i,k}=g_{i,k+1}-g_{i,k}\). A local quasi-Newton replacement \(B_{i,k+1}\) is required, when applied, to be symmetric and to satisfy \(B_{i,k+1}s_{i,k}=y_{i,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elementwise quasi-Newton model assigns a small quadratic model to every element function in a partially separable objective. The constant and linear terms are exact at the current element point, while a symmetric local matrix approximates the element Hessian. Substituting each full-space trial displacement through the element map and summing the local quadratics gives the global model. Curvature observations and secant equations are therefore formed separately in the intrinsic element spaces, where the dimension is the number of variables used by that element.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_i\) is differentiable at \(U_i x_k\) and \(U_i x_{k+1}\).
The element decomposition and the maps \(U_i\) are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global model Hessian is \(B_k=\sum_iU_i^TB_{i,k}U_i\), and every applied element update satisfies \(B_{i,k+1}s_{i,k}=y_{i,k}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(m_k(p)=\sum_i m_{i,k}(U_ip)\) after combining the element constants and gradients.
\(\nabla^2\phi_i(U_ix_k)\) is approximated by \(B_{i,k}\), while \(\nabla^2 f(x_k)\) is approximated by \(\sum_iU_i^TB_{i,k}U_i\).
special_cases_latex: For coordinate-selection matrices \(U_i\), each local matrix is scattered into its associated rows and columns of the global matrix.
A one-dimensional element has scalar curvature \(B_{i,k}\in\mathbb R\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The global matrix-vector product decomposes into independent local products.
Element overlap is accumulated additively in shared global entries.
boundary_notes: The element functions need not be convex; hence individual element Hessians and SR1 models may be indefinite.
This definition does not prescribe BFGS, SR1, or another particular local update formula.

notation.meaning: Quadratic model of element i in its intrinsic displacement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent secant updates for blocks in an additive objective decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q f_j(x)\) and maintain symmetric matrices \(B_j\), with \(B=\sum_{j=1}^q B_j\). For a step \(s=x^+-x\), compute \(y_j=
abla f_j(x^+)-
abla f_j(x)\). For each block, apply a chosen symmetric secant map \(B_j^+=U_j(B_j,s,y_j)\) satisfying \(B_j^+s=y_j\), or skip the block when its safeguard fails. Assemble \(B^+=\sum_{j=1}^q B_j^+\) and use it in the next quadratic model. If every block is updated, then \(B^+s=
abla f(x^+)-
abla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioned quasi-Newton methods update curvature approximations for additive objective components separately and sum them to form the global metric.
assumptions_latex: Each component \(f_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
Every accepted map \(U_j\) is symmetric and satisfies its component secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When all blocks are accepted, the assembled matrix satisfies the global secant equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partitioned quasi-Newton update map
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\phi_i(U_ix)\), let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and define \(s_{i,k}=U_is_k\) and \(y_{i,k}=\nabla\phi_i(U_ix_{k+1})-\nabla\phi_i(U_ix_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth partially separable objectives with simultaneous local secant updates. The definition isolates the update operation, rather than the resulting element models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partitioned quasi-Newton update is the product map \[\mathcal U_k:(B_{1,k},\ldots,B_{n_e,k})\mapsto(B_{1,k+1},\ldots,B_{n_e,k+1}),\] where, for each selected element \(i\), \[B_{i,k+1}=\mathcal Q_i(B_{i,k};s_{i,k},y_{i,k})\in\mathbb S^{n_i},\qquad B_{i,k+1}s_{i,k}=y_{i,k},\] and unselected elements satisfy \(B_{i,k+1}=B_{i,k}\). Its induced full-space update is \[B_{k+1}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}U_i^TB_{i,k+1}U_i.\] Thus the update acts independently on element matrices before their lifted contributions are summed; it is not defined by applying one dense update directly to \(B_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partitioned quasi-Newton update simultaneously applies local secant-update maps to a collection of element matrices. Each selected local matrix receives only the displacement and gradient change belonging to its element variables and satisfies its own local secant equation. Elements for which an update is skipped remain unchanged. The updated full-space metric is obtained by lifting and summing all local matrices. This distinguishes the operation from an ordinary dense quasi-Newton update, even when both yield matrices with the same dimensions.
assumptions_latex: The element maps and local gradient differences are available.
Each selected update map is defined for its local secant pair; any required BFGS curvature or SR1 denominator condition is enforced locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_k\) produces \(B_{k+1}=\sum_iU_i^TB_{i,k+1}U_i\) from locally updated matrices satisfying their selected secant equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The operation is a block-diagonal update on the product space \(\prod_i\mathbb S^{n_i}\), followed by the linear assembly map \((B_i)_i\mapsto\sum_iU_i^TB_iU_i\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(\mathcal Q_i\) as SR1 accommodates indefinite element curvature when its denominator safeguard holds.
Choosing local BFGS preserves positive definiteness of an updated element when \(s_{i,k}^Ty_{i,k}>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Different update families or safeguards may be used for different elements.
The update preserves the structural support induced by the maps \(U_i\).
boundary_notes: Local secant consistency is stronger and more structured than merely requiring one aggregate equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
Local BFGS curvature need not follow from positive curvature of the aggregate pair.

abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^T(A_k+C_k)p,\qquad B_k=A_k+C_k,\] where \(A_k\) preserves a known analytic, sparse, block, or element curvature component and only \(C_k\) is quasi-Newton updated. Given \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\), a structured secant update chooses \(C_{k+1}\in\mathbb S^n\) so that \[(A_{k+1}+C_{k+1})s_k=y_k,\quad	ext{equivalently}\quad C_{k+1}s_k=y_k-A_{k+1}s_k.\] Any additional sparsity, block, or low-rank restriction belongs to the admissible class for \(C_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured quasi-Newton model splits its curvature matrix into a component that is known from the problem structure and a component that must be estimated. The known component is retained explicitly, while the unknown component is updated from secant information. The defining secant equation is imposed on the sum, or equivalently on the unknown component using a residual gradient change obtained after subtracting the known component's action. This differs from elementwise modeling because the decomposition is by known versus unknown curvature, not necessarily by element functions.
assumptions_latex: A meaningful symmetric known-curvature matrix \(A_k\) is available at each iterate.
The residual secant data admit the chosen update of \(C_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model metric is \(B_k=A_k+C_k\), with the updated unknown component satisfying \(C_{k+1}s_k=y_k-A_{k+1}s_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual pair for updating \(C_k\) is \((s_k,\widehat y_k)\), where \(\widehat y_k=y_k-A_{k+1}s_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A_k=0\), the definition reduces to an ordinary quasi-Newton model.
If \(C_k=0\), the model uses only the known curvature contribution.
immediate_consequences_latex: Known structural curvature is not overwritten by the secant correction.
A matrix-free realization can apply \(A_k\) and \(C_k\) separately.
boundary_notes: Using \(A_k\) rather than \(A_{k+1}\) in the residual defines a nearby but distinct convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-subspace secant update taxonomy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S^n\) approximate a Hessian, and let \(S,Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), where \(1\le q\le n\) and \(S\) has full column rank. Let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional matrix secant updates. This is a candidate organizing definition; no supplied source directly defines the named taxonomy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block-subspace secant update is classified by the quadruple \[(\mathcal S,\;BS=Y,\;\mathcal A,\;\mathcal R),\] where \(\mathcal S\) is the sampled subspace, \(BS=Y\) is the exact or relaxed block-secant requirement, \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) is the admissible structural class, and \(\mathcal R\) is the realization. The principal classes are: a block update, which enforces \(B_+S=Y\) simultaneously; a multisecant update, which retains columns originating from several iterations; and a reduced-space transfer, which updates \(M=Z^TBZ\) in coordinates \(Z\) and lifts or applies that metric in the ambient space. Orthogonal invariance within the sampled subspace requires equivalent data \((S,Y)\mapsto(SQ,YQ)\) for every nonsingular \(Q\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) to define the same constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy identifies a secant update by four independent choices: the subspace on which curvature has been sampled, the matrix equations imposed there, the structural class allowed for the new metric, and the representation used to store or apply it. A block update processes several directions at once. A multisecant update retains equations from multiple observations. A reduced-space transfer updates a metric in subspace coordinates and connects it to the full space. These classes may overlap; the taxonomy records mathematical constraints rather than treating the labels as mutually exclusive algorithms.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(S\) are linearly independent, or dependent columns have been removed.
The block equations are compatible with the chosen admissible class \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update is identified by its sampled subspace, secant relation, admissible matrix class, and realization, with \(B_+S=Y\) as the exact block-secant case.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(B_+S=Y\) means that \(B_+v=Yc\) for every \(v=Sc\in\mathcal S\).
The inverse block-secant form is \(H_+Y=S\) when the relevant matrices are nonsingular.
special_cases_latex: For \(q=1\), the block equation is the ordinary secant equation.
For \(S=Z\widehat S\), the constraints can be expressed in reduced coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing the basis of \(\mathcal S\) does not change an exact block-secant constraint when both data matrices are transformed consistently.
boundary_notes: A multisecant system may be inconsistent with symmetry or positive definiteness.
The proposed class boundaries require an authoritative taxonomy source.

notation.meaning: Admissible structural class for the updated matrix.

Block Quasi-Newton Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric block-secant update enforcing several curvature observations simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), full-column-rank \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), choose a symmetric \(B^+\) satisfying the block secant equation \(B^+S=Y\). A block least-change update computes \[B^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{X=X^{\mathsf T}}\ \frac12\lVert X-B\rVert_W^2\quad\text{subject to }XS=Y,\] where \(W\) defines a positive-definite norm on symmetric matrices. If \(S^{\mathsf T}Y\) is not symmetric, declare the symmetric block-secant constraints infeasible; otherwise output the unique minimizer whenever the affine constraint set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block quasi-Newton update fits one symmetric metric to several step-curvature columns at once, commonly by a least-change projection.
assumptions_latex: The weighted norm is strictly convex on symmetric matrices.
The symmetric block-secant constraint set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is symmetric and satisfies \(B^+S=Y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block quasi-Newton update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(S_k=[s_k^{(1)},\ldots,s_k^{(q)}]\) and \(Y_k=[y_k^{(1)},\ldots,y_k^{(q)}]\) belong to \(\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), with \(S_k\) of full column rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact block-secant updating. The definition does not select a particular block BFGS, DFP, or least-change norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block quasi-Newton update is a map \[B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k;S_k,Y_k)\in\mathbb S^n\] whose defining interpolation condition is \[B_{k+1}S_k=Y_k.\] A least-change block update additionally solves \[B_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A}\|B-B_k\|_W\quad\text{subject to}\quad BS_k=Y_k,\] where \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) may encode positive definiteness, sparsity, or another structure and \(\|\cdot\|_W\) is a specified matrix norm. For a symmetric solution to exist, the block data must satisfy the compatibility condition \(S_k^TY_k=Y_k^TS_k\). A positive-definite solution additionally requires \(S_k^TY_k\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block quasi-Newton update replaces a symmetric metric using several displacement and gradient-change columns simultaneously. Its defining requirement is a matrix secant equation: the new metric maps every sampled displacement column to its corresponding curvature column. A particular update is obtained by adding an admissible matrix class and a least-change criterion. Symmetry imposes compatibility on the cross inner products of the data, and positive definiteness imposes positive curvature on their restriction to the sampled block.
assumptions_latex: The block data satisfy every compatibility condition required by the selected admissible class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated symmetric matrix satisfies \(B_{k+1}S_k=Y_k\); in the positive-definite regime, \(S_k^TY_k\succ0\) is required.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The column equations are \(B_{k+1}s_k^{(j)}=y_k^{(j)}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,q\).
When \(B_{k+1}\) is nonsingular, the inverse equation is \(H_{k+1}Y_k=S_k\), where \(H_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(q=1\), the definition is the standard one-pair quasi-Newton update.
If \(S_k\) is square and nonsingular, the block equation uniquely determines \(B_{k+1}=Y_kS_k^{-1}\), subject to the desired symmetry.
immediate_consequences_latex: The update interpolates curvature on all of \(\operatorname{range}(S_k)\).
Redundant displacement columns should be removed before applying a full-rank formulation.
boundary_notes: No exact locator in the supplied sources establishes this definition or its least-change variant.
Approximate multisecant regression replaces the equality by a residual minimization and is not covered.
review_flags: A precise source for simultaneous block quasi-Newton interpolation was not supplied or located.
knowledge_statements.title: Block quasi-Newton update
Multisecant Quasi-Newton Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous secant interpolation for a history of displacement pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For displacement matrices \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_m]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) and \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), a direct multisecant approximation is a matrix \(B^+\) satisfying \[B^+S=Y.\] If symmetry is required, feasibility implies \(S^{\mathsf T}Y=Y^{\mathsf T}S\); when \(S\) has full column rank, this compatibility condition is also sufficient for the existence of a symmetric solution. A multisecant update selects one feasible \(B^+\), typically by minimizing a declared distance to a reference matrix. An inverse multisecant approximation analogously satisfies \(H^+Y=S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multisecant update fits one matrix to several secant pairs simultaneously; symmetric fitting requires cross-pair compatibility.
assumptions_latex: \(S,Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) have the same number of columns.
For the stated sufficiency result, \(S\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A symmetric direct multisecant solution exists exactly when \(S^{\mathsf T}Y\) is symmetric.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-space quasi-Newton metric transfer
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(A_kZ_k=0\). Let \(M_k\in\mathbb S^{n-m}\) approximate \(Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained optimization using null-space coordinates. The definition covers transferring curvature observations to a reduced metric and its ambient-space action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reduced-space metric transfer forms a reduced secant pair from a tangential step and a projected Lagrangian-gradient difference, \[s_k^R=\alpha_kp_k^Z,\qquad y_k^R=Z_k^T\bigl(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\bigr),\] and updates \(M_k\) so that \[M_{k+1}s_k^R=y_k^R.\] The reduced metric is transferred to the ambient tangent space by the quadratic form \(p^TZ_kM_{k+1}Z_k^Tp\) when \(Z_k\) is orthonormal, or, more generally, by using reduced coordinates \(p=Z_kp^Z\), for which the curvature is \((p^Z)^TM_{k+1}p^Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-space metric transfer records and updates curvature only in the null space of the active constraint Jacobian. A full-space tangential step is represented in null-space coordinates, while the Lagrangian gradient change is projected with the transpose of the null-space basis. A quasi-Newton matrix in the reduced coordinates satisfies the resulting secant equation. That metric then supplies the curvature term for tangential steps without requiring a full ambient Hessian approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(Z_k\) spans its null space.
The multiplier \(\lambda_{k+1}\) and projected gradient difference are defined.
The selected reduced quasi-Newton formula is well defined for \((s_k^R,y_k^R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{k+1}s_k^R=y_k^R\), and \(M_{k+1}\) supplies the Hessian approximation in null-space coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reduced step equation is \(M_kp^Z=-Z_k^T\nabla f_k\) in the simplified null-space model.
For orthonormal \(Z_k\), an ambient tangent-space representative is \(Z_kM_kZ_k^T\).
special_cases_latex: When \(m=0\), \(Z_k=I\) and the construction becomes full-space updating.
A BFGS or SR1 formula may be applied to the reduced pair.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only an \((n-m)\times(n-m)\) curvature matrix is stored.
The range-space component of a constrained step is not controlled by the reduced metric.
boundary_notes: If the null-space basis changes, metric transport between old and new coordinates requires an additional convention.
Dropping range-null cross curvature is part of the cited reduced-Hessian approximation.

notation.meaning: Null-space coordinates of the tangential step.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Quasi-Newton Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced BFGS update on a fixed orthonormal subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,r\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(1\le r\le n\), let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) satisfy \(Z^{\mathsf T}Z=I_r\), and let \(\bar B_k\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^r\). Given a full-space secant pair \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), form \(p_k=Z^{\mathsf T}s_k\in\mathbb{R}^r\) and \(q_k=Z^{\mathsf T}y_k\in\mathbb{R}^r\). If \(p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k>0\), apply the reduced BFGS update
\[
\bar B_{k+1}=\bar B_k-\frac{\bar B_kp_kp_k^{\mathsf T}\bar B_k}{p_k^{\mathsf T}\bar B_kp_k}+\frac{q_kq_k^{\mathsf T}}{p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k}.
\]
Then \(\bar B_{k+1}p_k=q_k\) and \(\bar B_{k+1}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^r\). If \(p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k\le0\), do not apply this undamped update; any damping or pair modification must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the full-space secant pair into the fixed orthonormal subspace and apply BFGS when the reduced curvature is positive. The update then satisfies the reduced secant equation and preserves positive definiteness; otherwise the undamped update is not applied.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis matrix for the update subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Metric Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate representation of a metric restricted to a subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns and let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(Z)\). For a symmetric full-space metric \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), its reduced representation is
\[
\bar B=Z^{\mathsf T}BZ\in\mathbb{S}^r.
\]
Every \(v\in\mathcal S\) has the unique form \(v=Zp\), and its restricted quadratic form satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv=p^{\mathsf T}\bar Bp\). Conversely, any \(\bar B\in\mathbb{S}^r\) defines on \(\mathcal S\) the bilinear form \((Zp,Zq)\mapsto p^{\mathsf T}\bar Bq\). Moreover, \(B\succ0\) implies \(\bar B\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal basis represents the restriction of a full metric by its compression, preserving quadratic forms and positive definiteness on the selected subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar B=Z^{\mathsf T}BZ\) and \((Zp)^{\mathsf T}B(Zq)=p^{\mathsf T}\bar Bq\).

notation.meaning: Subspace spanned by the columns of the basis.
Compression of the full metric to reduced coordinates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard, internally consistent, and appropriate for the leaf, but it has no citation. A specific textbook section, proposition, or page supporting compression of a metric to subspace coordinates is required.

children.title: Full-Space Metric Transfer
children.top_down_role: Interfaces carrying reduced metric information back to the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Metric Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite lifting of a reduced metric to the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) satisfy \(Z^{\mathsf T}Z=I_r\), let \(P=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\), and choose \(\bar B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^r\) and \(\sigma>0\). The orthogonally completed full-space metric
\[
B=Z\bar BZ^{\mathsf T}+\sigma(I-P)
\]
satisfies \(Z^{\mathsf T}BZ=\bar B\), \(BZ=Z\bar B\), and \(Bv=\sigma v\) for every \(v\in\operatorname{range}(Z)^{\perp}\). Consequently \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), with eigenvalues consisting of those of \(\bar B\) together with \(n-r\) copies of \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a positive reduced metric by assigning it to the chosen subspace and using a positive scalar metric on the orthogonal complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=Z\bar BZ^{\mathsf T}+\sigma(I-ZZ^{\mathsf T})\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) and \(Z^{\mathsf T}BZ=\bar B\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the transfer subspace.
Metric assigned to the orthogonal complement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthogonal-complement lifting formula and spectral conclusion are mathematically coherent and the representation content kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for the metric-transfer construction.
