knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Newton computational realization system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\) or \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) be a quasi-Newton metric on \(\mathbb R^n\), generated from accepted secant pairs \((s_i,y_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional computational representations shared across quasi-Newton families. This umbrella-system formulation is a candidate synthesis, not a standard named definition established by one supplied source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quasi-Newton computational realization system is a tuple \[\mathfrak R_k=(\mathcal D_k,\mathcal A_k,\mathcal S_k,\mathcal C_k,\mathcal M_k),\] where \(\mathcal D_k\) stores either a dense matrix, matrix factors, or compact secant data; \(\mathcal A_k(v)\) returns \(B_kv\) or \(H_kv\); \(\mathcal S_k(r)\) returns an approximate or exact solution of \(B_kp=r\) when required; \(\mathcal C_k=(M_k,W_k)\) records storage and arithmetic costs; and \(\mathcal M_k\) records numerical diagnostics such as accepted curvature denominators, factor pivots, or condition estimates. The realization is mathematically faithful when every advertised action agrees with the metric represented by \(\mathcal D_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton computational realization system consists of the stored state and the operations needed to use an evolving metric. Its state may be an explicit dense matrix, a factorization, or a compact collection of correction pairs and small matrices. It exposes matrix actions or linear solves, records storage and work, and monitors quantities that can signal numerical failure. Faithfulness means that all exposed actions correspond to the same mathematical quasi-Newton matrix, even though that matrix need not be assembled.
assumptions_latex: The underlying quasi-Newton update and its accepted secant data are specified.
Every stored denominator or factor required by an exposed action is nonsingular to the working tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak R_k\) realizes one metric consistently through stored data, operator actions or solves, resource measures, and numerical monitoring.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An explicit realization takes \(\mathcal D_k=B_k\) or \(H_k\).
An operator-only realization stores correction pairs and defines \(\mathcal A_k\) recursively or through a compact low-rank formula.
special_cases_latex: Dense inverse BFGS uses \(\mathcal D_k=H_k\) and \(\mathcal A_k(v)=H_kv\).
Factorized BFGS stores \(B_k=L_kD_kL_k^T\) and solves by substitutions.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different realizations can produce the same exact search direction while having different storage and arithmetic costs.
boundary_notes: Stopping tests and globalization rules are external unless explicitly included in \(\mathcal M_k\).
No supplied source defines this five-component umbrella object as a named system.
review_flags: The blueprint combines several standard mechanisms, but no inspected source states this canonical system definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense matrix realization of a quasi-Newton metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k,H_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, with \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) when both are used, and let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quasi-Newton methods that store all entries of a generally dense direct or inverse metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense matrix realization stores an explicit array for \(H_k\) or \(B_k\), or dense factors of \(B_k\), and obtains the search direction by one of \[p_k=-H_kg_k,\qquad B_kp_k=-g_k.\] After a secant pair \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\) is accepted, the stored object is changed so that \[H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\quad\text{or}\quad B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.\] The realization is dense when its persistent matrix or factors have \(\Theta(n^2)\) potentially stored scalar entries, regardless of whether the correction itself has rank one or two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense matrix realization explicitly stores a full Hessian approximation, a full inverse-Hessian approximation, or dense factors of the former. The search direction is obtained by a dense matrix-vector product or by solving with the stored direct metric. Every accepted update enforces the appropriate direct or inverse secant equation. The classification concerns representation: low-rank update formulas still produce a dense realization when their cumulative matrix is stored entry by entry.
assumptions_latex: The stored matrix or factors represent a symmetric metric.
Any direct system used for the step is nonsingular; positive definiteness is imposed when a descent metric is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The realized step is \(p_k=-H_kg_k\) or the solution of \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), using \(\Theta(n^2)\) persistent dense storage.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Storing \(H_k\) turns the step computation into a matrix-vector product.
Storing \(B_k=L_kD_kL_k^T\) realizes the same direct matrix through dense factors.
special_cases_latex: Explicit inverse BFGS stores and updates \(H_k\) by a rank-two formula.
A factorized direct BFGS realization stores \(L_k,D_k\) rather than the entries of \(B_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Dense storage is unsuitable when \(n^2\) words exceed available memory.
Matrix-vector multiplication and factor substitution require quadratic arithmetic in the generic dense case.
boundary_notes: A compact formula representing a dense mathematical matrix is operator-only, not a dense-storage realization.
Sparsity may reduce costs and belongs to a different realization regime.

notation.meaning: Objective gradient at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Matrix Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense direct-Hessian BFGS realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable at \(x_k,x_{k+1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(B_k\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\). Define \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\in\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), explicitly form
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}B_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^{\mathsf T}}{s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.
\]
Store the resulting symmetric matrix for subsequent linear solves or matrix-vector products. The update satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and \(B_{k+1}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\). If \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\le0\), do not apply this undamped formula; any damping or other safeguard must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit BFGS stores and updates the dense direct-Hessian approximation. Under positive curvature it satisfies the secant equation and preserves positive definiteness; otherwise the undamped formula is not applied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit quasi-Newton matrix update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) or \(H_k\in\mathbb S^n\), and assume every denominator in the selected formula is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense finite-dimensional matrix updates. BFGS is used as the canonical explicit realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit matrix update computes and stores every entry of the new quasi-Newton matrix from the old matrix and the current secant pair. For inverse BFGS, with \(\rho_k=(y_k^Ts_k)^{-1}\), \[H_{k+1}=(I-\rho_ks_ky_k^T)H_k(I-\rho_ky_ks_k^T)+\rho_ks_ks_k^T.\] For direct BFGS, \[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}.\] The resulting arrays satisfy \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\) or \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\); when the curvature condition \(y_k^Ts_k>0\) holds and the old metric is positive definite, BFGS preserves positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit matrix update materializes the updated direct or inverse quasi-Newton matrix as a full array. In BFGS the new array is the old array plus a rank-two correction determined by the displacement and gradient change. The direct and inverse formulas enforce their respective secant equations. Although each correction is low rank, repeatedly materializing it retains a dense matrix and therefore requires quadratic storage and arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: For the positive-definite BFGS regime, \(B_k\succ0\) or \(H_k\succ0\) and \(y_k^Ts_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicitly stored new matrix satisfies the appropriate secant equation and, under positive curvature, preserves positive definiteness.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Inverse BFGS can be expanded as a sum of \(H_k\) and rank-one outer-product terms.
The direct and inverse formulas represent mutually inverse metrics when initialized consistently and evaluated exactly.
special_cases_latex: DFP and SR1 are explicit updates obtained by replacing the BFGS correction formula.
For \(n=1\), the secant equation fixes the updated scalar curvature.
immediate_consequences_latex: The direction \(p_k=-H_kg_k\) is available by one dense matrix-vector product.
Explicit materialization costs \(\Theta(n^2)\) storage.
boundary_notes: Small or negative curvature denominators require skipping, damping, or another safeguard not included in the definition.
Floating-point updates may lose exact symmetry unless the implementation preserves it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Newton secant condition and rank-one update family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit-matrix curvature accumulation, a general rank-one secant update, and the update's nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k=\alpha_kp_k\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and let \(B_k\) approximate the Hessian. The quasi-Newton direction satisfies \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), and the updated approximation is required to satisfy \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). If \(y_k\ne B_ks_k\) and \(v^Ts_k\ne0\), then \[B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{(y_k-B_ks_k)v^T}{v^Ts_k}\] is a rank-one update satisfying the secant condition. This condition does not determine a unique update: for any \(z\) and any \(w\) with \(w^Ts_k=0\), adding \(zw^T\) preserves it. The observed curvature satisfies \(s_k^TG_ks_k\approx y_k^Ts_k\), with equality for a quadratic objective. If \(B_0=I\), the first direction is \(p_0=-g_0\), the steepest-descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton matrix must map the observed step to the observed gradient change. A general rank-one correction can enforce this secant equation, but the equation alone does not select a unique update. Gradient changes approximate directional curvature, exactly so for a quadratic objective, and an identity initial approximation gives a first steepest-descent direction.
assumptions_latex: B_k\text{ is a Hessian approximation of compatible dimension}

knowledge_statements.title: Factorized Quasi-Newton Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-root realization of the inverse BFGS update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k=L_kL_k^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), let \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), set \(\rho_k=(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)^{-1}\), and define \(V_k=I-\rho_ks_ky_k^{\mathsf T}\). Form the rectangular factor
\[
W_k=\begin{bmatrix}V_kL_k&\sqrt{\rho_k}s_k\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Compute a rank-revealing orthogonal-triangular compression of \(W_k^{\mathsf T}\), equivalently obtaining a square \(L_{k+1}\) with \(L_{k+1}L_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}=W_kW_k^{\mathsf T}\). Then
\[
H_{k+1}=V_kH_kV_k^{\mathsf T}+\rho_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}=L_{k+1}L_{k+1}^{\mathsf T},
\]
so the factorized realization preserves symmetry and positive definiteness without storing an independently updated dense inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse BFGS can be updated through a rectangular square root and compressed back to a square factor, preserving positive definiteness by construction.

notation.meaning: Square-root factor of the inverse metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The square-root inverse-BFGS realization is plausible and the algorithm content kind fits, but no source is supplied for the rectangular-factor compression. A source must also confirm the orientation of the orthogonal-triangular factorization and the construction of the square factor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorized quasi-Newton update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\succ0\) be represented by dense factors \(B_k=L_kD_kL_k^T\), where \(L_k\) is nonsingular triangular and \(D_k\) is positive diagonal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional positive-definite direct quasi-Newton metrics, with BFGS as the cited canonical case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A factorized quasi-Newton update stores factors rather than the entries of \(B_k\) and transforms them to \((L_{k+1},D_{k+1})\) so that \[L_{k+1}D_{k+1}L_{k+1}^T=B_{k+1},\qquad B_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\] where \(B_{k+1}\) is the matrix prescribed by the selected quasi-Newton formula. The search direction is computed without forming \(B_k\): solve \[L_kw=-g_k,\qquad D_kz=w,
\qquad L_k^Tp_k=z.\] For BFGS with \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), the factor update can preserve a positive diagonal \(D_{k+1}\) and can be implemented in \(O(n^2)\) operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factorized quasi-Newton update represents the direct metric by triangular and diagonal factors and updates those factors so that their product equals the matrix prescribed by the quasi-Newton formula. The direction is obtained through triangular and diagonal substitutions. The full direct matrix need not be assembled, although the factors are generally dense and still use quadratic storage. Positive pivots expose positive definiteness and can be monitored or modified for numerical stability.
assumptions_latex: The selected update preserves positive definiteness; for BFGS this includes \(s_k^Ty_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The new factors represent the updated secant metric exactly, and the step is obtained by factor substitutions without explicitly forming \(B_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A Cholesky form \(B_k=R_k^TR_k\) is an equivalent factorized realization.
Solving \(B_kp=-g_k\) is equivalent to the three substitutions shown in the definition.
special_cases_latex: Diagonal modifications to \(D_k\) can prevent division by pivots that are too small.
Rank-one update and downdate routines can implement a rank-two quasi-Newton correction through factors.
immediate_consequences_latex: Factor pivots provide direct numerical diagnostics.
Generic dense factor storage and work remain \(\Theta(n^2)\).
boundary_notes: An indefinite SR1 matrix requires an indefinite factorization rather than positive diagonal \(D_k\).
Modifying pivots changes the exact quasi-Newton matrix unless the modification is included in the model definition.

notation.meaning: Triangular-diagonal-triangular factorization of the direct metric.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Operator-only quasi-Newton realization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\) or \(H_k\) denote a quasi-Newton metric determined by a basic operator and retained correction pairs \((s_i,y_i)\), but not stored as an \(n\times n\) array.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limited-memory or compact quasi-Newton representations that expose matrix actions without dense materialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An operator-only quasi-Newton realization stores data \(\mathcal D_k\) and defines a linear action \[\mathcal A_k(v)=B_kv\quad\text{or}\quad\mathcal A_k(v)=H_kv\qquad(v\in\mathbb R^n)\] such that the action equals that of the quasi-Newton matrix generated by the retained updates, while no dense \(n\times n\) matrix is persistently formed. Typical data are a basic action \(B_k^0v\) or \(H_k^0v\), matrices of correction vectors \(S_k,Y_k\), and a small coupling matrix; alternatively, an action is evaluated by a recursion over the correction pairs. A search direction is obtained directly as \(p_k=-\mathcal A_k(g_k)\) for an inverse action or by an iterative solve using a direct action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator-only realization represents a quasi-Newton metric through the information needed to multiply by it, rather than through all of its entries. The stored state usually consists of a simple initial operator, recent secant pairs, and possibly a small dense matrix. Applying the operator by a compact product or recursion must give the same vector as multiplication by the implicitly defined quasi-Newton matrix. An inverse action immediately supplies the search direction, whereas a direct action can be used inside an iterative linear solver.
assumptions_latex: The retained update denominators and any small coupling matrix are nonsingular.
The basic metric action is defined for every vector supplied to the operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the exposed action equals \(B_kv\) or \(H_kv\) for the implicitly represented quasi-Newton metric, without dense matrix storage.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A compact form \(B_k=B_k^0+\Psi_kM_k\Psi_k^T\) defines \(B_kv=B_k^0v+\Psi_k(M_k(\Psi_k^Tv))\).
The L-BFGS two-loop recursion is an inverse-action realization.
special_cases_latex: With no retained pairs, the action is the basic operator alone.
With \(m\) retained pairs, storage is typically \(O(mn+m^2)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The represented mathematical matrix may be dense even though it is never materialized.
The realization supports large \(n\) when \(m\ll n\).
boundary_notes: An approximate action obtained by truncating arithmetic is distinct from the exact implicit metric unless the approximation is specified.
Operator-only storage does not itself guarantee positive definiteness.

notation.meaning: Stored compact data defining the metric action.
Linear operator exposed by the realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Low-Rank Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-plus-low-rank representation of successive inverse BFGS updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For accepted pairs \((s_i,y_i)\), define \(\rho_i=(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i)^{-1}\) and \(V_i=I-\rho_is_iy_i^{\mathsf T}\). After \(m\) inverse-BFGS updates from \(H_0\), repeated substitution gives
\[
H_m=(V_{m-1}\cdots V_0)H_0(V_{m-1}\cdots V_0)^{\mathsf T}+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\rho_i(V_{m-1}\cdots V_{i+1})s_is_i^{\mathsf T}(V_{m-1}\cdots V_{i+1})^{\mathsf T},
\]
where an empty product is the identity. Thus \(H_m\) is represented using elementary rank-one transformations and propagated rank-one terms; its action can be evaluated from stored secant vectors without materializing \(H_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive inverse-BFGS matrices admit a product-plus-rank-one expansion, enabling operator evaluation from stored secant pairs instead of a dense matrix.

notation.meaning: Elementary inverse-BFGS transformation for pair i.
Inverse metric after m accepted updates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed product-plus-propagated-rank-one expansion is consistent with repeated inverse-BFGS substitution and fits a representation leaf, but it lacks an inspectable source for the exact formula and operator-only interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact low-rank product representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k^0\in\mathbb S^n\), \(\Psi_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(M_k\in\mathbb S^r\), where \(r\ll n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compact representations of limited-memory direct quasi-Newton matrices; the BFGS representation is canonical.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compact low-rank product representation of a quasi-Newton matrix has the form \[B_k=B_k^0+\Psi_kM_k\Psi_k^T,\] so its action is \[B_kv=B_k^0v+\Psi_k\bigl(M_k(\Psi_k^Tv)\bigr).\] For limited-memory BFGS with \(B_k^0=\delta_kI\), retained matrices \(S_k,Y_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), and \(\Psi_k=[\delta_kS_k\;Y_k]\), the middle matrix is the negative inverse of \[\begin{bmatrix}\delta_kS_k^TS_k&L_k\\L_k^T&-D_k\end{bmatrix},\] where \((L_k)_{ij}=s_i^Ty_j\) below the diagonal and \(D_k=\operatorname{diag}(s_i^Ty_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact low-rank product writes the quasi-Newton matrix as a simple basic matrix plus a correction obtained from a tall, narrow matrix, a small dense coupling matrix, and the transpose of the tall matrix. Matrix-vector products use only the basic action, products with the narrow matrices, and a small matrix multiplication. In limited-memory BFGS, the narrow matrix is built from recent displacement and gradient-change vectors, while the coupling matrix is determined by their inner products.
assumptions_latex: The small middle matrix defining \(M_k\) is nonsingular.
For the cited BFGS form, retained pairs satisfy \(s_i^Ty_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full quasi-Newton action is computed from \(B_k^0\), \(\Psi_k\), and the small matrix \(M_k\), without forming \(B_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The correction \(B_k-B_k^0\) has rank at most \(r\).
The limited-memory BFGS representation has \(r\le2m\).
special_cases_latex: The SR1 compact form uses \(\Psi_k=Y_k-B_k^0S_k\) with a different small coupling matrix.
When \(r=0\), the represented metric is the basic matrix.
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage is \(O(nr+r^2)\).
Factorization work involving the middle matrix depends on \(r\), not directly on \(n\).
boundary_notes: Nonsingularity of the small matrix is essential for the displayed BFGS representation.
The product may represent a dense matrix despite its low-rank correction form.

notation.meaning: Tall matrix spanning the low-rank correction.
Matrices of cross and diagonal secant inner products.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Action Recursions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-loop recursion for limited-memory BFGS inverse action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given stored pairs \((s_i,y_i)\) for \(i=k-m,\ldots,k-1\), with \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i>0\), set \(\rho_i=(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i)^{-1}\) and \(q=g_k\). In descending index order compute \(\alpha_i=\rho_i s_i^{\mathsf T}q\) and replace \(q\leftarrow q-\alpha_i y_i\). Set \(r=H_k^{(0)}q\), where \(H_k^{(0)}\succ0\) has inexpensive action. In ascending index order compute \(\beta_i=\rho_i y_i^{\mathsf T}r\) and replace \(r\leftarrow r+s_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i)\). Output \(p_k=-r\); in exact arithmetic, \(r=H_kg_k\) for the limited-memory inverse-BFGS matrix defined by those pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The L-BFGS two-loop recursion applies the implicit inverse metric using stored curvature pairs and a simple initial inverse, without forming a matrix.

notation.meaning: Initial inverse metric used by the recursion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-loop recursion is stated in its standard mathematical form and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no section, algorithm, theorem, or page locator is provided. A specific authoritative L-BFGS source is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limited-memory inverse-action recursion
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the retained pairs be \((s_i,y_i)\) for \(i=k-m,\ldots,k-1\), with \(y_i^Ts_i>0\), and let \(H_k^0\succ0\) be a basic inverse metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional L-BFGS inverse actions using the canonical two-loop recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inverse-action recursion computes \(r=H_kv\) without forming \(H_k\). Set \(q=v\). For \(i=k-1,\ldots,k-m\), define \[\rho_i=(y_i^Ts_i)^{-1},\qquad \alpha_i=\rho_i s_i^Tq,\qquad q\leftarrow q-\alpha_i y_i.\] Set \(r=H_k^0q\). For \(i=k-m,\ldots,k-1\), define \[\beta_i=\rho_i y_i^Tr,\qquad r\leftarrow r+s_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i).\] On termination, \(r=H_kv\), where \(H_k\) is obtained by applying the retained inverse-BFGS updates in chronological order to \(H_k^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inverse-action recursion evaluates the product of an implicitly represented inverse quasi-Newton matrix with a vector. In the L-BFGS two-loop recursion, a backward pass removes components associated with stored gradient changes, the basic inverse metric is applied once, and a forward pass restores the displacement corrections. The result equals the action of the inverse-BFGS matrix generated from the retained pairs, but that matrix is never assembled.
assumptions_latex: Every retained curvature product \(y_i^Ts_i\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final vector satisfies \(r=H_kv\) for the inverse-BFGS metric represented by \(H_k^0\) and the retained correction pairs.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Taking \(v=\nabla f_k\) gives the L-BFGS direction \(p_k=-r\).
If \(H_k^0=\gamma_kI\), the basic action is scalar multiplication.
special_cases_latex: For \(m=0\), the result is \(H_k^0v\).
For one retained pair, the recursion equals one explicit inverse-BFGS update applied to \(v\).
immediate_consequences_latex: With vector pairs stored, the recursion uses \(O(mn)\) work and storage.
The basic metric action is isolated and may change between iterations.
boundary_notes: The order of the two passes is part of the definition and cannot be interchanged.
Pairs with unsafe curvature denominators must be rejected or modified before entering the recursion.

notation.meaning: Scalar coefficients generated by the two recursion passes.
Basic inverse metric used before the retained updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Resource-complexity profile of a quasi-Newton realization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) be the ambient dimension and \(m\) the number of retained secant pairs in a limited-memory realization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and persistent-storage measures for one quasi-Newton update and one metric action, excluding objective and gradient evaluation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The resource-complexity profile of a quasi-Newton realization \(\mathfrak R\) is \[\mathcal C(\mathfrak R;n,m)=\bigl(M_{\rm store},W_{\rm update},W_{\rm action},W_{\rm solve}\bigr),\] where \(M_{\rm store}\) is the number of persistent scalar words, \(W_{\rm update}\) is arithmetic to incorporate new secant data, \(W_{\rm action}\) is arithmetic for one product by the represented metric, and \(W_{\rm solve}\) is arithmetic for a required direct-metric solve. Generic dense inverse BFGS has \(M_{\rm store}=\Theta(n^2)\) and \(W_{\rm update}=W_{\rm action}=\Theta(n^2)\). L-BFGS with \(m\) pairs has \(M_{\rm store}=\Theta(mn)\) and two-loop action \(W_{\rm action}=4mn+O(n)\) multiplications when the basic inverse metric is diagonal. Compact direct BFGS has update work approximately \(2mn+O(m^3)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasi-Newton resource complexity is a tuple rather than a single operation count. It separately measures persistent memory, incorporation of new curvature information, application of the metric, and any solve needed to obtain a step. This separation distinguishes dense inverse storage, dense direct factorization, limited-memory recursions, and compact low-rank products. Function and gradient evaluations are excluded because their costs depend on the optimization problem rather than only on the metric realization.
assumptions_latex: Scalar arithmetic and storage words are counted in the standard sequential model.
The memory parameter satisfies \(m\ll n\) when limited-memory asymptotics are invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The realization is assigned the four-component profile \(\mathcal C\), with dense storage scaling quadratically in \(n\) and limited-memory storage scaling linearly in \(mn\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A total per-iteration count may be formed by adding the update, action, and solve terms actually invoked by an algorithm.
special_cases_latex: For diagonal \(H_k^0\), the L-BFGS two-loop recursion adds \(n\) multiplications to its \(4mn\) pair-processing cost.
For fixed \(m\), limited-memory storage and action are linear in \(n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two mathematically identical metrics can have different resource profiles under different realizations.
Reporting only update rank does not determine storage complexity.
boundary_notes: Communication, cache behavior, parallelism, and finite-precision monitoring are not represented by these scalar counts.
Objective and derivative evaluation costs must be reported separately.

notation.meaning: Arithmetic cost of one metric-vector product.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Update Cost Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage costs for explicit dense rank-two updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the real-arithmetic RAM model, suppose an \(n\times n\) quasi-Newton matrix is stored explicitly and no exploitable sparsity or structure is assumed. A BFGS update requires forming \(B_ks_k\), two inner products, and two dense symmetric rank-one modifications. Consequently one update uses \(\Theta(n^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(\Theta(n^2)\) stored scalars. Applying the updated matrix to a vector also costs \(\Theta(n^2)\). These bounds concern metric maintenance and multiplication; solving a fresh unstructured dense linear system by factorization generally requires \(\Theta(n^3)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit unstructured quasi-Newton matrix needs quadratic storage and quadratic update or multiplication work; a fresh dense factorization is cubic.
assumptions_latex: The metric is an explicit dense \(n\times n\) matrix.
Scalar arithmetic and memory accesses have unit cost.

notation.meaning: Number of stored scalar entries up to constant factors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic dense-update, storage, and matrix-vector bounds are appropriate complexity claims under the stated model, and the separate cubic-factorization qualification is reasonable. No source with a specific complexity locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory Cost Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource bounds for an L-BFGS inverse action with m stored pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\le n\) curvature pairs of length \(n\) be retained, and suppose applying the initial inverse metric \(H_k^{(0)}\) costs \(T_0(n)\) work and \(S_0(n)\) storage. The two-loop L-BFGS recursion performs a constant number of vector inner products and saxpy operations per pair. Therefore one inverse action costs \(\Theta(mn)+T_0(n)\) arithmetic operations and the representation occupies \(\Theta(mn)+S_0(n)\) scalars. When \(H_k^{(0)}=\gamma_k I\), both additional terms are \(\Theta(n)\), so work and storage are \(\Theta(mn)\); for fixed \(m\), both are linear in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping m secant pairs makes L-BFGS inverse application and storage proportional to mn, and therefore linear in dimension when m is fixed.
assumptions_latex: Exactly \(m\) length-\(n\) secant pairs are stored.
The computation uses the two-loop recursion.
Scalar vector operations have unit cost per entry.

notation.meaning: Work and storage costs of the initial inverse metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The L-BFGS work and storage bounds match the stated two-loop model and the complexity-bound kind fits the cost-regime leaf, but the exact asymptotic claims require a specific source locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limited-memory quasi-Newton cost regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(m\in\mathbb N\) be fixed independently of \(n\), and define \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\), and \(\rho_i=(y_i^Ts_i)^{-1}\) for accepted pairs with \(y_i^Ts_i>0\). Let \(H_k^0\) be diagonal or otherwise applicable in \(O(n)\) work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic L-BFGS realization with fixed memory and an inexpensive base metric; objective and gradient evaluation costs are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The limited-memory cost regime is the class of quasi-Newton realizations that retain at iteration \(k\) only the pairs \(\{(s_i,y_i):i=\max\{0,k-m\},\ldots,k-1\}\), represent \(H_k\) implicitly, and compute \(H_kv\) by the two-loop recursion. Its stored numerical data occupy \(O(mn)\) scalars, and one application of \(H_k\) requires \(4mn+O(n)\) scalar multiplications when \(H_k^0\) is diagonal. Thus, for fixed \(m\), metric storage and application both scale linearly in \(n\), while no dense \(n\times n\) matrix is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton realization is in the limited-memory cost regime when it keeps only the most recent fixed number m of displacement and gradient-difference pairs and applies the resulting inverse-metric approximation through the L-BFGS two-loop recursion. It stores O(mn) scalars and, with a diagonal base metric, applies the metric in 4mn plus O(n) multiplications. For fixed m, both costs are linear in the dimension and no dense matrix is stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{storage}(H_k)=O(mn),\qquad \operatorname{cost}(H_kv)=4mn+O(n)=O(mn),\] with \(m\) fixed and \(H_k\) represented by at most \(m\) correction pairs.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed \(m\), the asymptotic resource bounds are \(\operatorname{storage}(H_k)=O(n)\) and \(\operatorname{cost}(H_kv)=O(n)\).
The metric is an implicit operator determined by \(H_k^0\) and the retained correction pairs rather than an explicitly stored dense matrix.
special_cases_latex: A standard base metric is \(H_k^0=\gamma_k I\), where \(\gamma_k=(s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})/(y_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})\).
During the first \(m-1\) iterations, retaining every available pair reproduces full BFGS when the same base matrix is used.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing \(m\) increases both storage and recursion work linearly in \(m\).
The regime is suitable when storing a dense matrix would require \(\Theta(n^2)\) scalars.
boundary_notes: The bound excludes objective and gradient evaluations and any non-linear-cost application of \(H_k^0\).
Limited memory does not by itself guarantee a dimension-independent iteration count or superlinear convergence.
If \(m\) grows proportionally to \(n\), the fixed-memory linear-cost interpretation no longer applies.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of retained curvature pairs.
Base inverse-metric operator used by the two-loop recursion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparsity-preserving quasi-Newton cost regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and let \(\Omega\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\) be a known symmetric structural pattern containing every potentially nonzero Hessian entry. Let \(\mathbb S_\Omega^n=\{B\in\mathbb S^n:B_{ij}=0\text{ for }(i,j)\notin\Omega\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sparse Hessian approximation; the definition concerns preservation and exploitation of a prescribed structural pattern, not limited-memory truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The structure-exploiting cost regime consists of quasi-Newton realizations whose metric approximations remain in \(\mathbb S_\Omega^n\) and whose update and application costs are governed by the stored pattern rather than by \(n^2\) dense entries. A canonical sparse secant update is any solution of \[B_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{B\in\mathbb S_\Omega^n}\|B-B_k\|_F^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Bs_k=y_k.\] If \(q=|\Omega|\), explicit structural storage is \(O(q)\); application of a stored sparse \(B_k\) costs \(O(q)\), subject to the chosen sparse representation. The defining distinction is exact structural admissibility \(B_k\in\mathbb S_\Omega^n\), not merely the use of fewer historical pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton realization is in the structure-exploiting cost regime when every metric approximation obeys a known Hessian sparsity pattern and storage and matrix-vector work are measured by the number q of allowed structural entries. The canonical sparse least-change update minimizes Frobenius change from the previous matrix subject to symmetry, the prescribed zeros, and the secant equation. Stored sparse application then uses O(q) storage and work, although computing the update can require solving a sparse linear system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Structural preservation is the invariant \((B_k)_{ij}=0\) for every \((i,j)\notin\Omega\) and every iteration \(k\).
The admissible metric space is the linear subspace \(\mathbb S_\Omega^n\), and each update is constrained to this subspace.
special_cases_latex: For a banded pattern with fixed bandwidth, \(|\Omega|=O(n)\), so storage and sparse matrix-vector multiplication are linear in \(n\).
A relaxed multisecant variant minimizes \(\|BS_k-Y_k\|_F^2\) over \(B\in\mathbb S_\Omega^n\) instead of imposing one exact secant equation.
immediate_consequences_latex: The regime can be subquadratic whenever \(|\Omega|=o(n^2)\).
Sparse structural preservation does not imply positive definiteness or good conditioning.
boundary_notes: The sparse least-change subproblem may be infeasible for an incompatible exact secant condition.
The update itself may require a sparse linear solve whose cost depends on fill and factorization structure.
This definition excludes implicit low-rank limited-memory representations that do not preserve \(\Omega\).

notation.meaning: Prescribed symmetric set of potentially nonzero Hessian indices.
Symmetric matrices supported on the pattern Ω.

children.title: Sparse Update Storage Costs
children.top_down_role: Memory requirements associated with sparse matrix-update representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Update Storage Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage bound for explicitly retained sparse BFGS correction factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\) be stored sparsely with \(z_k=\operatorname{nnz}(B_k)\), and write the direct BFGS correction as \(-u_ku_k^{\mathsf T}/\delta_k+y_ky_k^{\mathsf T}/\eta_k\), where \(u_k=B_ks_k\), \(\delta_k=s_k^{\mathsf T}u_k\), and \(\eta_k=s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\). If the correction is stored as vectors rather than expanded outer products, the additional storage is \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(u_k)+\operatorname{nnz}(y_k))\), giving total storage \(O(z_k+\operatorname{nnz}(u_k)+\operatorname{nnz}(y_k))\). Explicitly assembling the correction may instead require up to \(O(|\operatorname{supp}(u_k)|^2+|\operatorname{supp}(y_k)|^2)\) entries before duplicate merging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse vector-factor storage is linear in the factor nonzeros, whereas explicitly expanding sparse outer products can require quadratic storage in their support sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is stored in a sparse format.
The BFGS correction is retained either as vector factors or expanded outer products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Factor storage is \(O(z_k+\operatorname{nnz}(u_k)+\operatorname{nnz}(y_k))\), while expansion can be quadratic in support size.

notation.meaning: Number of stored nonzeros in the current metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between factor storage and expanded outer-product storage is plausible and appropriately scoped, but the bounds depend on sparse storage and duplicate-merging conventions. No source is provided to validate those conventions or bounds.

children.title: Sparse Update Work Costs
children.top_down_role: Computational costs associated with sparse update application.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Update Work Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic bound for sparse factor-form BFGS maintenance and application.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k\) have \(z_k\) stored nonzeros, let \(u_k=B_ks_k\), and retain the BFGS correction in factor form. In a sparse arithmetic model, computing \(u_k\) costs \(O(z_k)\) operations, while the required inner products cost \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(s_k)+\operatorname{nnz}(y_k)+\operatorname{nnz}(u_k))\). Once the factors and denominators are stored, applying
\[
B_{k+1}v=B_kv-u_k\frac{u_k^{\mathsf T}v}{s_k^{\mathsf T}u_k}+y_k\frac{y_k^{\mathsf T}v}{s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}
\]
costs \(O(z_k+\operatorname{nnz}(u_k)+\operatorname{nnz}(y_k))\). This bound excludes index-management overhead and any work used to assemble or refactor a filled matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With corrections kept as sparse factors, update preparation and matrix-vector application scale with existing matrix nonzeros and correction-vector nonzeros.
assumptions_latex: The rank-two correction remains in factor form.
Sparse dot products visit only stored indices.

notation.meaning: Number of nonzeros stored for the base metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factor-form application bound is plausible under the stated sparse-arithmetic assumptions, but its treatment of sparse dot products and excluded index-management overhead is model dependent. A specific sparse-complexity source is required.

children.title: Structured Representation Costs
children.top_down_role: Storage and work consequences of preserving exploitable problem structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Representation Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Costs of a base metric plus symmetric low-rank correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a quasi-Newton metric is represented as
\[
B=B_0+UMU^{\mathsf T},
\]
where \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), \(M\in\mathbb{S}^r\), and the base operator \(B_0\) has application cost \(T_0(n)\) and storage cost \(S_0(n)\). Storing the representation requires \(S_0(n)+O(nr+r^2)\) scalars. Computing \(Bv=B_0v+U(M(U^{\mathsf T}v))\) requires \(T_0(n)+O(nr+r^2)\) arithmetic operations. If \(M\) is diagonal or otherwise applicable in \(O(r)\) work, the application bound improves to \(T_0(n)+O(nr)\). These costs exclude construction or factorization of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base operator plus rank-r symmetric correction needs nr plus r-squared storage and comparable application work, with cheaper action when the core is simple.

notation.meaning: Tall correction basis or factor matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The storage and application bounds follow the stated base-plus-low-rank representation and the complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the exact bounds or exclusions.

children.title: Sparsity-Fill Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cost degradation caused by loss of the intended sparsity pattern.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Fill Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when a direct BFGS update loses matrix sparsity and dense costs become unavoidable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{n}\) be sparse and let nonzero \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\) satisfy \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\). The direct BFGS update is \[B_{+}=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.\] If \(Bs\) and \(y\) have support of order \(n\), their outer products are generically dense; absent exact cancellations or an explicitly closed sparsity pattern, \(B_{+}\) therefore has order \(n^{2}\) nonzeros. Explicit sparse-matrix storage and multiplication then cross to \(\Omega(n^{2})\) storage and work per update or product. Avoiding this boundary requires a structured representation, restricted update, or sparsification rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense curvature vectors make the BFGS outer products generically dense, so explicit sparse storage and work become quadratic unless structure or sparsification is imposed.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{n}\) is stored explicitly with a sparse pattern.
No cancellation or pattern closure is assumed beyond the displayed update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(B_{+})=\Theta(n^{2})\) generically, implying \(\Omega(n^{2})\) explicit storage and arithmetic.

notation.meaning: number of stored nonzero entries of B

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the generic Θ(n²) fill and resulting arithmetic claims require a source defining the asymptotic support and genericity assumptions. In particular, “support of order n,” absence of cancellation, and the cost model for forming versus multiplying by the updated matrix must be made source-inspectable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reliability monitor for quasi-Newton metrics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) approximate \(\nabla^2f(x_k)\), let \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) when nonsingular, and let \((s_k,y_k)\) be a nonzero curvature pair. Fix user thresholds \(0<\eta\leq1\), \(0<\underline\mu\leq\overline\mu\), and \(1\leq\overline\kappa<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional monitoring definition. Threshold selection and the corrective action taken after an alarm are external controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A metric-reliability monitor is the diagnostic map \[\mathcal R_k=(\operatorname{spd}_k,\kappa_k,c_k,\mu_k,
u_k),\] where \(\operatorname{spd}_k=1\) exactly when \(B_k\succ0\), \(\kappa_k=\|B_k\|_2\|B_k^{-1}\|_2\) when \(B_k\succ0\), \(c_k=s_k^Ty_k/(\|s_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2)\), \(\mu_k=s_k^Ty_k/\|s_k\|_2^2\), and \(
u_k=\|y_k\|_2^2/(s_k^Ty_k)\) when the denominators are positive. The metric-pair state is declared reliable precisely when \[B_k\succ0,\quad \kappa_k\leq\overline\kappa,\quad c_k\geq\eta,\quad \underline\mu\leq\mu_k\leq\overline\mu,\quad 
u_k\leq\overline\mu.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric-reliability monitor records positive definiteness and spectral conditioning of the current metric together with normalized alignment and two directional-curvature ratios for the latest correction pair. Given declared thresholds, the state is reliable exactly when the matrix is positive definite, its condition number is acceptable, and the pair has sufficiently positive, nondegenerate, and bounded curvature. The monitor diagnoses a state; it does not itself prescribe skipping, damping, resetting, or regularization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(B_k\succ0\), bounded conditioning is equivalent to the existence of \(0<\ell_k\leq u_k\) with \(\ell_k I\preceq B_k\preceq u_kI\) and \(u_k/\ell_k\leq\overline\kappa\).
The positivity test \(s_k^Ty_k>0\) is necessary for an SPD matrix satisfying \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
special_cases_latex: Under strong convexity bounds \(mI\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq MI\) along the step, the exact pair satisfies \(\mu_k\geq m\) and \(\nu_k\leq M\).
For BFGS with \(H_k\succ0\) and \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), the updated inverse metric remains positive definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of \(c_k\geq\eta\) identifies a nearly orthogonal or weakly informative pair.
A large \(\kappa_k\) identifies a metric capable of producing poorly scaled directions even when it remains positive definite.
boundary_notes: The numerical thresholds are algorithm parameters, not universal constants.
Computing \(\kappa_k\) exactly can be too expensive; practical implementations may monitor estimates.
The definition does not claim that passing the monitor guarantees convergence.

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the positive-definite metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial Metric Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scale-compatible positive-definite initialization for direct and inverse quasi-Newton metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quasi-Newton iteration in \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\), choose \(B_{0}=\gamma_{B}I\) with \(\gamma_{B}>0\) and set \(H_{0}=B_{0}^{-1}=\gamma_{B}^{-1}I\). Then both initial metrics are symmetric positive definite, and the direction \(p_{0}=-H_{0}g_{0}\) is a descent direction whenever \(g_{0}\ne0\). If a curvature pair \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\) satisfies \(y\ne0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\), the scalar \[\gamma_{H}=\frac{s^{\mathsf T}y}{y^{\mathsf T}y}\] uniquely minimizes \(\lVert \gamma y-s\rVert_{2}^{2}\) over \(\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\). One may therefore initialize \(H_{0}=\gamma_{H}I\) and its reciprocal direct metric \(B_{0}=\gamma_{H}^{-1}I\), after clipping \(\gamma_{H}\) to a prescribed interval contained in \((0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use mutually inverse positive scaled identities. A reliable curvature pair can set the inverse-metric scale by the scalar least-squares fit of Hy to s, with the resulting positive scale clipped to safe bounds.
assumptions_latex: Any clipping interval is contained in \((0,\infty)\).

notation.meaning: scalar inverse-metric scale estimated from a curvature pair

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Initial inverse-metric selection and secant scaling
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at a starting point \(x_0\), let \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), and suppose a first accepted pair \((s_0,y_0)\) satisfies \(s_0^Ty_0>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional BFGS or L-BFGS initialization using a symmetric positive-definite inverse-Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An initial metric selection is a choice \(H_0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) defining the first quasi-Newton direction \(p_0=-H_0g_0\). Canonical choices are \(H_0=I\), \(H_0=\beta I\) with \(\beta>0\), or an SPD problem-derived approximation to \(\nabla^2f(x_0)^{-1}\). After the first accepted curvature pair, the canonical scalar secant scaling replaces a provisional identity metric by \[H_0\leftarrow\gamma_0I,\qquad \gamma_0=\frac{y_0^Ts_0}{y_0^Ty_0}>0,\] before forming \(H_1\). In limited-memory BFGS the analogous per-iteration base metric is \(H_k^0=\gamma_kI\), with \(\gamma_k=(s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})/(y_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initial metric selection chooses a symmetric positive-definite inverse-Hessian approximation that defines the first search direction. Standard selections are the identity, a positive scalar multiple of it, or an available problem-based inverse-Hessian approximation. Once the first positive-curvature pair is available, scalar secant scaling chooses the identity multiple given by the pair’s curvature divided by the squared gradient change. L-BFGS uses the same rule for its base metric at later iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[H_0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n,\quad p_0=-H_0\nabla f(x_0),\quad H_k^0=\frac{s_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}}{y_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}}I\ \text{when pair scaling is used}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Choosing \(H_0=\beta I\) with \(\beta>0\) gives a scaled steepest-descent first direction.
For \(\gamma=(s^Ty)/(y^Ty)\), the reciprocal \(\gamma^{-1}\) is the Rayleigh quotient \((y^Ty)/(s^Ty)\) associated with the observed curvature pair.
special_cases_latex: A requested first-step norm \(\delta>0\) can be imposed by \(H_0=\delta\|g_0\|_2^{-1}I\), yielding \(\|p_0\|_2=\delta\).
Problem structure may supply an SPD finite-difference or preconditioning approximation instead of a scalar identity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(H_0\) makes \(-H_0g_0\) a descent direction whenever \(g_0\neq0\).
Pair scaling preserves positive definiteness whenever \(s_0^Ty_0>0\) and \(y_0\neq0\).
boundary_notes: No scalar choice is uniformly best for all objectives or variable scalings.
The pair-scaled value is unavailable before a nonzero accepted pair has been observed.
An indefinite initial approximation is outside this positive-definite selection regime.

notation.meaning: Scalar base-metric scaling estimated from the most recent pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Monitoring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A spectral reliability test for a symmetric positive-definite quasi-Newton metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_{k}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{n}\), and define \[\kappa_{2}(B_{k})=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(B_{k})}{\lambda_{\min}(B_{k})}.\] Given thresholds \(0<m\le M<\infty\), declare the metric spectrally reliable when \[m\le\lambda_{\min}(B_{k})\le\lambda_{\max}(B_{k})\le M,\] equivalently when \(mI\preceq B_{k}\preceq MI\). If exact eigenvalues are unavailable, let \(\underline\lambda_{k}\) and \(\overline\lambda_{k}\) be certified bounds satisfying \(\underline\lambda_{k}\le\lambda_{\min}(B_{k})\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(B_{k})\le\overline\lambda_{k}\). The conservative test accepts only if \(\underline\lambda_{k}\ge m\) and \(\overline\lambda_{k}\le M\); failure may trigger rejection, damping, regularization, or reinitialization according to the surrounding algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept the metric only when its exact spectrum, or certified enclosing bounds for it, lies inside the prescribed positive interval; otherwise invoke the algorithm’s repair or restart policy.
assumptions_latex: Approximate monitoring uses certified bounds \(\underline\lambda_{k}\le\lambda_{\min}(B_{k})\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(B_{k})\le\overline\lambda_{k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies \(mI\preceq B_{k}\preceq MI\) and hence \(\kappa_{2}(B_{k})\le M/m\).

notation.meaning: certified lower and upper spectral bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral conditioning monitor for a variable metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\), and use the Euclidean operator norm. Fix finite thresholds \(0<\underline\lambda\leq\overline\lambda\) and \(\overline\kappa\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional spectral definition; eigenvalue or norm estimates may replace exact quantities in implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditioning monitor of the quasi-Newton metric is the triple \[\mathcal C_k=\bigl(\lambda_{\min}(B_k),\lambda_{\max}(B_k),\kappa_2(B_k)\bigr),\qquad \kappa_2(B_k)=\|B_k\|_2\|B_k^{-1}\|_2=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(B_k)}{\lambda_{\min}(B_k)}.\] The metric is uniformly well conditioned on an index set \(K\) when there exist constants \(0<\ell\leq u<\infty\) such that \(\ell I\preceq B_k\preceq uI\) for every \(k\in K\). A threshold monitor accepts iteration \(k\) exactly when \(\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\geq\underline\lambda\), \(\lambda_{\max}(B_k)\leq\overline\lambda\), and \(\kappa_2(B_k)\leq\overline\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning monitoring tracks the smallest and largest eigenvalues of a positive-definite metric and their ratio, its spectral condition number. Uniform conditioning means that all monitored metrics lie between two fixed positive scalar multiples of the identity. A thresholded monitor accepts a metric only when its smallest eigenvalue is not too small, its largest is not too large, and its eigenvalue ratio is bounded.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For SPD \(B_k\), \(\kappa_2(B_k)=\lambda_{\max}(B_k)/\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\).
Uniform bounds \(\ell I\preceq B_k\preceq uI\) imply \(u^{-1}I\preceq H_k\preceq\ell^{-1}I\) and \(\kappa_2(H_k)=\kappa_2(B_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(B_k=\beta_kI\) with \(\beta_k>0\), \(\kappa_2(B_k)=1\).
A diagonal metric has \(\kappa_2(B_k)=\max_i(B_k)_{ii}/\min_i(B_k)_{ii}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniformly bounded SPD metrics keep the quasi-Newton search direction uniformly separated from orthogonality to the negative gradient.
A positive but very small \(\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\) signals near singularity even though definiteness has not been lost.
boundary_notes: Condition-number control alone does not control absolute metric scale; the eigenvalue bounds supply that information.
The definition applies to SPD metrics; indefinite matrices require a different conditioning and inertia monitor.
Exact spectral computation may cost more than the quasi-Newton iteration and is not required by the mathematical definition.

notation.meaning: Uniform lower and upper spectral bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Pair Quality Monitoring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scale-free acceptance test for secant pairs used by positive-definite updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero displacement and gradient-difference vectors \(s_{k},y_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), define the normalized curvature quality \[q_{k}=\frac{s_{k}^{\mathsf T}y_{k}}{\lVert s_{k}\rVert_{2}\lVert y_{k}\rVert_{2}}.\] Given \(\eta\in(0,1)\), accept the pair for an undamped positive-definite secant update only if \(q_{k}\ge\eta\), equivalently \(s_{k}^{\mathsf T}y_{k}\ge\eta\lVert s_{k}\rVert_{2}\lVert y_{k}\rVert_{2}\). If the test fails, skip, damp, or regularize the pair. The threshold simultaneously enforces positive curvature and excludes nearly orthogonal pairs whose secant information is numerically weak.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize the secant curvature by both vector norms and accept only sufficiently positive, non-negligible curvature pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies \(s_{k}^{\mathsf T}y_{k}>0\) and \(q_{k}\) is bounded away from zero.

The curvature-pair quality monitor assigns \[c_k= rac{s_k^Ty_k}{\|s_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2},\qquad \mu_k= rac{s_k^Ty_k}{\|s_k\|_2^2},\qquad

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature-pair quality monitoring evaluates a step and gradient-difference pair through its inner product, normalized alignment, curvature per squared step length, and squared gradient change per curvature. A pair is admissible when its curvature is positive, its vectors are not nearly orthogonal, and the two curvature scales stay within prescribed bounds. These requirements exclude negative, nearly singular, or excessively scaled information before it enters a positive-definite secant update.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The alignment condition is \(s_k^Ty_k\geq\eta\|s_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2\).
If \(y_k=\bar G_ks_k\) for an average Hessian satisfying \(mI\preceq\bar G_k\preceq MI\), then \(\mu_k\geq m\) and \(\nu_k\leq M\).
special_cases_latex: A Wolfe line search with a descent direction guarantees \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), but it need not satisfy stronger user-selected quality thresholds.
For the exact pair of a quadratic \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx\), \(y_k=As_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An accepted pair permits the BFGS coefficient \(\rho_k=(s_k^Ty_k)^{-1}\) to be formed with positive denominator.
Failure of the positivity condition rules out any SPD matrix satisfying \(Bs_k=y_k\).
boundary_notes: The stronger normalized thresholds are safeguards, not consequences of the Wolfe conditions alone.
The definition does not prescribe whether a rejected pair is skipped, damped, or replaced.
Noisy or stochastic gradients may require uncertainty-aware thresholds not covered here.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classification of quasi-Newton guarantee families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an algorithm generate iterates \(x_k\), steps \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), gradient differences \(y_k\), and symmetric Hessian approximations \(B_k\) or inverse approximations \(H_k\). Let \(x_*\) denote a stationary point or minimizer when one exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taxonomic definition for deterministic smooth finite-dimensional quasi-Newton analysis; individual guarantees require their own hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quasi-Newton guarantee family of an update-and-globalization pair is the ordered collection \(\mathfrak G=(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{alg}},\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{quad}},\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{glob}},\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{loc}})\), where: \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{alg}}\) contains invariants such as symmetry, secant satisfaction, and positive definiteness; \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{quad}}\) contains exact-arithmetic statements on strongly convex quadratics, including hereditary secant equations, conjugate-gradient equivalence, and finite termination; \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{glob}}\) contains conclusions valid from an arbitrary admitted starting point, such as \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\) or \(x_k\to x_*\); and \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) contains neighborhood-dependent convergence orders, such as Q-superlinear convergence \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|/\|x_k-x_*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasi-Newton guarantees are classified into four distinct families. Algebraic guarantees preserve matrix and secant properties. Quadratic-model guarantees describe exact behavior on strongly convex quadratics. Global guarantees state stationarity or iterate convergence from any starting point admitted by their assumptions. Local guarantees describe the rate after iterates enter a neighborhood of a regular solution. A method has a guarantee profile consisting of the supported members of these four classes; membership in one class does not imply membership in another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak G=\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{alg}}\times\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{quad}}\times\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{glob}}\times\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{loc}},\] with every component indexed by its explicit objective, line-search, update, arithmetic, and initialization hypotheses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A guarantee profile is a map assigning each result to one of the four scopes \(\{\mathrm{algebraic},\mathrm{quadratic},\mathrm{global},\mathrm{local}\}\) together with its hypotheses.
Q-superlinear local convergence means \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|/\|x_k-x_*\|=0\).
special_cases_latex: BFGS with positive curvature has symmetry and positive-definiteness preservation in \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{alg}}\).
The Broyden class with exact line searches on an SPD quadratic has finite termination and hereditary exactness in \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{quad}}\).
BFGS under uniform convexity on the initial level set has iterate convergence in \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{glob}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A quadratic finite-termination statement cannot be reported as a global nonlinear convergence result.
An algebraically valid update may lack a global or local convergence guarantee without globalization and regularity assumptions.
boundary_notes: The classification is not itself a convergence theorem.
Stochastic, nonsmooth, constrained, and infinite-dimensional variants require additional guarantee categories or modified definitions.
Finite-precision behavior is excluded from exact-arithmetic quadratic guarantees unless explicitly stated.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraically preserving secant update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be an admissible matrix class, let \((s_k,y_k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) with \(s_k\neq0\), and let \(U:\mathcal A\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be an update map on its domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact arithmetic; the preserved class may encode symmetry, definiteness, sparsity, or another explicitly declared invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An update \(U\) obeys an algebraic preservation principle for \(\mathcal A\) and the direct secant relation when, for every admissible \(B\in\mathcal A\) and pair in its update domain, \[U(B,s,y)\in\mathcal A,\qquad U(B,s,y)s=y.\] For an inverse update \(V\), the corresponding conditions are \(V(H,s,y)\in\mathcal A\) and \(V(H,s,y)y=s\). Joint preservation of several invariants means that \(\mathcal A\) is their intersection. For example, direct BFGS preserves \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\) when \(s^Ty>0\), whereas SR1 preserves symmetry when defined but does not generally preserve positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algebraic preservation principle specifies an admissible class of matrices and requires every defined update to remain in that class while satisfying the new secant equation. Multiple invariants are represented by intersecting their admissible classes. The inverse formulation exchanges the roles of displacement and gradient change. Positive curvature is the compatibility condition for preserving positive definiteness together with an exact secant relation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For inverse metrics, \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\) replaces \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
Preservation of symmetry and positive definiteness is closure of the update on \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
special_cases_latex: BFGS and DFP are rank-two symmetric secant updates that preserve positive definiteness under \(s_k^Ty_k>0\).
SR1 is the unique symmetric rank-one secant update when its denominator is nonzero, but its admissible preserved class is generally \(\mathbb S^n\), not \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B_{k+1}\succ0\) and \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), then necessarily \(s_k^Ty_k>0\).
Closure on \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\) makes every nonstationary direction \(-B_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) a descent direction.
boundary_notes: Preserving an invariant does not establish approximation accuracy or convergence.
A skipped update preserves the old matrix but generally does not satisfy the new secant equation.
Finite-precision implementations may violate exact symmetry or secant satisfaction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint preservation of symmetry and the secant equation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(s_k\neq0\), and let \(B_{k+1}=U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\) be a defined quasi-Newton update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact-arithmetic direct Hessian approximation; the inverse form is included as an equivalent formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The update \(U\) jointly preserves symmetry and the secant relation when, for every admissible symmetric input and every pair in its domain, \[B_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^T,\qquad B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.\] Equivalently, its correction \(E_k=B_{k+1}-B_k\) is symmetric and satisfies \(E_ks_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). For inverse approximations, joint preservation means \(H_{k+1}=H_{k+1}^T\) and \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\). The property constrains the update on the observed direction but leaves its action on complementary directions underdetermined unless an additional rank, variational, or family-selection condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton update jointly preserves symmetry and secant information when the new matrix is symmetric and maps the latest displacement exactly to the latest gradient change. The same condition can be stated for the correction matrix: it is symmetric and maps the step to the current secant residual. In inverse form, the updated inverse metric maps the gradient change to the displacement. These requirements alone generally do not determine a unique matrix.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[E_k=E_k^T,\qquad E_ks_k=y_k-B_ks_k,\qquad B_{k+1}=B_k+E_k.\]
For an invertible updated matrix, \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) is equivalent to \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\) with \(H_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: The BFGS and DFP corrections are symmetric rank-two realizations of the property.
When \((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k\neq0\), SR1 is the symmetric rank-one realization \(B_{k+1}=B_k+(y_k-B_ks_k)(y_k-B_ks_k)^T/((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The updated quadratic model has symmetric curvature and matches the observed gradient change along \(s_k\).
For \(n>1\), symmetry plus one secant equation generally leaves multiple admissible updates.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness is not part of this joint property.
If the SR1 denominator vanishes while the secant residual is nonzero, no symmetric rank-one correction satisfies the new secant equation.
The definition enforces only the latest secant equation, not hereditary satisfaction of earlier equations.

notation.meaning: Symmetric correction to the current Hessian approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry inheritance under the direct BFGS rank-two correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\), and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\) satisfy \(s^{\mathsf T}Bs\ne0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\). For the direct BFGS update \[B_{+}=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y},\] both correction terms are symmetric because \(Bss^{\mathsf T}B=(Bs)(Bs)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(yy^{\mathsf T}\) are symmetric outer products. Consequently \(B_{+}\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\). No positive-definiteness assumption is required solely for this symmetry conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric direct metric remains symmetric after BFGS because both rank-one terms in its rank-two correction are symmetric.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Preservation Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit symmetric correction satisfying one prescribed secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\), let \(s\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminus\{0\}\), and set \(r=y-Bs\). The correction \[E=\frac{rs^{\mathsf T}+sr^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}s}-\frac{r^{\mathsf T}s}{(s^{\mathsf T}s)^{2}}ss^{\mathsf T}\] is symmetric and satisfies \(Es=r\). Hence \(B_{+}=B+E\) is symmetric and obeys \(B_{+}s=y\). Therefore symmetry and a single secant equation are algebraically compatible for every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\); additional requirements such as positive definiteness impose further curvature conditions not needed for this compatibility result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any nonzero displacement and any target vector, an explicit symmetric rank-two correction produces a symmetric matrix satisfying the secant equation.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definiteness Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definiteness of the direct BFGS update under the curvature condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{n}\), let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and suppose \(s\ne0\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}y>0\). Define \[B_{+}=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{s^{\mathsf T}y}.\] Then \(B_{+}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{n}\). In particular, the positive curvature inequality makes both denominators positive and ensures that the BFGS correction preserves a valid positive-definite Hessian metric while simultaneously satisfying the secant equation \(B_{+}s=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite direct metric remains positive definite after BFGS whenever the accepted curvature pair has positive inner product.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-definiteness-preserving secant update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\) update direct Hessian approximations in \(\mathbb S^n\), and let its admissible curvature pairs satisfy \(s^Ty>0\). Let \(V\) denote the analogous inverse update when used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact arithmetic for undamped BFGS or DFP-type updates with strictly positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An update is positive-definiteness preserving when \[B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\ \text{and}\ s^Ty>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad U(B,s,y)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n.\] For inverse metrics, \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(s^Ty>0\) must imply \(V(H,s,y)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). The BFGS inverse update \[V(H,s,y)=(I-\rho sy^T)H(I-\rho ys^T)+\rho ss^T,\qquad \rho=(s^Ty)^{-1},\] has this property and satisfies \(V(H,s,y)y=s\). The strict curvature inequality is also necessary for any SPD matrix satisfying the corresponding exact secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant update preserves positive definiteness if every positive-definite input matrix and every strictly positive-curvature pair produce a positive-definite output. The definition applies separately to Hessian and inverse-Hessian forms. The BFGS inverse formula is the canonical example: under positive curvature it remains symmetric positive definite and satisfies the inverse secant equation. Positive curvature is necessary for any positive-definite exact secant matrix.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Positive definiteness means \(z^TU(B,s,y)z>0\) for every \(z\neq0\).
If \(B_{k+1}\succ0\), then \(H_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^{-1}\succ0\), and conversely.
special_cases_latex: Both BFGS and DFP preserve positive definiteness under \(s^Ty>0\).
A Wolfe line search along a descent direction supplies \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), making the undamped BFGS update admissible.
immediate_consequences_latex:
If \(H_k\succ0\) and \(
abla f(x_k)
eq0\), then \(-H_k
abla f(x_k)\) is a strict descent direction.
The update coefficient \(\rho=(s^Ty)^{-1}\) is positive.
boundary_notes: SR1 does not generally preserve positive definiteness.
The implication excludes zero or negative curvature pairs.
Positive definiteness can be lost numerically even when the exact-arithmetic update preserves it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted least-change and coordinate-invariance correspondence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and define \(\|A\|_W=\|W^{1/2}AW^{1/2}\|_F\) for an SPD weight \(W\) satisfying \(Wy_k=s_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact arithmetic under nonsingular linear changes of variables; the statement defines the correspondence used to select scale-invariant quasi-Newton updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variational-invariance correspondence assigns to a weighted least-change problem \[B_{k+1}\in\arg\min_B\|B-B_k\|_W\quad\text{subject to}\quad B=B^T,\ Bs_k=y_k\] an update formula whose transformed output agrees with updating transformed data. Under a nonsingular coordinate change \(x=Cz\), the data transform as \(\widehat B_k=C^TB_kC\), \(\widehat s_k=C^{-1}s_k\), and \(\widehat y_k=C^Ty_k\). Coordinate covariance means \[U(\widehat B_k,\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k)=C^TU(B_k,s_k,y_k)C.\] Choosing a dimensionally compatible weight satisfying the secant relation makes the least-change objective invariant under this transformation and yields scale-invariant DFP/BFGS constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The variational-invariance correspondence links a weighted minimum-change characterization of a secant update with covariance under nonsingular changes of variables. The update minimizes weighted Frobenius distance from the current metric subject to symmetry and the secant equation. Its coordinate-transformed result must equal the congruence transform of the original result. A secant-compatible weight makes the variational objective dimensionless and invariant, producing the standard scale-invariant DFP or BFGS update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[U(C^TB_kC,C^{-1}s_k,C^Ty_k)=C^TU(B_k,s_k,y_k)C\] for every nonsingular \(C\), when \(U\) is defined by the corresponding invariant weighted least-change problem.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For inverse updates, the transformed metric is \(\widehat H_k=C^{-1}H_kC^{-T}\), and covariance becomes \(V(\widehat H_k,\widehat s_k,\widehat y_k)=C^{-1}V(H_k,s_k,y_k)C^{-T}\).
Scale invariance is the diagonal-coordinate-change special case with nonsingular diagonal \(C\).
special_cases_latex: The weighted least-change problem for direct Hessian approximations yields DFP for the specified secant-compatible weight.
Applying the analogous variational principle to inverse approximations yields BFGS.

knowledge_statements.title: Variational Characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant updating as a unique least-change projection in a metric on symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb{S}^{n}\) carry an inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{W}\) with induced norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{W}\), let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\), and let \(s\ne0\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\). The least-change secant update is characterized by \[B_{+}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}}\frac12\lVert X-B\rVert_{W}^{2}\quad\text{subject to}\quad Xs=y.\] Because the objective is strictly convex and the affine constraint is nonempty, the minimizer exists and is unique. Particular admissible metric choices \(W\) yield standard symmetric rank-two quasi-Newton updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric quasi-Newton update can be characterized uniquely as the nearest matrix to the old metric among all matrices satisfying the new secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed constrained problem has a unique minimizer \(B_{+}\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\) satisfying \(B_{+}s=y\).

notation.meaning: norm induced by the selected matrix-space inner product

knowledge_statements.title: Invariance Characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine covariance of a direct quasi-Newton update under a nonsingular linear change of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\), let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and let \(U:\mathbb{S}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{S}^{n}\) be a direct-metric update map on the admissible triples under consideration. For a nonsingular matrix \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and the coordinate change \(x=Tz\), set \(\widetilde B=T^{\mathsf T}BT\), \(\widetilde s=T^{-1}s\), and \(\widetilde y=T^{\mathsf T}y\). The update map is linearly invariant when \[U(\widetilde B,\widetilde s,\widetilde y)=T^{\mathsf T}U(B,s,y)T\] for every admissible \((B,s,y)\) and every nonsingular \(T\). Under this identity, if \(U(B,s,y)s=y\), then \(U(\widetilde B,\widetilde s,\widetilde y)\widetilde s=\widetilde y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct-metric update is linearly invariant when updating transformed inputs gives the congruence transform of the update computed in the original coordinates; this covariance also carries the secant equation between the coordinate systems.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) maps each admissible direct-metric triple to a symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U(T^{\mathsf T}BT,T^{-1}s,T^{\mathsf T}y)=T^{\mathsf T}U(B,s,y)T\), and the secant equation is covariant under this identity.

notation.meaning: metric and secant quantities in transformed coordinates
