knowledge_statements.title: Variational–Invariance Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coordinate-covariant least-change construction induces a linearly invariant quasi-Newton update map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\), let \(s\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminus\{0\}\), let \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and let \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular. Suppose the original and transformed matrix-space norms are induced by inner products and satisfy \[\lVert T^{\mathsf T}XT\rVert_{\widetilde W}=\lVert X\rVert_{W}\quad\text{for every }X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}.\] Define \(B_{+}\) as the unique minimizer of \(\lVert X-B\rVert_{W}\) over \(X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\) subject to \(Xs=y\). Set \(\widetilde B=T^{\mathsf T}BT\), \(\widetilde s=T^{-1}s\), and \(\widetilde y=T^{\mathsf T}y\), and define \(\widetilde B_{+}\) by the corresponding transformed least-change problem using \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\widetilde W}\). Then congruence maps the original feasible set and objective bijectively to the transformed ones, and uniqueness implies \(\widetilde B_{+}=T^{\mathsf T}B_{+}T\). Thus covariance of the variational metric is sufficient for linear invariance of the induced update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the matrix norm in a unique least-change secant problem transforms covariantly, the resulting update transforms by congruence and is therefore linearly invariant.
assumptions_latex: Both norms are induced by inner products and satisfy the displayed covariance identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde B_{+}=T^{\mathsf T}B_{+}T\); norm covariance implies invariance of the induced least-change update.

notation.meaning: matrix-space metrics in the original and transformed coordinates
unique least-change updates in the two coordinate systems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-model guarantee class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) with \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), so that \(x_*=-A^{-1}b\), \(g(x)=Ax+b\), and every curvature pair satisfies \(y_k=As_k\). Consider exact-arithmetic quasi-Newton iterations with exact line searches.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex finite-dimensional quadratics and exact arithmetic; this regime is distinct from nonlinear local asymptotics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic-model result is a guarantee whose domain is the class \(\mathcal Q_{++}^n=\{x\mapsto\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c:A\succ0\}\) and whose conclusion uses the exact identity \(y_k=As_k\). Canonical members assert one or more of: finite termination \(x_j=x_*\) for some \(j\leq n\); hereditary exactness \(B_ks_i=y_i\) for all retained prior directions; equivalence of iterates with conjugate gradient under compatible initialization; mutual \(A\)-conjugacy \(s_i^TAs_j=0\) for \(i\neq j\); or full recovery \(B_n=A\) after \(n\) independent directions. Every such member must state its update family, exact-line-search condition, initialization, and nonsingularity or positivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic-model result is an exact-arithmetic guarantee restricted to strongly convex quadratic objectives, where gradient differences equal the true Hessian applied to steps. This class includes finite termination, persistence of earlier secant equations, equivalence with conjugate gradient, conjugacy of directions, and recovery of the exact Hessian after enough independent directions. The definition requires each result to record its update, line-search, initialization, and regularity assumptions rather than transferring the conclusion to general nonlinear objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak Q(U)=\{P:\ P\text{ is stated on }\mathcal Q_{++}^n,\ y_k=As_k,\text{ and has explicit update and exact-search hypotheses}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic regime is characterized by a constant Hessian \(\nabla^2q(x)=A\) and exact pair relation \(y_k=As_k\).
Finite termination means \(\exists j\leq n\) such that \(x_j=x_*\), not merely \(x_k\to x_*\).
special_cases_latex: The eligible Broyden class with exact searches has all five canonical properties listed in the definition.
SR1 with defined updates has finite termination and hereditary secant properties under its distinct hypotheses.
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic identities permit exact directional Hessian recovery from secant pairs.
The guarantee class supplies diagnostic benchmark properties for quasi-Newton formulas.
boundary_notes: Inexact line searches can destroy conjugate-gradient equivalence and hereditary exactness.
Finite precision can destroy finite termination and exact conjugacy.
A result in this class does not automatically extend to a nonlinear function that is only locally approximately quadratic.

notation.meaning: Class of strongly convex quadratic functions on n-dimensional Euclidean space.
Quadratic-model guarantee set associated with update U.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite convergence property on strongly convex quadratics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) with \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and unique minimizer \(x_*=-A^{-1}b\). Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) be an exact-arithmetic quasi-Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional strongly convex quadratics. The property is defined relative to a specified update, line-search rule, and admitted initialization class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quasi-Newton method has finite convergence on \(\mathcal Q_{++}^n\) with bound \(N(n)\) when \[\forall q\in\mathcal Q_{++}^n\ \forall(x_0,B_0)\in\mathcal I(q),\quad \exists j\in\{0,1,\ldots,N(n)\}:x_j=x_*.\] It has the canonical \(n\)-step property when \(N(n)=n\). For an eligible Broyden-class update with \(B_0\succ0\), exact line searches, and admissible parameters, the canonical property is \(x_j=x_*\) for some \(j\leq n\). For SR1, finite convergence is stated under defined nonzero update denominators and its specified unit-step iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite convergence on quadratic models means that, for every strongly convex quadratic and every admitted starting point and initial metric, the method reaches the exact minimizer after no more than a dimension-dependent finite number of iterations. The canonical quasi-Newton bound is n iterations in exact arithmetic under the update-specific assumptions. Reaching the solution is an equality at a finite index, not an asymptotic rate statement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Finite termination is \(r_j=Ax_j+b=0\) for some \(j\leq n\).
For exact line searches along \(n\) nonzero mutually \(A\)-conjugate directions, the resulting iterate reaches \(x_*\) within \(n\) steps.
special_cases_latex: Eligible Broyden-class methods with exact line searches satisfy the \(n\)-step property.
Linear conjugate gradient terminates in at most \(n\) iterations on an SPD quadratic.
immediate_consequences_latex: No asymptotic convergence factor is needed after the terminating index.
If fewer than \(n\) independent curvature directions span the active Krylov space containing the error, termination can occur earlier.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim finite convergence with inexact line searches.
The exact-arithmetic property is generally lost under rounding error.
Nonconvex or singular quadratics are outside the stated domain.

notation.meaning: Admitted initial points and initial metrics for the specified method.
Uniform finite iteration bound in dimension n.

Conjugate-Gradient Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned equivalence for BFGS on strictly convex quadratic models with exact line searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12 x^{T}Ax-b^{T}x\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite. Apply inverse-BFGS from \(x_0\), with \(H_0\) symmetric positive definite, directions \(p_k=-H_k\nabla q(x_k)\), and exact line searches. In exact arithmetic, the generated iterates coincide with those of preconditioned conjugate gradients using preconditioner \(H_0\): each BFGS direction is a nonzero scalar multiple of the corresponding preconditioned-CG direction. Consequently, the directions are \(A\)-conjugate, \(p_i^{T}Ap_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\), and the minimizer is reached in at most \(n\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a positive-definite quadratic, exact-line-search inverse-BFGS follows the same iterates as preconditioned conjugate gradients and terminates within the dimension in exact arithmetic.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the quadratic-model equivalence leaf and is mathematically plausible, including the dependence on the initial inverse metric H_0. Because the precise arbitrary-H_0 equivalence with preconditioned CG is a nontrivial theorem and no citation is supplied, authoritative source verification is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterate equivalence between quasi-Newton and conjugate gradient
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) with \(A\succ0\). Start both methods at the same \(x_0\), use exact line searches, and let the quasi-Newton method use an eligible Broyden-class update with initial Hessian approximation \(B_0\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact arithmetic on strongly convex quadratics; ordinary CG corresponds to \(B_0=I\), while general \(B_0\) gives preconditioned CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quasi-Newton method is conjugate-gradient equivalent when its iterate sequence equals the sequence generated by the corresponding conjugate-gradient method: \[x_k^{\mathrm{QN}}=x_k^{\mathrm{CG}}\quad\text{for every index before termination}.\] With \(B_0=I\), the correspondence is with ordinary linear CG. With general \(B_0\succ0\), it is with preconditioned CG using \(B_0\) as preconditioner. Direction vectors may differ by nonzero scalar factors, but exact line minimization makes the next iterates identical. The common displacement directions satisfy \(s_i^TAs_j=0\) for \(i\neq j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate-gradient equivalence means equality of the iterate sequences produced by a quasi-Newton method and conjugate gradient on the same strongly convex quadratic. Their search directions may have different scaling, but exact line searches select the same points. Identity initialization gives ordinary CG; a general positive-definite initial Hessian approximation gives the corresponding preconditioned CG method. The shared displacement directions are mutually conjugate with respect to the quadratic Hessian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Equality of exact line-search iterates allows search directions related by \(p_k^{\mathrm{QN}}=\tau_kp_k^{\mathrm{CG}}\) with \(\tau_k\neq0\).
The common steps obey \(s_i^TAs_j=0\) whenever \(i\neq j\).
special_cases_latex: BFGS and DFP belong to the eligible Broyden class covered by the equivalence under the stated assumptions.
When \(B_0=\beta I\) with \(\beta>0\), scalar preconditioning does not change the exact-line-search iterate sequence from ordinary CG.
immediate_consequences_latex: The quasi-Newton sequence terminates in at most \(n\) iterations in exact arithmetic.
Quadratic-model convergence properties of the common iterate sequence can be expressed through the associated Krylov subspaces.
boundary_notes: Inexact line searches generally destroy exact iterate equivalence.
The statement concerns iterates, not necessarily identical direction normalizations or step-length values.
The equivalence does not extend unchanged to nonlinear conjugate-gradient iterations on nonquadratic objectives.

notation.meaning: Preconditioned conjugate-gradient method using B₀ as preconditioner.

knowledge_statements.title: Hereditary Exactness Properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of accumulated secant equations by BFGS on a quadratic under conjugate displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{T}Ax-b^{T}x\) with \(A=A^{T}\succ0\), and let \(y_k=As_k\). Suppose \(B_k=B_k^{T}\succ0\), \(B_ks_i=As_i\) for \(0\le i<k\), and \(s_i^{T}As_k=0\) for \(i<k\). The BFGS update \[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^{T}B_k}{s_k^{T}B_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^{T}}{y_k^{T}s_k}\] satisfies every previous exactness equation and the new secant equation: \(B_{k+1}s_i=As_i\) for \(0\le i\le k\). Thus exactness on the expanding conjugate subspace is hereditary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For conjugate quadratic displacements, BFGS preserves every earlier exact secant equation while adding the current one.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is internally consistent and fits the hereditary-exactness leaf: the stated accumulated secant equations and A-conjugacy assumptions are sufficient for preservation under the displayed BFGS update. No evidence is supplied for this nontrivial property.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hereditary secant exactness on accumulated directions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) with \(A\succ0\), and let \(y_j=As_j\). Let \(B_k\) and \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) be direct and inverse quasi-Newton approximations when defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact arithmetic on a constant-Hessian quadratic; update-specific assumptions such as exact line searches or nonzero SR1 denominators remain required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \(\{B_k\}\) has hereditary exactness through iteration \(k\) when every previously acquired secant equation remains valid: \[B_ks_j=y_j=As_j\qquad(j=0,\ldots,k-1).\] Equivalently, \((B_k-A)s_j=0\) on the accumulated step subspace \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{span}\{s_0,\ldots,s_{k-1}\}\). In inverse form, \(H_ky_j=s_j=A^{-1}y_j\) for all prior pairs. If \(\mathcal S_k=\mathbb R^n\), hereditary exactness implies \(B_k=A\) and \(H_k=A^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hereditary exactness means that a new quasi-Newton update does not erase any earlier secant equation: the current approximation agrees with the true constant Hessian on the span of all previous steps. The inverse approximation similarly agrees with the true inverse on the span of the corresponding gradient changes. Once the accumulated independent steps span the whole space, the approximation equals the exact Hessian everywhere.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[H_ky_j=A^{-1}y_j=s_j\qquad(j<k).\]
Hereditary exactness of order \(r\) means exactness on an \(r\)-dimensional accumulated step subspace.
special_cases_latex: Eligible Broyden-class methods with exact line searches satisfy all previous secant equations on SPD quadratics.
SR1 satisfies the hereditary inverse relations when its successive updates are defined, without requiring exact line searches for the hereditary identity itself.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(s_0,\ldots,s_{n-1}\) are linearly independent, then \(B_n=A\).
The current quadratic model has exact curvature on every previously sampled step direction.
boundary_notes: The property is stronger than satisfaction of only the newest secant equation.
On a nonlinear objective, changing Hessians prevent the identity \(y_j=As_j\) with one fixed \(A\).
Rounding errors and inexact searches can destroy exact hereditary relations.

notation.meaning: Span of all displacement vectors acquired before iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global convergence guarantee families for quasi-Newton iterations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) be a line-search quasi-Newton iteration for a smooth \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), with \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) when \(B_k\succ0\). Let \(\mathcal I\) denote the initial states admitted by a stated hypothesis set \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth finite-dimensional optimization. Global means from every initial state admitted by the hypotheses, not convergence to a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A global convergence family is a collection of implications \[\mathcal H(f,x_0,B_0,\{\alpha_k\})\Longrightarrow\mathcal C(\{x_k\})\qquad orall(x_0,B_0)\in\mathcal I,\] classified by the strength of \(\mathcal C\): subsequential stationarity, \(\liminf_k\|
abla f(x_k)\|=0\); full stationarity, \(\|
abla f(x_k)\|	o0\); stationary cluster-point convergence; or iterate convergence, \(x_k	o x_*\). For Wolfe line searches on a function bounded below with Lipschitz gradient on the relevant level set, uniformly well-conditioned SPD metrics give full stationarity. For BFGS on a convex initial level set with \(mI\preceq
abla^2f(x)\preceq MI\), the stronger family member is \(x_k	o x_*\), the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global convergence family groups guarantees that hold from every starting state allowed by explicit hypotheses. Its conclusions are ordered from subsequential stationarity through vanishing of the full gradient sequence to convergence of the iterates. In quasi-Newton line searches, bounded-below smoothness, Wolfe steps, descent, and metric-angle control support stationarity. Under the stronger uniformly convex level-set assumptions used for BFGS, the iterates converge to the unique minimizer. Global convergence in this terminology does not mean finding a globally optimal point for a nonconvex function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{subseq}}\preceq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{stat}}\preceq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{iter}},\] where \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{subseq}}:\liminf_k\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\), \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{stat}}:\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\), and \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{iter}}:x_k\to x_*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Uniform angle control means \(\cos\theta_k\geq\delta>0\), where \(\cos\theta_k=-\nabla f(x_k)^Tp_k/(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\|p_k\|)\).
For SPD \(B_k\) with \(\|B_k\|\|B_k^{-1}\|\leq M_B\), the angle satisfies a uniform positive lower bound.
special_cases_latex: Zoutendijk-based line-search analysis yields full gradient convergence when the search-direction angle is uniformly bounded away from \(90^\circ\).
BFGS with an arbitrary SPD \(B_0\), Wolfe line search, and uniform Hessian bounds on a convex initial level set converges to the unique minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: A full-stationarity guarantee ensures every convergent subsequence has a stationary limit when the gradient is continuous.
Uniform convexity upgrades stationarity of cluster points to uniqueness of the possible minimizer.
boundary_notes: For a general nonconvex objective, \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\) does not imply convergence to a minimizer.
The standard BFGS iterate-convergence result cited here requires convexity and uniform Hessian bounds on the initial level set.
Global convergence does not specify a local rate.

notation.meaning: Explicit hypotheses defining a global guarantee member.
Angle between the search direction and the negative gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Line-Search Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient convergence for uniformly well-conditioned variable metrics and exact line minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^{n}	o\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable and bounded below on \(L=\{x:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\), and suppose \(
abla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of \(L\). Generate \(p_k=-H_k
abla f(x_k)\), where \(H_k\) is symmetric and \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for fixed \(0<m\le M<\infty\), and choose an exact minimizer \(\alpha_k\ge0\) along \(p_k\). Then either some iterate is stationary or \(\|
abla f(x_k)\|	o0\). Every accumulation point of the iterates is therefore stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact line minimization with uniformly positive-definite, bounded variable metrics drives the gradient to zero on a smooth bounded-below level set.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on \(L\), and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz near \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\), unless \(\nabla f(x_k)=0\) at a finite iteration.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(H_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be an inverse-Hessian approximation. Define \(d_k=-H_kg_k\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, smooth unconstrained minimization with an exact line search. The definition specifies a convergence property of a stated quasi-Newton family; it does not assert that every secant update has this property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quasi-Newton scheme has exact-line-search global convergence on a function class \(\mathcal F\) if, for every \(f\in\mathcal F\), every admissible \(x_0\), and every admissible \(H_0\succ0\), each nonstationary iteration chooses \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\ge0}f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\), and the resulting sequence satisfies the prescribed global conclusion, normally \(x_k\to x^*(f)\) when \(f\) has a unique minimizer, or at least \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\) when only stationarity is guaranteed. For the uniformly convex DFP regime, \(\mathcal F\) consists of twice continuously differentiable functions whose relevant convex level set obeys \(m\|u\|^2\le u^T\nabla^2f(x)u\le M\|u\|^2\), and the defining conclusion is \(x_k\to x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton method has exact-line-search global convergence on a specified class when every admissible initial point and positive-definite initial metric generates steps whose lengths minimize the objective along the search rays, and every resulting infinite sequence reaches the class’s stated global target. For uniformly convex DFP, the target is convergence of the iterates to the unique minimizer. The function class and update rule are part of the definition; exact line search alone does not give the property to an arbitrary update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall f\in\mathcal F\;\forall(x_0,H_0)\in\mathcal I_f:\quad \alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\ge0}f(x_k-\alpha H_k\nabla f(x_k)),\qquad x_k\to x^*(f).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(f\) is uniformly strongly convex on the invariant level set, \(x_k\to x^*\), \(f(x_k)\to f(x^*)\), and \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\) are equivalent convergence descriptions for a bounded descent sequence.
special_cases_latex: For DFP with exact line search and Assumption 5.3.1 of the cited source, the convergence target is the unique minimizer \(x^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact minimization gives the orthogonality relation \(\nabla f(x_{k+1})^Td_k=0\) whenever the one-dimensional minimizer is differentiable and interior.
Uniform convexity makes the global target unique.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes merely approximate minimization along the search ray.
Global convergence must always be qualified by a function class and an update rule; it is not a property of exact line search in isolation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Boundedness of Quasi-Newton Secant Ratios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A uniform-curvature secant-pair estimate used in exact-line-search quasi-Newton convergence analysis; exact line search is not itself a hypothesis of this lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f satisfy Assumption 5.3.1, and define s_k:=x_{k+1}-x_k and y_k:=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k). Over the indices for which s_k\neq0, the five sequences
\[
\frac{\lVert s_k\rVert}{\lVert y_k\rVert},\quad
\frac{\lVert y_k\rVert}{\lVert s_k\rVert},\quad
\frac{s_k^\top y_k}{\lVert s_k\rVert^2},\quad
\frac{s_k^\top y_k}{\lVert y_k\rVert^2},\quad
\frac{\lVert y_k\rVert^2}{s_k^\top y_k}
\]
are bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standing uniform Hessian bounds, nonzero quasi-Newton steps and their gradient differences are uniformly comparable, and the associated curvature ratios remain bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{k:s_k\neq0}\max\left\{\frac{\lVert s_k\rVert}{\lVert y_k\rVert},\frac{\lVert y_k\rVert}{\lVert s_k\rVert},\frac{s_k^\top y_k}{\lVert s_k\rVert^2},\frac{s_k^\top y_k}{\lVert y_k\rVert^2},\frac{\lVert y_k\rVert^2}{s_k^\top y_k}\right\}<\infty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact-line-search BFGS global convergence property
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(d_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\), \(s_k=\alpha_kd_k\), and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained minimization using the full-memory BFGS Hessian update and Wolfe-type inexact line search on a uniformly convex level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inexact-line-search BFGS scheme is defined by \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and \(B_{k+1}=B_k-B_ks_ks_k^TB_k/(s_k^TB_ks_k)+y_ky_k^T/(y_k^Ts_k)\), where \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies the Wolfe inequalities \(f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Td_k\) and \(\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)^Td_k\ge c_2g_k^Td_k\), with \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). It has the global-convergence property on the uniformly convex class if, for every starting point whose level set is convex, every \(B_0\succ0\), and every sequence of Wolfe-admissible step lengths, \(x_k\to x^*\), the unique minimizer. The Wolfe curvature inequality also entails \(y_k^Ts_k>0\), so every BFGS update is well defined and remains positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact-line-search BFGS global convergence is the property that the standard BFGS iteration, using any step lengths satisfying fixed Wolfe sufficient-decrease and curvature inequalities, converges from every admissible starting point and positive-definite initial Hessian approximation to the unique minimizer of each function in the stated uniformly convex class. The definition includes the BFGS formula, the line-search inequalities, the quantified initial data, and the convergence target.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under uniform convexity, the conclusion may equivalently be recorded as \(f(x_k)\to f(x^*)\) together with \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\).
special_cases_latex: The Wolfe-Powell conditions in the cited source are the two displayed inequalities with fixed parameters \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The curvature inequality yields \(y_k^Ts_k\ge(c_2-1)\alpha_kg_k^Td_k>0\).
If \(B_0\succ0\), then every defined BFGS matrix satisfies \(B_k\succ0\), and hence \(d_k\) is a descent direction whenever \(g_k\ne0\).
boundary_notes: Armijo decrease without a curvature condition is not the inexact line-search regime defined here.
The cited global theorem assumes uniform convexity; it does not establish the same conclusion for arbitrary nonconvex objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trace–determinant device in BFGS convergence analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An analysis device and stated limitation; the extract does not prove that a condition-number bound is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the BFGS Hessian approximations $B_k$ in the stated analysis, no bound on $\kappa(B_k)$ is established. Instead, the analysis uses
\[
\operatorname{trace}(B_k)=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i(B_k),\qquad
\det(B_k)=\prod_{i=1}^n\lambda_i(B_k)
\]
to estimate the largest and smallest eigenvalues of $B_k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because the stated BFGS analysis does not establish a condition-number bound for its Hessian approximations, it uses the trace and determinant—the sum and product of the eigenvalues—to estimate the extreme eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Modified-BFGS Nonconvex Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell-damped and spectrally safeguarded BFGS for smooth nonconvex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, bounded below on the initial level set, and have Lipschitz gradient there. Use \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\), a Wolfe line search, and the damped vector \(\bar y_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k\), with \(\theta_k\in[0,1]\) chosen so that \(s_k^{T}\bar y_k\ge\eta s_k^{T}B_ks_k\) for fixed \(\eta>0\). Apply the BFGS update with \(\bar y_k\), together with spectral safeguarding \(mI\preceq B_k\preceq MI\). Then \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\), so every accumulation point is first-order stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Damped BFGS with Wolfe steps and uniform spectral safeguards converges to first-order stationarity for a smooth nonconvex objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz there.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With genuinely enforced uniform spectral bounds, the convergence conclusion is plausible from standard line-search theory. However, the record does not identify a precise modified-BFGS algorithm that enforces those bounds, and no source supports the combined damping-and-safeguarding theorem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate family definition for deterministic smooth nonconvex unconstrained minimization. The exact modification and theorem hypotheses require a source specific to the intended modified-BFGS variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A modified-BFGS scheme replaces the raw secant vector \(y_k\) by a corrected vector \(r_k=y_k+\tau_ks_k\), or more generally by a specified \(r_k\), chosen so that \(s_k^Tr_k\ge\delta_k\|s_k\|^2>0\). It then applies \(B_{k+1}=B_k-B_ks_ks_k^TB_k/(s_k^TB_ks_k)+r_kr_k^T/(s_k^Tr_k)\). Such a scheme belongs to the nonconvex global-convergence family only when its complete specification includes a line-search or trust-region rule and a proved conclusion quantified over all admissible starts, typically \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\), or the stronger \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\). The correction rule, lower-curvature bound, globalization conditions, and function class are constitutive parts of the definition and cannot be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified-BFGS nonconvex global-convergence method corrects the observed gradient difference before inserting it into the BFGS formula, thereby enforcing positive curvature even when the objective is nonconvex. Membership in the named family additionally requires a fully specified globalization rule and a global stationarity conclusion for every admissible initial point. Because different publications use materially different corrections, the correction formula and theorem hypotheses must be fixed before this becomes a unique canonical variant.
special_cases_latex: A damped update uses a convex combination \(r_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k\) chosen to enforce a prescribed positive lower bound on \(s_k^Tr_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\) and \(s_k^Tr_k>0\), then the modified BFGS formula yields \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness of the matrices alone is not a global-convergence theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, bounded below on the initial level set, and have Lipschitz gradient there. At iteration \(k\), form \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^{T}p+\tfrac12p^{T}B_kp\), where \(B_k\) is produced by accepted, possibly skipped, SR1 updates and \(\sup_k\|B_k\|<\infty\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region SR1 convergence regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) be a possibly indefinite SR1 Hessian approximation defining \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained minimization with trust-region globalization, safeguarded SR1 updating, and the bounded-iterate regime of the cited result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region SR1 sequence uses a step \(s_k\) that provides an admissible approximate solution of \(\min_{\|s\|\le\Delta_k}g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\), accepts or rejects the trial point according to actual versus predicted reduction, updates \(\Delta_k\) by the same ratio, and, when accepted, sets \(y_k=\nabla f(x_k+s_k)-g_k\). The SR1 correction \(B_{k+1}=B_k+(y_k-B_ks_k)(y_k-B_ks_k)^T/((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k)\) is used only when \(|s_k^T(y_k-B_ks_k)|\ge r\|s_k\|\|y_k-B_ks_k\|\); otherwise the update is skipped. In the cited convergence regime, global convergence means \(x_k\to x^*\), where \(x^*\) is the unique stationary point in the closed bounded convex set containing the iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SR1 method builds a quadratic model with a symmetric, possibly indefinite Hessian approximation, computes a step inside a radius, accepts the trial point according to the model agreement ratio, and applies the SR1 formula only when its denominator is safely separated from zero. Its global-convergence regime is the quantified property that the entire bounded sequence converges to the unique stationary point under the specified smoothness, bounded-matrix, and non-skipping hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k\to x^*,\qquad \frac{\|x_{k+n+1}-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}\to0\quad\text{in the stronger regime of Theorem 6.7}.\]
special_cases_latex: The matrices \(B_k\) need not be positive definite; the trust-region constraint keeps the quadratic subproblem meaningful.
The cited theorem permits an admissible approximate, rather than necessarily exact, trust-region solution.
immediate_consequences_latex: The denominator safeguard prevents unstable division in the SR1 correction.
Under the full hypotheses of the cited theorem, convergence is accompanied by \((n+1)\)-step superlinear convergence.
boundary_notes: The theorem requires bounded \(\{B_k\}\) and assumes that the SR1 safeguard succeeds at every iteration.
The result is not an unrestricted global theorem for arbitrary nonconvex functions or arbitrary SR1 implementations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local convergence framework for quasi-Newton iterations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near a stationary point \(x^*\), with \(G_*=\nabla^2f(x^*)\) nonsingular, and consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kB_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic local analysis near a nondegenerate stationary point; positive definiteness of \(G_*\) specializes the framework to a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quasi-Newton iteration is locally convergent to \(x^*\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(V\) of \(G_*\), or another stated admissible set of initial metrics, such that every \(x_0\in U\) and \(B_0\in V\) generate a well-defined sequence remaining in the analysis neighborhood and satisfying \(x_k\to x^*\). Its local rate is Q-linear if \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le q\|x_k-x^*\|\) eventually for some \(q<1\), Q-superlinear if \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\), and Q-quadratic if \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le C\|x_k-x^*\|^2\) eventually. A complete local theory states the smoothness and nonsingularity assumptions, admissible initial neighborhood, step-length regime, matrix-update conditions, and resulting rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General local convergence theory specifies a neighborhood of a nondegenerate solution and a set of admissible initial metric approximations from which the iteration is well defined, stays nearby, and converges to that solution. The theory also classifies the rate by comparing consecutive errors. A local result is therefore stronger than merely assuming that a particular generated sequence already converges, but weaker than a global guarantee from arbitrary initial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists U\ni x^*,\;\exists V\ni G_*:\quad (x_0,B_0)\in U\times V\Longrightarrow x_k\to x^*.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a Q-superlinear sequence with \(x_k\ne x^*\), the rate condition is \(\|e_{k+1}\|=o(\|e_k\|)\), where \(e_k=x_k-x^*\).
special_cases_latex: When \(G_*\succ0\), \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer and sufficiently close Hessians are also positive definite.
Unit-step iterations set \(\alpha_k=1\); line-search theories additionally establish eventual acceptance of this value.
immediate_consequences_latex: Q-superlinear convergence implies Q-linear convergence with every fixed factor \(q\in(0,1)\) sufficiently late.
boundary_notes: A result conditional on an already convergent sequence is a rate characterization, not by itself a full attraction-neighborhood theorem.
Singular stationary points require a different local theory.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local linear convergence of general quasi-Newton iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence under either of two globally applied update-stability hypotheses. Conditions (a)–(c) of Assumption 5.4.1 are retained by reference because they are absent from this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfy conditions (a), (b), and (c) of Assumption 5.4.1. Suppose either, for every $(x_k,B_k)\in\operatorname{dom}U$ and every $B_{k+1}\in U(x_k,B_k)$,
\[
\|B_{k+1}-F'(x^*)\|\leq\|B_k-F'(x^*)\|+\frac{\gamma}{2}\bigl(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|+\|x_k-x^*\|\bigr),
\]
or, for every such admissible update,
\[
\|B_{k+1}-F'(x^*)\|\leq[1+\alpha_1\sigma(x_k,x_{k+1})]\|B_k-F'(x^*)\|+\alpha_2\sigma(x_k,x_{k+1}),
\]
where
\[
\sigma(x_k,x_{k+1})=\max\{\|x_k-x^*\|,\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\}.
\]
Then there exist $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ such that, if $\|x_0-x^*\|<\varepsilon$ and $\|B_0-F'(x^*)\|<\delta$, the iteration
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-B_k^{-1}F(x_k),\qquad B_{k+1}\in U(x_k,B_k)
\]
is well-defined and converges linearly to $x^*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the referenced regularity assumptions, either update-stability condition applied uniformly to all admissible updates guarantees well-defined local iteration and linear convergence from sufficiently close initial point and matrix approximations.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ satisfies conditions (a), (b), and (c) of Assumption 5.4.1}
\Bigl[\forall (x_k,B_k),B_{k+1}\text{ admissible, inequality (5.4.40) holds}\Bigr]\ \lor\ \Bigl[\forall (x_k,B_k),B_{k+1}\text{ admissible, inequality (5.4.41) holds}\Bigr]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon,\delta>0\ \forall (x_0,B_0):\ \bigl(\|x_0-x^*\|<\varepsilon\land\|B_0-F'(x^*)\|<\delta\bigr)\Longrightarrow\{x_k\}\text{ is well-defined and converges linearly to }x^*

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General quasi-Newton iteration for nonlinear equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration framework used in the local-convergence analysis, with a set-valued family of admissible Jacobian-approximation updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For $(x_k,B_k)\in\operatorname{dom}U$, where $U(x_k,B_k)$ is nonempty and $B_k$ is invertible, the general quasi-Newton iteration is
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-B_k^{-1}F(x_k),\qquad B_{k+1}\in U(x_k,B_k).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the current Jacobian approximation is invertible and the update set is nonempty, the method takes a quasi-Newton step and selects the next approximation from the admissible update set.

knowledge_statements.title: Dennis-Moré Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional consistency condition for local superlinear convergence of direct quasi-Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x_*\) in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\ne0\), and suppose \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice differentiable at \(x_*\), with nonsingular Hessian \(G_*=\nabla^2 f(x_*)\). A sequence of direct quasi-Newton matrices \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfies the Dennis-Moré condition along the iterates if \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|(B_k-G_*)s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}=0.\] This condition requires the matrix approximation to be asymptotically accurate along the realized displacement directions; it does not require \(\|B_k-G_*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dennis-Moré condition requires the direct quasi-Newton matrix error applied to each realized displacement to be negligible relative to that displacement; full operator-norm convergence is not required.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice differentiable at \(x_*\), and \(G_*=\nabla^2f(x_*)\) is nonsingular.
\(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is a direct quasi-Newton approximation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dennis–Moré characterization for nonlinear-equation iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient directional approximation condition for q-superlinear convergence of a convergent nonsingular quasi-Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) have \(J\in\operatorname{Lip}_\gamma(D)\), and let \(x_*\in D\) with \(J(x_*)\) nonsingular. Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, and suppose the iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k-A_k^{-1}F(x_k)\) remains in \(D\), satisfies \(x_k\ne x_*\) for every \(k\), and converges to \(x_*\). With \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \[\bigl(x_k\to x_*\text{ q-superlinearly in some norm and }F(x_*)=0\bigr)\iff\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|(A_k-J(x_*))s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated convergent quasi-Newton iteration, convergence to a root is q-superlinear exactly when the approximate Jacobians become asymptotically accurate along the generated step directions.
assumptions_latex: D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open and convex}
A_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ is nonsingular for every }k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(x_k\to x_*\text{ q-superlinearly in some norm and }F(x_*)=0\bigr)\iff\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|(A_k-J(x_*))s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual acceptance of the full quasi-Newton step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(p_k\) is a descent direction and a line-search procedure tests the trial value \(\alpha=1\) before shorter alternatives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth local line-search analysis near a stationary point with positive-definite Hessian; the admissibility test is the stated Wolfe or comparable line-search rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A line-search quasi-Newton sequence has eventual unit-step acceptance if there exists an index \(k_0\) such that, for every \(k\ge k_0\), the full trial step \(\alpha=1\) satisfies all acceptance inequalities and the algorithm therefore selects \(\alpha_k=1\). For Wolfe conditions this means, simultaneously, \(f(x_k+p_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1
abla f(x_k)^Tp_k\) and \(
abla f(x_k+p_k)^Tp_k\ge c_2
abla f(x_k)^Tp_k\). In the standard local result, \(x_k	o x^*\), \(
abla f(x^*)=0\), \(
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\), \(c_1\le1/2\), and the Newton residual satisfies \(\|
abla f(x_k)+
abla^2f(x_k)p_k\|/\|p_k\|	o0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventual unit-step acceptance means that after some finite iteration every full quasi-Newton trial step passes the line-search test and is actually chosen. It is not merely convergence of the accepted step lengths to one. For a Wolfe search, both the sufficient-decrease and curvature inequalities must hold at the full step, and the implementation must try and accept that value when admissible.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If the algorithm always tests \(1\) first and accepts every admissible trial, eventual admissibility of \(1\) and eventual equality \(\alpha_k=1\) are equivalent.
special_cases_latex: For Newton directions, the Newton residual is identically zero, so the local Wolfe result applies once the iterates approach a positive-definite solution.
For quasi-Newton directions, the Dennis–Moré condition supplies the required asymptotic Newton accuracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: After \(k_0\), the iteration reduces to \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), allowing unit-step rate characterizations to apply.
boundary_notes: The weaker relation \(\alpha_k\to1\) does not imply that any finite tail consists entirely of unit steps.
The restriction \(c_1\le1/2\) is material; larger sufficient-decrease parameters can reject the minimizer of a quadratic along the line.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Secant-consistency-to-superlinear-rate mechanism
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\), \(G_*=\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0\), \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth local analysis of nonterminating quasi-Newton sequences near a nondegenerate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The secant-consistency-to-rate mechanism is the implication chain in which directional Hessian consistency, \(\|(B_k-G_*)p_k\|/\|p_k\|\to0\), makes the quasi-Newton direction asymptotically Newton-like; a compatible line search then accepts \(\alpha_k=1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\); and the resulting errors satisfy \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\). For an already unit-step, convergent quasi-Newton sequence, the first and last limits are equivalent. The word secant consistency refers here to the directional Dennis–Moré limit produced or implied by the update analysis, not merely to the individual equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This mechanism links three distinct local facts: the approximate Hessian becomes accurate along the actual step directions, the globalization device stops shortening those directions, and the iterates consequently converge Q-superlinearly. In the unit-step setting, directional consistency is necessary and sufficient for the superlinear rate. A single secant equation is not enough; the required consistency is an asymptotic normalized limit along the generated directions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\alpha_k\equiv1\) and \(x_k\to x^*\), \[\frac{\|(B_k-G_*)p_k\|}{\|p_k\|}\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_k\to x^*\text{ Q-superlinearly}.\]
special_cases_latex: BFGS update analysis establishes the directional limit without requiring \(B_k\to G_*\) in operator norm.
Full matrix convergence \(B_k\to G_*\) is a sufficient but stronger consistency mechanism.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once full steps are accepted, local behavior is governed by the quality of the secant model rather than by line-search contraction.
boundary_notes: The implication presupposes convergence to a point with positive-definite Hessian; it is not a global convergence argument.
Hereditary secant equations on a quadratic model and the Dennis–Moré limit on a nonlinear problem are different statements.

Let \(x_k	o x_*\), \(G_*=
abla^{2}f(x_*)\), and \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k
e0\). Operator consistency is \(\|B_k-G_*\|	o0\); directional consistency is \(\|(B_k-G_*)s_k\|/\|s_k\|	o0\); and realized-secant consistency is \(\|B_ks_k-y_k\|/\|s_k\|	o0\), where \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\). If \(
abla^{2}f\) is continuous at \(x_*\), operator consistency implies directional consistency, and realized-secant consistency implies directional consistency. The converses need not hold without additional richness of the sampled directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Secant consistency may hold in operator norm, only along realized steps, or through residual secant equations; the directional form is weaker.

knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard quotient and majorant forms of local superlinear convergence for sequences that do not terminate finitely at the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x_*\) in a normed finite-dimensional space, define \(e_k=x_k-x_*\), and suppose \(e_k\ne0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). The sequence converges \(Q\)-superlinearly if \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|e_{k+1}\|}{\|e_k\|}=0.\] If \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\ne0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), this is equivalent to \(\|e_{k+1}\|/\|s_k\|\to0\). The sequence converges \(R\)-superlinearly if there exists a positive sequence \(v_k\) such that \(\|e_k\|\le v_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\) and \(v_{k+1}/v_k\to0\). Every \(Q\)-superlinearly convergent sequence is \(R\)-superlinearly convergent. A sequence that reaches \(x_*\) in finitely many iterations is treated separately as finitely terminating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonterminating sequence, Q-superlinear convergence means that successive nonzero error ratios vanish. R-superlinear convergence means that the errors admit a positive majorant whose successive ratios vanish. Q-superlinear convergence implies R-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(x_k\to x_*\) in a normed finite-dimensional space.
For the step-based characterization, \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\ne0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\text{-superlinear}\Rightarrow R\text{-superlinear}\), and \(Q\)-superlinearity is equivalent to \(\|e_{k+1}\|/\|s_k\|\to0\) under the stated nonvanishing assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency-to-Rate Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dennis-Moré directional consistency converts convergent unit quasi-Newton steps into a superlinear local rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^{n}	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), with \(
abla f(x_*)=0\), \(G_*=
abla^{2}f(x_*)\) nonsingular, and \(
abla^{2}f\) continuous at \(x_*\). Suppose \(x_k	o x_*\), full steps are eventually taken, and \(B_ks_k=-
abla f(x_k)\), where \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\). If \(\|(B_k-G_*)s_k\|/\|s_k\|	o0\), then \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|/\|x_k-x_*\|	o0\). Thus directional secant consistency, rather than full matrix convergence, suffices for local \(Q\)-superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once full steps are accepted, Dennis-Moré directional consistency turns quasi-Newton convergence into Q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla^{2}f\) is continuous near \(x_*\), and full steps are eventually used.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Method-specific local convergence specification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a fixed quasi-Newton method, including its update formula, step computation, safeguard, and globalization rule, applied near a nondegenerate minimizer \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic smooth unconstrained minimization; each method-specific statement fixes one update family rather than treating arbitrary quasi-Newton matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method-specific local convergence specification for \(\mathcal M\) is a tuple \((\mathcal U,\mathcal V,\mathcal A,\mathcal R)\), where \(\mathcal U\) is a neighborhood of \(x^*\), \(\mathcal V\) is the admissible set of initial matrices, \(\mathcal A\) states smoothness, curvature, line-search, and safeguard hypotheses, and \(\mathcal R\) is a rate class. The method has that specification if every \(x_0\in\mathcal U\) and \(B_0\in\mathcal V\) produce a well-defined sequence that stays in the prescribed neighborhood, converges to \(x^*\), and has rate \(\mathcal R\). Distinct formulas such as BFGS, DFP, a Broyden-class member, and SR1 generally have different admissible matrix sets and auxiliary hypotheses even when their conclusions are all called local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Method-specific local convergence records the attraction neighborhood, admissible initial metric approximations, exact update and safeguard rules, assumptions, and convergence rate for one named quasi-Newton method. It prevents a conclusion proved for BFGS, DFP, a restricted Broyden member, or SR1 from being silently transferred to another update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x_0,B_0)\in\mathcal U\times\mathcal V\ \text{and}\ \mathcal A\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_k\to x^*\ \text{with rate}\ \mathcal R.\]
special_cases_latex: For BFGS, \(\mathcal R\) is commonly Q-superlinear under a Dennis–Moré-producing local regime.
For SR1, local matrix consistency may require a denominator safeguard and uniformly linearly independent steps.
immediate_consequences_latex: A method-specific result identifies exactly which algorithmic details are essential to its rate claim.
boundary_notes: The tuple is incomplete if it names only an update formula but omits the step-length or trust-region rule.
Results for nonlinear equations and results for minimization must not be conflated without identifying \(F=\nabla f\).

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS Local Superlinear Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-superlinear convergence of line-search BFGS near a strongly regular minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^{n}	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable near a minimizer \(x_*\), with \(
abla^{2}f(x_*)\succ0\), and suppose its Hessian is Lipschitz near \(x_*\). Apply BFGS with \(B_0\succ0\), directions \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}
abla f(x_k)\), and an Armijo-Wolfe line search with Armijo parameter below \(	frac12\). If \(x_0\) and \(B_0\) are sufficiently close to \(x_*\) and \(
abla^{2}f(x_*)\), respectively, then the iterates remain local, unit steps are eventually accepted, the Dennis-Moré condition holds, and \(x_k	o x_*\) \(Q\)-superlinearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a close initialization near a positive-definite minimizer, line-search BFGS eventually takes full steps and converges Q-superlinearly.
assumptions_latex: \(B_0=B_0^{T}\succ0\), with \(x_0\) and \(B_0\) sufficiently close to their limiting values.
The line search satisfies Armijo-Wolfe conditions with \(0<c_1<\tfrac12<c_2<1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BFGS local Q-superlinear convergence regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\), \(x_k	o x^*\), \(G_*=
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\), and let \(B_k\succ0\) be generated by the BFGS Hessian update from \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth local BFGS analysis. The cited theorem is conditional on convergence and a summability condition; attraction-neighborhood theorems require additional initial-closeness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A BFGS sequence is locally Q-superlinearly convergent to \(x^*\) when its update is \(B_{k+1}=B_k-B_ks_ks_k^TB_k/(s_k^TB_ks_k)+y_ky_k^T/(y_k^Ts_k)\), its globalization eventually accepts full steps, and \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\). A standard sufficient regime assumes that \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable, \(\nabla^2f\) is Lipschitz near \(x^*\), \(x_k\to x^*\), and \(\sum_k\|x_k-x^*\|<\infty\). In this regime the BFGS matrices satisfy the Dennis–Moré directional condition, and a Wolfe line search that tests \(1\) accepts unit steps eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS local superlinear convergence is the property that the standard BFGS iterates approach a nondegenerate minimizer with the ratio of consecutive errors tending to zero. The local regime includes Lipschitz Hessian behavior, positive curvature of the secant pairs, eventual full steps, and sufficient control of the already-convergent iterates. It does not require the whole matrix sequence to converge to the exact Hessian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under unit steps and the stated nondegeneracy assumptions, Q-superlinear convergence is equivalent to \(\|(B_k-G_*)s_k\|/\|s_k\|\to0\).
special_cases_latex: If an independent local attraction result gives Q-linear convergence, then \(\sum_k\|x_k-x^*\|<\infty\) follows.
The Hessian-form and inverse-Hessian-form BFGS implementations describe the same exact-arithmetic iteration when the matrices are inverses.
immediate_consequences_latex: For every \(q\in(0,1)\), \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le q\|x_k-x^*\|\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
boundary_notes: The cited result does not claim Q-quadratic convergence.
Convergence of \(B_k\) to \(G_*\) in operator norm is not required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumption 6.2 used in the BFGS superlinear-convergence analysis. The subsequent transformed-update identities and estimates are derivational material and are not included as part of the assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)\). The Hessian is Lipschitz continuous at \(x^*\) if there exist \(L>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that \[\|G(x)-G(x^*)\|\le L\|x-x^*\|\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\]

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists L>0\ \exists U\ni x^*\ \forall x\in U:\ \|G(x)-G(x^*)\|\le L\|x-x^*\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local well-definedness and conditional superlinear convergence of inverse BFGS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inverse-BFGS theorem combining well-definedness and linear convergence with a summability-based superlinear rate upgrade.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) satisfy Assumption 5.4.2, and define
\[
\mu=\|\nabla^2f(x^*)^{-1}\|,\qquad \sigma(x_k,x_{k+1})=\max\{\|x_k-x^*\|,\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\}.
\]
Assume \(\mu\gamma\sigma(x_k,x_{k+1})\le \tfrac13\) in a neighborhood of \(x^*\). Then there exist \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\) such that
\[
\|x_0-x^*\|<\varepsilon,\qquad \|H_0-\nabla^2f(x^*)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{BFGS}}<\delta
\]
imply that the inverse-form BFGS method (5.4.130)--(5.4.131) is well-defined and \(x_k\to x^*\) linearly. If additionally
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_k-x^*\|<\infty,
\]
then \(x_k\to x^*\) superlinearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 5.4.2 and the stated one-third neighborhood bound, sufficiently close initial iterates and inverse-Hessian approximations make inverse BFGS well-defined and linearly convergent. Summability of the iterate errors further implies superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon,\delta>0:\ \Bigl(\|x_0-x^*\|<\varepsilon\ \wedge\ \|H_0-\nabla^2f(x^*)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{BFGS}}<\delta\Bigr)\Rightarrow\Bigl(\text{BFGS is well-defined and }x_k\to x^*\text{ linearly}\Bigr);\quad \left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_k-x^*\|<\infty\right)\Rightarrow x_k\to x^*\text{ superlinearly}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian-Scaled BFGS Update and Local Secant Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The normalization and local secant estimate used in BFGS superlinear-convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,
\qquad
y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k),
\qquad G_*=\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0,
\]
and define
\[
\widetilde s_k=G_*^{1/2}s_k,
\qquad \widetilde y_k=G_*^{-1/2}y_k,
\qquad \widetilde B_k=G_*^{-1/2}B_kG_*^{-1/2}.
\]
When its denominators are nonzero, the scaled update retains the BFGS form:
\[
\widetilde B_{k+1}=\widetilde B_k-\frac{\widetilde B_k\widetilde s_k\widetilde s_k^T\widetilde B_k}{\widetilde s_k^T\widetilde B_k\widetilde s_k}+\frac{\widetilde y_k\widetilde y_k^T}{\widetilde y_k^T\widetilde s_k}.
\]
Let
\[
\overline G_k=\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x_k+\tau s_k)\,d\tau,
\qquad
\epsilon_k=\max\{\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|,\|x_k-x^*\|\}.
\]
If \nabla^2f is Lipschitz with constant L on a neighborhood containing the segment from x_k to x_{k+1}, then
\[
\widetilde y_k-\widetilde s_k=G_*^{-1/2}(\overline G_k-G_*)G_*^{-1/2}\widetilde s_k
\]
and
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde y_k-\widetilde s_k\|}{\|\widetilde s_k\|}\le \|G_*^{-1/2}\|^2L\epsilon_k=:\bar c\epsilon_k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling the BFGS secant vectors and direct curvature matrices by the solution Hessian preserves the algebraic BFGS update. Under local Hessian Lipschitz continuity, the relative discrepancy between the scaled secant vectors is at most a constant times the maximum distance of two consecutive iterates from the solution.
assumptions_latex: \nabla^2f\text{ is Lipschitz with constant }L\text{ on a neighborhood containing }[x_k,x_{k+1}]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde B_{k+1}=\widetilde B_k-\frac{\widetilde B_k\widetilde s_k\widetilde s_k^T\widetilde B_k}{\widetilde s_k^T\widetilde B_k\widetilde s_k}+\frac{\widetilde y_k\widetilde y_k^T}{\widetilde y_k^T\widetilde s_k},\qquad \frac{\|\widetilde y_k-\widetilde s_k\|}{\|\widetilde s_k\|}\le \bar c\epsilon_k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local linear and superlinear regimes of DFP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(x^*\) be a minimizer with \(A=\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0\), and let \(H_k\) be inverse-Hessian approximations updated by DFP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unit-step DFP analysis near a strongly regular minimizer, with initial point and metric sufficiently close to their limiting values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The DFP local-rate regime uses \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_k\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(H_{k+1}=H_k-H_ky_ky_k^TH_k/(y_k^TH_ky_k)+s_ks_k^T/(s_k^Ty_k)\). Its local linear regime consists of neighborhoods in which sufficiently small \(\|x_0-x^*\|\) and sufficiently small weighted matrix error produce a well-defined sequence satisfying \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le q\|x_k-x^*\|\) for some \(q<1\). Its local superlinear regime strengthens the asymptotic conclusion to \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\), under the same smoothness and Lipschitz-Hessian structure and the associated bounded-deterioration estimates. The two regimes are nested: the linear result supplies neighborhood invariance and summability, while the superlinear result records the asymptotic rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DFP local rate theory has two levels. Close initial points and inverse-Hessian approximations first give a well-defined, locally linearly convergent unit-step iteration. Under the same regularity structure, the secant approximations acquire enough directional accuracy for the rate to become Q-superlinear. Both the update convention and the weighted norm used to measure the initial matrix error are part of the regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The superlinear conclusion is equivalent to the appropriate Dennis–Moré directional limit for the DFP Hessian approximations in the unit-step regime.
special_cases_latex: On a strictly convex quadratic with exact line search, DFP has finite termination in at most \(n\) independent directions; this is distinct from the nonlinear local-rate result.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local Q-linear convergence makes \(\sum_k\|x_k-x^*\|\) finite.
The DFP curvature denominators remain positive in the sufficiently small positive-definite neighborhood.
boundary_notes: These local regimes do not supply a nonconvex global guarantee.
DFP and BFGS are dual algebraically but their local estimates should not be interchanged without changing the weighted norm and update convention.

abla^2 f(x_*)\succ0\) and locally Lipschitz Hessian. Starting sufficiently near \(x_*\) with \(H_0\succ0\) sufficiently near \(G_*^{-1}\), define \(p_k=-H_k
abla f(x_k)\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfying the strong Wolfe conditions, set \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\), \(y_k=
abla f(x_k+s_k)-

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Linear Convergence of the DFP Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A neighborhood theorem guaranteeing well-defined DFP iterates and linear convergence from sufficiently accurate initial point and curvature approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R satisfy Assumption 5.4.2. Define
\[
\mu=\|\nabla^2f(x^*)^{-1}\|,
\qquad
\sigma(x_k,x_{k+1})=\max\{\|x_k-x^*\|,\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\}.
\]
Suppose that in a neighborhood of x^*,
\[
\mu\gamma\sigma(x_k,x_{k+1})\le \frac13.
\]
Then there exist \varepsilon>0 and \delta>0 such that
\[
\|x_0-x^*\|<\varepsilon,
\qquad
\|B_0-\nabla^2f(x^*)\|_{\mathrm{DFP}}<\delta
\]
imply that the stated DFP iteration is well-defined and that its iterates converge linearly to x^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the source's Assumption 5.4.2 and neighborhood bound μγσ≤1/3, there are positive initialization tolerances such that a sufficiently close initial point and DFP curvature matrix produce well-defined iterates converging linearly to the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon,\delta>0:\ \bigl(\|x_0-x^*\|<\varepsilon\ \land\ \|B_0-\nabla^2f(x^*)\|_{\mathrm{DFP}}<\delta\bigr)\Rightarrow\bigl(\text{the DFP iteration is well-defined and }x_k\to x^*\text{ linearly}\bigr)

knowledge_statements.title: DFP Superlinear Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dennis–Moré form of the local superlinear DFP regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the setting of local DFP convergence, suppose additionally that the accepted steps eventually satisfy \(\alpha_k=1\) and the inverse approximations obey the Dennis–Moré condition \[\frac{\|(H_k^{-1}-G_*)s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}\longrightarrow0.\] Then the quasi-Newton errors satisfy \(x_k\to x_*\) q-superlinearly: \[\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|}\longrightarrow0.\] For DFP, the condition is obtained in the standard local regime from the secant equation, positive curvature, Lipschitz continuity of the Hessian, and the bounded-deterioration analysis of the metric updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once full steps are accepted and DFP satisfies the Dennis–Moré approximation condition, its locally convergent iterates approach the minimizer q-superlinearly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have a locally Lipschitz Hessian near \(x_*\), with \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\) and \(G_*:=\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local convergence regime for the Broyden class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(B_k\succ0\). Define \(v_k=y_k/(y_k^Ts_k)-B_ks_k/(s_k^TB_ks_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Hessian-form Broyden class is \(B_{k+1}=B_k-B_ks_ks_k^TB_k/(s_k^TB_ks_k)+y_ky_k^T/(y_k^Ts_k)+\phi_k(s_k^TB_ks_k)v_kv_k^T\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broyden-class local convergence concerns the one-parameter family obtained by adding a symmetric rank-one correction to BFGS. A complete regime fixes the parameter range, curvature condition, line search, and neighborhood assumptions. Under the cited exact-line-search local hypotheses, the resulting iterates converge superlinearly. The family statement does not automatically cover parameter choices that make an updated matrix singular or indefinite.

special_cases_latex: \(\phi_k=0\) gives BFGS and \(\phi_k=1\) gives DFP.
For \(\phi_k\in[0,1]\) and \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), positive definiteness is inherited from BFGS and DFP.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded SR1 local consistency and convergence regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth local SR1 analysis. The canonical matrix-consistency result is conditional on a convergent iterate sequence and uniformly linearly independent steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The safeguarded SR1 update is \(B_{k+1}=B_k+(y_k-B_ks_k)(y_k-B_ks_k)^T/((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k)\) whenever \(|s_k^T(y_k-B_ks_k)|\ge r\|s_k\|\|y_k-B_ks_k\|\), with \(r\in(0,1)\); otherwise it sets \(B_{k+1}=B_k\). Its local consistency regime consists of sequences satisfying \(x_k\to x^*\), bounded and Lipschitz-continuous Hessian near \(x^*\), the safeguard at every applied update, and uniformly linearly independent steps. The defining conclusion is \(\|B_k-\nabla^2f(x^*)\|\to0\). When this consistency is coupled with an appropriate unit-step or trust-region iteration, it supplies the directional accuracy needed for a local superlinear rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SR1 local convergence theory uses the unique symmetric rank-one secant correction when its denominator is safely nonzero and skips it otherwise. Under a convergent sequence, Lipschitz Hessian, and sufficiently rich step directions, the entire SR1 matrix sequence converges to the limiting Hessian. An iterate-rate claim additionally requires a specified step-generation or trust-region mechanism; matrix consistency alone is not an attraction theorem.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the inverse form, interchange \((B_k,s_k,y_k)\) with \((H_k,y_k,s_k)\) wherever the inverse update is defined.
special_cases_latex: On a strongly convex quadratic, nonskipped SR1 updates recover the exact inverse Hessian in finitely many linearly independent directions.
Trust-region SR1 permits indefinite \(B_k\), unlike positive-definite line-search quasi-Newton schemes.
immediate_consequences_latex: Full matrix consistency implies the Dennis–Moré directional condition for every nonzero step sequence.
boundary_notes: Uniform linear independence is stronger than merely having nonzero steps.
The SR1 formula may lose positive definiteness; local line-search claims must address this separately.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quasi-Newton model failure is an iteration index \(k\) at which at least one of the following predicates holds: secant-pair failure, meaning the data \((s_k,y_k)\) violate a required curvature or compatibility condition; update-denominator failure, meaning a denominator such as \(s_k^Ty_k\), \(s_k^TB_ks_k\), or \((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k\) is zero or too small relative to its natural scaling; metric failure, meaning \(B_k\) is singular, excessively ill-conditioned, or lacks the definiteness required by the step mechanism; globalization failure, meaning the proposed step does not meet the stated decrease, curvature, or trust-region agreement test; information failure, meaning storage or sampling restrictions prevent the desired secant system from being represented; or smoothness-curvature mismatch, meaning the gradient differences do not reliably approximate Hessian action in the assumed model class. The failure set is the union of these predicates and may contain overlapping categories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The failure taxonomy classifies a quasi-Newton model by explicit mathematical predicates rather than by observed poor performance alone. Failures can arise in the secant pair, an update denominator, the metric, the globalization test, the available curvature information, or the assumed smooth second-order model. More than one category may apply at the same iteration. Each category identifies the structural condition that a safeguard or model change must address.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal F_k=\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{sec}}\cup\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{den}}\cup\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{met}}\cup\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{glob}}\cup\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{info}}\cup\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{smooth}}.\]
special_cases_latex: For BFGS, \(s_k^Ty_k\le0\) is simultaneously a secant-pair and positive-definiteness-preservation failure.
For SR1, a small normalized value of \((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k\) is an update-denominator failure even when \(s_k^Ty_k>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A skipped update changes the state-transition rule but does not erase the failure event.
Trust-region globalization can accommodate an indefinite metric that would be a failure for a positive-definite line-search model.
boundary_notes: The categories are not mutually exclusive.
Slow convergence without a violated predicate is not, by itself, classified as model failure.
A nonsmooth objective can require a different generalized-derivative model rather than a secant safeguard.

notation.meaning: Set of failure predicates active at iteration \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure predicates for a quasi-Newton secant pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s=x^+-x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y=\nabla f(x^+)-\nabla f(x)\in\mathbb R^n\), and consider a symmetric secant equation \(B^+s=y\) or \(H^+y=s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth quasi-Newton updating; the active predicate depends on whether the update requires positive definiteness, a particular denominator, or several secant equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A secant pair \((s,y)\) fails an update requirement if at least one required condition is violated. Basic failures include \(s=0\), which carries no displacement information; a curvature-sign failure \(s^Ty\le0\) for a positive-definite secant update; a near-degeneracy failure \(|s^Ty|\le\varepsilon\|s\|\|y\|\) when the update divides by \(s^Ty\); and update-specific orthogonality such as \(|s^T(y-Bs)|<r\|s\|\|y-Bs\|\) for SR1. For multisecant data \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_q]\) and \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_q]\), symmetric compatibility additionally requires \(S^TY=Y^TS\); violation means that no symmetric matrix can satisfy \(BS=Y\). A pair may be usable for one update and failed for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant-pair failure occurs when the observed displacement and gradient change cannot safely supply the conditions required by the chosen update. Examples are zero displacement, nonpositive curvature for positive-definite BFGS or DFP, a denominator too small relative to the vector norms, or the SR1 residual being almost orthogonal to the displacement. For several pairs, failure also includes incompatibility with a single symmetric secant matrix.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A symmetric multisecant solution \(B=B^T\) to \(BS=Y\) necessarily satisfies \(S^TY=Y^TS\).
special_cases_latex: Under a Wolfe line search and a descent direction, the generated pair satisfies \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), eliminating the BFGS curvature-sign failure.
If \(y=Bs\), the SR1 residual is zero and no correction is needed; this is not an SR1 breakdown.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failed BFGS curvature condition prevents simultaneous satisfaction of \(B^+s=y\) and \(B^+\succ0\).
A failed SR1 denominator safeguard calls for skipping the rank-one correction.
boundary_notes: Small curvature and negative curvature are distinct failure modes even when the same safeguard handles both.
Thresholds \(\varepsilon\) and \(r\) are algorithm parameters and must be stated.

notation.meaning: Matrices collecting multiple displacement and gradient-difference vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Sign Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite secant metrics are impossible for nonpositive pair curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero secant displacement \(s\) and gradient displacement \(y\), a symmetric positive-definite Hessian approximation \(B\) satisfying \(Bs=y\) can exist only if \[s^{\mathsf T}y=s^{\mathsf T}Bs>0.\] Consequently, a pair with \(s^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\) is incompatible with every positive-definite secant metric. Standard BFGS or DFP preservation arguments therefore fail at this boundary: their curvature denominators are zero when \(s^{\mathsf T}y=0\), while negative curvature can produce an indefinite updated metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant pair with nonpositive curvature cannot be fitted by any positive-definite Hessian metric, invalidating the usual BFGS or DFP definiteness guarantee.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonpositive secant-curvature failure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k
e0\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k)\). A positive-definite quasi-Newton update seeks \(B_{k+1}=B_{k+1}^T\succ0\) satisfying \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional quasi-Newton updating when the target Hessian or inverse-Hessian approximation is required to remain positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The secant pair \((s_k,y_k)\) has a curvature-sign failure precisely when \(s_k^Ty_k\le0\). The strict inequality \(s_k^Ty_k>0\) is necessary for any symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_{k+1}\) satisfying \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), and it is the curvature condition used by BFGS and DFP to preserve positive definiteness. The case \(s_k^Ty_k=0\) is a zero-curvature failure; \(s_k^Ty_k<0\) is a negative-curvature failure. A numerical implementation may strengthen the test to \(s_k^Ty_k\ge\delta\|s_k\|^2\) or \(s_k^Ty_k\ge\varepsilon\|s_k\|\|y_k\|\), but these quantitative safeguards define near-failure regions in addition to the canonical sign failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature-sign failure means that the displacement and gradient change have nonpositive inner product. In that case no positive-definite symmetric matrix can satisfy the secant equation for that pair, and the ordinary positive-definite BFGS or DFP update cannot be used as intended. Zero and negative curvature are distinguished, while small positive curvature is a separate numerical near-failure condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(s_k=\alpha_kd_k\) with \(\alpha_k>0\), then \(s_k^Ty_k=\alpha_k\bigl(\nabla f(x_{k+1})^Td_k-\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k\bigr)\).
special_cases_latex: For a strongly convex function, every nonzero pair satisfies \(s_k^Ty_k>0\).
For a descent direction and a Wolfe curvature step, \(s_k^Ty_k\ge(c_2-1)\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If curvature-sign failure occurs, an unmodified BFGS denominator is nonpositive and positive-definiteness preservation is lost.
Damping, regularization, rejection, or a model allowing indefinite curvature is required if the algorithm must continue.
boundary_notes: SR1 does not require \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), so this predicate is not automatically an SR1 failure.
A very small positive value is not a sign failure, although it may be a near-singular-denominator failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singular Update Denominators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small update denominators cause unbounded rank-one corrections and numerical sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inverse-SR1 residual \(r=s-Hy\), the accepted correction is \[\Delta H=\frac{rr^{\mathsf T}}{r^{\mathsf T}y},\qquad \|\Delta H\|_2=\frac{\|r\|_2^2}{|r^{\mathsf T}y|}.\] Thus, if \(r\neq0\) and \(|r^{\mathsf T}y|/\|r\|^2\to0\), the correction norm diverges. Analogously, BFGS and DFP formulas become sensitive as \(|s^{\mathsf T}y|\) approaches zero. A safeguard such as \(|r^{\mathsf T}y|\geq\eta\|r\|\|y\|\) separates accepted SR1 updates from this near-singular regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a secant-update denominator is tiny relative to its numerator, the low-rank correction becomes arbitrarily large and should be skipped or safeguarded.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is the spectral norm \(\|\cdot\|_2\).
