knowledge_statements.statement_title: Near-Singular Denominator Event in a Secant Update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\) be a Hessian approximation, let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be a secant pair, and let an update formula contain scalar divisors \(d_j(B,s,y)\), \(j=1,\ldots,q\). For each divisor choose a positive, dimensionally compatible scale \(\sigma_j(B,s,y)>0\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon_j\geq 0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic secant updates in exact or floating-point arithmetic. The definition is relative to explicitly chosen scales and tolerances and covers BFGS-type and other rational low-rank updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The data \((B,s,y)\) have a near-singular update denominator when \(\min_{1\leq j\leq q}|d_j(B,s,y)|/\sigma_j(B,s,y)\leq\varepsilon_j\), with the comparison interpreted componentwise for the selected tolerances. An exactly singular denominator is the case \(d_j(B,s,y)=0\) for some \(j\). For the direct BFGS update, the relevant divisors are \(d_1=y^Ts\) and \(d_2=s^TBs\); natural scales include \(\sigma_1=\|y\|_2\|s\|_2\) and \(\sigma_2=\|B^{1/2}s\|_2^2\) when \(B\succ0\). The designation concerns algebraic sensitivity of the update, independently of whether the resulting matrix is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant pair and current matrix exhibit a near-singular update denominator if at least one scalar used as a divisor by the update is small relative to a stated compatible scale. A zero divisor is the exactly singular case. For direct BFGS the principal divisors are yᵀs and sᵀBs. This classification concerns sensitivity of the update formula and does not by itself assert that the updated matrix is indefinite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed positive scales, the condition is equivalent to \(\min_j |d_j|/\sigma_j\leq\max_j\varepsilon_j\) when all tolerances are equal.
Exact singularity is equivalently membership in \(\bigcup_{j=1}^q\{(B,s,y):d_j(B,s,y)=0\}\).
special_cases_latex: For BFGS with \(B\succ0\) and \(s\neq0\), \(s^TBs>0\); hence exact singularity can arise from that divisor only if positive definiteness or nonzero displacement has already failed.
For SR1, the denominator is \((y-Bs)^Ts\), so the same definition applies with scale \(\|y-Bs\|_2\|s\|_2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A small normalized divisor can amplify perturbations in \(B\), \(s\), or \(y\) in any update term proportional to \(1/d_j\).
The definition supplies a scale-invariant skip-or-damp test when each \(d_j\) and \(\sigma_j\) transform identically under rescaling.
boundary_notes: A small unnormalized denominator is not necessarily near-singular when the associated vectors are proportionally small.
Curvature-sign failure and inconsistency of several secant equations are separate conditions.

Inconsistent Multisecant Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for fitting several secant pairs with one symmetric metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_m]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) have full column rank and let \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\). If a symmetric matrix \(B\) satisfies all multisecant equations \(BS=Y\), then \[S^{\mathsf T}Y=S^{\mathsf T}BS=(S^{\mathsf T}BS)^{\mathsf T}=Y^{\mathsf T}S.\] Hence nonsymmetry of \(S^{\mathsf T}Y\) certifies that the secant information is inconsistent with every symmetric metric. If \(B\succ0\) is required, the stronger necessary condition \(S^{\mathsf T}Y\succ0\) holds. For full-column-rank \(S\), these respective conditions also permit symmetric and positive-definite symmetric extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple secant equations admit a symmetric metric only when their cross-curvatures are symmetric; a positive-definite metric additionally requires a positive-definite cross-curvature matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) contains the paired gradient displacements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(BS=Y,\ B=B^{\mathsf T}\Longrightarrow S^{\mathsf T}Y=Y^{\mathsf T}S\), and \(B\succ0\Longrightarrow S^{\mathsf T}Y\succ0\).

notation.meaning: common Hessian metric fitted to all pairs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inconsistency of Exact Multisecant Data
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_m]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\), \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\), and let \(\mathcal{M}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be the admissible model class, such as all matrices, symmetric matrices, or symmetric positive-definite matrices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact multisecant equations. Approximate consistency is included through a separately declared residual tolerance; statistical inconsistency of noisy observations is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multisecant information \((S,Y)\) is inconsistent relative to \(\mathcal{M}\) when no admissible matrix satisfies every secant equation, that is, when \(\{B\in\mathcal{M}:BS=Y\}=\varnothing\). Given a matrix norm, weights \(W\succ0\), a scale \(\sigma(S,Y)>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), it is \(\varepsilon\)-inconsistent when \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal{M}}\|(BS-Y)W^{1/2}\|/\sigma(S,Y)>\varepsilon\). Thus inconsistency is relative to the structural restrictions imposed on the model; data may be consistent for unrestricted matrices but inconsistent for symmetric or positive-definite models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multisecant data are inconsistent relative to an admissible matrix class when there is no matrix in that class mapping every stored displacement column in S to the corresponding curvature column in Y. An approximate version declares inconsistency when the smallest normalized weighted residual over the admissible class exceeds a stated tolerance. Consistency therefore depends on whether the model is unrestricted, symmetric, positive definite, sparse, or otherwise structured.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For unrestricted \(B\), exact consistency is equivalent to \(\ker S\subseteq\ker Y\).
For a symmetric solution, exact consistency requires and, together with \(\ker S\subseteq\ker Y\), is characterized by symmetry of \(S^TY\).
special_cases_latex: If \(S\) has full column rank, unrestricted exact multisecant information is always consistent.
If \(B\succ0\) is required, consistency additionally forces \(S^TY\) to be positive definite on the quotient determined by nonzero combinations of columns of \(S\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If exact information is inconsistent, any update must discard, alter, weight, or approximately fit at least one secant relation.
The residual definition yields a quantitative certificate usable for regularized multisecant fitting.
boundary_notes: A large residual caused only by measurement noise is not distinguished from deterministic model incompatibility here.
Pairwise consistency does not guarantee joint consistency under symmetry or structural restrictions.

notation.meaning: matrices of stored displacement and curvature-difference columns
feasible set of exact multisecant models

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of an Intended Variable Metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be intended to define the quadratic metric \(\|p\|_{B_k}^2=p^TB_kp\). Fix admissibility constants \(0<\underline\lambda\leq\overline\lambda<\infty\) and symmetry tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\rm sym}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variable-metric methods. The definition treats a metric as an algorithmic object required to be approximately symmetric and uniformly positive definite with controlled scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matrix \(B_k\) has a metric failure relative to \((\underline\lambda,\overline\lambda,\varepsilon_{\rm sym})\) when it lies outside the admissible metric class \(\mathcal G=\{B:\|B-B^T\|_2\leq\varepsilon_{\rm sym}\|B\|_2,\ \underline\lambda\|p\|_2^2\leq p^T(B+B^T)p/2\leq\overline\lambda\|p\|_2^2\ \forall p\}\). Consequently a failure occurs through excessive asymmetry, nonpositive or insufficient curvature, or excessive maximum curvature. The definition is deliberately relative to quantitative bounds: a positive-definite matrix may still fail as an intended metric when its smallest eigenvalue is too small or its largest eigenvalue is too large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intended variable metric fails when its matrix is outside a declared admissible class requiring approximate symmetry and uniform lower and upper quadratic-form bounds. This includes asymmetry, loss of positive definiteness, curvature that is too small for numerical reliability, and curvature that is too large for the permitted conditioning or scale. Positive definiteness alone therefore does not preclude a metric failure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For exactly symmetric \(B_k\), admissibility is equivalent to \(\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\leq\lambda_{\max}(B_k)\leq\overline\lambda\).
For symmetric admissible matrices, \(B_k\) and \(B_k^{-1}\) induce norms uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean norm.
special_cases_latex: Taking \(\underline\lambda=0\) without strict inequality admits positive-semidefinite pseudometrics and changes the object class.
For inverse-Hessian metrics \(H_k\), the same definition applies directly to \(H_k\), with reciprocal spectral bounds corresponding to \(B_k=H_k^{-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Outside \(\mathcal G\), the expression \(p^TB_kp\) may fail to be a reliable squared norm.
Uniform admissibility bounds control the spectral condition number by \(\overline\lambda/\underline\lambda\).
boundary_notes: This is an umbrella admissibility definition; loss of positive definiteness and ill-conditioning are narrower subclasses.
Model inaccuracy relative to the true Hessian is not alone a metric failure if the admissibility bounds remain satisfied.

notation.meaning: required lower and upper quadratic-form bounds

review_flags: The supplied sources discuss positive definiteness and bounded conditioning but no exact canonical umbrella definition matching this taxonomy was located.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of an Intended Variable Metric
Loss of Positive Definiteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional counterexample showing definiteness loss under negative secant curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension, let the inverse metric be \(H>0\) and take nonzero scalars \(s,y\) with \(sy<0\). The inverse-form DFP update reduces to \[H_+=H+\frac{s^2}{sy}-\frac{H^2y^2}{Hy^2}=\frac{s}{y}<0.\] Thus a positive initial metric becomes negative after one update. The associated quasi-Newton direction \(p=-H_+g\) is then an ascent direction whenever \(g\neq0\), because \(gp=-H_+g^2>0\). Positive curvature is therefore essential to the usual DFP positive-definiteness and descent guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With negative curvature, even a positive scalar DFP metric becomes negative in one update, turning the nominal quasi-Newton direction into an ascent direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Strict Positive Definiteness
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb{S}^n\) be a symmetric Hessian or metric approximation that is required to satisfy \(B_k\succ0\). If an update is considered, write \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric matrices. Both singular positive-semidefinite matrices and indefinite matrices count as losing strict positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The metric approximation loses positive definiteness at iteration \(k+1\) when \(B_k\succ0\) but \(B_{k+1}\not\succ0\). Equivalently, there exists a nonzero direction \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(p^TB_{k+1}p\leq0\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(B_{k+1})\leq0\). If no predecessor is being compared, a matrix exhibits the failed state simply when it is not strictly positive definite. The equality case represents loss through singularity; a negative value represents an indefinite metric and supplies a direction of nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric metric approximation loses positive definiteness when an update takes a previously positive-definite matrix to one that is not positive definite. This is equivalent to the updated matrix having a nonzero direction with nonpositive quadratic form, or a smallest eigenvalue no greater than zero. A singular positive-semidefinite matrix counts as a loss because strict positive definiteness is required.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For symmetric \(B_{k+1}\), failure is equivalent to the nonexistence of a Cholesky factor with strictly positive diagonal.
Failure is equivalent to \(\inf_{\|p\|_2=1}p^TB_{k+1}p\leq0\).
special_cases_latex: For BFGS in exact arithmetic, \(B_k\succ0\) and \(s_k^Ty_k>0\) exclude this failure for the standard direct update.
For an inverse approximation \(H_{k+1}\), the definition is identical with \(H\) replacing \(B\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B_{k+1}\) is nonsingular but indefinite, \(-B_{k+1}^{-1}g\) need not be a descent direction.
If \(B_{k+1}\) is singular, the induced quadratic expression is not a norm.
boundary_notes: A very small but positive minimum eigenvalue is metric ill-conditioning, not loss of positive definiteness under this strict algebraic definition.
Floating-point Cholesky failure may occur before mathematical definiteness is lost and requires a numerical tolerance.

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-definiteness preservation under the DFP curvature condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient curvature condition preventing loss of positive definiteness in a DFP inverse-Hessian update, including the exact-line-search specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k=H_k^T\succ0\), and define
\[
H_{k+1}=H_k+\frac{p_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}-\frac{H_kq_kq_k^TH_k}{q_k^TH_kq_k}.
\]
If \(p_k^Tq_k>0\), then \(H_{k+1}=H_{k+1}^T\succ0\). In the DFP iteration, if \(p_k=\alpha_k(-H_kg_k)\), \(q_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and an attained exact line search has \(\alpha_k>0\), then \(p_k^Tg_{k+1}=0\) and
\[
p_k^Tq_k=\alpha_k g_k^TH_kg_k>0
\]
whenever \(g_k\ne0\). Exact line search is not necessary for preservation; the condition \(p_k^Tq_k>0\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The DFP update preserves symmetry and positive definiteness whenever the step and gradient difference have positive inner product. At a nonstationary iterate, a positive exact line-search step along the DFP direction yields this curvature condition, although any step satisfying it is sufficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral boundary at which positive-definite variable metrics lose uniform equivalence or exhibit unbounded forward or inverse sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) define \(p=-Hg\). Then \(\|H\|_2=\lambda_{\max}(H)\), \(\|H^{-1}\|_2=1/\lambda_{\min}(H)\), and \(\kappa_2(H)=\lambda_{\max}(H)/\lambda_{\min}(H)\). For perturbations \(\delta g\) and \(\delta p\), \[\|H\delta g\|_2\leq\lambda_{\max}(H)\|\delta g\|_2,\qquad \|H^{-1}\delta p\|_2\leq\frac{1}{\lambda_{\min}(H)}\|\delta p\|_2.\] Hence a sequence \((H_k)\) is uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean metric exactly when constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\) exist such that \[mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\quad\text{for every }k.\] If \(\lambda_{\max}(H_k)\) is unbounded, forward direction sensitivity can be unbounded; if \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\downarrow0\), inverse sensitivity can be unbounded. Either event destroys uniform metric equivalence even though every \(H_k\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive definiteness alone does not provide uniform numerical control. Unbounded largest eigenvalues can amplify gradient errors, while smallest eigenvalues approaching zero can amplify errors when the metric is inverted; either behavior destroys uniform metric equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \(p=-H_kg\), with perturbations measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform metric equivalence holds if and only if \(0<m\leq\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\leq\lambda_{\max}(H_k)\leq M<\infty\) for every \(k\); loss of either outer bound permits unbounded forward or inverse sensitivity.

notation.meaning: smallest and largest eigenvalues of the metric
uniform positive lower and finite upper spectral bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Ill-Conditioning of a Positive-Definite Metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) be a positive-definite metric matrix, let \(\kappa_{\max}\geq1\) be an admissible condition-number bound, and optionally let \(0<\underline\lambda\leq\overline\lambda\) be absolute spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric positive-definite metrics. Indefinite or singular matrices are excluded so that this slot remains distinct from loss of positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The metric \(B\) is ill-conditioned relative to \(\kappa_{\max}\) when its spectral condition number \(\kappa_2(B)=\|B\|_2\|B^{-1}\|_2=\lambda_{\max}(B)/\lambda_{\min}(B)\) exceeds \(\kappa_{\max}\). Under absolute spectral requirements it is also scale-inadmissible when \(\lambda_{\min}(B)<\underline\lambda\) or \(\lambda_{\max}(B)>\overline\lambda\), even if the ratio is acceptable. A sequence \(\{B_k\}\subset\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) becomes asymptotically ill-conditioned when \(\kappa_2(B_k)\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric is ill-conditioned when the ratio of its largest to smallest eigenvalue exceeds a declared bound. A sequence becomes asymptotically ill-conditioned when this ratio diverges. Separate absolute eigenvalue limits may also identify an inadmissible scale even when the eigenvalue ratio is moderate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Ill-conditioning is equivalent to the absence of any \(c>0\) with \(c\|p\|_2^2\leq p^TBp\leq\kappa_{\max}c\|p\|_2^2\) for every \(p\).
special_cases_latex: For diagonal \(B=\operatorname{diag}(b_i)\succ0\), \(\kappa_2(B)=\max_i b_i/\min_i b_i\).
A scalar multiple \(cB\), \(c>0\), has the same condition number as \(B\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Large \(\kappa_2(B)\) means that the metric strongly distorts Euclidean lengths in different eigendirections.
Solving systems with \(B\) can amplify relative perturbations by a factor governed by its condition number.
boundary_notes: A matrix with \(\lambda_{\min}(B)=0\) is singular and belongs to loss of positive definiteness rather than this positive-definite regime.
Condition-number thresholds are application- and precision-dependent.
review_flags: The definition is standard linear algebra, but an inspected source with an exact supporting locator was not attached.
The optional absolute-scale criterion is a taxonomy choice requiring validation.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Ill-Conditioning of a Positive-Definite Metric
Unstable Low-Rank Realizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation and denominator sensitivity in factored low-rank metric updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a realized symmetric low-rank correction \(H_+=H+\sigma uu^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\sigma=(u^{\mathsf T}v)^{-1}\), then \[\|H_+-H\|_2=\frac{\|u\|_2^2}{|u^{\mathsf T}v|}.\] Hence nearly orthogonal \(u\) and \(v\) can produce an arbitrarily large correction. Moreover, when \(H\) and \(\sigma uu^{\mathsf T}\) are individually large but nearly cancel in some direction, floating-point addition incurs large relative error in the small resulting eigenvalue. Stable realization therefore requires denominator safeguards and monitoring of the updated spectrum or factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank update is unstable when its denominator is tiny or when large terms nearly cancel, because either mechanism magnifies errors in the realized metric.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerically Unstable Low-Rank Matrix Realization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Represent a matrix as \(B=B_0+\sum_{j=1}^r u_jv_j^T\), or by a symmetric specialization of this form. Let \(u_{\rm mach}>0\) be unit roundoff and let \(\tau\in(0,1)\) be an allowed relative realization-error level.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point realization of finite-rank updates. The definition addresses cancellation and factor sensitivity, not merely the mathematical rank of the correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the cancellation factor \(\Gamma=(\|B_0\|+\sum_{j=1}^r\|u_j\|_2\|v_j\|_2)/\|B\|\) for \(B\neq0\), using the same subordinate matrix norm in numerator and denominator. The low-rank realization is unstable relative to \((u_{\rm mach},\tau)\) when \(u_{\rm mach}\Gamma>\tau\), or when an equivalent factorized evaluation has relative condition number exceeding \(\tau/u_{\rm mach}\). For \(B=0\), a representation with a nonzero numerator is maximally cancellation-prone. Instability is a property of the chosen realization: the same matrix may admit another factorization with a much smaller cancellation factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank realization is numerically unstable when the norms of its base and rank-one terms are large compared with the norm of their assembled sum, so that roundoff multiplied by this cancellation factor exceeds an allowed relative error. The property belongs to the representation, not solely to the represented matrix; refactoring can therefore remove the failure without changing the exact matrix.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The threshold condition is equivalent to \(\Gamma>\tau/u_{\rm mach}\).
A normwise backward-stability formulation may replace \(\Gamma\) by the relative condition number of the factor-to-matrix assembly map.
special_cases_latex: Oppositely signed, nearly equal rank-one terms can yield large \(\Gamma\) even when every factor has moderate norm.
A compact representation \(B=B_0+UMV^T\) uses the analogous numerator \(\|B_0\|+\|U\|\|M\|\|V\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A large cancellation factor permits small relative perturbations of stored factors to cause a large relative perturbation of the assembled matrix.
Recompression or refactorization can improve stability while preserving the exact represented matrix.
boundary_notes: A near-singular scalar update denominator may cause large factors but is a distinct upstream failure.
The criterion does not assert that matrix-vector products are unstable under every evaluation scheme.

notation.meaning: normwise cancellation factor of the realization

review_flags: No authoritative source was located for this exact cancellation-factor definition in quasi-Newton low-rank realizations.
The threshold and normwise stability model are proposed operational choices requiring specialist review.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of a Globalization Mechanism
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider an iterative method producing trial steps \(p_{k,j}\) at iterate \(x_k\), with an acceptance predicate \(A_k(p_{k,j})\in\{0,1\}\), globalization parameters \(\theta_{k,j}\), and a stationarity measure \(\chi(x)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic line-search or trust-region globalization. The definition separates inability to accept a trial from accepted-step stagnation away from stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globalization failure at iteration \(k\) occurs if the inner trial process does not produce an accepted step in its permitted domain, namely \(A_k(p_{k,j})=0\) for every admissible trial \(j\), or if it produces an infinite accepted subsequence for which \(\chi(x_k)\geq\epsilon>0\) while \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\to0\) and the globalization parameter collapses. For a line search, collapse means \(\alpha_k\to0\); for a trust region, it means \(\Delta_k\to0\). The acceptance predicate must be specified, because failure is relative to the sufficient-decrease, curvature, ratio, feasibility, or filter conditions imposed by the method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globalization mechanism fails when its allowed trial process cannot find an acceptable step, or when accepted steps and their controlling step lengths or trust-region radii collapse to zero while a declared stationarity measure stays bounded away from zero. The failure is relative to the method's explicit acceptance predicate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The first alternative says that the acceptable-trial set \(\{p\in\mathcal P_k:A_k(p)=1\}\) is empty.
For a terminating implementation, exhausting the prescribed trial budget without acceptance is the finite operational counterpart of the first alternative.
special_cases_latex: In an Armijo line search, the predicate may be \(f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha g_k^Tp_k\).
In a trust-region method, the predicate is commonly based on a ratio of actual to predicted reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failed globalization step cannot furnish the progress guarantee encoded by its acceptance predicate.
Repeated collapse away from stationarity invalidates a standard route to global convergence.
boundary_notes: Rejection of one trial is normal algorithmic behavior and is not by itself a globalization failure.
Convergence to a stationary point with vanishing steps is excluded from the stagnation alternative.

notation.meaning: step length, trust-region radius, or analogous globalization parameter

review_flags: The inspected sources describe line-search and trust-region acceptance but do not supply this exact umbrella definition.
The disjunctive operational taxonomy requires authoritative validation.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of a Globalization Mechanism
Line-Search Curvature Incompatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong Wolfe curvature forces positive secant curvature along every descent line-search step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=
abla f(x)\), choose a descent direction \(p\) with \(g^{\mathsf T}p<0\), and set \(s=\alpha p\), \(y=
abla f(x+s)-g\) for \(\alpha>0\). If the strong Wolfe curvature condition \[|
abla f(x+s)^{\mathsf T}p|\leq c_2|g^{\mathsf T}p|,\qquad 0<c_2<1,\] holds, then \[s^{\mathsf T}y\geq\alpha(1-c_2)(-g^{\mathsf T}p)>0.\] Therefore a computed pair with \(s^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\) cannot simultaneously arise from an exact-gradient descent step satisfying strong Wolfe curvature; noise, nonsmoothness, inconsistent gradients, or line-search failure must have violated the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong Wolfe step along a descent direction necessarily has positive secant curvature; a nonpositive measured curvature pair signals incompatible data or a failed line search.
assumptions_latex: The strong Wolfe curvature inequality holds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incompatibility of Line-Search and Secant Curvature Requirements
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable along \(x+\alpha p\), let \(g=\nabla f(x)\), and let \(\mathcal A\subset(0,\alpha_{\max}]\) be the step lengths satisfying the line-search acceptance conditions. For \(\alpha>0\), set \(s(\alpha)=\alpha p\) and \(y(\alpha)=\nabla f(x+\alpha p)-g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic line searches coupled to a secant update requiring a stated positive-curvature margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a curvature margin \(\eta>0\) and scale \(\sigma(\alpha)>0\). The line search is curvature-incompatible with the secant update when no accepted step supplies the required curvature, that is, \(\{\alpha\in\mathcal A:y(\alpha)^Ts(\alpha)\geq\eta\sigma(\alpha)\}=\varnothing\). With the unscaled requirement \(y^Ts>0\), incompatibility means that every line-search-acceptable step has nonpositive secant curvature. The definition also includes the case \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\), but distinguishes it explicitly as failure of the line-search conditions themselves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Line-search curvature incompatibility occurs when no step length accepted by the line search also provides the positive secant curvature, with its stated margin and scale, required by the matrix update. Under the basic BFGS requirement this means every accepted step has yᵀs no greater than zero. An empty line-search acceptance set is a separate subcase.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Incompatibility is equivalent to \(\sup_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}(y(\alpha)^Ts(\alpha)-\eta\sigma(\alpha))<0\) when \(\mathcal A\) is nonempty and the supremum is attained.
For the ordinary Wolfe curvature condition and a descent direction, \(y(\alpha)^Ts(\alpha)\geq(1-c_2)(-\alpha g^Tp)>0\); hence exact Wolfe acceptance excludes the zero-margin incompatibility.
special_cases_latex: Strong Wolfe acceptance also supplies positive secant curvature for a descent direction when \(0<c_2<1\).
A restricted interval \((0,\alpha_{\max}]\) may be incompatible even if acceptable curvature exists for a larger step.
immediate_consequences_latex: An undamped BFGS update cannot simultaneously use an accepted pair and preserve its usual positive-definiteness condition when the basic incompatibility holds.
The algorithm must modify acceptance, damp the pair, skip the update, or change the direction.
boundary_notes: Failure caused by inaccurate gradients belongs additionally to noisy-curvature reliability analysis.
A merely small positive value of \(y^Ts\) is a near-singular-denominator issue unless it violates the declared margin.

notation.meaning: secant displacement and gradient difference generated by a trial step

review_flags: Standard Wolfe formulas support the relationship between accepted steps and positive secant curvature, but no inspected locator was attached for this exact set-incompatibility definition.
The scaled-margin variant requires source validation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Rejection Followed by Nonstationary Stagnation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At an outer iterate \(x_k\), let \(p_{k,j}\) be successive trial steps, \(a_{k,j}\in\{0,1\}\) their acceptance indicators, and \(r_{k,j}>0\) a controlling radius or step-length bound. Let \(\chi(x)\) be a stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic globalization with repeated inner trials. A finite implementation may replace the asymptotic definition by explicit rejection-count and minimum-radius thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rejection-stagnation failure cascade occurs when there is an infinite sequence of trials or outer iterations for which rejected trials force \(r_{k,j+1}\leq\gamma r_{k,j}\) with a fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), so that \(r_{k,j}\to0\), while the accepted displacement is absent or satisfies \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\to0\), and stationarity does not improve: \(\liminf\chi(x_k)>0\). The term cascade records the ordered conjunction of repeated rejection, parameter contraction, vanishing displacement, and persistence away from stationarity; none of these events alone is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejection-stagnation cascade is an ordered failure in which repeated rejected trials contract the permitted step size or trust-region radius toward zero, the iterate consequently remains fixed or moves by vanishing amounts, and a stationarity measure stays bounded away from zero. Rejection, contraction, or small steps alone do not constitute the cascade.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At a fixed outer iterate, infinitely many contractions with \(0<\gamma<1\) imply that all trial displacements constrained by \(\|p_{k,j}\|\leq r_{k,j}\) vanish.
A finite failure certificate may require \(J\) consecutive rejections, \(r_{k,J}\leq r_{\min}\), and \(\chi(x_k)\geq\epsilon\).
special_cases_latex: For backtracking, \(r_{k,j}=\alpha_{k,j}\|p_k\|\).
For trust regions, \(r_{k,j}=\Delta_{k,j}\) and rejected steps leave the outer iterate unchanged.
immediate_consequences_latex: The cascade prevents a nontrivial accepted displacement while stationarity remains unresolved.
A safeguard must change the model, direction, acceptance test, or termination diagnosis to exit the cascade.
boundary_notes: A finite number of rejected trials followed by acceptance is ordinary globalization behavior.
Vanishing steps at a stationary solution do not satisfy the nonstationarity condition.

notation.meaning: trial step bound or trust-region radius

review_flags: No authoritative source was located that defines this named four-stage cascade.
The asymptotic and finite operational variants require validation against the intended taxonomy.

children.title: Persistent Step Rejection
children.top_down_role: Globalization regimes repeatedly refusing proposed quasi-Newton steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Step Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region rejection at a fixed accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be the current accepted iterate, and let trial steps \(p_j\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(\lVert p_j\rVert\leq\Delta_j\). For predicted reductions \(d_j=m_j(0)-m_j(p_j)>0\), define \(\rho_j=(f(x)-f(x+p_j))/d_j\). Given an acceptance threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), persistent step rejection occurs when there exists \(j_0\) such that \(\rho_j<\eta\) for every \(j\geq j_0\), so no such trial point replaces \(x\). If every rejection also satisfies \(\Delta_{j+1}\leq\gamma\Delta_j\) for a fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), then \(\Delta_j\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent step rejection occurs when all trials from some index onward fail the acceptance test at one accepted iterate. If each rejection geometrically contracts the trust-region radius, the admissible trial size converges to zero while the accepted iterate remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No trial with \(j\geq j_0\) replaces \(x\), and under geometric rejection contraction, \(\Delta_j\to0\).

notation.meaning: actual-to-predicted reduction ratio for trial j
positive predicted reduction for trial j

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstationary stagnation of accepted quasi-Newton iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be accepted iterates for continuously differentiable \(f\). Iteration stagnation at a nonstationary scale is the simultaneous occurrence of \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\to0\) and \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\geq\varepsilon\) for some \(\varepsilon>0\). Thus diminishing displacement is not accompanied by convergence to first-order stationarity. Exact stagnation is the special case in which \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted iterates stagnate when their displacements vanish while the gradient remains bounded away from zero; eventual repetition is exact stagnation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed nonstationary-stagnation predicate is mathematically coherent and matches the leaf, but no citation supports this particular definition or its exact-stagnation specialization. An authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Rejection-to-Stagnation Transition

knowledge_statements.title: Rejection-to-Stagnation Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-radius contraction converts repeated rejection into vanishing trial motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that after an accepted iterate \(x\), every trial \(x+p_j\) is rejected, \(\lVert p_j\rVert\leq\Delta_j\), and the rejection rule satisfies \(\Delta_{j+1}\leq\gamma\Delta_j\) for a fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\). Then \(\Delta_j\leq\gamma^{j-j_0}\Delta_{j_0}\) and hence \(\lVert p_j\rVert\to0\), while the accepted-iterate sequence remains equal to \(x\). If additionally \(\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert>0\), this transition produces exact nonstationary stagnation rather than convergence to a stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated rejection plus geometric radius contraction forces trial steps to zero and freezes the accepted iterate, even when that iterate is nonstationary.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert p_j\rVert\leq\Delta_j\) and every trial is rejected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert p_j\rVert\to0\) and all subsequent accepted iterates equal \(x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch measured by disagreement between actual and quadratic-model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), and define \(m(p)=f(x)+g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Bp\). Choose \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(\lVert p\rVert\leq\Delta\) and \(d=m(0)-m(p)>0\). For \(\tau\in(0,1)\), trust-region model mismatch occurs when \(\lvert f(x+p)-m(p)\rvert>\tau d\). Defining \(\rho=(f(x)-f(x+p))/d\), this condition is equivalent to \(\lvert1-\rho\rvert>\tau\). Separately, under an acceptance rule with threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the trial crosses the rejection boundary when \(\rho<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region model is mismatched when its prediction error exceeds a prescribed fraction of the predicted reduction. This is equivalent to the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio lying more than that fraction away from one. A separate acceptance threshold determines whether the trial is rejected.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\in(0,1)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\) when the rejection boundary is considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model mismatch is equivalent to \(\lvert1-\rho\rvert>\tau\); under the stated acceptance rule, rejection occurs when \(\rho<\eta\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Actual-to-Predicted Reduction Mismatch
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(m_k\) be a local model satisfying \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\), and let \(p_k\) obey \(\|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k\). Define \(\operatorname{ared}_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)\) and \(\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic trust-region steps with positive predicted reduction. Undefined or nonpositive predicted reduction is treated as a separate model-subproblem failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
When \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), define \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\). For a declared tolerance \(\eta_{\rm mm}\in(0,1)
\), the trial exhibits trust-region model mismatch when \(|\rho_k-1|>\eta_{\rm mm}\); it exhibits rejection-level mismatch when \(\rho_k<\eta_{\rm acc}\), where \(\eta_{\rm acc}\) is the algorithm's acceptance threshold. Equivalently, the absolute error in predicted reduction exceeds \(\eta_{\rm mm}\operatorname{pred}_k\). Persistent mismatch means that this condition holds along a sequence with \(\Delta_k\to0\), rather than merely for an isolated trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a trust-region trial with positive predicted reduction, model mismatch is measured by the ratio of actual objective reduction to predicted model reduction. A trial is mismatched when this ratio differs from one by more than a stated tolerance, and it reaches rejection level when the ratio falls below the method's acceptance threshold. Persistence as the radius shrinks is stronger than an isolated mismatch.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is equivalent to \(|\operatorname{ared}_k-\operatorname{pred}_k|>\eta_{\rm mm}\operatorname{pred}_k\).
Rejection-level mismatch is \(\operatorname{ared}_k<\eta_{\rm acc}\operatorname{pred}_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\operatorname{ared}_k<0<\operatorname{pred}_k\), then \(\rho_k<0\) and the model predicts decrease while the objective increases.
If \(\rho_k>1\), the model underpredicts the achieved reduction; this is mismatch but need not cause rejection.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small ratio normally triggers rejection and contraction of the trust-region radius.
A ratio near one certifies agreement only for the sampled step, not uniform accuracy throughout the region.
boundary_notes: When \(\operatorname{pred}_k\leq0\), the ratio is not used by this definition.
Mismatch tolerances and acceptance thresholds are algorithm-specific.
review_flags: Trust-region sources support the reduction ratio and acceptance mechanism, but no inspected exact locator was attached for the tolerance-based mismatch definition.
The symmetric mismatch threshold is an operational convention rather than a verified canonical term.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Compressed Curvature Information at Scale
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal I_k\) be the curvature information retained at iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal R(\mathcal I_k)\) be the induced linear model \(B_k\), and let \(\mathcal T_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the directions on which adequate curvature action is required. Let \(C_k\) denote a reference curvature operator when available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale methods using limited-memory, sparse, structured, sampled, or matrix-free curvature representations. Adequacy is relative to declared directions and resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The retained information has a large-scale information failure relative to tolerance \(\varepsilon\) when it satisfies the storage or application budget but cannot produce an admissible model with normalized action error at most \(\varepsilon\): \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal M(\mathcal I_k)}\sup_{v\in\mathcal T_k\setminus\{0\}}\|(B-C_k)v\|/(\|C_kv\|+\delta\|v\|)>\varepsilon\), where \(\delta>0\) regularizes zero reference action. The failure may arise because retained pairs are stale, sparsity is destroyed, or the representation class omits problem structure. This is an adequacy failure, not merely the fact that less than full-matrix information is stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large-scale curvature information fails when, despite meeting its storage or application budget, every model realizable from that information has normalized curvature-action error above a declared tolerance on the directions relevant to the algorithm. Limited storage by itself is not a failure; the defining feature is inadequate recoverable action. Staleness, fill-in, and structure mismatch are narrower mechanisms.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a finite test matrix \(V_k\), the directional supremum may be replaced by a normalized residual norm \(\|(B-C_k)V_k\|/\sigma_k\).
If \(C_k\) is unavailable, observed Hessian-vector products or secant pairs may define the reference tests.
special_cases_latex: Limited-memory failure restricts \(\mathcal M(\mathcal I_k)\) to models generated by the retained pairs.
Sparse failure restricts the class to a prescribed nonzero pattern or fill budget.
immediate_consequences_latex: No reconstruction from the retained data can meet the declared directional accuracy without acquiring or preserving additional information.
The definition separates information insufficiency from a poor choice among otherwise adequate reconstructions.
boundary_notes: The reference operator and test directions must be specified; otherwise adequacy is not identifiable.
This definition does not require forming \(C_k\) as a dense matrix.

notation.meaning: models realizable from the retained information under the resource budget
directions on which curvature action must be accurate

Stale Limited-Memory Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stored secant pairs cease to represent curvature at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\), let \(x_k\) be current, and let \((s_i,y_i)\) be a stored limited-memory pair with \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) and \(y_i=
abla f(x_{i+1})-
abla f(x_i)\). For tolerance \(	au>0\), the pair is stale at \(x_k\) when \(\lVert y_i-
abla^2 f(x_k)s_iVert>	au\lVert s_iVert\). A memory is stale when this predicate holds for enough retained pairs that their aggregate update no longer approximates the current curvature action within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limited-memory information is stale when old gradient differences no longer approximate the current Hessian acting on their stored displacements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-pair residual is well defined, but the memory-level phrase “enough retained pairs” and the aggregate approximation criterion are unspecified. No source establishes the proposed staleness threshold or a reliable corrected formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Staleness of a Retained Limited-Memory Secant Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2\) near the current iterate \(x_k\), and let a limited-memory method retain pairs \((s_i,y_i)\) generated at earlier iterations \(i<k\). Let \(C_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), choose \(\delta>0\), and assign pair tolerances \(\varepsilon_i\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic objectives where the current Hessian is a meaningful reference. The Hessian may be replaced by a trusted Hessian-vector oracle in matrix-free use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A retained pair \((s_i,y_i)\), with \(s_i\neq0\), is stale at \(x_k\) when its current normalized secant residual \(r_{i,k}=\|y_i-C_ks_i\|_2/(\|y_i\|_2+\|C_ks_i\|_2+\delta\|s_i\|_2)\) exceeds \(\varepsilon_i\). A memory set is stale when a declared aggregation, such as \(\max_{i\in I_k}r_{i,k}\), exceeds its threshold. Age \(k-i\) is not itself staleness: an old pair remains current if it accurately represents present curvature action, while a recent pair can already be stale after a sharp curvature change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored limited-memory secant pair is stale at the current iterate when its recorded curvature difference no longer approximates the current Hessian action on its stored displacement within a stated normalized tolerance. A memory is stale when a declared aggregation of these residuals exceeds its threshold. Iteration age alone is neither necessary nor sufficient.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using a trusted Hessian-vector product \(h_k(s_i)\), replace \(\nabla^2f(x_k)s_i\) by \(h_k(s_i)\).
A weighted memory-level criterion is \(\sum_{i\in I_k}w_ir_{i,k}^2>\varepsilon_{m mem}^2\) for declared positive weights.
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic objective with constant Hessian and exact gradients, every exact stored secant pair remains nonstale.
Lipschitz Hessian continuity permits spatial displacement from the pair's sampling segment to serve as a conservative staleness proxy.
immediate_consequences_latex: Using a stale pair can impose curvature appropriate to an earlier region on the current model.
Discarding by age is only a heuristic proxy for the residual-based definition.
boundary_notes: Noisy gradient differences require a noise-adjusted denominator or statistical test.
At nonsmooth points, a unique Hessian reference may not exist; that regime belongs to nonsmooth secant mismatch.

notation.meaning: normalized current-action residual of stored pair i
indices of pairs retained at iteration k

review_flags: No authoritative limited-memory source was located defining staleness by this exact current-Hessian residual.
The normalization and aggregation rules are proposed and require source validation.

Sparsity Fill-In
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense rank-two secant corrections destroy a sparse metric pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) be sparse and let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(y^{\mathsf T}s>0\). The BFGS update is \(B_+=B-Bss^{\mathsf T}B/(s^{\mathsf T}Bs)+yy^{\mathsf T}/(y^{\mathsf T}s)\). Sparsity fill-in occurs at an index pair \((r,q)\) when \(B_{rq}=0\) but \((B_+)_{rq}\neq0\). If \(Bs\) and \(y\) are dense, both rank-one correction terms are generically dense; absent exact cancellation, previously zero off-diagonal entries become nonzero and explicit sparse storage can grow to quadratic size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS fill-in occurs when dense rank-one corrections turn zeros of a sparse metric into nonzeros, potentially making explicit storage quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{rq}=0\) may coexist with \((B_+)_{rq}\neq0\), and \(B_+\) may be dense.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fill-In Relative to a Prescribed Sparsity Pattern
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\) be a prescribed symmetric sparsity pattern containing the diagonal, let \(B\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfy \(B_{ij}=0\) for \((i,j)\notin P\), and let \(B^+=B+E\) be an updated matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional explicit sparse matrices. Structural nonzeros may be defined algebraically or relative to a numerical drop tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The update produces sparsity fill-in relative to \(P\) when the fill set \(F_P(B^+)=\{(i,j)
otin P:(B^+)_{ij}
eq0\}\) is nonempty. With numerical threshold \(	au\geq0\), define \(F_{P,	au}(B^+)=\{(i,j)
otin P:|(B^+)_{ij}|>	au\}\). A fill-budget failure occurs when the weighted cardinality or storage cost of this set exceeds a declared budget. Fill-in is pattern-relative: the same update can preserve one admissible pattern and violate another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An update creates sparsity fill-in when the updated matrix has a nonzero entry outside a prescribed sparsity pattern that the previous matrix respected. A numerical version counts only entries exceeding a drop tolerance, and a resource failure occurs when their number or storage cost exceeds a stated budget. Fill-in is always relative to the chosen pattern.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Pi_P\) is the entrywise projector onto pattern \(P\), fill-in occurs exactly when \((I-\Pi_P)B^+\neq0\).
For \(B^+=B+E\) with \(B\) supported on \(P\), the fill set equals the off-pattern support of \(E\).
special_cases_latex: A dense rank-one correction \(uv^T\) generally fills every off-pattern position where \(u_iv_j\neq0\).
Projection \(B^+\leftarrow\Pi_P(B^+)\) removes algebraic fill but can destroy an exact secant equation or positive definiteness.
immediate_consequences_latex: Fill-in can increase storage and matrix-operation costs beyond those predicted by the original pattern.
A fill budget supplies a precise accept, project, or compress criterion.
boundary_notes: Fill in a matrix factorization is distinct from fill in the updated matrix itself.
Entries below a drop tolerance are numerical rather than algebraic zeros.

notation.meaning: set of nonzeros outside the prescribed pattern

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance of a secant metric from an application-prescribed structure class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{S}^n\) be a prescribed closed class of admissible curvature models, such as matrices with a fixed sparsity pattern, block structure, or linear invariance constraints. For a computed secant metric \(B_k\), define \(d_{\mathcal{S}}(B_k)=\inf_{M\in\mathcal{S}}\lVert B_k-M\rVert\). Given tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), structure-model mismatch occurs when \(d_{\mathcal{S}}(B_k)>\tau\). When \(\mathcal{S}\) is a linear subspace and the norm is Frobenius, the mismatch equals \(\lVert B_k-P_{\mathcal{S}}B_k\rVert_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant model is structurally mismatched when its distance from the prescribed sparse, block, or invariant matrix class exceeds tolerance.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projection onto a linear structure class

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mismatch Between an Admissible Structural Model and Curvature Data
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal C_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be the curvature-model class imposed by known problem structure, and let \(S_k,Y_k\) be observed secant data. Choose a norm, a positive scale \(\sigma_k\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional structured quasi-Newton modeling. The structural class may encode block separability, sparsity, symmetry, invariance, Kronecker form, or another explicitly declared constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is structure-model mismatch at iteration \(k\) when no matrix in the imposed structural class fits the observed curvature information to the required accuracy: \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal C_k}\|BS_k-Y_k\|/\sigma_k>\varepsilon_k\). If a reference curvature operator \(C_k\) is available, intrinsic model-class mismatch is \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal C_k}\|B-C_k\|/\|C_k\|>\varepsilon_k\). The definition distinguishes an inadequate structural class from a poor parameter choice within an adequate class; mismatch persists after minimizing over every admissible model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structure-model mismatch occurs when no curvature matrix satisfying the imposed problem structure can fit the observed secant data within a declared normalized tolerance. If a reference curvature operator is available, the same idea is the distance from that operator to the entire structural class. Because the residual is minimized over the class, the failure concerns the class itself rather than a single poorly selected model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact mismatch is the emptiness of \(\{B\in\mathcal C_k:BS_k=Y_k\}\).
If \(\mathcal C_k\) is closed and convex under a Hilbert-space matrix norm, the mismatch residual is the distance of the data-fitting constraint to that class.
special_cases_latex: For a prescribed block-diagonal class, cross-block curvature observed in \((S_k,Y_k)\) may make exact fitting impossible.
For a sparsity class, off-pattern curvature action can produce mismatch even when storing the model remains inexpensive.
immediate_consequences_latex: Resolving mismatch requires relaxing the structural class, changing the data model, or accepting approximation error.
Projecting an unconstrained update into \(\mathcal C_k\) does not guarantee the secant residual is below tolerance.
boundary_notes: Sparsity fill-in concerns an update leaving a pattern; structure mismatch concerns the inability of the entire allowed class to represent required curvature.
Noisy data require tolerances calibrated to uncertainty.
review_flags: No inspected source was found supporting this exact class-distance definition for structured quasi-Newton models.
The alternative operator-distance formulation requires a dedicated structured-method source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary of Validity for Smooth Secant Curvature Modeling
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and let a secant model assume that gradient differences along segments satisfy \(y=\int_0^1H(x+ts)s\,dt\) for a single-valued bounded curvature field \(H\). Fix an admissible regularity region \(\mathcal R\subseteq\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between smooth curvature modeling and regimes with nondifferentiability, discontinuous gradients, unbounded curvature variation, noise, or saddle-type curvature. The definition is model-relative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The smoothness-curvature compatibility region is the set of points having a neighborhood on which \(f\in C^{1,1}\) and the selected curvature model class can represent gradient increments within tolerance. Its boundary is \(\partial\mathcal R=\overline{\mathcal R}\cap\overline{\Omega\setminus\mathcal R}\). A secant pair crosses a mismatch boundary when the segment \([x,x+s]\) is not contained in \(\mathcal R\), or when its normalized best-fit residual \(\inf_{H\in\mathcal H(x,s)}\|y-Hs\|/\sigma(x,s)\) exceeds the declared tolerance. Thus the boundary marks where assumptions supporting a stable smooth curvature interpretation cease to hold, not necessarily where the objective itself is discontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smoothness-curvature compatibility region consists of points with a neighborhood where the objective has a Lipschitz gradient and the chosen curvature model can represent gradient changes within tolerance. Its topological boundary separates this region from points where those requirements fail. A secant pair crosses the boundary if its segment leaves the compatible region or cannot be fitted by the admissible curvature models.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A point lies on \(\partial\mathcal R\) exactly when every neighborhood intersects both compatible and incompatible regimes.
For an open compatibility region, boundary crossing is detected whenever the closed secant segment is not contained in that region.
special_cases_latex: At a kink of a locally Lipschitz function, a unique classical gradient increment model may fail.
With noisy gradients, the compatibility boundary depends on the declared noise-aware tolerance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Smooth quasi-Newton secant interpretations require qualification for pairs crossing the boundary.
Different curvature model classes may induce different compatibility regions for the same objective.
boundary_notes: Indefinite but smooth Hessian curvature need not violate smoothness; it violates a positive-curvature model only if that restriction is imposed.
The definition does not claim that all algorithms fail outside \(\mathcal R\).

notation.meaning: region where the selected smooth curvature model is valid
admissible average-curvature models for the secant segment

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary of Validity for Smooth Secant Curvature Modeling
Nonsmooth Secant Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A kink makes gradient-based secant curvature unbounded under shrinking crossings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\lvert x\rvert\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), choose \(x_-=-t\) and \(x_+=t\) with \(t>0\). Using the classical gradients away from the kink gives \(s=x_+-x_-=2t\) and \(y=f'(x_+)-f'(x_-)=2\). The scalar secant curvature is therefore \(y/s=1/t\to\infty\) as \(t\downarrow0\). Hence no bounded Hessian model can satisfy these crossing secant equations uniformly near the kink, although \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the absolute-value function, secant curvature across the kink diverges as the crossing interval shrinks, so bounded smooth Hessian models cannot fit it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mismatch of a Nonsmooth Generalized Secant Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz, choose \(g\in\partial f(x)\) and \(g^+\in\partial f(x+s)\), and set \(y=g^+-g\). Let \(\mathcal H(x,s)\) be a declared admissible class of generalized curvature matrices, with scale \(\sigma(x,s,y)>0\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally Lipschitz nonsmooth optimization with explicitly selected subgradients or generalized gradients. The definition is relative to the chosen generalized derivative and curvature model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generalized secant pair \((s,y)\), with \(s\neq0\), has nonsmooth secant mismatch when no admissible generalized curvature matrix maps the displacement to the selected generalized-gradient difference within tolerance: \(\inf_{H\in\mathcal H(x,s)}\|Hs-y\|_2/\sigma(x,s,y)>\varepsilon\). Exact mismatch is the emptiness of \(\{H\in\mathcal H(x,s):Hs=y\}\). Because subgradients may be set-valued, mismatch can depend on the selections \(g\) and \(g^+\); a selection-robust variant takes the infimum or supremum over all allowed endpoint selections, as explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz objective, a selected generalized secant pair is mismatched when no admissible generalized curvature matrix maps its displacement to its selected subgradient difference within a stated normalized tolerance. Exact mismatch means no such matrix exists. Since endpoint subgradients need not be unique, the diagnosis depends on their selection unless a robust quantifier over all selections is specified.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact compatibility is \(g^+-g\in\{Hs:H\in\mathcal H(x,s)\}\); exact mismatch is failure of this membership.
A selection-existential mismatch test minimizes the residual jointly over \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \(g^+\in\partial f(x+s)\), and \(H\in\mathcal H(x,s)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is \(C^2\) along the segment and \(\mathcal H(x,s)\) contains the averaged Hessian, the exact classical gradient pair is compatible.
Across a kink, different legitimate subgradient selections can produce different \(y\) for the same displacement.
immediate_consequences_latex: A mismatched pair cannot impose an exact secant equation within the chosen generalized-curvature class.
Changing the subgradient selection or enlarging the admissible model class can alter the diagnosis.
boundary_notes: This definition does not identify a unique generalized Hessian; the derivative notion must be declared.
Noise-induced mismatch is not separated from genuine set-valued nonsmoothness without an uncertainty model.

notation.meaning: declared generalized-gradient or subdifferential set at x
admissible generalized curvature matrices for the segment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deterministic reliability boundary for a noisy secant-curvature measurement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x_0,x_1\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s=x_1-x_0
e0\), and suppose that the available gradients are \(\widetilde g_i=
abla h(x_i)+e_i\), where \(\|e_i\|_\infty\leq\delta_i\) for known bounds \(\delta_i\geq0\), \(i\in\{0,1\}\). Define the exact and observed secant vectors by \(y=
abla h(x_1)-
abla h(x_0)\) and \(\widetilde y=\widetilde g_1-\widetilde g_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic error-bound regime. The definition concerns whether the sign of directional secant curvature can be certified from perturbed gradients; it does not assume convexity or a particular quasi-Newton update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the observed curvature and its worst-case uncertainty radius by
\[
\widetilde\kappa=s^T\widetilde y,
\qquad
E(s,\delta_0,\delta_1)=\|s\|_1(\delta_0+\delta_1).
\]
The noisy curvature observation is reliably positive when \(\widetilde\kappa>E\), reliably negative when \(\widetilde\kappa<-E\), and sign-indeterminate when \(|\widetilde\kappa|\leq E\). The noisy curvature reliability boundary is
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{noise}}=
\{(s,\widetilde y,\delta_0,\delta_1):s\ne0,\ \delta_0,\delta_1\geq0,\ |s^T\widetilde y|=\|s\|_1(\delta_0+\delta_1)\}.
\]
Equivalently, the positive-curvature certificate has signed reliability margin \(m_+=\widetilde\kappa-E\), while the negative-curvature certificate has margin \(m_-=-\widetilde\kappa-E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero displacement \(s\), form the observed secant vector \(\widetilde y\) from two perturbed gradients. If the endpoint errors are bounded in the infinity norm by \(\delta_0\) and \(\delta_1\), the observed scalar curvature \(\widetilde\kappa=s^T\widetilde y\) has uncertainty radius \(E=\|s\|_1(\delta_0+\delta_1)\). Curvature is reliably positive when \(\widetilde\kappa>E\), reliably negative when \(\widetilde\kappa<-E\), and unresolved when \(|\widetilde\kappa|\leq E\). Equality \(|\widetilde\kappa|=E\) is the reliability boundary separating certified signs from the indeterminate band.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde g_i=\nabla h(x_i)+e_i\) with deterministic bounds \(\|e_i\|_\infty\leq\delta_i\), where \(\delta_i\geq0\) for \(i=0,1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign classification is determined by comparing \(s^T\widetilde y\) with \(\pm\|s\|_1(\delta_0+\delta_1)\), and the boundary is the equality \(|s^T\widetilde y|=\|s\|_1(\delta_0+\delta_1)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(\kappa=s^Ty\), the endpoint error bounds give the uncertainty interval \(\kappa\in[\widetilde\kappa-E,\widetilde\kappa+E]\). Thus reliable positivity means that this entire interval lies in \((0,\infty)\), reliable negativity means that it lies in \(( -\infty,0)\), and indeterminacy means that it contains \(0\).
For a candidate positive-definite secant update, the robust curvature condition is \(s^T\widetilde y>\|s\|_1(\delta_0+\delta_1)\), rather than merely \(s^T\widetilde y>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\delta_0=\delta_1=0\), then \(E=0\), and the classification reduces to the exact secant-curvature sign of \(s^Ty\).
If both errors have the common bound \(\delta\), then \(E=2\delta\|s\|_1\).
For scalar problems, \(n=1\), the boundary becomes \(|s\widetilde y|=|s|(\delta_0+\delta_1)\), or equivalently \(|\widetilde y|=\delta_0+\delta_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(\widetilde\kappa>E\), every exact gradient pair compatible with the error bounds satisfies \(s^Ty>0\); hence the secant data pass the positive-curvature condition required by a positive-definite BFGS-type update.
When \(|\widetilde\kappa|\leq E\), the same observed data and error bounds are compatible with zero or oppositely signed exact curvature, so the sign cannot be certified deterministically.
The normalized quantity \((|\widetilde\kappa|-E)/\|s\|_2^2\), for \(s\ne0\), measures signed distance from the boundary in directional-curvature units.
boundary_notes: The definition requires finite deterministic error bounds. Unbounded stochastic noise requires a probabilistic confidence boundary instead.
The case \(s=0\) is excluded because no directional secant curvature is sampled.
The bound is norm-dependent: replacing the infinity-norm error model by another norm replaces \(\|s\|_1\) by the corresponding dual norm.
The condition identifies reliability of the curvature sign only; it does not certify that the complete Hessian approximation is accurate or well-conditioned.

children.title: Deterministic Curvature Noise
children.top_down_role: Curvature-information distortion caused by persistent deterministic error.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Curvature Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded deterministic gradient errors can dominate a secant curvature signal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the observed gradient be \(\widetilde g(x)=
abla f(x)+e(x)\), where \(\lVert e(x)Vert\leq\delta\). For \(s=x_+-x_-\), define \(y=
abla f(x_+)-
abla f(x_-)\) and \(\widetilde y=\widetilde g(x_+)-\widetilde g(x_-)\). Then \(\lVert\widetilde y-yVert\leq2\delta\) and \(\lvert s^{\mathsf T}(\widetilde y-y)vert\leq2\delta\lVert sVert\). Thus the curvature-sign reliability boundary is \(s^{\mathsf T}y\leq2\delta\lVert sVert\), where admissible deterministic errors can make \(s^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniformly bounded gradient error, secant curvature error scales as the step length and can reverse curvature sign when the true signal is too small.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic error bounds and sign-reversal possibility are mathematically plausible, but the proposed quantity is presented as a curvature reliability boundary without any authoritative source or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Stochastic Curvature Variability
children.top_down_role: Curvature-information variability caused by stochastic observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Curvature Variability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent gradient noise determines the variance of observed secant curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\widetilde g(x)=
abla f(x)+\xi(x)\), where endpoint noises \(\xi_-\) and \(\xi_+\) are independent, have zero mean, and share covariance \(\Sigma\). For \(s=x_+-x_-\), \(y=
abla f(x_+)-
abla f(x_-)\), and \(\widetilde y=y+\xi_+-\xi_-\), one has \(\mathbb{E}[\widetilde y]=y\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde y)=2\Sigma\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(s^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y)=2s^{\mathsf T}\Sigma s\). Thus unbiased gradients do not imply low-variance curvature pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent unbiased gradient noise doubles the endpoint covariance in a secant difference, giving curvature variance proportional to the noise covariance along the step.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi_-\) and \(\xi_+\) are independent and zero mean.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covariance and directional-variance formulas follow under the stated independent equal-covariance endpoint-noise model, and the property fits the leaf. Nevertheless, no source supports using this stochastic model as candidate knowledge in the taxonomy.

children.title: Secant-Pair Reliability Loss
children.top_down_role: Degradation of usable secant information under noisy curvature observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant-Pair Reliability Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signal-to-noise condition for accepting a noisy curvature pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\neq0\) and let the observed secant difference be \(\widetilde y=y+\zeta\), with \(\mathbb{E}[\zeta]=0\) and covariance \(C\). Define the curvature signal-to-noise ratio by \(R=(s^{\mathsf T}y)/\sqrt{s^{\mathsf T}Cs}\) when \(s^{\mathsf T}Cs>0\). For a prescribed reliability threshold \(\kappa>0\), secant-pair reliability is lost when \(R\leq\kappa\). In this regime the mean curvature signal is no more than \(\kappa\) standard deviations above zero, so the observed curvature condition can be noise-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant pair loses reliability when its true directional curvature is too small relative to the standard deviation of its noise-induced curvature error.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signal-to-noise ratio is well defined under the stated positive-variance assumption, but the threshold \(\kappa\) and the declaration that reliability is lost at \(R\leq\kappa\) are conventional choices requiring an authoritative secant-filtering source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary between positive-definite secant models and saddle curvature
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(\mathcal D\). For \(x,x+s\in\mathcal D\) with \(s
e0\), define \(y=
abla f(x+s)-
abla f(x)\) and the averaged Hessian \(\overline G(x,s)=\int_0^1
abla^2f(x+ts)\,dt\), so that \(y=\overline G(x,s)s\). A positive-definite quasi-Newton model uses a symmetric matrix \(B\succ0\) and seeks to impose the secant equation \(Bs=y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth, exact-gradient regime. The definition describes representability of sampled curvature by a symmetric positive-definite secant model and its infinitesimal relation to strict saddles; it does not cover nonsmooth generalized Hessians or noisy secant data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the sampled directional curvature by
\[
\kappa(x,s)=s^Ty=s^T\overline G(x,s)s.
\]
The positive-definite model region, saddle-curvature region, and saddle-curvature model boundary are respectively
\[
\mathcal R_+=\{(x,s):s\ne0,\ \kappa(x,s)>0\},
\qquad
\mathcal R_-=\{(x,s):s\ne0,\ \kappa(x,s)<0\},
\]
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{saddle}}=\{(x,s):s\ne0,\ \kappa(x,s)=0\}.
\]
A symmetric positive-definite matrix satisfying \(Bs=y\) exists exactly on \(\mathcal R_+\). On \(\mathcal R_-\cup\mathcal B_{\mathrm{saddle}}\), the exact secant equation is incompatible with \(B\succ0\). Infinitesimally, at a stationary point \(x_*\), the corresponding spectral boundary is \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x_*))=0\); the strict-saddle side has \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x_*))<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero step \(s\), the exact gradient change \(y\) samples directional curvature through \(\kappa=s^Ty\). Positive sampled curvature, \(\kappa>0\), is precisely the regime in which some symmetric positive-definite matrix can satisfy the secant equation \(Bs=y\). Negative sampled curvature, \(\kappa<0\), is the saddle-curvature side, where no positive-definite secant model can reproduce the observation. The equality \(\kappa=0\) is the model boundary. At infinitesimal scale around a stationary point, this boundary corresponds to a zero smallest Hessian eigenvalue, while a negative smallest eigenvalue identifies a strict saddle direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(f\in C^2(\mathcal D)\).
\(x,x+s\in\mathcal D\), the segment \(\{x+ts:0\leq t\leq1\}\) lies in \(\mathcal D\), and \(s\ne0\).
The secant data are exact: \(y=\nabla f(x+s)-\nabla f(x)\).
The model class under comparison consists of real symmetric positive-definite matrices \(B\succ0\) constrained by \(Bs=y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality \(s^Ty=0\) is the boundary separating positive-definite secant representability \((s^Ty>0)\) from negative sampled saddle curvature \((s^Ty<0)\), and every pair with \(s^Ty\leq0\) is incompatible with an exact positive-definite secant model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(y=\overline G(x,s)s\), the boundary condition is equivalently \(s^T\overline G(x,s)s=0\), where \(\overline G(x,s)=\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x+ts)\,dt\).

For a stationary point \(x_*\), the infinitesimal model boundary is \(\min_{\|d\|_2=1}d^T
abla^2f(x_*)d=0\). A strict saddle satisfies \(
abla f(x_*)=0\) and \(\min_{\|d\|_2=1}d^T
abla^2f(x_*)d<0\).
Positive-definite secant representability may be written \(\{B=B^T\succ0:Bs=y\}\ne\varnothing\), which is equivalent to \(s^Ty>0\) for \(s\ne0\).
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic objective \(f(x)=c+g^Tx+\tfrac12x^TGx\) with \(G=G^T\), one has \(y=Gs\) and \(\kappa=s^TGs\); hence the boundary is exactly the null cone \(s^TGs=0\).
If \(G\succ0\), every nonzero step lies in \(\mathcal R_+\), so the saddle-curvature boundary is empty for that quadratic model.

If \(x_*\) is stationary and \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\) has a negative eigenpair \((\lambda,d)\), then the infinitesimal direction \(d\) lies on the saddle-curvature side because \(d^T\nabla^2f(x_*)d=\lambda\|d\|_2^2<0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A BFGS or DFP update required to remain positive definite cannot satisfy exact secant data with \(s^Ty\leq0\) without damping, altering the secant vector, skipping the update, or changing the model class.
An indefinite update such as SR1 can represent negative curvature and is therefore not subject to the positive-definite representability restriction \(s^Ty>0\).

A positive-definite quadratic model assigns strictly positive curvature to every nonzero direction and consequently suppresses any negative-curvature direction present in the true or averaged Hessian.
At a strict saddle, a step method using only a positive-definite model may retain descent directions but cannot encode the saddle's negative curvature exactly.
boundary_notes: The equality \(s^Ty=0\) belongs to the incompatibility side for strictly positive-definite models, because \(s^TBs>0\) for every \(s\ne0\) when \(B\succ0\).
Negative sampled curvature does not by itself prove that either endpoint is a stationary saddle; it certifies only negative average curvature along the sampled segment.
A stationary point with a positive-semidefinite singular Hessian lies on the spectral boundary but need not be a saddle, since higher-order terms may determine its local type.
Allowing symmetric indefinite models removes the positive-definite secant obstruction and changes the relevant model boundary.

children.title: Saddle-Point Proximity
children.top_down_role: Quasi-Newton model behavior near stationary points lacking local minimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Proximity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate first-order stationarity combined with certified negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\), and fix tolerances \(\varepsilon\geq0\) and \(\gamma>0\). A point \(x\) is in \((\varepsilon,\gamma)\)-saddle-point proximity when \(\lVert
abla f(x)Vert\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 f(x))\leq-\gamma\). Equivalently, there exists a unit vector \(v\) such that \(v^{\mathsf T}
abla^2 f(x)v\leq-\gamma\). The condition separates approximate first-order stationarity from approximate second-order minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is near a strict saddle when its gradient is small but its Hessian retains a direction of sufficiently negative curvature.

children.title: Negative-Curvature Regimes
children.top_down_role: Model regimes containing directions of negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where a positive-definite quasi-Newton metric cannot represent genuine negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable at \(x\), let \(H=\nabla^2 f(x)\), and suppose a unit vector \(d\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=-\gamma<0\). For every symmetric metric \(B\succeq mI\) with \(m\ge 0\),
\[
\lVert B-H\rVert_2\ge d^{\mathsf T}(B-H)d\ge m+\gamma.
\]
Thus no positive-semidefinite variable metric can reproduce the curvature of \(f\) along \(d\). Moreover, the true quadratic term \(\tfrac12t^2d^{\mathsf T}Hd\) decreases with \(t^2\), whereas the metric-model term \(\tfrac12t^2d^{\mathsf T}Bd\) is nonnegative. A method enforcing positive definiteness must therefore regularize, truncate, or otherwise treat this negative-curvature direction separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quasi-Newton metric cannot approximate a negative Hessian direction without an operator-norm error at least equal to the conflicting curvature magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert B-\nabla^2f(x)\rVert_2\ge m+\gamma\), so the positive metric cannot represent the negative-curvature direction.

nonnegative lower spectral bound imposed on the metric

children.title: Positive-Metric Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Conflict between enforced positive metrics and locally indefinite curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Metric Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant-curvature boundary for updates constrained to remain uniformly positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(s\ne0\), where \(s\) is a displacement and \(y\) is the corresponding gradient difference. If a symmetric metric \(B\succeq mI\), with \(m>0\), satisfies the secant equation \(Bs=y\), then necessarily
\[
y^{\mathsf T}s=s^{\mathsf T}Bs\ge m\lVert s\rVert_2^2>0.
\]
Consequently, when \(y^{\mathsf T}s<m\lVert s\rVert_2^2\), no such metric satisfies the secant equation. More quantitatively, every \(B\succeq mI\) obeys
\[
\lVert Bs-y\rVert_2\ge \frac{m\lVert s\rVert_2^2-y^{\mathsf T}s}{\lVert s\rVert_2}.
\]
Thus exact secant fitting and the prescribed positive spectral bound are incompatible in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact secant equation is incompatible with a uniformly positive metric when the observed secant curvature falls below the metric’s required spectral lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(y^{\mathsf T}s<m\lVert s\rVert_2^2\), then \(Bs=y\) is impossible for every \(B\succeq mI\), with the displayed residual lower bound.

notation.meaning: gradient difference associated with the displacement
strict lower spectral bound required of the metric
